T6-0001.ex: 검찰은 증거 불충분으로 그 사건을 불기소 처분했습니다.
T6-0001.x: Prosecutors decided not to prosecute the case due to insufficient evidence.
T6-0001.e: Literally 'not raising a lawsuit' — prosecutors decline to bring charges.
T6-0001.t: Usually appears as 불기소 처분 'decision not to indict' in news reports.

T6-0002.ex: 검사는 피고인에 대해 법원에 공소를 제기했습니다.
T6-0002.x: The prosecutor filed charges against the defendant with the court.
T6-0002.e: Literally 'public lawsuit' — the state, not the victim, brings the case.
T6-0002.t: 공소를 제기하다 'to institute a prosecution' is a formal synonym of 기소하다.

T6-0003.ex: 그 사건은 공소시효가 이미 지나서 처벌할 수 없어요.
T6-0003.x: The statute of limitations on that case has already run out, so no one can be punished.

T6-0004.m: dismissal (of a suit without review on the merits)
T6-0004.ex: 법원은 요건을 갖추지 못한 소송을 각하했습니다.
T6-0004.x: The court dismissed the lawsuit because it failed to meet the requirements.
T6-0004.e: Literally 'reject down'; the homonym 각하 also means 'Your Excellency'.
T6-0004.t: Don't confuse with 기각: 각하 throws a case out on procedure, while 기각 rejects it after review.

T6-0005.x: Refusing to accept the appellate ruling, the defendant appealed to the Supreme Court.
T6-0005.t: Korea's ladder: 항소 goes from the first trial to the second, 상고 from the second to the Supreme Court.

T6-0006.ex: 판결에 불복하는 당사자는 상급 법원에 상소할 수 있습니다.
T6-0006.x: A party who disputes a ruling can appeal to a higher court.
T6-0006.e: Literally 'sue upward' — the umbrella term covering 항소 and 상고.

T6-0007.m: written judgment, text of a ruling
T6-0007.x: The judge began reading the judgment in the courtroom.
T6-0007.e: Literally 'decision text': 판결 'ruling' plus 문 'written text'.

T6-0008.x: The prosecution asked for a 10-year prison sentence for the defendant.
T6-0008.t: Don't confuse 구형 (the prosecutor's demand) with 선고 (the judge's actual sentence); news often reports both.

T6-0009.x: He was sentenced to one year in prison, suspended for two years.
T6-0009.e: Literally 'hesitating on execution' — the sentence is held off unless you reoffend.
T6-0009.t: Headlines often shorten it to 집유, e.g. 징역 2년 집유 3년.

T6-0010.ex: 그는 모범적으로 생활한 덕분에 형기 만료 전에 가석방되었습니다.
T6-0010.x: Thanks to good behavior, he was paroled before his term ended.

T6-0012.x: The court issued an arrest warrant, citing the seriousness of the crime.
T6-0012.e: Literally 'a document ordering someone held and bound'.
T6-0012.t: Prosecutors 구속영장을 청구하다 'request a warrant'; the court 발부하다 'issues' or 기각하다 'rejects' it.

T6-0013.ex: 경찰은 오늘 아침 그 회사 본사를 압수수색했습니다.
T6-0013.x: Police raided the company's headquarters this morning.
T6-0013.e: 압수 'seizure' plus 수색 'search': a raid to search and confiscate.

T6-0014.ex: 변호사는 법정에서 피고인을 위해 열심히 변론했습니다.
T6-0014.x: The lawyer argued hard for the defendant in court.
T6-0014.t: Pronounced [별론] — ㄴ before ㄹ becomes ㄹ (liquidization).

T6-0015.ex: 피의자는 변호인의 도움을 받을 권리가 있습니다.
T6-0015.x: A suspect has the right to the assistance of counsel.
T6-0015.e: Literally 'a person who speaks to protect' someone.
T6-0015.t: 변호사 is the profession; 변호인 is the role of defending a particular client in a case.

T6-0016.ex: 피의자가 조사를 받기 위해 검찰청에 출석했습니다.
T6-0016.x: The suspect appeared at the prosecutors' office for questioning.

T6-0017.ex: 헌법재판소는 그 법률이 헌법에 위반된다고 결정했습니다.
T6-0017.x: The Constitutional Court ruled that the law violates the Constitution.
T6-0017.t: News usually shortens it to 헌재.

T6-0018.ex: 헌법재판소는 그 조항에 대해 합헌 결정을 내렸습니다.
T6-0018.x: The Constitutional Court ruled that the provision is constitutional.
T6-0018.e: Literally 'agreeing with the constitution'; the opposite is 위헌.
T6-0018.t: Pronounced [하펀] — ㅂ plus ㅎ becomes an aspirated ㅍ.

T6-0019.x: He filed a constitutional complaint, saying his basic rights had been violated.
T6-0019.e: Literally 'constitutional petition' — a citizen asks the court to protect basic rights.

T6-0020.ex: 국회는 대통령에 대한 탄핵 소추안을 통과시켰습니다.
T6-0020.x: The National Assembly passed the motion to impeach the president.
T6-0020.e: Literally 'sue and pursue'; mostly seen in 탄핵소추 'impeachment'.

T6-0021.ex: 고소인은 경찰서에서 피해 사실을 자세히 진술했습니다.
T6-0021.x: The complainant described the harm in detail at the police station.
T6-0021.e: -인 = person in a legal role: 고소인, 피고인, 변호인.
T6-0021.t: 고소 is filed by the victim; 고발 is filed by a third party who isn't the victim.

T6-0022.ex: 목격자는 경찰서에서 사건 당시 상황에 대한 진술서를 작성했습니다.
T6-0022.x: At the police station, the witness wrote a statement about what happened at the time.

T6-0023.x: He was indicted on charges of committing perjury in court.
T6-0023.t: The verb is 위증하다; the crime itself is 위증죄.

T6-0024.x: Police secured the weapon at the scene as evidence.
T6-0024.e: 증거 'evidence' plus 물 'object': a physical item of evidence.

T6-0025.ex: 심증은 있지만 확실한 물증이 없어서 기소하기 어려워요.
T6-0025.x: There's a strong suspicion, but without solid physical evidence it's hard to indict.
T6-0025.e: Literally 'object proof'; contrasts with 심증 'inner conviction'.
T6-0025.t: 심증은 있는데 물증이 없다 'I'm sure, but I can't prove it' is also used jokingly in daily life.

T6-0026.x: The detective became convinced that he was the culprit.
T6-0026.e: Literally 'proof in the heart' — what you believe before you can prove it.

T6-0027.ex: 여러 정황으로 보아 그가 범인일 가능성이 높습니다.
T6-0027.x: Judging from the various circumstances, he is likely the culprit.

T6-0028.ex: 용의자는 사건 당일 친구와 함께 있었다는 알리바이를 댔습니다.
T6-0028.x: The suspect gave an alibi that he was with a friend on the day of the incident.
T6-0028.t: Common verbs: 알리바이를 대다 'give an alibi', 알리바이가 있다 or 없다, 알리바이를 입증하다 'prove an alibi'.

T6-0029.ex: 경찰은 이번 사건의 주범을 해외에서 검거했습니다.
T6-0029.x: Police caught the mastermind of the case overseas.
T6-0029.t: Often figurative in the news: 대기 오염의 주범 'the main culprit behind air pollution'.

T6-0030.x: He was punished as the instigator who ordered the murder.
T6-0030.e: Here 교사 means 'incitement', not 'teacher' — a homonym trap.

T6-0031.ex: 그는 사기 범행을 방조한 혐의로 재판에 넘겨졌습니다.
T6-0031.x: He was put on trial for aiding and abetting the fraud.
T6-0031.e: Literally 'helping and assisting' — knowingly helping someone commit a crime.

T6-0032.ex: 그는 살인 미수 혐의로 경찰에 체포되었습니다.
T6-0032.x: He was arrested by police on charges of attempted murder.
T6-0032.e: Literally 'not yet accomplished' — a crime tried but not completed.
T6-0032.t: It goes after the crime name: 살인 미수 'attempted murder', 강도 미수 'attempted robbery'.
rel: to end as a mere attempt

T6-0033.ex: 트럭 운전자는 업무상 과실치사 혐의로 경찰에 입건되었습니다.
T6-0033.x: The truck driver was booked by police on charges of negligent homicide in the course of work.
T6-0033.e: Literally 'causing death by mistake' — killing through negligence, not intent.

T6-0034.ex: 국회의원은 국회에서 한 발언에 대해 면책 특권을 가집니다.
T6-0034.x: Lawmakers have immunity for statements made in the National Assembly.

T6-0035.m: dismissal of prosecution (e.g., after the statute of limitations or an amnesty)
T6-0035.ex: 공소시효가 지나 법원은 면소 판결을 내렸습니다.
T6-0035.x: Because the statute of limitations had expired, the court dismissed the case.
T6-0035.e: Literally 'released from the lawsuit' — ends the case without judging guilt.
T6-0035.t: Unlike 무죄, 면소 doesn't declare innocence; the case simply can't go forward.

T6-0036.x: On appeal, his sentence was reduced from five years to three.

T6-0037.m: length of a sentence, severity of punishment
T6-0037.ex: 피해자 가족은 형량이 너무 가볍다고 반발했습니다.
T6-0037.x: The victim's family protested that the sentence was too light.
T6-0037.t: Pronounced [형냥] — ㄹ becomes ㄴ after ㅇ.

T6-0038.x: He was sentenced to one year of imprisonment without labor for professional negligence.
T6-0038.e: Literally 'confine and shut in'; the homonym 금고 means 'safe, vault'.
T6-0038.t: 징역 includes prison labor; 금고 is confinement only, often given for negligence crimes.

T6-0039.ex: 그는 음주 운전으로 500만 원의 벌금형을 선고받았습니다.
T6-0039.x: He was sentenced to a fine of 5 million won for drunk driving.
T6-0039.e: -형 = type of sentence: 벌금형, 징역형, 사형.
T6-0039.t: 과태료 is an administrative penalty (like a parking fine), while 벌금형 is a criminal sentence.

T6-0040.ex: 법원은 범죄로 얻은 재산을 모두 몰수했습니다.
T6-0040.x: The court confiscated all the assets gained through the crime.
T6-0040.e: Literally 'take away and collect' — the state takes the property for good.
T6-0040.t: 압수 is a temporary seizure during an investigation; 몰수 is permanent forfeiture by judgment.

T6-0041.m: forfeiture of equivalent value; collection (of illegal gains or back taxes)
T6-0041.ex: 법원은 피고인에게 뇌물로 받은 1억 원을 추징했습니다.
T6-0041.x: The court ordered the defendant to forfeit the 100 million won he took in bribes.
T6-0041.e: Literally 'pursue and collect' — taking the cash value when the item itself is gone.
T6-0041.t: Also used for taxes: 세금을 추징하다 'to collect back taxes'.

T6-0042.ex: 그는 빚을 기한 안에 모두 변제했습니다.
T6-0042.x: He repaid all his debts before the deadline.
T6-0042.t: In daily speech say 빚을 갚다; 변제 shows up in contracts and court documents.

T6-0043.ex: 채권자들이 회사에 빌려준 돈을 갚으라고 요구했습니다.
T6-0043.x: The creditors demanded that the company pay back the money they had lent.
T6-0043.e: Literally 'person with a right to a debt'; -자 = person: 채권자, 소비자.
T6-0043.t: Pronounced [채꿘자] with a tensed ㄱ; don't mix it up with 채무자 'debtor'.

T6-0044.ex: 채무자가 돈을 갚지 않고 연락을 끊어 버렸습니다.
T6-0044.x: The debtor cut off contact without paying the money back.

T6-0045.m: mortgage, pledge of property as collateral
T6-0045.ex: 그는 집을 저당 잡히고 은행에서 돈을 빌렸습니다.
T6-0045.x: He mortgaged his house and borrowed money from the bank.
T6-0045.t: The borrower says 집을 저당 잡히다 'to mortgage the house'; the bank 저당 잡다 'holds it as collateral'.

T6-0046.m: maximum-amount mortgage (securing future debts up to a ceiling)
T6-0046.ex: 이 아파트에는 은행의 근저당이 설정되어 있어요.
T6-0046.x: This apartment has a bank mortgage registered on it.
T6-0046.e: 근 'root' plus 저당 'mortgage' — a ceiling-amount mortgage covering future debts.
T6-0046.t: Before renting a jeonse apartment, check the property register for any 근저당 — a key tenant safety step.

T6-0047.x: The creditor applied for a provisional attachment on the debtor's house.
T6-0047.e: Literally 'provisional seizing and holding' — freezes assets before the trial ends.
T6-0047.t: Pronounced [가암뉴] — ㄹ becomes ㄴ, which turns ㅂ into ㅁ.

T6-0048.ex: 그 회사는 법원에 기업 회생 절차를 신청했습니다.
T6-0048.x: The company filed for corporate rehabilitation with the court.
T6-0048.e: Literally 'returning to life' — also used for patients and economies.

T6-0049.ex: 사업이 커지자 그는 회사를 법인으로 전환했습니다.
T6-0049.x: As the business grew, he turned the company into a corporation.
T6-0049.e: Literally 'legal person' — a company the law treats like a person.
T6-0049.t: Pronounced [버빈]; 법인 카드 means a corporate credit card.

T6-0050.x: Legally, persons are divided into natural persons and corporations.
T6-0050.e: Literally 'natural person'; on Korean TV it also means a recluse living in the mountains.

T6-0051.x: A minor needs the consent of a legal representative to sign a contract.
T6-0051.e: Here 법정 means 'set by law', not 'courtroom'; usually a minor's parents.

T6-0052.x: The court appointed the grandmother as the child's guardian.
T6-0052.e: Literally 'a person who watches from behind' and looks after someone.
T6-0052.t: Also figurative: a powerful backer or patron in politics or business.

T6-0053.x: The heirs agreed to divide the property equally.

T6-0054.x: Grandfather left a will before he passed away.
T6-0054.e: Literally 'a document of words left behind'.

T6-0055.m: legally reserved portion (an heir's forced share)
T6-0055.ex: 그는 아버지의 유언에도 불구하고 유류분 반환을 청구했습니다.
T6-0055.x: Despite his father's will, he sued to claim his legally reserved share.
T6-0055.e: Literally 'portion kept back' — heirs get it even if the will says otherwise.

T6-0056.m: acquisition by transfer, taking over (rights or property)
T6-0056.ex: 그 회사는 경쟁사의 사업 부문을 양수했습니다.
T6-0056.x: The company acquired a business division from its competitor.
T6-0056.e: Literally 'receive what's handed over'; homonyms mean 'positive number' and 'amniotic fluid'.
T6-0056.t: Pairs with 양도: the 양도인 hands over, the 양수인 receives, as in a 양도양수 계약.

T6-0057.ex: 그는 그 땅을 20년 동안 점유해 왔습니다.
T6-0057.x: He has occupied that land for 20 years.
T6-0057.e: Literally 'occupy and have' — physical control, not necessarily ownership.
T6-0057.t: 점유 is actual possession, 소유 is legal ownership, and 시장 점유율 means 'market share'.

T6-0058.m: surface right, superficies (right to use another's land for buildings or trees)
T6-0058.ex: 건물 주인은 남의 땅에 대한 지상권을 가지고 있습니다.
T6-0058.x: The building owner holds a surface right on someone else's land.
T6-0058.e: Literally 'right above the land' — to build on land you don't own.

T6-0059.x: I signed a two-year lease with the landlord.
T6-0059.e: Literally 'rent, lend and borrow' — both sides of a lease in one word.
T6-0059.t: 임대 is renting out (landlord), 임차 is renting from (tenant), and 임대차 covers the whole deal.

T6-0060.m: jeonse right (registered right of a lump-sum deposit tenant)
T6-0060.ex: 세입자는 보증금을 지키기 위해 전세권을 등기했습니다.
T6-0060.x: The tenant registered a jeonse right to protect the deposit.
T6-0060.e: 전세 is Korea's lump-sum deposit lease: no monthly rent, deposit returned at the end.

T6-0061.m: terms and conditions, terms of service
T6-0061.ex: 가입하기 전에 이용 약관을 꼼꼼히 읽어 보세요.
T6-0061.x: Read the terms of service carefully before signing up.
T6-0061.e: Literally 'agreement clauses'; a literary homonym 약관 means 'age twenty'.
T6-0061.t: On websites you'll often see a checkbox saying 약관에 동의합니다 'I agree to the terms'.

T6-0062.ex: 정부는 새 법의 시행령을 다음 달에 발표할 예정입니다.
T6-0062.x: The government plans to announce the enforcement decree for the new law next month.
T6-0062.e: Literally 'implementation order' — a presidential decree that fills in a law's details.
T6-0062.t: Pronounced [시행녕] — ㄹ becomes ㄴ after ㅇ.

T6-0063.ex: 신청 서류에 대한 자세한 내용은 시행규칙에 나와 있습니다.
T6-0063.x: Details about the application documents are given in the enforcement rules.
T6-0063.e: Ministry-level rules ranked below the decree: law, then 시행령, then 시행규칙.

T6-0064.m: text of a legal provision, statute article
T6-0064.ex: 변호사는 관련 법조문을 찾아 꼼꼼히 확인했습니다.
T6-0064.x: The lawyer looked up the relevant provisions and checked them carefully.

T6-0065.ex: 사법 개혁에 대한 국민의 요구가 커지고 있습니다.
T6-0065.x: Public demand for judicial reform is growing.
T6-0065.e: Literally 'administering the law'; a homonym 사법 means 'private law'.
T6-0065.t: It pairs with 입법 and 행정 as the three branches; 사법부 means 'the judicial branch'.

T6-0066.ex: 삼권분립은 권력의 남용을 막기 위한 민주주의의 기본 원칙입니다.
T6-0066.x: The separation of powers is a basic democratic principle meant to prevent abuse of power.
T6-0066.e: Literally 'three powers standing divided' — legislative, executive and judicial.
T6-0066.t: Pronounced [삼꿘불립] — ㄴ before ㄹ becomes ㄹ.

T6-0067.x: When the rule of law collapses, social order is shaken too.
rel: principle of the rule of law

T6-0068.m: principle of legality (no crime or punishment without law)
T6-0068.ex: 죄형법정주의에 따라 법에 없는 행위는 처벌할 수 없습니다.
T6-0068.x: Under the principle of legality, acts not defined by law cannot be punished.
T6-0068.e: Literally 'crime-and-punishment-fixed-by-law-ism': no crime without a prior law.

T6-0069.ex: 모든 피고인은 유죄 판결이 확정되기 전까지 무죄추정의 원칙을 적용받습니다.
T6-0069.x: Every defendant is presumed innocent until a guilty verdict becomes final.

T6-0070.m: double jeopardy rule (no retrial for the same case)
T6-0070.ex: 일사부재리 원칙 때문에 같은 사건으로 다시 재판받지 않습니다.
T6-0070.x: Because of the double jeopardy rule, no one is tried twice for the same case.
T6-0070.e: Literally 'one matter is not handled again' — no retrial after a final verdict.

T6-0071.ex: 새 법은 과거의 사건에 소급하여 적용되지 않습니다.
T6-0071.x: The new law does not apply retroactively to past cases.
T6-0071.e: Literally 'go upstream and reach' — reaching back into the past.

T6-0072.ex: 개정된 법의 소급적용 여부를 두고 논란이 일고 있습니다.
T6-0072.x: There is controversy over whether the amended law should apply retroactively.
T6-0072.t: Pronounced [소급쩌굥] — tensing after ㅂ, then linking.

T6-0073.ex: 중요한 계약서는 공증을 받아 두는 게 좋아요.
T6-0073.x: It's a good idea to get important contracts notarized.
T6-0073.t: 공증을 받다 means 'to get something notarized'; a notary office is a 공증 사무소.

T6-0074.ex: 계약서 마지막 장에 서명하고 날인해 주세요.
T6-0074.x: Please sign and stamp your seal on the last page of the contract.
T6-0074.e: Literally 'pressing a seal' — Koreans often stamp a personal 도장 instead of signing.

T6-0075.ex: 본인 확인 후 아래 칸에 서명날인해 주시기 바랍니다.
T6-0075.x: After verifying your identity, please sign and stamp in the box below.
T6-0075.e: 서명 'signature' plus 날인 'seal' — formal documents often want both.

T6-0076.m: letter of authorization, power of attorney
T6-0076.ex: 대신 서류를 떼려면 본인의 위임장이 필요합니다.
T6-0076.x: To get documents on someone's behalf, you need their letter of authorization.
T6-0076.t: Bring a 위임장 when picking up official documents for a family member at a community center.

T6-0077.m: power of agency, authority to act for someone
T6-0077.ex: 그는 아버지로부터 부동산 매매에 대한 대리권을 받았습니다.
T6-0077.x: He received authority from his father to act for him in the real estate sale.
T6-0077.e: Literally 'right to act in someone's place'.

T6-0078.x: Contracts and wills are typical examples of juristic acts.
T6-0078.e: 법률 'law' plus 행위 'act': an act meant to create legal effects.
T6-0078.t: Pronounced [범뉼행위] — nasalization plus ㄹ becoming ㄴ.

T6-0079.m: illegal act, unlawful conduct; tort (civil law)
T6-0079.ex: 회사의 불법행위가 드러나자 많은 사람들이 분노했습니다.
T6-0079.x: When the company's illegal acts came to light, many people were outraged.
T6-0079.e: Literally 'a not-lawful act'; in civil law it is the term for a tort.
T6-0079.t: Pronounced [불뻐팽위]: ㅂ after ㄹ in 불법 is tensed, and ㅂ+ㅎ merges into ㅍ.

T6-0080.m: evasion of the law, circumventing the law
T6-0080.ex: 탈법은 불법은 아니지만 법의 취지를 무시하는 행위입니다.
T6-0080.x: Evading the law isn't technically illegal, but it ignores the purpose of the law.
T6-0080.e: Literally 'slipping out of the law': dodging it through loopholes.

T6-0081.ex: 그는 편법을 써서 세금을 줄이려고 했어요.
T6-0081.x: He tried to reduce his taxes by using a shady workaround.
T6-0081.e: Literally 'convenient method': an easy way around proper procedure.
T6-0081.t: Usually negative: 편법을 쓰다 'to use a shortcut' implies bending the rules.

T6-0082.ex: 정부의 초법적 조치에 대해 비판이 쏟아졌습니다.
T6-0082.x: Criticism poured in over the government's extralegal measures.
T6-0082.t: -적 words work as determiners (초법적 권력) or nouns with 이다 (초법적인 결정).

T6-0083.ex: 이번 합의 내용은 계약서에 명문화될 예정입니다.
T6-0083.x: The terms of this agreement will be written into the contract.
T6-0083.e: Literally 'turning into clear writing': putting a rule explicitly on paper.

T6-0084.m: becoming a dead letter, falling into disuse (of a law)
T6-0084.x: That law effectively became a dead letter long ago.
T6-0084.e: Literally 'becoming dead writing': a law that exists on paper but is never enforced.
T6-0084.t: Mostly used as 사문화되다; it is the exact counterpart of the English idiom 'dead letter'.

T6-0085.ex: 어제 국회에서 노동법 개정안이 드디어 통과되었습니다.
T6-0085.x: The labor law amendment bill finally passed the National Assembly yesterday.
T6-0085.t: Common verbs: 개정안을 발의하다 'propose', 개정안이 통과되다 'be passed', 개정안을 부결하다 'vote down'.

T6-0086.ex: 두 나라는 새 무역 협정을 비준했습니다.
T6-0086.x: The two countries ratified the new trade agreement.
T6-0086.e: Literally 'approve and permit': final official sign-off on a treaty.

T6-0087.x: The United States has run a jury system for a long time.
T6-0087.e: Literally 'system of those who sit in on the hearing'.
T6-0087.t: Korea has no full jury system; its version is 국민참여재판, where the jury's verdict is only advisory.

T6-0088.x: The defendant can request a citizen participation trial.
T6-0088.e: Literally 'trial with the people taking part'; introduced in Korea in 2008.

T6-0089.ex: 헌법재판소 재판관 아홉 명이 만장일치로 결정했습니다.
T6-0089.x: All nine Constitutional Court justices decided unanimously.
T6-0089.t: In everyday speech a judge is 판사; 재판관 is the formal title for Constitutional Court justices.

T6-0090.ex: 법관은 법과 양심에 따라 독립하여 재판합니다.
T6-0090.x: Judges rule independently according to the law and their conscience.

T6-0091.x: People usually leave real estate registration to a judicial scrivener.
T6-0091.t: Pronounced [범무사] by nasalization; a 법무사 prepares legal filings but is not a trial lawyer (변호사).

T6-0092.x: He filed a civil lawsuit against his neighbor.
T6-0092.t: Collocation: 소송을 제기하다 / 걸다 'to file a suit'; 소송에서 이기다 'to win a suit'.

T6-0093.x: In criminal proceedings, the prosecutor must prove the crime.

T6-0094.ex: 주민들은 시청의 결정에 불복해 행정소송을 냈어요.
T6-0094.x: The residents rejected city hall's decision and filed an administrative suit.
T6-0094.e: Literally 'lawsuit over administration': challenging a public authority's decision.

T6-0095.ex: 피해자 수천 명이 회사를 상대로 집단소송을 준비하고 있어요.
T6-0095.x: Thousands of victims are preparing a class action against the company.

T6-0096.m: written answer, statement of defense (court filing)
T6-0096.ex: 피고는 한 달 안에 법원에 답변서를 제출해야 합니다.
T6-0096.x: The defendant must submit a written answer to the court within a month.
T6-0096.t: -서 marks an official document: 신청서 application, 계약서 contract, 답변서 answer.

T6-0097.m: ex-convict, person with a criminal record
T6-0097.ex: 전과자라는 이유로 취업이 어려운 경우가 많아요.
T6-0097.x: It's often hard to get a job just because you have a criminal record.
T6-0097.e: Literally 'person with a previous penalty'; 전과 alone means 'criminal record'.
T6-0097.t: Counting records: 전과 3범 means 'a three-time convict'.

T6-0098.m: repeat offense (within the legal period), repeat offender
T6-0098.ex: 누범은 일반적으로 더 무거운 처벌을 받습니다.
T6-0098.x: Repeat offenders generally receive heavier punishment.
T6-0098.t: 재범 is the everyday word for reoffending; 누범 is the legal term for reoffending within three years of a prison sentence.

T6-0099.x: Because it was his first offense, he got a suspended sentence from the court.

T6-0100.x: The suspect was held in a detention center while awaiting trial.
T6-0100.e: Literally 'place where people are held in custody'.
T6-0100.t: 구치소 holds people before or during trial; after sentencing they go to 교도소 (prison).

T6-0101.x: He was released after serving five years in prison.
T6-0101.t: Pronounced [보격]: the batchim ㄱ links to the next vowel.

T6-0102.ex: 교도소의 목적은 처벌뿐 아니라 교화에도 있습니다.
T6-0102.x: The purpose of prison lies not only in punishment but also in reform.

T6-0103.ex: 출소자의 갱생을 돕는 프로그램이 늘고 있어요.
T6-0103.x: Programs that help released prisoners rehabilitate are increasing.
T6-0103.e: Literally 'living again'; here the character usually read 경 is read 갱.

T6-0104.x: The court placed him on probation for two years.

T6-0105.ex: 법정에서 소란을 피운 남성이 감치 처분을 받았습니다.
T6-0105.x: A man who caused a disturbance in the courtroom was ordered into detention for contempt.
T6-0105.e: Literally 'place under supervision'; a judge can order it for up to 20 days.
T6-0105.t: Also used for people who refuse to pay child support or ignore court orders: 감치 명령.

T6-0106.ex: 그는 재산을 해외에 은닉한 혐의로 조사를 받고 있어요.
T6-0106.x: He is under investigation for hiding assets overseas.
T6-0106.e: Literally 'hide and conceal'; formal and legal in tone.
T6-0106.t: Everyday speech uses 숨기다; 은닉 appears in news and legal language, e.g. 재산 은닉 'hiding assets'.

T6-0107.m: breach of trust, breach of fiduciary duty
T6-0107.ex: 회사 대표가 업무상 배임 혐의로 기소되었습니다.
T6-0107.x: The company's CEO was indicted on charges of occupational breach of trust.
T6-0107.e: Literally 'turning your back on your duty'.
T6-0107.t: Often paired in news as 횡령·배임: embezzlement takes money directly, while 배임 harms the company by abusing your position.

T6-0108.x: The former mayor was arrested on charges of taking bribes.

T6-0109.ex: 건설사 사장은 증뢰 혐의로 재판을 받았어요.
T6-0109.x: The construction company president was tried for offering bribes.
T6-0109.e: Literally 'giving a bribe'; the counterpart of the receiving side.
T6-0109.t: Pronounced [증뇌]: ㄹ after ㅇ becomes ㄴ.

T6-0110.m: mediation, arranging, brokering; (law) acting as a go-between
T6-0110.ex: 이 센터는 외국인 노동자에게 일자리를 알선해 줍니다.
T6-0110.x: This center arranges jobs for foreign workers.
T6-0110.e: Literally 'turning around': going between two parties to arrange a deal.

T6-0111.ex: 그는 투자자들을 속인 사기죄로 징역형을 선고받았습니다.
T6-0111.x: He was sentenced to prison for fraud after deceiving investors.
T6-0111.e: -죄 = the crime of: 사기죄, 모욕죄, 절도죄.
T6-0111.t: Pronounced [사기쬐]: 죄 is tensed after the noun, as in most -죄 crimes.

T6-0112.m: criminal insult (public insult as an offense)
T6-0112.ex: 온라인에서 욕설을 한 사람이 모욕죄로 고소당했어요.
T6-0112.x: A person who posted insults online had a criminal complaint filed against them for insult.
T6-0112.t: 모욕죄 covers insults without facts; stating damaging facts or lies is 명예훼손 (defamation).

T6-0113.ex: 거짓으로 신고한 사람은 무고죄로 처벌받을 수 있습니다.
T6-0113.x: A person who files a false report can be punished for false accusation.
T6-0113.e: Literally 'slanderous report'. Homonym warning: 무고 can also mean 'innocent' (with different characters).
T6-0113.t: Don't mix up 무고 'false accusation' with 무고한 'innocent' (무고한 시민 'innocent citizens').

T6-0114.ex: 경찰은 이번 화재가 방화일 가능성을 조사하고 있습니다.
T6-0114.x: Police are investigating the possibility that this fire was arson.
T6-0114.e: Literally 'letting fire loose'. Homonym warning: another 방화 means 'fire prevention' (방화문 fire door).

T6-0115.ex: 범인은 피해자를 며칠 동안 창고에 감금했습니다.
T6-0115.x: The criminal held the victim captive in a warehouse for several days.

T6-0116.m: extortion, blackmail, intimidation; (slang) a lie, bluff
T6-0116.ex: 그는 사업가를 협박해 돈을 뜯어낸 공갈 혐의를 받고 있어요.
T6-0116.x: He is accused of extortion for threatening a businessman to squeeze money out of him.
T6-0116.t: In casual speech 공갈 치지 마 means 'Stop lying / bluffing'.

T6-0117.x: A gang extorted money from the merchants.

T6-0118.x: Customs caught a ring trying to smuggle gold bars.
T6-0118.e: Literally 'secret transport'; short for 밀수출입, secret export and import.

T6-0119.m: alteration, tampering (of a genuine document); (tech) modulation
T6-0119.ex: 그는 신분증의 생년월일을 변조한 혐의를 받았어요.
T6-0119.x: He was accused of altering the date of birth on his ID card.
T6-0119.t: 위조 is faking a document from scratch; 변조 is tampering with a real one.

T6-0120.m: unauthorized use, theft (of identity, ideas, designs)
T6-0120.ex: 개인 정보 도용 피해가 늘고 있어요.
T6-0120.x: Cases of personal information theft are increasing.

T6-0121.m: right of publicity, right to one's own image
T6-0121.ex: 허락 없이 사진을 올리면 초상권 침해가 될 수 있어요.
T6-0121.x: Posting someone's photo without permission can violate their image rights.
T6-0121.t: Pronounced [초상꿘]; collocation: 초상권을 침해하다 'to violate image rights'.

T6-0122.ex: 정부는 경기부양을 위해 대규모 예산을 투입했습니다.
T6-0122.x: The government poured in a large budget to stimulate the economy.
T6-0122.e: Literally 'lifting the economy's mood afloat'; 경기 means business conditions.
T6-0122.t: 경기 'economy' and 경기 'game, match' are homonyms with different characters; context tells them apart.

T6-0123.ex: 경기침체가 길어지면서 실업률이 계속 오르고 있어요.
T6-0123.x: As the recession drags on, the unemployment rate keeps rising.

T6-0124.ex: 1929년의 대공황은 전 세계 경제에 큰 충격을 주었습니다.
T6-0124.x: The Great Depression of 1929 dealt a huge blow to the world economy.
T6-0124.e: Literally 'fear and panic', for markets and for people alike.
T6-0124.t: Same word in psychology: 공황장애 'panic disorder', 공황 상태 'a state of panic'.

T6-0125.ex: 전문가들은 스태그플레이션이 올 수도 있다고 경고했습니다.
T6-0125.x: Experts warned that stagflation could be coming.

T6-0126.ex: 초인플레이션 때문에 빵 하나 값이 하루 만에 두 배가 됐어요.
T6-0126.x: Because of hyperinflation, the price of a loaf of bread doubled in a single day.
T6-0126.e: 초- 'super' + English 'inflation'; 초- is productive: 초고속, 초대형.

T6-0127.x: The government implemented austerity to reduce its budget deficit.

T6-0128.ex: 중앙은행은 양적완화를 통해 시장에 돈을 풀었습니다.
T6-0128.x: The central bank released money into the market through quantitative easing.
T6-0128.t: Often shortened in news to QE; the opposite policy is 양적긴축 'quantitative tightening'.

T6-0129.ex: 통화량이 늘어나면 물가가 오를 수 있습니다.
T6-0129.x: When the money supply increases, prices can rise.
T6-0129.t: 통화 also means 'phone call' (通話); 통화량 can mean 'call volume' in telecom contexts.

T6-0130.ex: 한국은행은 물가 안정을 위해 통화정책을 결정합니다.
T6-0130.x: The Bank of Korea sets monetary policy to keep prices stable.
T6-0130.t: 통화정책 is run by the central bank; 재정정책 (taxing and spending) is run by the government.

T6-0131.ex: 정부는 확장적 재정정책으로 일자리를 늘리려고 합니다.
T6-0131.x: The government plans to create jobs through expansionary fiscal policy.
T6-0131.e: Literally 'public-finance policy': decisions about taxes and government spending.

T6-0132.ex: 올해 재정적자는 사상 최대 규모를 기록했습니다.
T6-0132.x: This year's budget deficit hit a record high.
T6-0132.e: 적자 is literally 'red figures', from losses written in red ink.
T6-0132.t: 적자 = deficit and 흑자 'black letters' = surplus, just like 'in the red / in the black'.

T6-0133.ex: 고령화로 국가부채가 빠르게 늘어날 것으로 보입니다.
T6-0133.x: National debt is expected to grow quickly due to population aging.
T6-0133.t: Everyday speech often says 나랏빚 'the country's debt'; 국가부채 is the news and policy term.

T6-0134.ex: 그 회사는 부채비율이 너무 높아서 대출을 받기 어려워요.
T6-0134.x: That company's debt ratio is so high it's hard for it to get a loan.
T6-0134.t: The suffix for 'rate' is written 율 after a vowel or ㄴ (비율, 환율) and 률 elsewhere (성장률).

T6-0135.ex: 달러 가치가 오르면서 수출 기업들이 큰 환차익을 얻었어요.
T6-0135.x: As the dollar rose, exporters made big currency gains.

T6-0136.ex: 원화 가치가 떨어져서 수입 업체들이 환차손을 입었습니다.
T6-0136.x: Importers suffered currency losses as the won weakened.

T6-0137.ex: 그 나라는 수출을 늘리려고 통화를 평가절하했습니다.
T6-0137.x: That country devalued its currency to boost exports.
T6-0137.e: Literally 'cutting the par value down'; here 평가 means par value, not evaluation.
T6-0137.t: Also used figuratively: 그의 업적이 평가절하되었다 'his achievements were underrated'.

T6-0138.ex: 위안화가 평가절상되면 중국 제품 가격이 오를 수 있어요.
T6-0138.x: If the yuan is revalued, prices of Chinese goods may go up.

T6-0139.x: Korea's foreign exchange reserves exceed 400 billion dollars.
T6-0139.t: Koreans call the 1997 crisis 외환위기 or simply IMF, as in IMF 때 'during the IMF crisis'.

T6-0140.ex: 국제수지는 한 나라와 외국 사이의 모든 거래를 보여 줍니다.
T6-0140.x: The balance of payments shows all transactions between a country and the rest of the world.
T6-0140.e: 수지 is literally 'income and outgo': money in versus money out.
T6-0140.t: 수지가 맞다 means 'to pay off, be profitable', a common everyday phrase.

T6-0141.x: Last month's current account posted a surplus of 5 billion dollars.

T6-0142.ex: 반도체 수출 덕분에 무역수지가 흑자로 돌아섰어요.
T6-0142.x: Thanks to chip exports, the trade balance turned to a surplus.

T6-0143.ex: 보호무역이 강화되면서 수출 기업들의 걱정이 커지고 있어요.
T6-0143.x: As protectionism intensifies, exporters are growing more worried.
T6-0143.e: Literally 'protective trade': shielding domestic industry with tariffs and quotas.

T6-0144.ex: 정부는 외국산 철강에 반덤핑 관세를 부과했습니다.
T6-0144.x: The government imposed anti-dumping duties on foreign steel.
T6-0144.e: From English 'dumping'; also used casually for selling goods off cheap.
T6-0144.t: In daily life 덤핑 often just means a clearance sale at rock-bottom prices, e.g. 덤핑 판매.

T6-0145.x: The U.S. imposed import restrictions on Korean-made washing machines.
T6-0145.t: Pronounced [수입뀨제]; don't confuse 수입 'import' (輸入) with 수입 'income' (收入).

T6-0146.x: This year's GDP grew 2% over last year.
T6-0146.e: A word-for-word translation of 'gross domestic product'.
T6-0146.t: Pronounced [궁내총생산] by nasalization; in speech Koreans usually just say GDP (지디피).

T6-0147.x: Per capita gross national income topped 30,000 dollars for the first time.
T6-0147.e: Literally 'total income of the nation's people'.

T6-0148.ex: 인구 감소로 한국의 잠재성장률이 계속 낮아지고 있어요.
T6-0148.x: Korea's potential growth rate keeps falling because of population decline.
T6-0148.e: Literally 'hidden growth rate': how fast an economy could grow without causing inflation.
T6-0148.t: Pronounced [잠재성장뉼]: ㄹ after ㅇ becomes ㄴ.

T6-0149.ex: 물가가 크게 올라서 실질소득은 오히려 줄었어요.
T6-0149.x: Prices rose so much that real income actually shrank.

T6-0150.ex: 명목임금은 올랐지만 물가가 더 많이 올랐습니다.
T6-0150.x: Nominal wages went up, but prices went up even more.
T6-0150.e: Literally 'wages in name only', before adjusting for inflation.
T6-0150.t: 명목 also means 'pretext': ~라는 명목으로 'under the pretext of ~'.

T6-0151.ex: 고물가 때문에 근로자들의 실질임금이 3년째 줄고 있어요.
T6-0151.x: Because of high inflation, workers' real wages have been falling for three years.
T6-0151.e: Literally 'wages in real substance': what your pay can actually buy.

T6-0152.ex: 세금과 이자가 늘면서 가계의 가처분소득이 줄었습니다.
T6-0152.x: As taxes and interest rose, household disposable income fell.
T6-0152.e: Literally 'income that can be disposed of': what remains after taxes.
T6-0152.t: Not to be confused with legal 가처분 'injunction'; 가처분소득 is always about income.

T6-0153.ex: 소득분배가 불평등할수록 사회 갈등이 커질 수 있어요.
T6-0153.x: The more unequal income distribution is, the more social conflict can grow.

T6-0154.x: The closer the Gini coefficient is to 1, the worse income inequality is.
T6-0154.e: Named after Italian statistician Corrado Gini; 계수 means 'coefficient'.

T6-0155.ex: 누진세는 소득이 많을수록 더 높은 세율을 적용합니다.
T6-0155.x: A progressive tax applies a higher rate the more you earn.
T6-0155.e: Literally 'tax that climbs step by step'.
T6-0155.t: Koreans meet 누진제 in electricity bills: the more power you use, the higher the rate per unit.

T6-0156.ex: 부가가치세는 저소득층에게 부담이 큰 역진세라는 비판을 받습니다.
T6-0156.x: VAT is criticized as a regressive tax that weighs heavily on low-income people.
T6-0156.e: Literally 'reverse-progression tax': the burden falls harder on lower incomes.

T6-0157.ex: 정부는 내년부터 중소기업에 대한 감세를 추진할 계획입니다.
T6-0157.x: The government plans to push for tax cuts for small and midsize businesses starting next year.
T6-0157.t: 감세 정책 'tax-cut policy' is a common news collocation; the opposite is 증세 'tax hike.'

T6-0158.ex: 경기가 나빠지면서 올해 세수가 크게 줄었습니다.
T6-0158.x: As the economy worsened, tax revenue dropped sharply this year.
T6-0158.e: Literally 'tax collected'; don't confuse it with 세수 'washing your face.'
T6-0158.t: Common news phrases: 세수 부족 'revenue shortfall' and 세수 확보 'securing tax revenue.'

T6-0159.x: The government raised the income tax rate by 2 percent.
T6-0159.t: The 'rate' syllable is 율 after a vowel or ㄴ (세율, 비율) and 률 elsewhere (확률, 성공률).

T6-0160.m: tax saving (legal ways to pay less tax)
T6-0160.ex: 연말정산 때 절세 방법을 미리 알아 두세요.
T6-0160.x: Learn some tax-saving tips ahead of your year-end tax settlement.
T6-0160.e: Literally 'economizing on tax' — legal, unlike 탈세 'tax evasion.'
T6-0160.t: Pronounced [절쎄]: ㅅ becomes tense after ㄹ in Sino-Korean words.

T6-0161.ex: 회사는 월급을 줄 때 소득세를 원천징수합니다.
T6-0161.x: Companies withhold income tax when they pay salaries.
T6-0161.e: Literally 'collecting at the source (the spring)' — tax taken before you get paid.
T6-0161.t: Use 원천징수하다 for the employer withholding and 원천징수되다 for tax being withheld.

T6-0162.ex: 정부는 기업 투자를 늘리기 위해 법인세를 낮췄습니다.
T6-0162.x: The government lowered the corporate tax to boost business investment.
T6-0162.e: 법인 'legal person' means a corporation; add 세 'tax.'

T6-0163.x: I paid capital gains tax after selling my house.
T6-0163.e: 양도 'transfer' + 소득 'income' + 세 'tax': tax on profit from selling property.
T6-0163.t: Usually shortened to 양도세 in everyday talk and in the news.

T6-0164.ex: 부모에게 큰돈을 받으면 증여세를 내야 합니다.
T6-0164.x: If you receive a large sum of money from your parents, you have to pay gift tax.
T6-0164.e: 증여 'giving property as a gift' + 세 'tax.'
T6-0164.t: For an everyday present, say 선물.

T6-0165.x: We pay property tax every July and September.

T6-0166.ex: 비싼 집을 여러 채 가진 사람은 종합부동산세를 냅니다.
T6-0166.x: People who own several expensive homes pay the comprehensive real estate tax.
T6-0166.e: Literally 'comprehensive real-estate tax'; 부동산 is literally 'property that does not move.'
T6-0166.t: Almost always shortened to 종부세 in the news.

T6-0167.x: Seoul's officially assessed land prices rose sharply this year.
T6-0167.t: Property taxes are based on 공시지가, which is usually lower than the market price, 시가.

T6-0168.x: This apartment's market price is over one billion won.
T6-0168.e: Literally 'market price'; homonyms include 'cigar' and 'a husband's family home.'

T6-0169.ex: 집주인들이 아파트 호가를 계속 올리고 있어요.
T6-0169.x: Owners keep raising the asking prices for their apartments.
T6-0169.e: Literally 'calling out a price' — what the seller asks, not what's finally paid.
T6-0169.t: As 호가하다 it means 'to be priced at': 10억 원을 호가하는 아파트 'an apartment going for a billion won.'

T6-0170.m: capital gain, profit from a price difference
T6-0170.ex: 그는 주식을 팔아서 큰 시세차익을 얻었어요.
T6-0170.x: He made a big profit by selling his stocks.
T6-0170.e: 시세 'current market price' + 차익 'profit from a difference.'

T6-0171.ex: 정부는 부동산 투기꾼을 막기 위해 규제를 강화했습니다.
T6-0171.x: The government tightened regulations to stop real estate speculators.
T6-0171.e: 투기 'speculation' + native -꾼 'someone who habitually does it,' as in 사기꾼 'con artist.'
T6-0171.t: -꾼 sounds negative or slangy; the neutral word for an investor is 투자자.

T6-0172.x: Legally, cars and jewelry count as movable property.
T6-0172.e: Literally 'movable property' — the opposite of 부동산 'real estate.'
T6-0172.t: Don't confuse it with 동산 'small hill, garden,' as in 에덴동산 'the Garden of Eden.'

T6-0173.x: The bank keeps its customers' securities safe.
T6-0173.e: Literally 'certificates that have value' — stocks, bonds, checks and the like.

T6-0174.x: The bond market became unstable as interest rates rose.
T6-0174.t: 채권 'bond' sounds the same as 채권 'a creditor's claim'; context tells them apart.

T6-0175.x: The stock index fell more than 2 percent today.

T6-0176.x: The company's market cap topped 100 trillion won.
T6-0176.t: Often shortened to 시총 in news and investor talk.

T6-0177.x: The company was delisted because of accounting fraud.
T6-0177.t: Usually used with 되다: 상장폐지되다 'to be delisted.'

T6-0178.ex: 요즘 공모주 청약에 젊은 투자자들이 많이 몰립니다.
T6-0178.x: These days, lots of young investors are flocking to apply for IPO shares.
T6-0178.e: Literally 'publicly recruited stock' — shares offered to the public in an IPO.
T6-0178.t: Key collocation: 공모주 청약 'applying to buy IPO shares.'

T6-0179.ex: 이 회사는 매년 주주들에게 배당금을 줍니다.
T6-0179.x: This company pays dividends to its shareholders every year.

T6-0180.ex: 그 회사의 대주주가 주식을 대량으로 팔았습니다.
T6-0180.x: The company's major shareholder sold off a large amount of stock.

T6-0181.x: Minority shareholders strongly opposed the company's decision.
T6-0181.t: Small retail investors are jokingly called 개미 'ants' in Korean.

T6-0182.m: shareholders' meeting, general meeting of shareholders
T6-0182.ex: 다음 달에 정기 주주총회가 열릴 예정입니다.
T6-0182.x: The annual shareholders' meeting will be held next month.
T6-0182.t: Often shortened to 주총 in the news.

T6-0183.ex: 어제 열린 이사회에서 새로운 사장을 뽑았습니다.
T6-0183.x: At yesterday's meeting, the board of directors chose a new president.
T6-0183.e: 이사 'director' + 회 'group, meeting'; unrelated to 이사 'moving house.'

T6-0184.ex: 두 형제가 회사의 경영권을 두고 다투고 있어요.
T6-0184.x: Two brothers are fighting over control of the company.
T6-0184.e: 경영 'management' + -권 'right, power,' a productive suffix: 인권, 투표권.
T6-0184.t: Pronounced [경영꿘]; 경영권 분쟁 'a fight for control' is a common headline phrase.

T6-0185.ex: 두 회사는 인수합병을 통해 하나의 회사가 되었습니다.
T6-0185.x: The two firms became one company through a merger.
T6-0185.e: 인수 'takeover' + 합병 'merger' — the Korean term for M&A.
T6-0185.t: Korean news also just says M&A, read 엠앤에이.

T6-0186.ex: 그 그룹은 몇 년 전에 지주회사 체제로 바뀌었습니다.
T6-0186.x: The group switched to a holding company structure a few years ago.

T6-0187.ex: 모회사가 자회사의 빚을 대신 갚아 주었습니다.
T6-0187.x: The parent company paid off its subsidiary's debt.
T6-0187.e: Literally 'mother company'; a subsidiary is a 'child company,' 자회사.

T6-0188.ex: 정부는 시장의 독과점을 막기 위해 노력하고 있습니다.
T6-0188.x: The government is working to prevent monopolies and oligopolies in the market.
T6-0188.e: A blend of 독점 'monopoly' and 과점 'oligopoly.'

T6-0189.ex: 국내 통신 시장은 세 회사의 과점 상태입니다.
T6-0189.x: The domestic telecom market is an oligopoly of three companies.
T6-0189.e: Literally 'a few occupying' — a market held by a handful of firms.

T6-0190.ex: 여러 회사가 카르텔을 만들어 가격을 올렸습니다.
T6-0190.x: Several companies formed a cartel and raised prices.
T6-0190.e: From German 'Kartell' (English 'cartel'); also used loosely for any closed, self-serving clique.
T6-0190.t: For price-fixing, news reports more often use 담합 'collusion.'

T6-0191.x: The Fair Trade Commission investigated illegal practices by large corporations.
T6-0191.e: 공정 'fair' + 거래 'trade, deal,' literally 'going and coming.'
T6-0191.t: 공정거래위원회, Korea's antitrust agency, is usually called 공정위.

T6-0192.ex: 금융 당국은 주식 불공정거래를 엄격하게 처벌합니다.
T6-0192.x: Financial authorities strictly punish unfair stock trading.

T6-0193.ex: 그 임원은 내부자거래 혐의로 조사를 받았습니다.
T6-0193.x: The executive was investigated on suspicion of insider trading.
T6-0193.e: Literally 'insider dealing'; -자 = person who does or is it: 내부자 'insider.'

T6-0194.ex: 검찰은 대규모 주가조작 사건을 수사하고 있습니다.
T6-0194.x: Prosecutors are investigating a large-scale stock manipulation case.
T6-0194.t: 조작 means 'rigging' (여론 조작) but also simply 'operating' a machine (기계 조작).

T6-0195.x: The company inflated its profits through accounting fraud.
T6-0195.e: Literally 'powdered-up accounting' — making the books look prettier than they are.
T6-0195.t: Unrelated to 분식 'snack food' like 떡볶이, a different word with the same sound.

T6-0196.x: An outside firm conducts an audit every year.
T6-0196.t: 감사 'audit' sounds like 감사 'thanks' (감사합니다) — totally different words.

T6-0197.ex: 감사보고서에 따르면 회사의 부채가 크게 늘었습니다.
T6-0197.x: According to the audit report, the company's debt rose sharply.

T6-0198.ex: 투자하기 전에 회사의 재무제표를 꼼꼼히 확인하세요.
T6-0198.x: Check a company's financial statements carefully before you invest.

T6-0199.ex: 대차대조표를 보면 회사의 자산과 부채를 알 수 있어요.
T6-0199.x: A balance sheet shows you a company's assets and liabilities.
T6-0199.t: The official accounting term is now 재무상태표, but 대차대조표 is still widely used.

T6-0200.m: income statement, profit and loss statement
T6-0200.ex: 손익계산서에서 매출과 비용을 확인할 수 있습니다.
T6-0200.x: You can check revenue and expenses on the income statement.

T6-0201.x: Sales went up, but cash flow isn't good.
T6-0201.e: 현금 'cash' + native 흐름 'flow,' from 흐르다 'to flow.'

T6-0202.x: Third-quarter operating profit rose 20 percent from last year.
T6-0202.t: 영업이익 is profit from the core business; 순이익 is what's left after everything, including taxes.

T6-0203.x: The company's net profit this year is 50 billion won.
T6-0203.e: Literally 'pure profit' — what remains after all costs and taxes.

T6-0204.ex: 자동차는 시간이 지나면 감가상각 때문에 가치가 떨어져요.
T6-0204.x: Cars lose value over time because of depreciation.
T6-0204.e: 감가 'value reduction' + 상각 'writing off' a cost over time.
T6-0204.t: In everyday talk, 감가 alone means resale value dropping: 이 차는 감가가 커요.

T6-0205.ex: 매달 내는 월세와 보험료는 대표적인 고정비입니다.
T6-0205.x: Monthly rent and insurance are typical fixed costs.
T6-0205.e: 고정 'fixed' + -비 'cost,' a common suffix: 교통비, 식비.

T6-0206.ex: 생산량이 늘면 재료비 같은 변동비도 늘어납니다.
T6-0206.x: When output rises, variable costs like materials rise too.

T6-0207.x: The new shop passed its break-even point in just a year.
T6-0207.e: Literally 'the point where loss and gain fork apart.'
T6-0207.t: Common verbs: 손익분기점을 넘다 'pass break-even' and 손익분기점에 도달하다 'reach break-even.'

T6-0208.x: Digital products have a marginal cost close to zero.
T6-0208.e: 한계 'limit, margin' + 비용 'cost' — the cost of producing one more unit.
T6-0208.t: In economics 한계 means 'marginal'; in daily speech it means 'limit': 한계가 있다 'there's a limit.'

T6-0209.x: Money you've already spent is a sunk cost, so forget about it.
T6-0209.e: Literally 'buried, sunk cost' — money you can never get back.

T6-0210.forms: 규모의 경제를 누리다 · 규모의 경제 효과
T6-0210.ex: 대기업은 규모의 경제 덕분에 생산 비용이 낮습니다.
T6-0210.x: Large companies have lower production costs thanks to economies of scale.
T6-0210.e: A direct translation: 규모 'scale' + 의 'of' + 경제 'economy.'
T6-0210.t: The particle 의 here is usually pronounced [에]: [규모에 경제].

T6-0211.ex: 가격이 오르면 수요곡선을 따라 수요량이 줄어듭니다.
T6-0211.x: When the price rises, the quantity demanded falls along the demand curve.

T6-0212.ex: 생산 비용이 내려가면 공급곡선이 오른쪽으로 이동합니다.
T6-0212.x: When production costs fall, the supply curve shifts to the right.

T6-0213.ex: 수요와 공급이 만나는 점에서 균형가격이 결정됩니다.
T6-0213.x: The equilibrium price is set where supply and demand meet.

T6-0214.ex: 쌀 같은 생필품은 가격탄력성이 낮은 편입니다.
T6-0214.x: Necessities like rice tend to have low price elasticity.
T6-0214.t: 탄력 is pronounced [탈력]: ㄴ becomes ㄹ before ㄹ.

T6-0215.ex: 같은 음식을 계속 먹으면 한계효용이 줄어듭니다.
T6-0215.x: If you keep eating the same food, its marginal utility decreases.
T6-0215.t: Key phrase: 한계효용 체감의 법칙 'the law of diminishing marginal utility.'

T6-0216.x: Diamonds are expensive because of their scarcity.
T6-0216.e: Literally 'the quality of being rare and few.'
T6-0216.t: 희 is pronounced [히] and 성 tenses: [히소썽].

T6-0217.x: All kinds of goods and services are traded in the market.
T6-0217.e: Literally 'wealth and goods'; paired with 용역 'services' in economics.

T6-0218.ex: 청소는 외부 용역 업체에 맡기고 있습니다.
T6-0218.x: We leave the cleaning to an outside contractor.
T6-0218.t: In daily news, 용역 usually means outsourced contract work, as in 용역 업체 'contractor' or 용역 직원 'contract worker.'

T6-0219.ex: 도로와 국방은 누구나 이용하는 대표적인 공공재입니다.
T6-0219.x: Roads and national defense are classic public goods that everyone uses.

T6-0220.ex: 민주 국가의 법은 개인의 사유재산을 보호합니다.
T6-0220.x: The laws of democratic countries protect individuals' private property.

T6-0221.ex: 환경오염은 시장실패를 보여 주는 대표적인 예입니다.
T6-0221.x: Pollution is a classic example of market failure.

T6-0222.ex: 잘못된 규제는 정부실패를 낳을 수 있습니다.
T6-0222.x: Bad regulations can lead to government failure.
T6-0222.e: 정부 'government' + 실패 'failure' — when intervention makes things worse.

T6-0223.x: Pollution from factories creates a negative externality.
T6-0223.e: Literally 'outside effect' — costs or benefits that land on someone else.

T6-0224.forms: 보이지 않는 손이 작용하다 · 시장의 보이지 않는 손
T6-0224.ex: 애덤 스미스는 시장을 움직이는 힘을 보이지 않는 손이라고 불렀습니다.
T6-0224.x: Adam Smith called the force that moves the market the invisible hand.
T6-0224.e: A translation of Adam Smith's phrase: 보이다 'to be seen' + -지 않는 'not' + 손 'hand.'

T6-0225.x: Nineteenth-century Britain followed laissez-faire economic policies.
T6-0225.e: Literally 'freedom and leaving things alone' — a translation of 'laissez-faire.'
T6-0225.t: Also used for parenting: 자유방임형 부모 'a hands-off parent.'

T6-0226.x: Starting in the 1980s, many countries adopted neoliberal policies.
T6-0226.e: 신- 'new' + 자유 'freedom' + -주의 '-ism,' a hugely productive suffix: 민주주의, 자본주의.

T6-0227.ex: 케인스주의는 불황기에 정부 지출을 늘려야 한다고 봅니다.
T6-0227.x: Keynesianism holds that government spending should increase during a recession.
T6-0227.e: From the economist John Maynard Keynes + -주의 '-ism.'

T6-0228.x: The former Soviet Union ran a planned economy.

T6-0229.ex: 오늘날 대부분의 나라는 혼합경제를 채택하고 있습니다.
T6-0229.x: Most countries today have adopted a mixed economy.
T6-0229.e: 혼합 'mixture' + 경제 'economy' — markets plus government planning.

T6-0230.ex: 청년들의 노동시장 진입이 점점 어려워지고 있습니다.
T6-0230.x: Entering the labor market is getting harder and harder for young people.

T6-0231.x: Many workers still suffer from unpaid wages.
T6-0231.t: In casual speech, people say 월급이 밀렸어요 'my pay is overdue.'

T6-0232.x: As the labor dispute dragged on, the factory stopped operating.

T6-0233.ex: 노조는 임금 인상을 위해 회사와 단체교섭을 시작했습니다.
T6-0233.x: The union began collective bargaining with the company for a wage increase.

T6-0234.ex: 노사는 오랜 협상 끝에 단체협약을 맺었습니다.
T6-0234.x: Labor and management signed a collective agreement after long negotiations.
T6-0234.e: 단체 'group' + 협약 'agreement' — the contract that comes out of collective bargaining.
T6-0234.t: Common verbs: 단체협약을 맺다 or 체결하다 'to sign a collective agreement.'

T6-0235.m: work slowdown, go-slow (as a labor protest)
T6-0235.x: The union started a work slowdown instead of a strike.
T6-0235.t: Unlike 파업 (strike), in a 태업 workers still show up but work slowly on purpose.

T6-0236.ex: 임금 문제로 노사 간 쟁의가 계속되고 있습니다.
T6-0236.x: The labor-management dispute over wages is still going on.
T6-0236.t: Usually appears in set phrases: 노동쟁의 (labor dispute) and 쟁의 행위 (industrial action).

T6-0237.m: capital contribution, investment (in a company as an owner)
T6-0237.ex: 두 회사가 절반씩 출자해서 새 회사를 세웠습니다.
T6-0237.x: The two companies each put in half the capital and set up a new company.
T6-0237.t: 출자 means putting money in as an owner; 투자 is the broader word for any investment.

T6-0238.m: contributed funds, donated endowment (to a foundation or fund)
T6-0238.x: The foundation was established with funds contributed by the government and companies.
T6-0238.e: Literally 'money put out as a donation'; unrelated to 출연 'appearing on TV'.
T6-0238.t: Pronounced [추련금]; the ㄹ carries over into the next syllable.

T6-0239.m: default (on a debt), failure to repay
T6-0239.x: That country eventually declared a default.
T6-0239.t: For a country's default, news often uses the loanword 디폴트; 채무불이행 is the formal term.

T6-0240.ex: 카드값을 못 갚아서 신용불량 상태가 됐어요.
T6-0240.x: I couldn't pay my credit card bills, so I ended up with bad credit.
T6-0240.t: Most often heard as 신용불량자, a person blacklisted for unpaid debts.

T6-0241.x: I took out a secured loan from the bank to buy a house.
T6-0241.e: Literally 'guaranteed lending' — a loan backed by property.
T6-0241.t: Say 대출을 받다 for taking out a loan; 대출을 갚다 means paying it back.

T6-0242.x: Banks made huge profits from the loan-deposit spread.
T6-0242.e: 예(금) 'deposit' + 대(출) 'loan' + English 'margin': the gap between their interest rates.

T6-0243.ex: 복리로 오래 저축하면 돈이 빠르게 불어나요.
T6-0243.x: If you save for a long time with compound interest, your money grows fast.
T6-0243.e: Literally 'repeated interest'; don't confuse with 복리 'welfare', as in 복리후생.

T6-0244.x: This savings plan calculates interest as simple interest.
T6-0244.e: Literally 'single interest' — paid only on the original principal.
T6-0244.t: Pronounced [달리] — the ㄴ turns into ㄹ before ㄹ.

T6-0245.x: When the economy improves, investors flock to risk assets.
T6-0245.e: Literally 'dangerous assets' — like stocks, whose value can swing widely.

T6-0246.ex: 불안할 때는 금 같은 안전자산의 가격이 올라요.
T6-0246.x: In uncertain times, the price of safe assets like gold goes up.
T6-0246.e: Literally 'safe assets' — gold, bonds or dollars that hold value in a crisis.

T6-0247.ex: 위험을 줄이려면 분산투자를 하는 것이 좋아요.
T6-0247.x: To reduce risk, it's good to diversify your investments.
T6-0247.t: Korean has the same proverb: 달걀을 한 바구니에 담지 마라 — don't put all your eggs in one basket.

T6-0248.x: He built a portfolio of stocks and bonds.
T6-0248.e: From English 'portfolio'; also used for a designer's or job applicant's work samples.

T6-0249.x: Crude oil futures prices rose sharply.
T6-0249.e: Literally 'goods in advance' — a homonym of the everyday word 선물 'gift'.
T6-0249.t: Context tells it apart from 'gift': 선물 거래, 선물 시장 and 원유 선물 all mean futures.

T6-0250.ex: 옵션 거래는 위험이 커서 주의해야 해요.
T6-0250.x: Options trading is very risky, so you have to be careful.
T6-0250.e: From English 'option'; in apartment ads, 풀옵션 means fully furnished with appliances.

T6-0251.ex: 파생상품 투자로 큰 손실을 본 사람이 많아요.
T6-0251.x: Many people suffered big losses investing in derivatives.
T6-0251.e: Literally 'products that branch off' — their value comes from another asset.

T6-0252.ex: 헤지펀드가 그 회사 주식을 대량으로 사들였습니다.
T6-0252.x: A hedge fund bought up a large amount of that company's stock.
T6-0252.e: From English 'hedge fund'; 'hedge' means protecting against risk.

T6-0253.x: A private equity fund acquired the company.
T6-0253.e: 사모 'privately recruited' + English 'fund': money raised from a few investors.
T6-0253.t: Its opposite is 공모펀드, a fund openly sold to the general public.

T6-0254.x: We got investment from venture capital and grew the company.
T6-0254.e: From English 'venture capital'; often shortened to VC.

T6-0255.m: change of government, transfer of power (to another party)
T6-0255.x: This election brought a change of government for the first time in ten years.
T6-0255.e: Literally 'exchanging political power' — power passes to the other party.
T6-0255.t: Pronounced [정꿘교체] — the ㄱ in 권 is tensed.

T6-0256.ex: 집권당이 이번 선거에서 과반 의석을 잃었습니다.
T6-0256.x: The ruling party lost its majority of seats in this election.
T6-0256.t: In everyday news 여당 is the more common word for the ruling party.

T6-0257.m: divided government (a ruling party in the minority, opposition in the majority)
T6-0257.ex: 여소야대 국회에서는 법안 통과가 쉽지 않아요.
T6-0257.x: With the opposition controlling the National Assembly, passing bills isn't easy.
T6-0257.t: 여 = 여당 and 야 = 야당; news uses this pair constantly, as in 여야 (both parties).

T6-0258.ex: 두 정당이 손을 잡고 연립정부를 구성했습니다.
T6-0258.x: Two parties joined hands and formed a coalition government.

T6-0259.ex: 일부 정치인들은 대통령제 대신 내각제를 주장합니다.
T6-0259.x: Some politicians argue for a parliamentary system instead of a presidential one.

T6-0260.x: Britain and Japan have adopted a parliamentary system.
T6-0260.e: Literally 'parliament-cabinet system' — the cabinet is formed from parliament.
T6-0260.t: 내각제 is the everyday short form of this full official term.

T6-0261.x: The president presided over a Cabinet meeting this morning.

T6-0262.x: The list of cabinet members for the new government was announced.

T6-0263.m: joining the cabinet, appointment as a minister
T6-0263.x: He joined the cabinet in this reshuffle.

T6-0264.x: The ministerial nominee's confirmation hearing was held at the National Assembly.
T6-0264.e: Literally 'personnel hearing' — lawmakers question a nominee before appointment.
T6-0264.t: 인사 here means personnel appointments, not its everyday sense of greeting.

T6-0265.m: parliamentary audit of the government (annual inspection)
T6-0265.x: Every fall, the National Assembly carries out its audit of the government.
T6-0265.t: News usually shortens it to 국감.

T6-0266.ex: 야당은 그 사건에 대한 국정조사를 요구했습니다.
T6-0266.x: The opposition demanded a parliamentary investigation into the incident.
T6-0266.t: 국정감사 is a regular yearly review; 국정조사 targets one specific scandal when needed.

T6-0267.ex: 대통령은 국정운영에 대한 국민의 신뢰를 회복해야 합니다.
T6-0267.x: The president must restore public trust in how the country is run.

T6-0268.ex: 의원들이 많이 빠져서 정족수를 채우지 못했어요.
T6-0268.x: So many lawmakers were absent that they couldn't reach a quorum.
T6-0268.t: Common phrases: 정족수를 채우다 (reach a quorum) and 정족수 미달 (lacking a quorum).

T6-0269.m: approval (of a bill or motion), passage
T6-0269.x: Whether the motion passes will be decided tomorrow.
T6-0269.t: Bills and motions are 가결되다 (passed) or 부결되다 (voted down).

T6-0270.m: rejection (of a bill or motion), voting down
T6-0270.ex: 반대표가 많아서 결국 그 개정안이 부결되었습니다.
T6-0270.x: With so many votes against it, the amendment was eventually voted down.

T6-0271.m: ramming a bill through; purse-snatching, snatch theft
T6-0271.ex: 여당이 예산안을 날치기로 통과시켰다는 비판을 받았어요.
T6-0271.x: The ruling party was criticized for ramming the budget bill through.
T6-0271.e: Probably from 날치다 'to dart about swiftly'; first meant snatching purses.
T6-0271.t: In politics it's usually 날치기 통과; in daily life it means grabbing someone's bag and running.

T6-0272.ex: 야당 의원들이 법안을 막으려고 필리버스터를 시작했습니다.
T6-0272.x: Opposition lawmakers started a filibuster to block the bill.
T6-0272.e: From English 'filibuster'; officially called 무제한 토론 in Korea's National Assembly.

T6-0273.ex: 대통령이 그 법안에 대해 거부권을 행사했습니다.
T6-0273.x: The president exercised his veto on the bill.
T6-0273.e: Literally 'right to refuse'. -권 = a right: 투표권, 참정권.
T6-0273.t: The fixed collocation is 거부권을 행사하다, to exercise a veto.

T6-0274.m: reconsideration (of a vetoed bill), second vote
T6-0274.ex: 거부권이 행사된 법안은 국회에서 재의에 부쳐집니다.
T6-0274.x: A vetoed bill is put to a second vote in the National Assembly.
T6-0274.t: 재의를 요구하다 is the formal way to say the president sends a bill back, in effect a veto.

T6-0275.ex: 정부는 경기 회복을 위해 추경을 편성했습니다.
T6-0275.x: The government drew up a supplementary budget to revive the economy.
T6-0275.t: Common collocation: 추경을 편성하다 (draw up a supplementary budget).

T6-0276.ex: 국회는 재난 대응을 위한 추가경정예산을 통과시켰습니다.
T6-0276.x: The National Assembly passed a supplementary budget for disaster response.
T6-0276.e: Literally 'additional revised budget' — extra spending added after the main budget.

T6-0277.m: settlement of accounts, closing of the books; final accounts
T6-0277.ex: 연말에는 한 해 동안의 예산을 결산해야 합니다.
T6-0277.x: At year-end, we have to settle the accounts for the year's budget.
T6-0277.t: 예산 is the plan before spending; 결산 is the final reckoning afterward.

T6-0278.ex: 보통선거는 재산과 관계없이 모든 성인에게 투표권을 줍니다.
T6-0278.x: Universal suffrage gives every adult the right to vote, regardless of property.
T6-0278.e: Literally 'common election' — every adult citizen gets to vote.
T6-0278.t: Korea's constitution names four election principles: 보통, 평등, 직접, 비밀선거.

T6-0279.ex: 그는 지난 선거에서 비례대표로 국회의원이 되었습니다.
T6-0279.x: He became a lawmaker through proportional representation in the last election.
T6-0279.e: Literally 'representation by ratio' — seats follow each party's share of votes.

T6-0280.ex: 그 의원은 자기 지역구 주민들을 자주 만납니다.
T6-0280.x: That lawmaker often meets the residents of his district.

T6-0281.ex: 의원이 사퇴하면서 그 지역에서 보궐선거가 열립니다.
T6-0281.x: Because the lawmaker resigned, a by-election will be held in that area.
T6-0281.t: 재선거 reruns an election that was declared void.

T6-0282.ex: 그는 당의 공천을 받아 국회의원 선거에 출마했어요.
T6-0282.x: He got his party's nomination and ran for the National Assembly.
T6-0282.t: Common phrases: 공천을 받다 (get the nomination) and 공천에서 탈락하다 (be passed over).

T6-0283.m: primary, party race (a competitive vote to pick a candidate or leader)
T6-0283.ex: 당내 경선에서 이긴 후보가 대선에 나갑니다.
T6-0283.x: The candidate who wins the party primary runs in the presidential election.

T6-0284.ex: 그 후보는 과반이 넘는 득표로 당선되었습니다.
T6-0284.x: That candidate was elected with more than half the votes.

T6-0285.m: share of the vote, percentage of votes won
T6-0285.x: He won 60% of the vote in this election.
T6-0285.e: Literally 'rate of ballots gained'. -율/률 = rate: 투표율, 실업률.
T6-0285.t: Use 율 after a vowel or ㄴ (득표율, 비율) and 률 elsewhere (실업률).

T6-0286.ex: 선거 전에 현금을 나눠 주는 것은 매표 행위입니다.
T6-0286.x: Handing out cash before an election is an act of vote buying.
T6-0286.e: Literally 'buying ballots'; a homonym of 매표 'ticket selling', as in 매표소.
T6-0286.t: Politicians often attack rivals' cash handouts as 매표용 포퓰리즘, 'vote-buying populism'.

T6-0287.x: The lawmakers voted against it, following the party line.

T6-0288.x: During the Joseon dynasty, factional fighting was fierce.
T6-0288.e: Literally 'party branch'; recalls the famous factional feuds of the Joseon court.

T6-0289.ex: 회사 안에 파벌이 생기면 분위기가 나빠져요.
T6-0289.x: When cliques form inside a company, the atmosphere goes bad.
T6-0289.e: Literally 'faction clan' — any closed group, in politics, business or academia.
T6-0289.t: 파벌 has a negative feel; common phrases are 파벌 싸움 and 파벌을 만들다.

T6-0290.ex: 당내 계파 갈등이 점점 심해지고 있습니다.
T6-0290.x: Factional conflict within the party is growing worse.
T6-0290.t: News labels factions with -계 after a leader's name, often with 친- (pro-), e.g. 친○계.

T6-0291.x: The public is tired of the endless partisan fighting.

T6-0292.x: The ruling and opposition parties promised to cooperate for people's livelihoods.
T6-0292.e: Literally 'governing together'; a fairly recent buzzword in Korean politics.

T6-0293.ex: 유럽에서 극우 정당의 지지율이 오르고 있습니다.
T6-0293.x: Support for far-right parties is rising in Europe.
T6-0293.t: Pronounced [그구]: the ㄱ moves over to the next syllable.

T6-0294.ex: 그 단체는 극좌 성향이라는 비판을 받았습니다.
T6-0294.x: The group was criticized for having far-left leanings.

T6-0295.x: During the Cold War, ideological confrontation was intense.
T6-0295.e: From German 'Ideologie' — hence the -기 ending instead of English '-gy'.
T6-0295.t: The Sino-Korean word 이념 means the same and is more common in news headlines.

T6-0296.ex: 지나친 국수주의는 다른 문화를 배척하게 만듭니다.
T6-0296.x: Excessive ultranationalism leads people to reject other cultures.
T6-0296.e: Literally 'ism of the nation's pure essence' — nothing to do with 국수 'noodles'.
T6-0296.t: 주의 is usually pronounced [주이] in everyday speech.

T6-0297.ex: 많은 아시아 국가들이 식민주의의 피해를 입었습니다.
T6-0297.x: Many Asian countries suffered under colonialism.
T6-0297.e: Literally 'planting people' — settling one's own people in another land.

T6-0298.ex: 전체주의 국가에서는 개인의 자유가 철저히 제한됩니다.
T6-0298.x: In a totalitarian state, individual freedom is strictly restricted.
T6-0298.e: Literally 'whole-ism' — the state as a whole outranks the individual. -주의 = -ism.

T6-0299.ex: 그 나라는 권위주의 정권에서 민주주의로 바뀌었습니다.
T6-0299.x: That country changed from an authoritarian regime to a democracy.
T6-0299.t: 권위적이다 also describes bossy people: 권위적인 상사 is an authoritarian boss.

T6-0300.x: Koreans fought against military dictatorship in the 1980s.
T6-0300.e: Literally 'military rule by one person deciding alone'.
T6-0300.t: Pronounced [군사독째] — the ㅈ after ㄱ is tensed.

T6-0302.ex: 일본과 영국은 지금도 왕이 있는 입헌군주제 국가입니다.
T6-0302.x: Japan and Britain are constitutional monarchies that still have a monarch.
T6-0302.e: Literally 'monarchy under an established constitution' — the king reigns but doesn't rule.
T6-0302.t: Pronounced [이펀군주제] — ㅂ and ㅎ merge into ㅍ.

T6-0303.m: popular sovereignty, sovereignty of the people
T6-0303.ex: 헌법은 국민주권의 원칙을 분명히 밝히고 있습니다.
T6-0303.x: The constitution clearly states the principle of popular sovereignty.
T6-0303.t: Article 1 of Korea's constitution says 주권은 국민에게 있다, 'sovereignty lies with the people'.

T6-0304.m: right to participate in politics, suffrage
T6-0304.ex: 여성의 참정권은 오랜 투쟁 끝에 얻어졌습니다.
T6-0304.x: Women's suffrage was won after a long struggle.
T6-0304.e: Literally 'right to take part in government'.
T6-0304.t: Pronounced [참정꿘] — the ㄱ in 권 is tensed.

T6-0305.x: Freedom of expression is a typical civil liberty.
T6-0305.e: Rights that protect you from the state: speech, religion, movement.

T6-0306.ex: 평등권은 성별이나 종교에 따른 차별을 금지합니다.
T6-0306.x: The right to equality forbids discrimination based on gender or religion.

T6-0307.ex: 일부 학자들은 저항권을 국민의 기본권으로 봅니다.
T6-0307.x: Some scholars see the right of resistance as a basic right of the people.
T6-0307.e: Literally 'right to resist' — against a government that abuses power.

T6-0308.ex: 시민사회 단체들이 정부 정책에 반대하는 성명을 냈습니다.
T6-0308.x: Civil society groups issued a statement opposing the government policy.
T6-0308.e: Literally 'citizens' society' — the space between government and business.

T6-0309.m: public sphere, forum for public debate
T6-0309.ex: 인터넷은 새로운 공론장의 역할을 하고 있습니다.
T6-0309.x: The internet is playing the role of a new public sphere.
T6-0309.e: Literally 'place for public discussion'; translates Habermas's 'public sphere'.

T6-0310.x: In a recent poll, the president's approval rating fell into the 30s.
T6-0310.e: Literally 'degree of support for the running of state affairs'.
T6-0310.t: Also called 국정 수행 지지도, or simply 지지율 in everyday talk.

T6-0311.ex: 임기 말이 되면서 대통령의 레임덕이 시작됐습니다.
T6-0311.x: As the end of his term neared, the president's lame-duck period began.
T6-0311.e: From English 'lame duck'; in Korea it means a leader's fading power late in the term.

T6-0312.ex: 관료주의 때문에 간단한 일도 처리가 늦어져요.
T6-0312.x: Because of red tape, even simple matters take a long time.
T6-0312.t: Pronounced [괄료주의] — the ㄴ becomes ㄹ before ㄹ.

T6-0313.ex: 관료제의 비효율성을 개선해야 한다는 목소리가 높아요.
T6-0313.x: There are growing calls to fix the inefficiency of the bureaucracy.
T6-0313.t: Pronounced [괄료제] — ㄴ before ㄹ becomes ㄹ.

T6-0314.m: high-ranking public official, senior government official
T6-0314.x: Senior public officials must disclose their assets every year.
T6-0314.e: Literally 'person in a high-ranking public post'.
T6-0314.t: Often heard in the news with 공수처, the agency investigating crimes by senior officials.

T6-0315.m: spoils system (handing out government jobs to party supporters)
T6-0315.ex: 엽관제는 선거에서 이긴 정당이 공직을 나누어 주는 제도예요.
T6-0315.x: The spoils system is a system in which the party that wins the election hands out public posts.
T6-0315.e: Literally 'office-hunting system' — winners hunt for government posts as their spoils.

T6-0316.ex: 행정부는 국회가 만든 법을 집행하는 역할을 해요.
T6-0316.x: The executive branch carries out the laws made by the National Assembly.
T6-0316.t: The three branches: 입법부 (makes laws), 행정부 (carries them out), 사법부 (judges).

T6-0317.ex: 지방자치단체마다 청년을 위한 지원 정책이 달라요.
T6-0317.x: Each local government has different support policies for young people.
T6-0317.t: In everyday news it is almost always shortened to 지자체.

T6-0318.m: head of a local government (mayor, governor, county chief)
T6-0318.ex: 이번 선거에서 새로운 자치단체장이 많이 뽑혔어요.
T6-0318.x: Many new local government heads were elected in this election.

T6-0319.ex: 지방정부와 중앙정부가 협력해서 문제를 해결해야 해요.
T6-0319.x: Local and central governments need to work together to solve the problem.

T6-0320.ex: 권력이 한곳에 모이지 않도록 분권이 필요해요.
T6-0320.x: Decentralization is needed so that power isn't concentrated in one place.
T6-0320.t: Pronounced [분꿘] — the ㄱ of 권 is tensed.

T6-0321.m: decentralization (transfer of power to local governments)
T6-0321.ex: 정부는 지방분권을 더욱 강화하겠다고 공식 발표했어요.
T6-0321.x: The government officially announced that it would further strengthen decentralization.
T6-0321.e: Literally 'dividing power out to the regions'.

T6-0322.ex: 조선은 왕을 중심으로 한 중앙집권 국가였어요.
T6-0322.x: Joseon was a centralized state built around the king.

T6-0323.ex: 효율적인 업무를 위해서는 적절한 권한위임이 필요해요.
T6-0323.x: Proper delegation of authority is needed for efficient work.
T6-0323.e: Literally 'entrusting one's powers' to someone else.
T6-0323.t: The verb form is 권한을 위임하다 (to delegate authority to someone).

T6-0324.ex: 정부는 기업 투자를 늘리기 위해 규제완화를 추진하고 있어요.
T6-0324.x: The government is pushing deregulation to increase corporate investment.

T6-0325.ex: 정부는 위기에 빠진 은행을 국유화하기로 했어요.
T6-0325.x: The government decided to nationalize the bank in crisis.
T6-0325.t: -화 = turning into something: 국유화, 민주화, 세계화.

T6-0326.ex: 대통령이 이민과 관련된 새로운 행정명령에 서명했어요.
T6-0326.x: The president signed a new executive order on immigration.
T6-0326.t: Pronounced [행정명녕] — ㄹ after ㅇ becomes ㄴ.

T6-0327.x: He received an administrative sanction of a license suspension for drunk driving.
T6-0327.e: Literally 'a government handling' of a case, such as a fine or license suspension.

T6-0328.ex: 공장을 지으려면 여러 가지 인허가 절차를 거쳐야 해요.
T6-0328.x: To build a factory, you have to go through various permit procedures.
T6-0328.e: A blend of 인가 (authorization) and 허가 (permission).
T6-0328.t: Usually combined: 인허가 절차 (permit process), 인허가를 받다 (obtain permits).

T6-0329.ex: 이 지역에서는 노점 영업이 허가제로 운영돼요.
T6-0329.x: In this area, street vending is run on a permit system.
T6-0329.e: Literally 'permission system' — you must get approval before acting.
T6-0329.t: 허가제 needs approval first; 신고제 only needs you to notify the authorities.

T6-0330.x: Assemblies are handled not by a permit system but by a notification system.
T6-0330.e: Literally 'reporting system' — you just inform officials instead of asking permission.

T6-0331.m: Board of Audit and Inspection (Korea's national audit agency)
T6-0331.ex: 감사원은 정부 기관의 예산 사용을 감사합니다.
T6-0331.x: The Board of Audit and Inspection audits how government agencies use their budgets.
T6-0331.t: Don't confuse this 감사 (audit) with 감사 (thanks); context makes it clear.

T6-0332.ex: 시민들은 옴부즈맨에게 행정에 대한 불만을 제기할 수 있어요.
T6-0332.x: Citizens can raise complaints about administration with the ombudsman.
T6-0332.e: From English 'ombudsman', originally a Swedish word; Korean drops the 'd' sound.

T6-0333.ex: 정책결정 과정에 시민의 의견이 반영되어야 해요.
T6-0333.x: Citizens' opinions should be reflected in the policy-making process.

T6-0334.ex: 언론은 사회의 의제설정에 큰 영향을 미쳐요.
T6-0334.x: The media has a big influence on setting society's agenda.
T6-0334.t: A key term in media studies: 언론의 의제설정 기능 (the press's agenda-setting function).

T6-0335.x: The government gave 40 days' advance notice of the proposed amendment.
T6-0335.e: Literally 'announcing a law in advance' so the public can comment.

T6-0336.x: The government postponed implementing the new system for one year.
T6-0336.e: Literally 'hesitating' — holding off on action for a set period.
T6-0336.t: Common pairs: 집행유예 (suspended sentence), 입영 유예 (military deferment), 유예 기간 (grace period).

T6-0337.x: The government decided to freeze public utility rates this year.
T6-0337.e: Literally 'frozen solid' — used figuratively for prices, wages and assets.

T6-0338.x: The government ordered that the improper practices be corrected.
T6-0338.t: Homonym alert: 시정 (市政) also means city administration, as in 시정 활동.

T6-0339.ex: 새 정부는 적폐 청산을 가장 중요한 과제로 내세웠어요.
T6-0339.x: The new government made rooting out deep-seated corruption its top priority.
T6-0339.t: Almost always used in the political slogan 적폐 청산 (cleaning up accumulated evils).

T6-0340.m: past history (especially painful or unresolved past events)
T6-0340.ex: 두 나라는 과거사 문제로 오랫동안 갈등을 겪어 왔어요.
T6-0340.x: The two countries have long been in conflict over issues of their past history.
T6-0340.t: In politics it usually means unresolved historical wrongs, as in 과거사 청산 or 과거사 반성.

T6-0341.x: The bereaved families are demanding that the truth about the accident be uncovered.
T6-0341.e: Literally 'investigating until the true picture is clear'.

T6-0342.ex: 국회는 그 사건에 대해 특검을 도입하기로 했어요.
T6-0342.x: The National Assembly decided to appoint a special prosecutor for that case.
T6-0342.t: 특검 can mean the prosecutor or the whole investigation, as in 특검 수사.

T6-0343.ex: 특별검사가 대통령 측근의 비리를 수사하고 있어요.
T6-0343.x: The special prosecutor is investigating corruption by the president's close aides.
T6-0343.e: Literally 'specially appointed prosecutor', chosen outside the regular prosecution.

T6-0344.x: A bill expanding the police's investigative authority was passed.
T6-0344.t: Pronounced [수사꿘] — 권 is tensed after many Sino nouns.

T6-0345.ex: 한국에서는 검찰이 기소권을 대부분 가지고 있어요.
T6-0345.x: In Korea, the prosecution holds most of the power to indict.

T6-0346.x: The prosecution and police worked together to investigate the crime ring.
T6-0346.e: A short combo of 검찰 'prosecution' and 경찰 'police'.
T6-0346.t: Mostly appears in news compounds like 검경 갈등 or 검경 수사권 조정.

T6-0347.m: governmental authority, state power (often police force)
T6-0347.x: State force was deployed to disperse the protesters.
T6-0347.t: Pronounced [공꿘녁], not [공궐력]; 공권력 투입 usually means sending in police.

T6-0348.x: The government declared martial law, citing a state of emergency.
T6-0348.t: Pronounced [계엄] or [게엄]; collocations: 계엄을 선포하다 (declare), 계엄을 해제하다 (lift).

T6-0349.x: When martial law was declared, soldiers were deployed in the streets.
T6-0349.t: Pronounced [계엄녕] — ㄹ after ㅁ becomes ㄴ.

T6-0350.ex: 국가보안법 폐지를 둘러싸고 논쟁이 계속되고 있어요.
T6-0350.x: Debate continues over abolishing the National Security Act.
T6-0350.e: Literally 'law for keeping the nation safe'.
T6-0350.t: Often shortened to 국보법 in news headlines.

T6-0351.ex: 정부는 국가안보를 위해 국방 예산을 늘렸어요.
T6-0351.x: The government increased the defense budget for the sake of national security.
T6-0351.e: 안보 is short for 안전보장 'guaranteeing safety'.

T6-0352.ex: 모병제로 바꾸자는 주장이 다시 나오고 있어요.
T6-0352.x: Arguments for switching to a volunteer military are coming up again.
T6-0352.e: Literally 'system of recruiting soldiers' (as opposed to drafting them).
T6-0352.t: South Korea currently uses 징병제 (conscription); 모병제 is the frequently debated alternative.

T6-0353.m: alternative (civilian) service in place of military service
T6-0353.ex: 양심적 병역거부자를 위한 대체복무 제도가 도입됐어요.
T6-0353.x: An alternative service system was introduced for conscientious objectors.
T6-0353.t: Pronounced [대체봉무] — ㄱ before ㅁ becomes ㅇ.

T6-0354.ex: 두 나라는 핵무기 군축 협상을 시작했어요.
T6-0354.x: The two countries began nuclear arms reduction talks.

T6-0355.x: I lost my passport, so I got help from the consul.
T6-0355.e: Literally 'one who oversees affairs' for citizens abroad.
T6-0355.t: 영사 (consul) handles citizens and visas; 대사 (ambassador) represents the country.

T6-0356.m: diplomatic mission (embassy or consulate); official residence
T6-0356.x: Overseas voting for Korean nationals took place at diplomatic missions abroad.
T6-0356.e: Literally 'public hall' — the building of an official or a mission.

T6-0357.ex: 두 나라는 영토 분쟁으로 결국 단교했어요.
T6-0357.x: The two countries eventually cut diplomatic ties over a territorial dispute.

T6-0358.x: Korea and that country established diplomatic relations in 1990.
T6-0358.t: Homonym alert: 국교 (國敎) also means 'state religion'; context tells which.

T6-0359.x: The normalization of diplomatic relations between Korea and Japan took place in 1965.
T6-0359.e: Literally 'making relations between nations normal again'.

T6-0360.ex: 대통령은 이번 순방에서 활발한 정상외교를 펼쳤어요.
T6-0360.x: The president engaged in active summit diplomacy on this tour.
T6-0360.t: Homonym alert: 정상 (頂上) = summit/leader, while 정상 (正常) = normal.

T6-0361.x: Multilateral diplomacy is important for solving international problems.

T6-0362.x: The foreign ministers of the two countries held bilateral talks.
T6-0362.e: Literally 'meeting and talks between two parties'.

T6-0363.ex: 정상회담에 앞서 양측의 실무회담이 판문점에서 열렸어요.
T6-0363.x: Ahead of the summit, working-level talks between the two sides were held at Panmunjom.
T6-0363.e: Literally 'talks about the actual work' before leaders meet.

T6-0364.x: Many countries signed the Kyoto Protocol.

T6-0365.ex: 양국 정상은 회담 후 공동성명을 발표했어요.
T6-0365.x: After the talks, the leaders of the two countries issued a joint statement.

T6-0366.ex: 회의가 끝난 뒤 참가국들은 선언문을 채택했어요.
T6-0366.x: After the conference, the participating countries adopted a declaration.

T6-0367.x: The resolution was adopted overwhelmingly at the UN General Assembly.
T6-0367.t: Pronounced [겨리안]; common verbs: 결의안을 채택하다 (adopt) and 결의안을 통과시키다 (pass).

T6-0368.x: The Security Council condemned North Korea's missile launch.
T6-0368.t: News nearly always uses the short form 안보리.

T6-0369.m: permanent member (of the UN Security Council)
T6-0369.ex: 안보리의 다섯 상임이사국은 모두 거부권을 가지고 있어요.
T6-0369.x: All five permanent members of the Security Council have veto power.
T6-0369.e: Literally 'nation permanently appointed as a director'.

T6-0370.x: Several NGOs provided food to the refugees.
T6-0370.e: Literally 'non-government organization', a direct translation of NGO.
T6-0370.t: In speech, many Koreans simply say 엔지오 (NGO).

T6-0371.ex: 미국은 한국의 가장 중요한 동맹국 중 하나예요.
T6-0371.x: The U.S. is one of Korea's most important allies.

T6-0372.x: The government said it would cooperate closely with its friendly nations.
T6-0372.t: 우방 is looser than 동맹국: a friendly country without a formal alliance treaty.

T6-0373.x: That country designated us as a hostile state.
T6-0373.t: Pronounced [적썽국] — ㅅ is tensed after ㄱ.

T6-0374.ex: 많은 나라가 강대국의 패권주의를 비판하고 있어요.
T6-0374.x: Many countries criticize the hegemonism of the great powers.

T6-0375.ex: 냉전 시대에는 두 초강대국이 세계를 나누어 지배했어요.
T6-0375.x: During the Cold War, two superpowers divided and dominated the world.

T6-0376.x: The balance of power in Northeast Asia is changing rapidly.

T6-0377.x: He is researching geopolitics at a university.

T6-0378.ex: 한국은 지정학적 위치 때문에 강대국 사이에서 어려움을 겪었어요.
T6-0378.x: Because of its geopolitical location, Korea has had difficulties between great powers.
T6-0378.e: -적 turns a noun into '-ic/-al': 지정학 to 지정학적.
T6-0378.t: Used directly before nouns (지정학적 위치) or with -으로 / -인: 지정학적으로 중요한.

T6-0379.ex: 탈냉전 이후 국제 질서가 크게 바뀌었어요.
T6-0379.x: The international order changed greatly after the end of the Cold War.
T6-0379.t: Pronounced [탈랭전] — ㄴ after ㄹ becomes ㄹ.

T6-0380.x: In the 1970s, détente began between the U.S. and the Soviet Union.
T6-0380.e: From French 'détente' via English; Korean adds ㅡ: 데-탕-트.

T6-0381.ex: 남북 대화가 한반도의 긴장완화에 도움이 됐어요.
T6-0381.x: Inter-Korean dialogue helped ease tensions on the Korean Peninsula.
T6-0381.e: Literally 'loosening what is tight and stretched'.
T6-0381.t: 긴장 고조 (rising tension) is the opposite you'll see in the same news stories.

T6-0382.ex: 정상회담 이후 두 나라 사이에 화해무드가 조성됐어요.
T6-0382.x: After the summit, a mood of reconciliation formed between the two countries.
T6-0382.e: 화해 'reconciliation' plus English 'mood'; Konglish 무드 means 'atmosphere'.

T6-0383.x: There are discussions about replacing the armistice with a peace treaty.

T6-0384.x: The fighting in the Korean War stopped with the 1953 armistice agreement.
T6-0384.e: Literally 'agreement to stop the war' — fighting halts but no peace treaty.
T6-0384.t: Also called 휴전협정; it halted fighting but didn't formally end the Korean War.

T6-0385.ex: 휴전선 근처에는 민간인이 들어갈 수 없어요.
T6-0385.x: Civilians can't enter the area near the armistice line.

T6-0386.x: The DMZ has become home to rare plants and animals.

T6-0387.ex: 그는 한국으로 귀화해서 국가대표 선수가 됐어요.
T6-0387.x: He became a naturalized Korean citizen and joined the national team.
T6-0387.e: Literally 'turning and coming over' to another country's rule.
T6-0387.t: Pattern: (나라)로 귀화하다 — 한국으로 귀화하다 (become a naturalized Korean).

T6-0388.ex: 그 선수는 미국과 한국의 이중국적을 가지고 있어요.
T6-0388.x: That athlete holds dual U.S. and Korean citizenship.
T6-0388.t: The official legal term is now 복수국적, but 이중국적 is still common in speech.

T6-0389.ex: 전쟁으로 많은 사람들이 무국적 상태가 되었어요.
T6-0389.x: Because of the war, many people became stateless.

T6-0390.ex: 그 나라는 외국의 비판을 내정간섭이라고 반발했어요.
T6-0390.x: That country pushed back, calling the foreign criticism interference in its internal affairs.
T6-0390.t: 간섭 is everyday too: 간섭하지 마세요 means 'Stop meddling'.

T6-0391.ex: 두 나라는 내정불간섭 원칙을 지키기로 합의했습니다.
T6-0391.x: The two countries agreed to uphold the principle of non-interference in internal affairs.

T6-0392.m: violation of sovereignty, infringement of sovereignty
T6-0392.ex: 정부는 이번 사건을 명백한 주권침해로 규정했습니다.
T6-0392.x: The government defined the incident as a clear violation of sovereignty.

T6-0393.ex: 두 나라는 작은 섬을 둘러싸고 영토분쟁을 벌이고 있습니다.
T6-0393.x: The two countries are engaged in a territorial dispute over a small island.

T6-0394.ex: 양국은 그 섬에 대한 영유권을 서로 주장하고 있습니다.
T6-0394.x: Both countries claim sovereignty over that island.
T6-0394.e: Literally 'the right to govern and possess'.

T6-0395.ex: 외국 어선이 허가 없이 우리 영해에 들어왔습니다.
T6-0395.x: A foreign fishing boat entered our territorial waters without permission.

T6-0396.x: An unidentified aircraft violated our airspace.

T6-0397.ex: 중국 어선이 우리 배타적경제수역에서 불법 조업을 했습니다.
T6-0397.x: Chinese fishing boats fished illegally in our exclusive economic zone.
T6-0397.e: Literally 'other-excluding economic water area'; it reaches 200 nautical miles offshore.
T6-0397.t: News often just says EEZ, read as 이이지.

T6-0398.ex: 국제사회는 그 나라에 강력한 경제제재를 가했습니다.
T6-0398.x: The international community imposed strong economic sanctions on that country.

T6-0399.ex: 정부는 그 나라에 대한 석유 금수조치를 발표했습니다.
T6-0399.x: The government announced an oil embargo against that country.

T6-0400.ex: 미국이 관세를 올리자 중국도 보복관세로 맞섰습니다.
T6-0400.x: When the U.S. raised tariffs, China fought back with retaliatory tariffs.

T6-0401.ex: 두 나라 사이의 통상마찰이 점점 심해지고 있습니다.
T6-0401.x: Trade friction between the two countries is getting worse.

T6-0402.ex: 정부는 통상 문제를 논의하기 위해 대표단을 보냈습니다.
T6-0402.x: The government sent a delegation to discuss trade issues.
T6-0402.t: Don't confuse with the homonym 통상 'usually' (通常), as in 통상 9시에 시작해요.
rel: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy

T6-0403.x: Korea has signed free trade agreements with many countries.
T6-0403.e: Literally 'a fixed cooperation on free trade'.
T6-0403.t: In everyday news it's usually just called FTA (에프티에이).

T6-0404.ex: 정상회의장 밖에서 대규모 반세계화 시위가 열렸습니다.
T6-0404.x: A large anti-globalization protest was held outside the summit venue.

T6-0405.forms: 초국적 + noun: 초국적 기업 · 초국적 자본
T6-0405.ex: 초국적 기업들이 세계 경제에 큰 영향을 미치고 있습니다.
T6-0405.x: Transnational corporations have a big influence on the world economy.
T6-0405.t: Pronounced [초국쩍]; 다국적 기업 is the more common everyday term.

T6-0406.ex: 정부는 상호주의 원칙에 따라 비자 정책을 바꿨습니다.
T6-0406.x: The government changed its visa policy according to the principle of reciprocity.
T6-0406.t: 주의 is pronounced [주이] in natural speech.

T6-0407.ex: 두 나라는 호혜 원칙에 따라 관세를 낮추기로 했습니다.
