T6-0407.x: The two countries decided to lower tariffs on the principle of mutual benefit.
T6-0407.t: Pronounced [호헤]; mostly used in compounds like 호혜적 관계, 호혜 평등.

T6-0408.ex: 한국은 원조를 받던 나라에서 공적개발원조를 주는 나라가 되었습니다.
T6-0408.x: Korea went from a country that received aid to one that gives official development assistance.
T6-0408.e: Literally 'public aid for development'; usually just called ODA.

T6-0409.forms: 인도적 지원을 하다 · 인도적 지원이 필요하다
T6-0409.ex: 정부는 지진 피해 국가에 인도적 지원을 보내기로 했습니다.
T6-0409.x: The government decided to send humanitarian aid to the earthquake-hit country.
T6-0409.e: Literally 'aid in the way of humanity'.
T6-0409.t: Don't confuse 인도 'humanity' with the homonyms 인도 'India' and 인도 'sidewalk'.

T6-0410.x: Korean troops have also been dispatched overseas as UN peacekeepers.

T6-0411.x: The government announced it would complete the troop withdrawal by the end of the year.

T6-0412.ex: 그 나라에는 아직도 외국 주둔군이 남아 있습니다.
T6-0412.x: Foreign troops are still stationed in that country.

T6-0413.ex: 여러 나라가 군비를 늘리면서 긴장이 높아지고 있습니다.
T6-0413.x: Tensions are rising as many countries build up their armaments.
T6-0413.t: A homonym 군비 (軍費) means 'military spending'; context usually tells them apart.

T6-0414.ex: 냉전 시대에 미국과 소련은 치열한 군비경쟁을 벌였습니다.
T6-0414.x: During the Cold War, the U.S. and the Soviet Union waged a fierce arms race.

T6-0415.ex: 국제사회는 핵확산을 막기 위해 노력하고 있습니다.
T6-0415.x: The international community is working to prevent nuclear proliferation.

T6-0416.ex: 북한의 핵실험에 대해 유엔이 강하게 규탄했습니다.
T6-0416.x: The UN strongly condemned North Korea's nuclear test.

T6-0417.ex: 그 나라는 선제공격의 가능성을 배제하지 않았습니다.
T6-0417.x: That country did not rule out the possibility of a preemptive strike.

T6-0418.ex: 러시아의 우크라이나 침공으로 많은 난민이 발생했습니다.
T6-0418.x: Russia's invasion of Ukraine created many refugees.
T6-0418.t: 침공 is a military invasion; 침략 stresses the aggression behind it.

T6-0419.ex: 적군이 수도를 점령하자 시민들이 피란을 떠났습니다.
T6-0419.x: When enemy forces captured the capital, citizens fled as refugees.

T6-0420.x: In 1910, Japan forcibly annexed the Korean Empire.

T6-0421.ex: 그 지역 주민들은 더 많은 자치권을 요구하고 있습니다.
T6-0421.x: Residents of that region are demanding more autonomy.

T6-0422.x: Scotland held a referendum on independence.

T6-0423.ex: 기자들은 위험을 무릅쓰고 분쟁지역에서 취재를 했습니다.
T6-0423.x: Reporters risked danger to cover the news in the conflict zone.

T6-0424.ex: 세계 각국은 테러리즘에 맞서 협력하고 있습니다.
T6-0424.x: Countries around the world are cooperating against terrorism.
T6-0424.e: From English 'terrorism'; in everyday speech Koreans usually just say 테러.

T6-0425.forms: 대테러 + noun: 대테러 작전 · 대테러 훈련
T6-0425.x: A large-scale counterterrorism drill was held at the airport.
T6-0425.t: Almost always used before another noun, like 대테러 부대 'counterterrorism unit'.

T6-0426.ex: 양측은 전쟁이 끝난 뒤 포로를 교환했습니다.
T6-0426.x: Both sides exchanged prisoners after the war ended.

T6-0427.ex: 그는 전쟁이 끝난 후 전범으로 재판을 받았습니다.
T6-0427.x: He was tried as a war criminal after the war ended.
T6-0427.t: Koreans call Japan's Rising Sun flag 전범기 'war criminal flag'.

T6-0428.x: The international community defined attacks on civilians as war crimes.

T6-0429.ex: 그 마을에서 민간인 학살이 일어났다는 보도가 나왔습니다.
T6-0429.x: There were reports that a massacre of civilians took place in that village.

T6-0430.ex: 이 박물관은 대량학살의 희생자들을 기억하기 위해 세워졌습니다.
T6-0430.x: This museum was built to remember the victims of the mass killing.

T6-0431.ex: 국제법은 제노사이드를 가장 심각한 범죄로 봅니다.
T6-0431.x: International law regards genocide as the most serious crime.
T6-0431.e: From English 'genocide'; the Korean equivalent is 집단학살 or 대량학살.

T6-0432.ex: 두 나라는 분쟁을 국제사법재판소에 맡기기로 했습니다.
T6-0432.x: The two countries decided to take their dispute to the International Court of Justice.
T6-0432.e: Literally 'international place for administering law and judging'.
T6-0432.t: Don't mix it up with 국제형사재판소 (ICC), which tries individuals, not states.

T6-0433.ex: 양국 정부는 포로 송환 문제를 놓고 교섭을 벌였습니다.
T6-0433.x: The two governments negotiated over the repatriation of prisoners.
T6-0433.t: 교섭 sounds more formal than 협상; labor talks are 단체교섭.

T6-0434.ex: 오랜 논의 끝에 무역 협상이 마침내 타결되었습니다.
T6-0434.x: After long discussions, the trade negotiations were finally concluded.
T6-0434.t: Opposite of 결렬; news often says 협상이 타결되다 versus 협상이 결렬되다.

T6-0435.ex: 양측의 입장 차이로 회담이 결국 결렬되었습니다.
T6-0435.x: The talks eventually broke down because of the two sides' differences.

T6-0436.ex: 핵 협상이 서로의 요구 때문에 난항을 겪고 있습니다.
T6-0436.x: The nuclear talks are running into difficulties because of each side's demands.

T6-0437.ex: 남북 대화가 몇 년째 교착상태에 빠져 있습니다.
T6-0437.x: Inter-Korean dialogue has been stuck in a deadlock for several years.

T6-0438.ex: 두 나라는 정상회담을 앞두고 물밑접촉을 이어 가고 있습니다.
T6-0438.x: Ahead of the summit, the two countries are continuing backchannel contacts.
T6-0438.e: Native 물밑 'under the water' + 'contact': talks happening out of sight.

T6-0439.ex: 그는 막후에서 협상을 성사시킨 핵심 인물입니다.
T6-0439.x: He is the key figure who made the deal happen behind the scenes.
T6-0439.t: Pronounced [마쿠]; usually 막후에서 or 막후 + noun, like 막후 실세.

T6-0440.x: The Foreign Ministry carefully prepared the protocol for the summit.
T6-0440.t: Also used for VIP treatment generally: 의전을 받다 'to get the red-carpet treatment'.

T6-0441.ex: 대통령은 공항에서 외국 국빈을 직접 맞이했습니다.
T6-0441.x: The president personally welcomed the foreign state guest at the airport.

T6-0442.ex: 대통령은 다음 주에 미국을 국빈방문할 예정입니다.
T6-0442.x: The president is scheduled to make a state visit to the U.S. next week.
T6-0442.e: Literally 'visiting as a guest of the nation'.

T6-0443.ex: 새로 부임한 대사가 외교부 장관을 예방했습니다.
T6-0443.x: The newly appointed ambassador paid a courtesy call on the foreign minister.
T6-0443.t: Don't confuse with the far more common homonym 예방 (豫防) 'prevention', as in 예방 접종.

T6-0444.ex: 두 정상은 회담 전에 잠시 환담을 나눴습니다.
T6-0444.x: The two leaders had a brief friendly chat before the talks.

T6-0445.m: personal letter (from a head of state)
T6-0445.ex: 대통령은 특사를 통해 상대국 정상에게 친서를 전달했습니다.
T6-0445.x: The president delivered a personal letter to the other country's leader through a special envoy.

T6-0446.x: The government released diplomatic documents that were over 30 years old.

T6-0447.forms: 외교적 수사에 불과하다 · 외교적 수사로 들리다
T6-0447.ex: 그 발언은 단순한 외교적 수사에 불과하다는 평가가 나왔습니다.
T6-0447.x: Some judged the remark to be nothing more than diplomatic rhetoric.
T6-0447.t: Don't confuse 수사 'rhetoric' with the more common homonym 수사 'criminal investigation'.

T6-0448.ex: 상대국은 공식 사과 대신 유감표명만 했습니다.
T6-0448.x: The other country only expressed regret instead of making an official apology.
T6-0448.t: In diplomacy, 유감 is noticeably weaker than a real 사과 'apology'.

T6-0449.ex: 시민들은 광장에 모여 정부의 결정을 규탄했습니다.
T6-0449.x: Citizens gathered in the square and denounced the government's decision.
T6-0449.t: Mostly used as 규탄하다 in news and protest slogans.

T6-0450.ex: 회의에서 여러 나라 대표들이 그 나라의 행동을 성토했습니다.
T6-0450.x: At the meeting, delegates from many countries denounced that country's actions.

T6-0451.ex: 외교부는 일본 대사를 초치해 강하게 항의했습니다.
T6-0451.x: The Foreign Ministry summoned the Japanese ambassador and lodged a strong protest.
T6-0451.t: In news, 초치 almost always means calling in a foreign envoy to protest.

T6-0452.ex: 정부는 그 외교관을 기피인물로 지정하고 추방했습니다.
T6-0452.x: The government declared the diplomat persona non grata and expelled him.

T6-0453.x: The diplomat was not arrested because of his diplomatic immunity.
T6-0453.e: Literally 'special right of exemption from responsibility'.

T6-0454.ex: 대사관은 치외법권 지역이라서 경찰이 함부로 들어갈 수 없습니다.
T6-0454.x: An embassy is extraterritorial ground, so police can't just go in.
T6-0454.e: Literally 'the right to be outside the governing law'.

T6-0455.ex: 형이상학은 존재의 근본 원리를 탐구하는 학문입니다.
T6-0455.x: Metaphysics is the field that studies the fundamental principles of existence.
T6-0455.e: Literally 'study of what lies above form', from an ancient Chinese classic.

T6-0456.ex: 인식론은 우리가 무엇을 어떻게 알 수 있는지 묻습니다.
T6-0456.x: Epistemology asks what we can know and how.

T6-0457.ex: 존재론은 존재한다는 것이 무엇인지 묻는 철학 분야입니다.
T6-0457.x: Ontology is the branch of philosophy that asks what it means to exist.

T6-0458.ex: 윤리학 수업에서 안락사 문제를 두고 토론했습니다.
T6-0458.x: In ethics class, we debated the issue of euthanasia.
T6-0458.t: Pronounced [율리학] — ㄴ becomes ㄹ before ㄹ.

T6-0459.x: He is majoring in aesthetics in graduate school.

T6-0460.ex: 논리학을 공부하면 생각을 더 체계적으로 할 수 있습니다.
T6-0460.x: Studying logic helps you think more systematically.
T6-0460.t: Pronounced [놀리학] — ㄴ becomes ㄹ before ㄹ.

T6-0461.ex: 헤겔의 변증법은 흔히 정, 반, 합의 단계로 설명됩니다.
T6-0461.x: Hegel's dialectic is often explained as the stages of thesis, antithesis and synthesis.

T6-0462.x: Marx interpreted history from a materialist standpoint.
T6-0462.t: Philosophical only; for loving possessions, say 물질주의 instead.

T6-0463.ex: 관념론은 정신이나 관념을 세계의 근본으로 봅니다.
T6-0463.x: Idealism sees the mind or ideas as the foundation of the world.
T6-0463.t: Pronounced [관념논]; for idealism meaning 'high ideals', use 이상주의.

T6-0464.x: Locke is the philosopher who represents British empiricism.

T6-0465.ex: 데카르트는 근대 합리론을 대표하는 프랑스 철학자입니다.
T6-0465.x: Descartes is the French philosopher who represents modern rationalism.

T6-0466.ex: 콩트는 실증주의를 처음 체계화한 사람으로 알려져 있습니다.
T6-0466.x: Comte is known as the first person to systematize positivism.

T6-0467.x: Sartre is a French philosopher who represents existentialism.

T6-0468.ex: 구조주의는 언어학에서 시작되어 인류학과 철학으로 퍼졌습니다.
T6-0468.x: Structuralism began in linguistics and spread to anthropology and philosophy.

T6-0469.ex: 탈구조주의는 텍스트의 의미가 고정되어 있지 않다고 봅니다.
T6-0469.x: Post-structuralism holds that the meaning of a text is not fixed.
T6-0469.t: 탈- is a productive prefix for 'post-' or 'de-': 탈원전 (nuclear phase-out), 탈권위 (anti-authoritarian).

T6-0470.ex: 포스트모더니즘은 거대 담론에 대한 불신에서 출발했습니다.
T6-0470.x: Postmodernism started from a distrust of grand narratives.
T6-0470.e: From English 'postmodernism'; the ending '-ism' becomes 이즘 [ijeum].
T6-0470.t: In academic writing you will also see the Sino-Korean term 탈근대주의 for the same idea.

T6-0471.ex: 그는 전쟁을 겪은 후 깊은 허무주의에 빠졌어요.
T6-0471.x: After going through the war, he fell into deep nihilism.
T6-0471.t: The everyday adjective is 허무하다: 인생이 허무해요 (Life feels empty).

T6-0472.ex: 쾌락주의는 즐거움을 삶의 최고 가치로 봅니다.
T6-0472.x: Hedonism sees pleasure as the highest value in life.
T6-0472.t: 쾌락 often has a sensual or indulgent ring, so use 즐거움 for everyday 'fun' or 'enjoyment'.

T6-0473.x: The monks lived by practicing strict asceticism.
T6-0473.t: Pronounced [그묙쭈의]: the ㅁ links over to the next vowel.

T6-0474.ex: 공리주의는 최대 다수의 최대 행복을 추구합니다.
T6-0474.x: Utilitarianism pursues the greatest happiness of the greatest number.
T6-0474.e: Literally 'merit-and-benefit-ism'; not the same 공리 as 'axiom'.
T6-0474.t: Pronounced [공니주의]: ㄹ turns into ㄴ after ㅇ.

T6-0475.ex: 칸트의 윤리학은 대표적인 의무론으로 알려져 있어요.
T6-0475.x: Kant's ethics is known as a classic example of deontology.
T6-0475.e: Literally 'duty theory'; -론 = theory or '-ism': 무신론, 결정론.

T6-0476.ex: 결과주의에 따르면 행위의 옳고 그름은 결과로 결정돼요.
T6-0476.x: According to consequentialism, whether an act is right or wrong is decided by its results.
T6-0476.e: Literally 'result-ism'; 결과 pictures a tree bearing fruit.

T6-0477.ex: 도덕적 상대주의는 보편적인 윤리 기준을 부정합니다.
T6-0477.x: Moral relativism denies universal ethical standards.
T6-0477.e: Literally 'facing-each-other-ism': things are judged only in relation to others.
T6-0477.t: 상대 alone also means 'the other person' or 'opponent': 대화 상대 (someone to talk to).

T6-0478.x: Seventeenth-century France is a classic example of an absolutist monarchy.
T6-0478.t: 절대 alone is a strong adverb, 'never' or 'absolutely': 절대 안 돼요! (Absolutely not!)

T6-0479.ex: 보편주의는 모든 인간에게 같은 권리가 있다고 주장해요.
T6-0479.x: Universalism claims that all humans have the same rights.

T6-0480.ex: 그는 신의 존재에 대해 불가지론의 입장을 취해요.
T6-0480.x: He takes an agnostic position on the existence of God.
T6-0480.e: Literally 'cannot-know theory', a neat match for Greek 'a-gnostic'.
T6-0480.t: Add -자 for the person: 불가지론자 is an agnostic, 무신론자 an atheist.

T6-0481.ex: 무신론을 주장하는 사람들도 종교의 역할은 인정하기도 해요.
T6-0481.x: Even people who argue for atheism sometimes acknowledge the role of religion.
T6-0481.t: Pronounced [무신논]: in this word ㄹ becomes ㄴ after ㄴ.

T6-0482.ex: 유신론은 세상을 창조한 신이 있다고 믿는 입장이에요.
T6-0482.x: Theism is the position that a god created the world.
T6-0482.e: Literally 'there-is-a-god theory'; 유 and 무 (have/lack) are a common opposite pair.

T6-0483.x: Spinoza's philosophy is often interpreted as pantheism.
T6-0483.e: Literally 'god-in-everything theory': nature itself is divine.

T6-0484.ex: 결정론이 옳다면 우리의 선택도 이미 정해져 있는 셈이에요.
T6-0484.x: If determinism is right, then our choices are, in effect, already decided.
T6-0484.e: Literally 'decided theory': everything is fixed in advance.
T6-0484.t: Pronounced [결쩡논]: tensing after ㄹ, then ㄹ becomes ㄴ after ㅇ.

T6-0485.ex: 인간에게 정말 자유의지가 있는지는 오래된 철학적 질문이에요.
T6-0485.x: Whether humans really have free will is an old philosophical question.
T6-0485.t: Also often written with a space, 자유 의지; both spellings appear.

T6-0486.x: Aristotle explained nature from a teleological perspective.
T6-0486.e: Literally 'goal theory'; 목적 pictures the eye fixed on a target.
T6-0486.t: Pronounced [목쩡논]: ㄱ before ㄹ makes both sounds nasal.

T6-0487.ex: 데카르트의 이원론은 정신과 육체를 분리해서 봅니다.
T6-0487.x: Descartes' dualism views the mind and the body as separate.
T6-0487.t: Standard pronunciation is [이원논], not [이월론], a textbook exception.

T6-0488.ex: 일원론은 세계가 하나의 근본 원리로 이루어졌다고 봐요.
T6-0488.x: Monism holds that the world is made of a single fundamental principle.

T6-0489.ex: 후설은 현상학을 엄밀한 학문으로 세우려고 했어요.
T6-0489.x: Husserl tried to establish phenomenology as a rigorous science.
T6-0489.t: 현상 alone is everyday: 자연 현상 (natural phenomenon), 사회 현상 (social phenomenon).

T6-0490.ex: 많은 종교는 시간과 공간의 초월을 이야기해요.
T6-0490.x: Many religions speak of transcending time and space.
T6-0490.t: Most common as a verb: 상상을 초월하다 (to be beyond imagination).

T6-0491.ex: 많은 사람들이 초월적 존재에게서 위안을 얻어요.
T6-0491.x: Many people find comfort in a transcendent being.

T6-0492.ex: 칸트는 시간과 공간을 선험적 형식으로 보았어요.
T6-0492.x: Kant saw time and space as a priori forms.
T6-0492.e: Literally 'before-experience', a direct match for Latin 'a priori'.

T6-0493.ex: 경험을 통해 얻는 지식을 후험적 지식이라고 해요.
T6-0493.x: Knowledge gained through experience is called a posteriori knowledge.
T6-0493.e: Literally 'after-experience', the mirror image of 선험적.
T6-0493.t: Outside philosophy, 경험적 (empirical) is far more common than 후험적.

T6-0494.ex: 이 결론은 몇 가지 전제에서 연역을 통해 얻은 거예요.
T6-0494.x: This conclusion was reached through deduction from a few premises.
T6-0494.e: Literally 'drawing out and unraveling': pulling conclusions out of premises.
T6-0494.t: Pronounced [여녁]: the ㄴ carries over into the next vowel.

T6-0495.ex: 여러 사례를 관찰해서 일반 법칙을 끌어내는 것이 귀납이에요.
T6-0495.x: Observing many cases and drawing out a general law is induction.
T6-0495.e: Literally 'returning and gathering in': collecting many cases into one rule.

T6-0496.x: Mathematical proofs mainly use deductive reasoning.
T6-0496.t: Pronounced [여녁뻡]: the ㅂ tenses after ㄱ.

T6-0497.ex: 과학자들은 실험 결과를 바탕으로 귀납법을 활용해요.
T6-0497.x: Scientists use inductive reasoning based on experimental results.

T6-0498.ex: 삼단논법에서 대전제가 틀리면 결론도 믿을 수 없어요.
T6-0498.x: In a syllogism, if the major premise is wrong, the conclusion can't be trusted either.
T6-0498.e: Literally 'big premise'; 전제 is something put forward beforehand.
T6-0498.t: Also used figuratively for a non-negotiable starting point: 안전이 대전제입니다 (Safety is the top priority).

T6-0499.x: 'All men are mortal' is the major premise of a famous syllogism.

T6-0500.ex: 그의 주장은 앞뒤가 맞지 않는 자가당착에 빠졌어요.
T6-0500.x: His argument fell into self-contradiction, with its parts not fitting together.
T6-0500.e: Literally 'one's own house colliding': your own words clash with each other.
T6-0500.t: A four-character idiom, usually in 자가당착에 빠지다 (to fall into self-contradiction).

T6-0501.ex: 결론을 전제로 사용하는 것은 전형적인 순환논증이에요.
T6-0501.x: Using the conclusion as a premise is typical circular reasoning.
T6-0501.t: Also written with a space, 순환 논증.

T6-0502.ex: 유클리드 기하학은 다섯 개의 공리에서 시작합니다.
T6-0502.x: Euclidean geometry starts from five axioms.
T6-0502.e: Literally 'public principle': a truth everyone accepts without proof.
T6-0502.t: Pronounced [공니]; the 공리 in 공리주의 (utility) is a different word written with other characters.

T6-0503.ex: 칸트의 정언명령은 조건 없이 따라야 하는 도덕 법칙이에요.
T6-0503.x: Kant's categorical imperative is a moral law that must be followed unconditionally.
T6-0503.e: Literally 'fixed-statement command': an order with no 'if' attached.
T6-0503.t: Pronounced [정언명녕]; its opposite is 가언명령, an 'if-then' command.

T6-0504.ex: 칸트는 마음속의 도덕률을 늘 경이롭게 여겼어요.
T6-0504.x: Kant always regarded the moral law within him with wonder.
T6-0504.t: Pronounced [도덩뉼]; this ending is spelled -율 after a vowel or ㄴ, as in 규율 and 비율.

T6-0505.ex: 교육은 지식뿐만 아니라 덕성도 길러야 합니다.
T6-0505.x: Education must cultivate not only knowledge but also virtue.

T6-0506.x: Greed has long been regarded as a classic vice.
T6-0506.e: Literally 'evil character trait', the opposite of 미덕.
T6-0506.t: Often used before a noun: 악덕 기업 (unscrupulous company), 악덕 업주 (exploitative employer).

T6-0507.ex: 아이들은 자라면서 선악을 구별하는 법을 배워요.
T6-0507.x: Children learn to tell good from evil as they grow up.
T6-0507.e: Literally 'good-evil', a pair compound like 남녀 or 대소.
T6-0507.t: Pronounced [서낙]: the ㄴ moves into the next syllable.

T6-0508.ex: 법원은 이번 사건의 시비를 가려야 합니다.
T6-0508.x: The court must determine who is right and who is wrong in this case.
T6-0508.e: Literally 'right-wrong'; 시비를 가리다 = to sort out who is right.
T6-0508.t: In everyday speech, 시비를 걸다 means 'to pick a quarrel': 왜 시비를 걸어요?

T6-0509.ex: 세금 제도는 형평에 맞게 설계되어야 합니다.
T6-0509.x: The tax system should be designed to be fair.
T6-0509.t: Most often seen as 형평성: 형평성에 어긋나다 (to be unfair).

T6-0510.m: basic human morality, moral duties between people
T6-0510.ex: 부모를 버리는 것은 인륜에 어긋나는 일이에요.
T6-0510.x: Abandoning your parents goes against basic human morality.
T6-0510.e: Literally 'human order': the proper relations between people.
T6-0510.t: Pronounced [일륜]: ㄴ before ㄹ becomes ㄹ.

T6-0511.m: natural bond of kinship, blood ties
T6-0511.ex: 부모와 자식 사이의 천륜은 끊을 수 없어요.
T6-0511.x: The natural bond between parents and children cannot be broken.
T6-0511.e: Literally 'heaven's order': family ties no one chooses.
T6-0511.t: Pronounced [철륜]: ㄴ before ㄹ becomes ㄹ.

T6-0512.m: gross immorality, violation of human morality (esp. toward family)
T6-0512.ex: 부모를 폭행한 패륜 사건이 뉴스에 보도되었습니다.
T6-0512.x: A shocking case of someone assaulting their parents was reported on the news.
T6-0512.t: A very strong word, typically for crimes against one's own family; 패륜아 is the person who commits them.

T6-0513.m: duty, the right thing to do; way, means
T6-0513.ex: 어른을 공경하는 것은 사람의 도리라고 생각해요.
T6-0513.x: I think respecting your elders is a person's moral duty.
T6-0513.t: Common patterns: 자식 된 도리 (one's duty as a child); 어쩔 도리가 없다 (there's nothing one can do).

T6-0514.ex: 이번 사고를 계기로 업계 전체의 자성이 필요합니다.
T6-0514.x: This accident calls for soul-searching across the whole industry.
T6-0514.t: Common in the news: 자성의 목소리가 나오다 (calls for self-reflection arise).

T6-0515.ex: 일기를 쓰면 하루를 성찰하는 데 도움이 돼요.
T6-0515.x: Keeping a diary helps you reflect on your day.
T6-0515.t: 성찰 is deeper and more philosophical than 반성, which usually implies regret over a mistake.

T6-0516.ex: 혼자 하는 여행은 자아성찰의 좋은 기회가 될 수 있어요.
T6-0516.x: Traveling alone can be a good opportunity for self-reflection.

T6-0517.ex: 노년의 시인은 삶을 담담하게 관조하는 시를 썼어요.
T6-0517.x: In old age, the poet wrote poems calmly contemplating life.
T6-0517.e: Literally 'view and illuminate': quiet, detached gazing.

T6-0518.ex: 불교에서는 집착을 버려야 해탈에 이를 수 있다고 해요.
T6-0518.x: Buddhism teaches that you must let go of attachment to reach liberation.
T6-0518.e: Literally 'untie and escape': freedom from the cycle of rebirth.

T6-0519.m: nirvana; death of the Buddha or a great monk
T6-0519.ex: 부처는 여든 살에 열반에 들었다고 전해집니다.
T6-0519.x: The Buddha is said to have entered nirvana at the age of eighty.
T6-0519.e: A sound transliteration of Sanskrit 'nirvana', so the syllables themselves carry no meaning.
T6-0519.t: 열반에 들다 is also a respectful way to say a revered monk has passed away.

T6-0520.x: Both Buddhism and Hinduism believe in reincarnation.
T6-0520.e: Literally 'wheel turning': life and death spinning round and round.

T6-0521.ex: 사람들은 그의 불행을 지난 잘못의 업보라고 말했어요.
T6-0521.x: People said his misfortune was karma for his past wrongs.
T6-0521.e: Literally 'deeds repaid'; 업 is the Buddhist word for karma.
T6-0521.t: In everyday talk, 자업자득 or 인과응보 are common ways to say 'you reap what you sow'.

T6-0522.ex: 부처님의 자비는 모든 생명에게 미친다고 해요.
T6-0522.x: The Buddha's compassion is said to reach all living beings.
T6-0522.e: Literally 'loving-kindness and sorrow': sharing others' joy and pain.
T6-0522.t: A homonym 자비 means 'one's own expense', as in 자비로 출판하다 (to self-publish).

T6-0523.ex: 스님은 보시가 마음을 나누는 일이라고 말씀하셨어요.
T6-0523.x: The monk said that almsgiving is a way of sharing your heart.
T6-0523.e: Literally 'spreading and giving'; this first syllable is usually read 포, as in 포교.

T6-0524.ex: 그는 산속 절에서 십 년 동안 수도를 했어요.
T6-0524.x: He practiced spiritual discipline at a mountain temple for ten years.
T6-0524.t: Watch the homonyms: 수도 also means 'capital city' and 'water supply', which are far more common.

T6-0525.ex: 수도승들은 새벽마다 함께 모여 기도를 드려요.
T6-0525.x: The monks gather together every dawn to pray.
T6-0525.e: Literally 'Way-cultivating monk'; used for monks of any religion.
T6-0525.t: For Korean Buddhist monks, people normally say 스님 rather than 수도승.

T6-0526.ex: 그 수녀는 평생 가난한 아이들을 돌보며 살았어요.
T6-0526.x: That nun spent her whole life caring for poor children.
T6-0526.e: Literally 'cultivating woman'; 녀 becomes 여 at the start of a word, as in 여자.
T6-0526.t: Address a nun as 수녀님, with the honorific -님.

T6-0527.ex: 법당에 들어갈 때는 신발을 벗어야 해요.
T6-0527.x: You have to take off your shoes when you enter the temple hall.
T6-0527.e: Literally 'dharma hall': where the Buddha's teaching is given.

T6-0528.ex: 성서는 세계에서 가장 많이 번역된 책이에요.
T6-0528.x: The Bible is the most translated book in the world.
T6-0528.t: In daily speech 성경 is more common; 성서 sounds more formal or academic.

T6-0529.ex: 코란은 이슬람교의 경전으로 아랍어로 쓰여 있어요.
T6-0529.x: The Quran is the scripture of Islam and is written in Arabic.
T6-0529.e: From English 'Koran' (Arabic 'Qur'an'); the newer spelling 꾸란 is closer to Arabic.

T6-0530.ex: 각 종교는 서로 다른 교리를 가지고 있어요.
T6-0530.x: Each religion has its own doctrines.

T6-0531.ex: 그 교단은 전국에서 수백 개의 교회를 운영합니다.
T6-0531.x: That religious body runs hundreds of churches nationwide.
T6-0531.t: Don't confuse with the homonym in 교단에 서다, 'to stand at the lectern', meaning to work as a teacher.

T6-0532.ex: 개신교에는 장로교, 감리교 같은 여러 교파가 있어요.
T6-0532.x: Protestantism has many denominations, such as Presbyterian and Methodist.
T6-0532.e: Literally 'religion branch'; -파 = faction or school: 보수파, 인상파.

T6-0533.ex: 불교에도 여러 종파가 있어서 수행 방법이 조금씩 달라요.
T6-0533.x: Buddhism also has several sects, so their practices differ slightly.
T6-0533.t: 종파 is common for Buddhism and Islam, while 교파 is the usual word for Christian denominations.

T6-0534.ex: 중세 교회는 새로운 사상을 이단으로 몰기도 했어요.
T6-0534.x: The medieval church sometimes branded new ideas as heresy.
T6-0534.e: Literally 'a different end': straying from the main line.
T6-0534.t: In Korea, 이단 often refers to controversial new religious groups that mainstream churches reject.

T6-0535.ex: 사이비 종교에 빠져 재산을 모두 잃은 사람도 있어요.
T6-0535.x: Some people have lost everything after getting caught up in a cult.
T6-0535.e: Literally 'looks like it, and yet isn't'; from a saying in Mencius.
T6-0535.t: Works like a prefix: 사이비 종교 (cult), 사이비 의사 (quack doctor), 사이비 기자 (fake journalist).

T6-0536.x: My grandmother is very devout and prays every day.
T6-0536.t: The usual collocation is 신앙심이 깊다 (to be devout).

T6-0537.x: Many believers gathered at the church on Easter.

T6-0538.ex: 그 목회자는 지역 사회를 위해 봉사 활동을 많이 해요.
T6-0538.x: That pastor does a lot of volunteer work for the local community.
T6-0538.e: Literally 'one who shepherds the congregation'; -자 = person: 과학자, 운전자.
T6-0538.t: 목사 is the title (목사님); 목회자 is the broader, more formal word for clergy.

T6-0539.ex: 그는 아프리카에서 이십 년 동안 선교 활동을 했어요.
T6-0539.x: He did missionary work in Africa for twenty years.
T6-0539.t: 선교 is used mainly for Christianity; for Buddhism, 포교 is the usual word.

T6-0540.ex: 그 스님은 해외 포교를 위해 미국으로 떠났어요.
T6-0540.x: The monk left for America to spread Buddhism overseas.

T6-0541.ex: 길거리에서 전도하는 사람들을 자주 볼 수 있어요.
T6-0541.x: You can often see people evangelizing on the street.
T6-0541.e: Literally 'passing on the Way'; homonyms mean 'conduction' and 'tumbling over'.
T6-0541.t: 전도하다 usually means street or door-to-door evangelism, which is very visible in Korea.

T6-0542.ex: 그는 결혼 후 아내의 종교로 개종했어요.
T6-0542.x: After getting married, he converted to his wife's religion.
T6-0542.t: Pattern: [religion]으로 개종하다, e.g. 불교로 개종하다 (to convert to Buddhism).

T6-0543.ex: 아기는 다음 주 일요일에 성당에서 세례를 받을 거예요.
T6-0543.x: The baby will be baptized at the Catholic church next Sunday.
T6-0543.t: Also figurative: 질문 세례를 받다 means 'to face a barrage of questions'.

T6-0544.ex: 아이들은 식사 전에 짧은 기도문을 외웠어요.
T6-0544.x: The children recited a short prayer before the meal.

T6-0545.ex: 예배가 시작되자 신도들이 함께 찬송을 불렀어요.
T6-0545.x: When the service began, the congregation sang a hymn together.
T6-0545.t: 찬송가 is the hymn or hymnbook itself; 찬송 can also mean the act of praising.

T6-0546.ex: 많은 사람들이 종교에서 영혼의 구원을 찾아요.
T6-0546.x: Many people seek salvation for their souls in religion.
T6-0546.t: A homonym 구원 means 'an old grudge', as in 구원을 풀다; context tells them apart.

T6-0547.ex: 그는 평생 봉사하며 자신의 잘못을 속죄했어요.
T6-0547.x: He atoned for his wrongdoing by serving others his whole life.
T6-0547.e: Literally 'buying back a sin' — paying off a wrong.
T6-0547.t: Usually used as 속죄하다, often with 죄를 or 잘못을 as the object.

T6-0548.ex: 기독교에서는 인간이 원죄를 안고 태어난다고 봐요.
T6-0548.x: Christianity holds that humans are born carrying original sin.

T6-0549.ex: 할머니는 돌아가신 할아버지가 극락에 가셨다고 믿으세요.
T6-0549.x: Grandma believes our late grandfather went to paradise.
T6-0549.e: Literally 'utmost joy' — the Buddhist land of perfect happiness.
T6-0549.t: Pronounced [긍낙] — nasalization; 극락 is Buddhist, while Christians say 천국.

T6-0550.ex: 많은 종교가 내세에 대한 믿음을 가지고 있어요.
T6-0550.x: Many religions hold a belief in the afterlife.

T6-0551.m: this world, this life, the present world
T6-0551.ex: 그 종교는 내세보다 현세의 행복을 더 중요하게 여겨요.
T6-0551.x: That religion values happiness in this life more than the afterlife.
T6-0551.t: Formal word; in everyday speech people say 이승 (this world) versus 저승 (the next).

T6-0552.ex: 옛날 황제들은 영생을 얻으려고 불로초를 찾았어요.
T6-0552.x: Ancient emperors searched for the herb of immortality to gain eternal life.

T6-0553.x: Easter is the day that celebrates the resurrection of Jesus.
T6-0553.t: Also used for comebacks: 그 브랜드가 부활했어요 means the brand made a comeback.

T6-0554.ex: 그는 꿈에서 신의 계시를 받았다고 주장했어요.
T6-0554.x: He claimed he received a revelation from God in a dream.
T6-0554.e: Literally 'opening up and showing' — a truth disclosed from above.

T6-0555.ex: 그 예언자는 큰 홍수가 올 거라고 경고했어요.
T6-0555.x: The prophet warned that a great flood would come.
T6-0555.e: Literally 'a person who speaks beforehand'. -자 = person: 과학자, 운전자.

T6-0556.ex: 고대 그리스 사람들은 델포이에서 신탁을 들었어요.
T6-0556.x: The ancient Greeks heard oracles at Delphi.
T6-0556.e: Literally 'what a god entrusts' to people.
T6-0556.t: Homonym warning: 신탁 also means a financial trust (신탁 회사), written with different hanja.

T6-0557.ex: 그 배우는 신비주의 전략으로 사생활을 공개하지 않아요.
T6-0557.x: That actor keeps their private life hidden as a strategy of mystique.
T6-0557.t: In K-pop and celebrity news, 신비주의 means deliberately keeping a mysterious, private image.

T6-0558.x: The Korean gut is a representative ritual of shamanism.
T6-0558.e: From English 'shamanism'; the Sino-Korean term for Korean shamanism is 무속.

T6-0559.ex: 무속은 오랫동안 한국인의 생활 속에 남아 있었어요.
T6-0559.x: Shamanism has long remained part of Korean daily life.

T6-0560.ex: 마을 입구의 장승은 토속신앙과 관련이 있어요.
T6-0560.x: The totem poles at the village entrance are tied to folk religion.
T6-0560.e: Literally 'local-custom faith' — beliefs rooted in the land.
T6-0560.t: Pronounced [토속씨낭] — ㅅ tenses after ㄱ, and ㄴ links into 앙.

T6-0561.x: Jesa ancestral rites began from the tradition of ancestor worship.

T6-0562.ex: 조선 시대에는 유학이 나라의 중심 사상이었어요.
T6-0562.x: In the Joseon era, Confucianism was the nation's central ideology.
T6-0562.t: Don't confuse it with 유학 (studying abroad); context usually makes it clear: 미국 유학 vs. 유학 사상.

T6-0563.x: Toegye Yi Hwang is a representative Neo-Confucian scholar of Joseon.
T6-0563.e: Literally 'study of human nature and principle'.
T6-0563.t: Pronounced [성니학] — ㄹ after ㅇ becomes ㄴ.

T6-0564.m: Silhak, the Practical Learning movement (late Joseon)
T6-0564.x: Jeong Yak-yong is a scholar who greatly developed Practical Learning.
T6-0564.e: Literally 'real learning' — scholarship aimed at practical problems, not abstract theory.

T6-0565.ex: 도교는 자연과 조화롭게 사는 것을 중요하게 생각해요.
T6-0565.x: Taoism considers living in harmony with nature important.

T6-0566.m: the philosophy of Laozi and Zhuangzi, Taoist thought
T6-0566.ex: 노장사상은 욕심을 버리고 자연을 따르라고 가르쳐요.
T6-0566.x: Taoist thought teaches us to let go of greed and follow nature.
T6-0566.e: 노 = Laozi and 장 = Zhuangzi, plus 사상 'thought'.

T6-0567.m: non-action and naturalness (Taoist ideal); living naturally without striving
T6-0567.ex: 그는 은퇴 후 시골에서 무위자연의 삶을 살고 있어요.
T6-0567.x: After retiring, he is living a simple, natural life in the countryside.
T6-0567.e: Literally 'without forced action, as things naturally are'.

T6-0568.m: benevolence, righteousness, propriety and wisdom (the four Confucian virtues)
T6-0568.ex: 옛 선비들은 인의예지를 가장 중요한 덕목으로 여겼어요.
T6-0568.x: Classical scholars regarded the four virtues as the most important.
T6-0568.e: Four virtues in one word; Seoul's gates 흥인지문, 돈의문, 숭례문 use three of them.
T6-0568.t: Pronounced [이늬예지]; in casual speech the 의 often sounds like [이].

T6-0569.m: the Three Bonds and Five Relationships (Confucian moral code)
T6-0569.x: The Three Bonds and Five Relationships were the basic ethics of Joseon society.
T6-0569.e: Literally 'three main ropes and five human relationships'.

T6-0570.ex: 이 마을은 예로부터 충효의 고장으로 유명해요.
T6-0570.x: This village has long been famous as a home of loyalty and filial piety.
T6-0570.e: Loyalty to the ruler plus devotion to parents.

T6-0571.x: The Analects says filial piety and brotherly respect are the root of benevolence.
T6-0571.e: Respect for parents plus respect for older siblings.

T6-0572.m: a man of virtue, a noble person (Confucian ideal)
T6-0572.ex: 군자는 어려울 때에도 예의를 지킨다고 해요.
T6-0572.x: It is said that a person of virtue keeps their manners even in hard times.
T6-0572.e: Literally 'a lord's son' — later, anyone noble in character.
T6-0572.t: Common in sayings like 군자는 말이 적다; the opposite is 소인 or 소인배.

T6-0573.ex: 작은 일에 화를 내면 소인배라는 말을 들을 수 있어요.
T6-0573.x: If you get angry over small things, people may call you petty.
T6-0573.e: Literally 'the small-person crowd' — opposite of the virtuous 군자.
T6-0573.t: Common insult for petty behavior; the playful slang opposite is 대인배 (a magnanimous person).

T6-0574.m: the scholar's spirit (integrity, frugality and principle of Joseon scholars)
T6-0574.ex: 그는 가난해도 정직하게 사는 선비정신을 지켰어요.
T6-0574.x: He kept the scholar's spirit of living honestly even in poverty.

T6-0575.m: contentment in poverty, finding joy in the right way despite being poor
T6-0575.x: The poet sang of a life content in poverty.
T6-0575.e: Literally 'at ease in poverty, enjoying the Way'.
T6-0575.t: Pronounced [안빈낙또]; a common theme in classical Korean poetry (시조, 가사).

T6-0576.m: cultivating oneself and managing one's family (first steps of good leadership)
T6-0576.ex: 수신제가도 못 하면서 나라를 다스리겠다는 거예요?
T6-0576.x: You can't even manage yourself and your family, and you want to run the country?
T6-0576.e: From the saying 수신제가치국평천하: self, family, state, then the world.
T6-0576.t: Often used to criticize leaders whose family or personal life is a mess.

T6-0577.ex: 어릴 때의 기억이 잠재의식 속에 남아 있을 수 있어요.
T6-0577.x: Childhood memories can remain in the subconscious.

T6-0578.ex: 사춘기에는 자의식이 강해져서 남의 시선을 신경 써요.
T6-0578.x: In puberty, self-consciousness grows and teens worry about how others see them.
T6-0578.t: 자의식 과잉 is a common phrase for someone who thinks everyone is watching them.

T6-0579.ex: 프로이트는 초자아가 도덕적인 판단을 한다고 설명했어요.
T6-0579.x: Freud explained that the superego makes moral judgments.
T6-0579.e: Literally 'the self above the self' — a direct translation of 'superego'.

T6-0580.ex: 프로이트는 리비도를 인간 행동의 중요한 에너지로 보았어요.
T6-0580.x: Freud saw libido as an important energy behind human behavior.
T6-0580.e: From Latin/English 'libido'; Korean uses it mostly in psychology, less in casual talk.

T6-0581.ex: 이 약은 염증을 억제하는 효과가 있어요.
T6-0581.x: This medicine has the effect of suppressing inflammation.
T6-0581.t: Used in medicine and economics too: 물가 억제 (curbing prices), 식욕 억제제 (appetite suppressant).

T6-0582.m: sublimation (psychology, chemistry); turning something into a higher form
T6-0582.x: He sublimated his sorrow into art.
T6-0582.t: Common pattern: A를 B(으)로 승화시키다 — to transform A into B.

T6-0583.ex: 남을 탓하는 것은 자기 감정의 투사일 수 있어요.
T6-0583.x: Blaming others may be a projection of your own feelings.
T6-0583.e: Literally 'throwing and shooting out' your feelings onto others.
T6-0583.t: Homonym warning: 투사 also means 'fighter' (e.g. 독립 투사, independence fighter).

T6-0584.x: Brushing things off with jokes is also a kind of defense mechanism.

T6-0585.ex: 동생이 태어나자 아이에게 퇴행 행동이 나타났어요.
T6-0585.x: When the baby sibling was born, the child showed regressive behavior.

T6-0586.ex: 사고 이후 그는 외상후스트레스장애로 치료를 받고 있어요.
T6-0586.x: Since the accident, he has been receiving treatment for PTSD.
T6-0586.t: In speech, people usually just say PTSD [피티에스디] or 트라우마.

T6-0587.ex: 완벽해야 한다는 강박관념 때문에 늘 피곤해요.
T6-0587.x: I'm always tired because of my obsession with being perfect.
T6-0587.e: Literally 'a thought that forces and presses on you'.

T6-0588.ex: 그는 문을 여러 번 확인하는 강박증이 있어요.
T6-0588.x: He has an obsessive habit of checking the door many times.

T6-0589.ex: 그는 누군가 자기를 감시한다는 편집증에 시달렸어요.
T6-0589.x: He suffered from paranoia that someone was watching him.
T6-0589.t: Don't confuse it with 편집 (editing); 편집증 always means paranoia.

T6-0590.ex: 고열 때문에 환각을 보는 경우도 있어요.
T6-0590.x: Sometimes people see hallucinations because of a high fever.

T6-0591.ex: 밤새 잠을 못 자서 환청이 들리는 것 같아요.
T6-0591.x: I haven't slept all night, so I think I'm hearing things.
T6-0591.t: Used with 들리다: 환청이 들리다 (to hear voices); jokingly said when you think you misheard.

T6-0592.ex: 조현병은 꾸준히 치료하면 증상을 관리할 수 있어요.
T6-0592.x: Schizophrenia symptoms can be managed with consistent treatment.
T6-0592.e: Literally 'tuning-string illness' — the mind as an instrument out of tune.
T6-0592.t: Since 2011 조현병 has replaced the stigmatizing older term 정신분열증.

T6-0593.x: With bipolar disorder, your mood swings to extremes.
T6-0593.t: Pronounced [조울쯩]; casually people may say 조울증 같아 about mood swings, but it can sound insensitive.

T6-0594.x: Medication is important in treating bipolar disorder.

T6-0595.ex: 불안장애가 있는 사람은 작은 일에도 크게 걱정해요.
T6-0595.x: People with anxiety disorders worry a lot even about small things.

T6-0596.m: anthropophobia, fear of people, avoiding social contact
T6-0596.ex: 그는 대인기피증 때문에 몇 달 동안 집 밖에 안 나갔어요.
T6-0596.x: Because of his fear of people, he didn't leave the house for months.
T6-0596.e: Literally 'condition of shunning and avoiding face-to-face people'.
T6-0596.t: Often used loosely in daily talk for 'I just don't want to see anyone right now'.

T6-0597.ex: 사회공포증이 있으면 사람들 앞에서 말하기가 힘들어요.
T6-0597.x: With social anxiety, it's hard to speak in front of people.

T6-0598.x: I can't ride elevators because of my claustrophobia.

T6-0599.m: mysophobia, compulsive cleanliness, being a neat freak
T6-0599.ex: 제 룸메이트는 결벽증이 있어서 하루에 세 번 청소해요.
T6-0599.x: My roommate is a neat freak and cleans three times a day.
T6-0599.t: Very common in casual speech for a neat freak, not only a medical diagnosis.

T6-0600.ex: 기면증이 있으면 낮에도 갑자기 잠이 들어요.
T6-0600.x: With narcolepsy, you suddenly fall asleep even during the day.

T6-0601.ex: 무리한 다이어트가 거식증으로 이어질 수 있어요.
T6-0601.x: Extreme dieting can lead to anorexia.
T6-0601.t: Pronounced [거식쯩]; its counterpart is 폭식증, and both fall under 식이장애.

T6-0602.x: My binge eating gets worse when I'm stressed.

T6-0603.ex: 자폐증이 있는 아이들은 특별한 재능을 보이기도 해요.
T6-0603.x: Children with autism sometimes show special talents.
T6-0603.t: In formal or medical contexts, 자폐 스펙트럼 장애 is now preferred.

T6-0604.ex: 주의력결핍 과잉행동 장애는 줄여서 ADHD라고 해요.
T6-0604.x: Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder is called ADHD for short.

T6-0605.x: If a child's hyperactivity is severe, consult a specialist.

T6-0606.ex: 나이가 들면 인지능력이 조금씩 떨어질 수 있어요.
T6-0606.x: As we age, cognitive ability can gradually decline.
T6-0606.t: Pronounced [인지능녁] — ㄹ becomes ㄴ after ㅇ.

T6-0607.ex: 담배가 해롭다는 걸 알면서 피우는 것은 인지부조화예요.
T6-0607.x: Smoking while knowing it's harmful is cognitive dissonance.

T6-0608.x: Cognitive behavioral therapy is effective for treating depression.

T6-0609.ex: 사람마다 색에 대한 지각이 조금씩 달라요.
T6-0609.x: Each person's perception of color is slightly different.
T6-0609.t: Homonym: 지각 'being late' is far more common in daily life — 학교에 지각했어요.

T6-0610.ex: 두 선의 길이가 다르게 보이는 건 착시 때문이에요.
T6-0610.x: The two lines look different in length because of an optical illusion.

T6-0611.ex: 그는 성정이 온화해서 화를 잘 내지 않아요.
T6-0611.x: He has a gentle nature, so he rarely gets angry.

T6-0612.ex: 그 아이는 심성이 착해서 친구들을 잘 도와줘요.
T6-0612.x: That child has a kind heart and helps friends a lot.
T6-0612.e: Literally 'heart nature' — who you are deep inside.
T6-0612.t: Usually paired with 착하다 or 곱다: 심성이 착하다, 심성이 곱다.

T6-0613.ex: 좋은 품성은 어릴 때부터 길러야 해요.
T6-0613.x: Good character should be cultivated from childhood.

T6-0614.m: shame, feeling ashamed of oneself, self-reproach
T6-0614.x: I feel ashamed of myself for repeating the same mistake.
T6-0614.e: Literally 'feeling ashamed of oneself'. -감 = feeling: 무력감, 자책감.
T6-0614.t: Used with 들다 or 느끼다: 자괴감이 들다 is the most natural pattern.

T6-0615.forms: 상대적 박탈감을 느끼다 · 상대적 박탈감이 들다
T6-0615.m: relative deprivation, feeling left behind compared to others
T6-0615.ex: 친구들이 집을 사는 걸 보니 상대적 박탈감을 느껴요.
T6-0615.x: Seeing my friends buy homes makes me feel relatively deprived.
T6-0615.e: 상대적 'relative' + 박탈감 'feeling of being stripped of something'.
T6-0615.t: Very common in news and social media about wealth gaps, housing prices and social comparison.

T6-0616.ex: 아무것도 할 수 없다는 무력감에 빠졌어요.
T6-0616.x: I sank into a sense of helplessness, feeling I couldn't do anything.
T6-0616.t: Pronounced [무력깜]; often with 빠지다 or 느끼다.

T6-0617.ex: 그는 사고가 자기 탓이라는 자책감에 시달렸어요.
T6-0617.x: He was tormented by guilt, believing the accident was his fault.

T6-0618.m: humiliation, feeling insulted or looked down on
T6-0618.ex: 사람들 앞에서 무시를 당해서 모멸감을 느꼈어요.
T6-0618.x: I felt humiliated after being ignored in front of people.

T6-0619.ex: 큰 점수 차로 지고 나서 굴욕감을 느꼈어요.
T6-0619.x: We felt humiliated after losing by a huge margin.
T6-0619.e: Literally 'feeling of being bent and disgraced'.
T6-0619.t: 모멸감 stresses being looked down on; 굴욕감 stresses being forced to submit or losing face.

T6-0620.m: sense of incongruity, feeling out of place, discomfort
T6-0620.ex: 비싼 차를 자랑하면 주변 사람들에게 위화감을 줄 수 있어요.
T6-0620.x: Showing off an expensive car can make people around you feel uncomfortable.
T6-0620.t: Common pattern: 위화감을 주다/조성하다 — often about wealth gaps causing social friction.

T6-0621.m: sense of difference, feeling of foreignness
T6-0621.ex: 외국에서 오래 살다 와서 한국 문화에 이질감을 느꼈어요.
T6-0621.x: After living abroad for a long time, I felt Korean culture was foreign to me.
T6-0621.e: Literally 'feeling that the quality is different'.

T6-0622.m: sense of disconnect, gap between expectation and reality
T6-0622.ex: 이상과 현실 사이에서 괴리감을 느낄 때가 많아요.
T6-0622.x: I often feel a gap between my ideals and reality.
T6-0622.t: Common pattern: A와 B 사이의 괴리감 — the gap between A and B.

T6-0623.ex: 전쟁 후에도 두 나라 사이의 적개심은 쉽게 사라지지 않았어요.
T6-0623.x: Even after the war, hostility between the two countries didn't easily disappear.
T6-0623.e: Literally 'rage toward an enemy in one's heart'.

T6-0624.ex: 폭력적인 장면은 많은 사람에게 혐오감을 줘요.
T6-0624.x: Violent scenes cause disgust in many people.
T6-0624.t: 혐오 is common in social debates: 혐오 표현 means hate speech.

T6-0625.x: Seeing my friend's success, I started to feel envious.
T6-0625.t: 시기심 is spiteful envy; 부러움 is harmless, often admiring envy.

T6-0626.m: desire for fame and credit, ambition for glory
T6-0626.ex: 그는 공명심 때문에 무리하게 일을 추진했습니다.
T6-0626.x: He pushed the project too hard out of a desire for glory.
T6-0626.e: Literally 'a heart set on merit and a name.'
T6-0626.t: Usually negative: it suggests chasing credit rather than doing the right thing.

T6-0627.m: desire for honor, thirst for fame
T6-0627.ex: 명예욕이 강한 사람은 남의 평가에 민감해요.
T6-0627.x: People with a strong desire for honor are sensitive to how others judge them.
T6-0627.e: -욕 = a craving for something: 명예욕, 물욕, 소유욕.

T6-0628.m: lust for power, desire for power
T6-0628.ex: 권력욕에 사로잡힌 정치인은 결국 신뢰를 잃었습니다.
T6-0628.x: The politician consumed by a lust for power eventually lost the public's trust.
T6-0628.t: Pronounced [궐려굑]: ㄴ before ㄹ becomes ㄹ, then ㄱ links to 욕.

T6-0629.x: He has no desire for material things, so he lives simply.
T6-0629.t: Pronounced [물룍]: an ㄴ sound is inserted before 욕 and then becomes ㄹ after the ㄹ.

T6-0630.ex: 스트레스가 심하면 성욕이 줄어들 수 있습니다.
T6-0630.x: Severe stress can reduce sexual desire.

T6-0631.ex: 연인에게 지나친 소유욕을 보이면 관계가 힘들어져요.
T6-0631.x: Being overly possessive of your partner makes the relationship hard.
T6-0631.t: Used for both things and people; with people it means controlling possessiveness.

T6-0632.m: urge to show off, desire to flaunt
T6-0632.ex: 비싼 차를 산 건 과시욕 때문이었어요.
T6-0632.x: Buying the expensive car was just about wanting to show off.

T6-0633.x: That athlete has a really strong will to win.
T6-0633.t: Often a compliment: 승부욕이 강하다 means 'very competitive.'

T6-0634.forms: 내적 동기가 강하다 · 내적 동기를 부여하다
T6-0634.ex: 내적 동기가 있으면 공부를 오래 계속할 수 있어요.
T6-0634.x: If you have intrinsic motivation, you can keep studying for a long time.
T6-0634.t: Pronounced [내쩍 똥기]; -적 turns nouns into adjectives like '-al'.

T6-0635.forms: 외적 동기가 되다 · 외적 동기를 주다
T6-0635.ex: 돈이나 칭찬 같은 보상은 외적 동기에 해당합니다.
T6-0635.x: Rewards like money or praise count as extrinsic motivation.

T6-0636.m: compensatory mindset, urge to make up for something
T6-0636.ex: 야근을 많이 한 날에는 보상심리로 쇼핑을 하게 돼요.
T6-0636.x: On days I work late, I end up shopping to make up for it.
T6-0636.t: Pronounced [보상심니] — ㄹ after ㅁ becomes ㄴ.

T6-0637.ex: 그는 피해의식이 심해서 농담도 공격으로 받아들여요.
T6-0637.x: He has such a victim mentality that he takes even jokes as attacks.

T6-0638.ex: 자기가 천재라고 믿는 건 과대망상일 수도 있어요.
T6-0638.x: Believing you're a genius might be a delusion of grandeur.

T6-0639.x: Some argue that social media feeds narcissism.
T6-0639.e: From English 'narcissism'; the many ㅡ vowels break up the English consonant clusters.

T6-0640.ex: 적당한 자기애는 정신 건강에 도움이 돼요.
T6-0640.x: A healthy amount of self-love is good for your mental health.
T6-0640.t: Neutral or positive in everyday talk, unlike English 'narcissism.'

T6-0642.ex: 주인공에게 감정이입이 돼서 영화를 보며 울었어요.
T6-0642.x: I identified so much with the main character that I cried during the movie.
T6-0642.t: Common pattern: (누구에게) 감정이입이 되다 — to get emotionally drawn into someone.

T6-0643.ex: 슬픈 영화를 보고 나면 카타르시스를 느껴요.
T6-0643.x: I feel a sense of catharsis after watching a sad movie.

T6-0644.ex: 그는 밤새 번민에 잠겨 잠을 이루지 못했습니다.
T6-0644.x: He was lost in anguish all night and couldn't sleep.
T6-0644.t: Literary; in conversation people say 고민.

T6-0645.m: worldly anguish, earthly desires and suffering
T6-0645.x: The monk told us to let go of the anguish in our hearts.
T6-0645.e: A Buddhist term: the mental passions that cause suffering.
T6-0645.t: Buddhism counts 108 번뇌, which is why prayer beads have 108 beads and people do 108 bows (108배).

T6-0646.ex: 그 결정에는 오랜 고뇌가 담겨 있었습니다.
T6-0646.x: That decision came out of long anguish.

T6-0647.ex: 그 소설은 이민자의 비애를 잘 그렸어요.
T6-0647.x: That novel captures the sorrow of immigrants well.
T6-0647.t: Often in 'X의 비애' for the sad lot of a group, e.g. 직장인의 비애.

T6-0648.x: You can feel the melancholy of autumn in that song.
T6-0648.e: Literally 'grief and sorrow' — a gentle, lingering sadness.

T6-0649.x: The families fell into grief at the news of the accident.
T6-0649.t: Typical collocation: 비탄에 빠지다 / 잠기다 — to sink into grief.

T6-0650.ex: 할머니는 지난 세월을 회한에 젖어 이야기하셨어요.
T6-0650.x: Grandma talked about the past years, full of regret.

T6-0651.m: joys and sorrows, ups and downs of life
T6-0651.ex: 이 영화는 서민들의 애환을 담고 있습니다.
T6-0651.x: This film captures the joys and sorrows of ordinary people.
T6-0651.t: Collocates with 담다 and 서민, 직장인: the everyday struggles of a group.

T6-0653.m: to be deeply regrettable, full of sorrow and resentment
T6-0653.x: I deeply regret never having taken good care of my mother.
T6-0653.e: 한 'deep sorrow' + -스럽다 'feeling like': feeling full of han.

T6-0654.ex: 나이가 들수록 혼자인 게 서글플 때가 있어요.
T6-0654.x: The older I get, sometimes being alone feels sad.
T6-0654.e: Related to 슬프다 'sad': a quieter, lonelier kind of sadness.

T6-0655.ex: 비 오는 날 혼자 앉아 있는 그의 모습이 처연했어요.
T6-0655.x: The sight of him sitting alone on the rainy day was heartbreaking.
T6-0655.e: Literally 'in a sorrowful state'; mostly literary.
T6-0655.t: Literary: usually describes a scene, look or atmosphere rather than your own feelings.

T6-0656.m: to be heartrending, poignant, achingly sad
T6-0656.x: The song longing for someone who left is heartbreaking.
T6-0656.e: Probably from 애 'insides, heart' (as in 애타다) + 닳다 'wear away': heart-wearing sadness.

T6-0657.ex: 밤에 들리는 피리 소리가 너무 구슬퍼요.
T6-0657.x: The sound of the flute at night is so mournful.
T6-0657.e: Contains 슬프다 'sad'; used mainly for sounds like songs, cries or rain.
T6-0657.t: Typically describes sounds: 구슬픈 노래, 구슬픈 목소리, 구슬프게 울다.

T6-0658.ex: 오랫동안 준비한 일이 하루아침에 끝나서 허망해요.
T6-0658.x: Something I prepared for so long ended overnight, and it feels so empty.

T6-0659.ex: 돌이켜 보면 젊은 시절은 참 덧없이 지나갔어요.
T6-0659.x: Looking back, my younger days really slipped by so fleetingly.
T6-0659.e: 덧 'a brief moment' + 없다 'not exist': gone before you know it.
T6-0659.t: Pronounced [더덥따]; the adverb 덧없이 is very common with 흐르다, 지나가다.

T6-0660.x: The bereaved families held the funeral with grief-stricken hearts.
T6-0660.t: Formal and strong; common in news about deaths and disasters.

T6-0661.m: to be unsettled, troubled, restless in mind
T6-0661.ex: 이사 문제로 요즘 마음이 좀 심란해요.
T6-0661.x: I've been feeling pretty unsettled lately over the move.
T6-0661.t: Pronounced [심난하다] — ㄹ after ㅁ becomes ㄴ.

T6-0662.m: to be uneasy, unsettled; restless (of mood or atmosphere)
T6-0662.ex: 이상한 꿈을 꿔서 하루 종일 기분이 뒤숭숭했어요.
T6-0662.x: I had a weird dream, so I felt uneasy all day.
T6-0662.e: A mimetic word suggesting things jumbled and messy; also used for a tense social mood.
T6-0662.t: Common collocations: 꿈자리가 뒤숭숭하다 (bad dreams), 분위기가 뒤숭숭하다 (tense atmosphere).

T6-0663.m: to feel restless, fidgety, unable to settle (often from spring or excitement)
T6-0663.x: Now that spring's here, I feel restless for no reason.
T6-0663.e: Playful rhyming mimetic word; the bouncing sounds mirror a fluttering, unsettled heart.
T6-0663.t: Lighter than 뒤숭숭하다: often a pleasant, distracted restlessness, especially in spring.

T6-0664.m: to be on pins and needles, unable to keep still from anxiety
T6-0664.ex: 합격자 발표를 기다리면서 하루 종일 안절부절못했어요.
T6-0664.x: I was on pins and needles all day waiting for the list of who passed.
T6-0664.e: 안절부절 'fidgeting' + 못하다 'cannot': literally can't settle down.
T6-0664.t: Standard form is 안절부절못하다, not 안절부절하다; pronounced [안절부절모타다].

T6-0665.m: to be on edge, live in constant fear, tremble with worry
T6-0665.x: He lived in fear that his secret would come out.
T6-0665.e: A four-character idiom from classical poetry: 'trembling and cautious', as if on thin ice.
T6-0665.t: Often paired with -(으)ㄹ까 봐: 들킬까 봐 전전긍긍하다.

T6-0666.ex: 어머니는 아들이 다칠까 봐 늘 노심초사하셨어요.
T6-0666.x: Mom was always fretting that her son would get hurt.

T6-0667.m: to be tender and affectionate (with longing); touching, poignant
T6-0667.ex: 두 사람의 애틋한 사랑 이야기가 감동적이었어요.
T6-0667.x: The two people's tender love story was moving.
T6-0667.e: Probably from 애 'heart, insides' as in 애타다: love mixed with ache.
T6-0667.t: Pronounced [애트타다]; captures affection tinged with longing, often for family or distant lovers.

T6-0668.m: to be faint, hazy; wistfully dim (of memories)
T6-0668.x: Memories of my childhood come back faintly.
T6-0668.e: Native word for something blurry and far away, often with a nostalgic, bittersweet feel.
T6-0668.t: Common pattern: 아련한 추억 / 기억, 아련하게 떠오르다.

T6-0669.m: to be overwhelmed with emotion, deeply moved
T6-0669.x: Coming back to my hometown after 30 years, I'm overwhelmed with emotion.

T6-0670.x: I was puzzled when he suddenly acted nice.
T6-0670.t: For other people's reactions, use the verb 의아해하다: 그는 의아해했다.

T6-0671.m: to be embarrassed, perplexed, put on the spot
T6-0671.x: The minister looked put on the spot by the reporter's sudden question.

T6-0672.m: to be ashamed, embarrassed (to face someone)
T6-0672.ex: 도와주신 분께 연락을 못 드려서 면구스러워요.
T6-0672.x: I feel ashamed that I never got in touch with the person who helped me.
T6-0672.e: Hanja suggest a face that burns, as with shame; rather old-fashioned today.

T6-0673.m: to be sorry, feel deeply apologetic (very formal)
T6-0673.x: We sincerely apologize for the inconvenience.
T6-0673.e: Literally 'fearful and afraid' — humbly frightened at having troubled someone.
T6-0673.t: Very formal apology, used to superiors or in public statements; 송구합니다 is stronger than 죄송합니다.

T6-0674.m: to be humbled, overwhelmed with gratitude (by undeserved kindness)
T6-0674.x: I'm truly humbled that you would give me such a precious gift.
T6-0674.e: Literally 'awed and fearful' — overwhelmed by a superior's kindness.
T6-0674.t: Used toward elders or superiors; 황송하다 mixes gratitude with feeling unworthy.
rel: to be more than one deserves

T6-0675.x: I felt sheepish at the praise, so I just smiled.
T6-0675.e: Sino 겸연 + native -쩍다 'feeling like'; the variant 계면쩍다 is also standard and common in speech.
T6-0675.t: Pronounced [겨면쩍따]; common pattern: 겸연쩍게 웃다 — to smile sheepishly.

T6-0676.m: to be bitterly resentful (over an injustice), feel wronged
T6-0676.ex: 억울하게 누명을 쓰고 감옥에 가다니 정말 원통합니다.
T6-0676.x: Going to prison on a false charge is truly bitter and unjust.

T6-0677.m: to be hurtfully cold, unkind (making you feel let down)
T6-0677.x: I felt a little hurt that my friend forgot my birthday.
T6-0677.e: Hanja mean 'rustic, vulgar'; today it means feeling hurt by someone's coldness.
T6-0677.t: Pronounced [야소카다]; also for things like 야속한 세월 — time that cruelly flies.

T6-0678.m: pathology (the nature and causes of disease)
T6-0678.ex: 이 질환의 병리는 아직 완전히 밝혀지지 않았습니다.
T6-0678.x: The pathology of this disease has not yet been fully uncovered.
T6-0678.t: Pronounced [병니]; also used figuratively: 사회적 병리 현상 'social pathologies.'

T6-0679.ex: 그녀는 의대에서 병리학을 전공하고 대학 병원에서 일해요.
T6-0679.x: She majored in pathology in medical school and works at a university hospital.
T6-0679.e: -학 = field of study: 병리학, 역학, 심리학.

T6-0680.ex: 연구진은 새로운 병인을 찾기 위해 노력하고 있습니다.
T6-0680.x: The research team is working to find a new cause of the disease.

T6-0681.ex: 검사 결과 폐에서 작은 병변이 발견됐습니다.
T6-0681.x: The test found a small lesion in the lung.
T6-0681.e: Literally 'disease change' — tissue altered by illness.

T6-0682.ex: 의사는 수술로 병소를 완전히 제거했다고 말했습니다.
T6-0682.x: The doctor said the affected site had been completely removed in surgery.
T6-0682.e: Literally 'disease nest' — where the illness lives in the body.

T6-0683.m: patient's condition, state of an illness
T6-0683.x: Grandpa's condition suddenly got worse starting last night.

T6-0684.ex: 새 학기가 되면 새 학기 증후군을 겪는 학생이 많아요.
T6-0684.x: Lots of students go through 'new semester syndrome' when classes start.
T6-0684.e: Literally 'a group of symptoms and signs.'

T6-0685.ex: 담배를 끊으면 처음 며칠 동안 금단증상이 나타나요.
T6-0685.x: When you quit smoking, withdrawal symptoms appear for the first few days.

T6-0686.x: A headache can be a warning sign of a migraine.
T6-0686.t: Homonym warning: 전구 also means 'light bulb' (電球); context makes it clear.

T6-0687.x: The incubation period of this virus is usually about five days.

T6-0688.x: Regular exercise lowers the incidence of diabetes.
T6-0688.e: -률/-율 = rate: written 율 after a vowel or ㄴ (치사율), 률 elsewhere (발병률).

T6-0689.x: The prevalence of high blood pressure was high among the elderly.
T6-0689.t: 유병률 counts everyone who has the disease now; 발병률 counts only new cases.

T6-0690.x: This disease has a very high fatality rate.

T6-0691.ex: 의료 기술이 발달하면서 영아 사망률이 크게 줄었습니다.
T6-0691.x: As medical technology advanced, the infant mortality rate fell sharply.
T6-0691.t: 사망률 is deaths per whole population; 치사율 is deaths among those infected.

T6-0692.m: morbidity rate, rate of falling ill
T6-0692.ex: 겨울철에는 어린이들의 독감 이환율이 크게 높아집니다.
T6-0692.x: In winter, the rate of children catching the flu rises sharply.
T6-0692.e: Literally 'rate of being struck by illness.'

T6-0693.ex: 역학 전문가들이 감염 경로를 분석하고 있습니다.
T6-0693.x: Epidemiology experts are analyzing the routes of infection.
T6-0693.t: Homonym warning: 역학 (力學) also means 'mechanics/dynamics' in physics; pronounced [여칵].

T6-0694.ex: 보건 당국은 확진자의 동선에 대한 역학조사를 실시했습니다.
T6-0694.x: Health authorities carried out an epidemiological investigation into the patient's movements.

T6-0695.x: Malaria is an endemic disease in some tropical regions.
T6-0695.e: Literally 'wind-and-soil disease' — tied to a region's climate and land.
T6-0695.t: Pronounced [풍토뼝]; the -병 suffix is usually tensed.

T6-0696.ex: 옛날에는 유행병으로 많은 사람이 목숨을 잃었어요.
T6-0696.x: In the old days, many people lost their lives to epidemics.
T6-0696.e: Literally 'disease that is in fashion' — it spreads like a trend.

T6-0697.ex: 코로나19 대유행으로 세계 경제가 큰 타격을 입었습니다.
T6-0697.x: The COVID-19 pandemic dealt a heavy blow to the global economy.
T6-0697.e: Literally 'big spread'; also used for a massive fashion trend.

T6-0698.ex: 인구의 70% 이상이 백신을 맞아야 집단면역이 생깁니다.
T6-0698.x: More than 70% of the population must be vaccinated for herd immunity to form.

T6-0699.ex: 신속 항원 검사는 결과가 빨리 나와요.
T6-0699.x: Rapid antigen tests give results quickly.
T6-0699.e: Literally 'what the resistance originates from' — it triggers antibodies.
T6-0699.t: Easy to mix up: 항원 is the invader (antigen), 항체 is your defense (antibody).

T6-0700.ex: 면역결핍 환자는 작은 감염에도 위험할 수 있습니다.
T6-0700.x: Immunodeficient patients can be at risk from even minor infections.

T6-0701.x: Rheumatoid arthritis is a typical autoimmune disease.
T6-0701.e: Literally 'immunity against one's own house' — the body attacks itself.

T6-0702.ex: 손을 자주 씻으면 병원균의 전파를 막을 수 있어요.
T6-0702.x: Washing your hands often can stop the spread of germs.

T6-0703.ex: 바이러스와 세균은 질병을 일으키는 대표적인 병원체입니다.
T6-0703.x: Viruses and bacteria are typical pathogens that cause disease.
T6-0703.e: Literally 'the body that is the origin of disease'.

T6-0704.x: Athlete's foot is a skin disease caused by a fungus.
T6-0704.t: 진균 is the clinical term; in daily life people just say 곰팡이 (mold, fungus).

T6-0705.ex: 날고기를 먹으면 기생충에 감염될 수 있어요.
T6-0705.x: Eating raw meat can give you a parasite infection.
T6-0705.e: Literally 'a bug that lives lodged in another'.
T6-0705.t: Used figuratively for a freeloader who lives off others, as in the film 기생충 (Parasite, 2019).

T6-0706.m: host (organism a parasite or virus lives on)
T6-0706.ex: 이 바이러스는 박쥐를 숙주로 삼는 것으로 알려져 있습니다.
T6-0706.x: This virus is known to use bats as its host.
T6-0706.e: Literally 'the master of the lodging' — the one who houses the guest.
T6-0706.t: Don't confuse it with 숙주나물 (mung bean sprouts) — same sound, unrelated food word.

T6-0707.ex: 새로운 변종 바이러스가 빠르게 퍼지고 있습니다.
T6-0707.x: A new variant of the virus is spreading quickly.

T6-0708.x: The first antibiotic substance was discovered by chance in blue mold.
T6-0708.e: Literally 'substance against life' — it fights living microbes.
T6-0708.t: 항생물질 is the substance itself; the medicine you take is usually called 항생제.

T6-0709.ex: 의사가 무릎 통증 때문에 소염제를 처방해 줬어요.
T6-0709.x: The doctor prescribed an anti-inflammatory for my knee pain.
T6-0709.e: Literally 'drug that puts out inflammation'; -제 = medicine/agent: 진통제, 수면제.
T6-0709.t: Often paired as 소염진통제, a drug that both reduces inflammation and relieves pain.

T6-0710.x: An anesthetic was given to the patient before surgery.

T6-0711.x: This surgery is done under general anesthesia.
T6-0711.t: Say 전신마취를 하다 or 전신마취 상태에서; you 'wake up' from it with 마취에서 깨다.

T6-0712.ex: 간단한 수술이라서 전신마취 대신 국소마취만 했어요.
T6-0712.x: It was a simple procedure, so I only had local anesthesia instead of general.

T6-0713.x: The patient was so agitated that they gave him a sedative.
T6-0713.e: Literally 'drug that presses down and calms'.

T6-0714.ex: 그는 몇 달 동안 항우울제를 복용하고 있어요.
T6-0714.x: He has been taking antidepressants for several months.
T6-0714.e: Literally 'drug against gloom'; 항- = anti-: 항생제, 항암제.

T6-0715.ex: 이 약은 하루에 두 번 투여해야 합니다.
T6-0715.x: This drug must be administered twice a day.
T6-0715.e: Literally 'throw in and give' — putting a drug into the body.
T6-0715.t: 투여하다 is what medical staff do; the patient 복용하다 (takes) the medicine.

T6-0716.x: I was treated with an injection instead of pills.
T6-0716.e: Literally 'drug that is poured and shot in'.

T6-0717.ex: 동맥은 심장에서 몸 전체로 피를 보내요.
T6-0717.x: Arteries carry blood from the heart to the whole body.
T6-0717.e: Literally 'moving vessel' — you can feel it pulse.

T6-0718.x: The nurse gave an injection into a vein in my arm.
T6-0718.e: Literally 'quiet vessel' — no strong pulse, unlike an artery.

T6-0719.ex: 날씨가 추우면 피부 가까이에 있는 모세혈관이 수축합니다.
T6-0719.x: When the weather is cold, the capillaries near the skin contract.
T6-0719.e: Literally 'blood tubes as thin as hair'.

T6-0720.ex: 오래 앉아 있으면 다리에 혈전이 생길 수 있어요.
T6-0720.x: Sitting for a long time can cause blood clots in your legs.
T6-0720.e: Literally 'blood plug' — a clot that stoppers the vessel.
T6-0720.t: Don't confuse it with 혈전 meaning 'bloody battle' (血戰) — same sound, different word.

T6-0721.ex: 운전자의 혈중 알코올 농도가 기준을 넘었습니다.
T6-0721.x: The driver's blood alcohol level exceeded the limit.
T6-0721.e: Literally 'in the blood'; almost always before another noun.
T6-0721.t: Used like a prefix: 혈중 농도 (blood level), 혈중 콜레스테롤, 혈중 알코올 농도.

T6-0722.ex: 기름진 음식을 많이 먹으면 고지혈증에 걸리기 쉬워요.
T6-0722.x: Eating a lot of fatty food makes you prone to high cholesterol.

T6-0723.ex: 흡연은 동맥경화의 주요 원인 중 하나입니다.
T6-0723.x: Smoking is one of the main causes of hardening of the arteries.
T6-0723.e: Literally 'arteries becoming hard'; -화 = becoming: 노화, 경화.

T6-0724.x: My father was rushed to the emergency room with a heart attack.
T6-0724.e: Literally 'heart muscle blocked and stopped up'.
T6-0724.t: Everyday speech often says 심장마비 loosely, but 심근경색 is the precise medical term for a heart attack.

T6-0725.ex: 계단을 오를 때 가슴이 아프면 협심증을 의심해 봐야 해요.
T6-0725.x: If your chest hurts when climbing stairs, you should suspect angina.
T6-0725.e: Literally 'narrow-heart condition' — the heart's vessels narrow.

T6-0726.ex: 건강검진 때 받은 심전도 검사에서 부정맥이 발견되었습니다.
T6-0726.x: An arrhythmia was found on the ECG I had during my checkup.

T6-0727.x: My grandmother suddenly collapsed from a brain hemorrhage last month.
T6-0727.e: Literally 'blood coming out in the brain'.

T6-0728.x: The sooner a cerebral infarction is treated, the fewer the aftereffects.
T6-0728.e: Literally 'brain blocked up' — a vessel in the brain is clogged.

T6-0729.x: My grandfather was diagnosed with Alzheimer's last year.
T6-0729.e: From the German doctor's name Alzheimer; the German z sound becomes 츠.
T6-0729.t: Often said as 알츠하이머병 or 알츠하이머성 치매; 치매 is the general word for dementia.

T6-0730.ex: 파킨슨병에 걸리면 손이 떨리는 증상이 나타나요.
T6-0730.x: With Parkinson's disease, symptoms like trembling hands appear.
T6-0730.e: Named after English doctor James Parkinson, plus Korean -병 'disease'.

T6-0731.x: The patient was eventually declared brain-dead.

T6-0732.ex: 그는 사고 후 몇 년째 식물인간 상태로 지내고 있어요.
T6-0732.x: He has been in a vegetative state for years since the accident.
T6-0732.e: Literally 'plant person' — alive but without awareness.

T6-0733.ex: 교통사고 환자가 사흘째 혼수상태에 빠져 있어요.
T6-0733.x: The car accident victim has been in a coma for three days.
T6-0733.t: Collocations: 혼수상태에 빠지다 (fall into a coma), 혼수상태에서 깨어나다 (come out of a coma).

T6-0734.ex: 사고 직후 운전자는 의식불명 상태로 병원에 옮겨졌습니다.
T6-0734.x: Right after the accident, the driver was taken to the hospital unconscious.

T6-0735.ex: 이번 수술은 김 교수님이 직접 집도하셨어요.
T6-0735.x: Professor Kim personally performed this surgery.
T6-0735.t: Pronounced [집또]; used as 집도하다, mostly in news or formal speech.

T6-0736.x: The doctor made a small incision in the abdomen to operate.
T6-0736.t: Don't confuse with 절개 (節槪, integrity, loyalty) — same sound, used in old stories about virtue.

T6-0737.x: After the surgery, they stitched the wound closed.
T6-0737.t: In casual speech people say 꿰매다 (to stitch up); 봉합하다 is the medical word.

T6-0738.x: The doctor said the tumor was completely removed.
T6-0738.t: Homonym warning: 절제 (節制) also means self-control, as in 절제된 생활 (a disciplined life).

T6-0739.x: He waited three years to receive an organ transplant.
T6-0739.t: 장기 here (臟器) means organ, not 장기 'long-term' or the board game 장기.

T6-0740.x: He pledged to donate his organs after death.
T6-0740.t: 기증 is for things like organs, books or art; donating money is usually 기부.

T6-0741.ex: 정확한 진단을 위해 조직검사를 해야 합니다.
T6-0741.x: A biopsy is needed for an accurate diagnosis.

T6-0742.ex: 자기공명영상을 찍으면 뇌를 자세히 볼 수 있어요.
T6-0742.x: An MRI lets you see the brain in detail.
T6-0742.e: A word-for-word translation of 'magnetic resonance imaging'.
T6-0742.t: In real life almost everyone just says 엠알아이 (MRI); the full term appears in formal writing.

T6-0743.ex: 넘어져서 머리를 다쳐 응급실에서 컴퓨터단층촬영을 했어요.
T6-0743.x: I fell and hurt my head, so I had a CT scan in the emergency room.
T6-0743.t: People normally say 씨티 (CT) or 씨티를 찍다; the long form is used in documents.

T6-0744.m: reading, interpretation (of scans or test results)
T6-0744.ex: 영상 판독 결과는 다음 주에 나옵니다.
T6-0744.x: The results of the image reading will come out next week.

T6-0745.x: In the doctor's opinion, surgery isn't necessary.

T6-0746.m: doctor's note, medical opinion letter, referral
T6-0746.ex: 큰 병원에 가려면 동네 병원에서 소견서를 받아 오세요.
T6-0746.x: To go to a big hospital, get a referral letter from your local clinic.
T6-0746.e: Literally 'document of what was seen'; -서 = written document: 신청서, 계약서.
T6-0746.t: 진단서 officially certifies a diagnosis; 소견서 is the doctor's opinion, often used for referrals.

T6-0747.x: It was misdiagnosed as a simple cold, so treatment was delayed.

T6-0748.x: A medical dispute arose over side effects after the surgery.

T6-0749.ex: 이 신약은 현재 임상시험 단계에 있습니다.
T6-0749.x: This new drug is currently in the clinical trial stage.
T6-0749.t: 임상시험 is the officially preferred term today; 임상실험 sounds like experimenting on people.

T6-0750.ex: 그 회사는 동물 실험 후 임상실험을 시작했어요.
T6-0750.x: The company began clinical experiments after animal testing.
T6-0750.t: Still common in everyday speech, but officials and doctors prefer 임상시험.

T6-0751.ex: 참가자의 절반은 진짜 약 대신 위약을 먹었어요.
T6-0751.x: Half of the participants took a placebo instead of the real drug.
T6-0751.t: Homonym warning: 위약 (違約) also means breach of contract, as in 위약금 (cancellation fee).

T6-0752.ex: 가짜 약을 먹고 좋아졌다면 위약효과일 수도 있어요.
T6-0752.x: If you got better after taking a fake pill, it may be the placebo effect.
T6-0752.t: Pronounced [위야쿄과] — ㄱ and ㅎ merge into ㅋ.

T6-0753.x: The doctor used sugar pills as a placebo.
T6-0753.e: From English 'placebo'; in Korean it appears most often in 플라시보 효과.

T6-0754.ex: 조직검사 결과 그 혹은 악성종양으로 밝혀졌습니다.
T6-0754.x: The biopsy revealed that the lump was a malignant tumor.
T6-0754.t: Opposite: 양성종양 (benign tumor); 악성 also appears in 악성 댓글 (malicious online comments).

T6-0755.ex: 항암 치료 후 백혈병이 완전 관해 상태가 되었어요.
T6-0755.x: After chemotherapy, the leukemia went into complete remission.
T6-0755.e: Literally 'loosening and releasing' — the disease lets go.
T6-0755.t: 관해 is a technical term; patients more often hear 완치 (cure) or 재발 (relapse).

T6-0756.x: He was diagnosed with terminal cancer.

T6-0757.x: She was told she had six months to live.

T6-0758.ex: 아버지는 마지막 몇 주를 호스피스 병동에서 보내셨어요.
T6-0758.x: My father spent his last few weeks in a hospice ward.

T6-0759.ex: 완화의료는 환자의 고통을 줄이는 데 중점을 둡니다.
T6-0759.x: Palliative care focuses on reducing the patient's suffering.
T6-0759.e: Literally 'easing medical care' — soothing, not curing.

T6-0760.ex: 할머니는 연명치료를 원하지 않는다고 미리 밝히셨어요.
T6-0760.x: Grandma made it clear in advance that she didn't want life support.

T6-0761.x: Euthanasia is still illegal in many countries.
T6-0761.t: Pronounced [알락싸] — ㄴ becomes ㄹ next to ㄹ.

T6-0762.m: death with dignity (by stopping life support)
T6-0762.x: In Korea, death with dignity has been legally allowed since 2018.
T6-0762.t: In Korea, 존엄사 usually means refusing life support, unlike 안락사, which actively ends life.

T6-0763.x: I go to neurosurgery for my herniated disc.
T6-0763.e: Literally 'nerve surgery department'; -과 = hospital department: 내과, 안과.
T6-0763.t: Pronounced [신경외꽈]; 신경과 treats nerves with medicine, while 신경외과 operates.

T6-0764.x: I went to urology for a urination problem.
T6-0764.t: Officially renamed 비뇨의학과, but most people still say 비뇨기과.

T6-0765.ex: 침술은 한국 전통 의학의 중요한 치료법이에요.
T6-0765.x: Acupuncture is an important treatment in traditional Korean medicine.

T6-0766.ex: 어제 한의원에 가서 배에 뜸을 떴어요.
T6-0766.x: Yesterday I went to a Korean medicine clinic and had moxibustion on my stomach.
T6-0766.t: The verb is 뜸을 뜨다; 뜸을 들이다 means 'to let rice steam' or 'to hesitate before speaking'.

T6-0767.x: The Korean medicine doctor took my wrist and read my pulse.

T6-0768.m: qi and blood, vital energy and blood
T6-0768.ex: 한의학에서는 기혈 순환이 건강의 핵심이라고 봐요.
T6-0768.x: Korean medicine sees the circulation of qi and blood as the key to health.
T6-0768.e: Literally 'energy and blood' — the two flows of traditional medicine.

T6-0769.ex: 나이가 들면 신진대사가 느려져서 살이 찌기 쉬워요.
T6-0769.x: As you age, your metabolism slows, so it's easier to gain weight.

T6-0770.x: Belly fat is a warning sign of metabolic syndrome.
T6-0770.e: Literally 'a group of metabolic symptoms and signs'.

T6-0771.x: Hormone problems are treated in the endocrinology department.
T6-0771.e: Literally 'secreting inside' — hormones go into the blood.

T6-0772.ex: 이번 건강검진에서 갑상선에 작은 혹이 발견되었어요.
T6-0772.x: A small lump was found on my thyroid in this checkup.
T6-0772.t: Pronounced [갑쌍선]; the newer official term is 갑상샘, but 갑상선 is far more common.

T6-0773.ex: 췌장은 혈당을 조절하는 인슐린을 만드는 기관이에요.
T6-0773.x: The pancreas is the organ that makes insulin, which controls blood sugar.
T6-0773.e: Literally 'pancreas organ'; -장 = internal organ: 심장, 신장, 간장.

T6-0774.ex: 술을 많이 마시면 간장에 무리가 갑니다.
T6-0774.x: Drinking a lot puts strain on your liver.
T6-0774.t: Homonym warning: 간장 usually means soy sauce; for the organ, people normally just say 간.

T6-0775.ex: 신장 기능이 떨어져서 투석을 받고 있어요.
T6-0775.x: My kidney function has declined, so I'm getting dialysis.
T6-0775.t: Homonym warning: 신장 (身長) also means height; the native word for kidney is 콩팥.

T6-0776.ex: 그 환자는 교통사고로 비장이 파열되어 수술을 받았습니다.
T6-0776.x: The patient had surgery after his spleen ruptured in a car accident.
T6-0776.t: Homonym warning: 비장 also means 'secretly kept', as in 비장의 무기 (secret weapon).

T6-0777.x: I had surgery because gallstones formed in my gallbladder.
T6-0777.t: In everyday speech the native word 쓸개 is more common.

T6-0778.ex: 검사해 보니 위와 십이지장에 궤양이 있대요.
T6-0778.x: The tests showed I have ulcers in my stomach and duodenum.
T6-0778.e: Literally 'twelve-finger intestine' — about twelve finger-widths long.

T6-0779.ex: 50세가 넘으면 대장 내시경을 받는 게 좋아요.
T6-0779.x: After 50, it's good to get a colonoscopy.

T6-0780.x: I think some food is stuck in my esophagus.

T6-0781.ex: 기관지가 약해서 겨울마다 기침을 오래 해요.
T6-0781.x: My bronchial tubes are weak, so I cough for a long time every winter.
T6-0781.e: Literally 'branches of the air pipe' — the tubes that split off the windpipe.
T6-0781.t: 기관지염 (bronchitis) is the most common collocation you'll hear at a clinic.

T6-0782.ex: 결핵은 기침으로 전염될 수 있는 질병입니다.
T6-0782.x: Tuberculosis is a disease that can spread through coughing.
T6-0782.e: Literally 'knotted core' — named for the hard nodules it forms in the lungs.
T6-0782.t: Doctors often specify 폐결핵 (pulmonary TB), the most common form.

T6-0783.x: I got an ulcer in my mouth because of stress.

T6-0784.ex: 아버지는 위궤양 때문에 매운 음식을 못 드세요.
T6-0784.x: My father can't eat spicy food because of his stomach ulcer.
T6-0784.t: 위 + illness is a handy pattern: 위염 (gastritis), 위암 (stomach cancer).

T6-0785.x: I dislocated my shoulder when I fell and went to the hospital.
T6-0785.t: Everyday speech often says 어깨가 빠졌어요 ('my shoulder came out') instead of 탈구.

T6-0786.x: An ankle sprain is a common injury for athletes.
T6-0786.e: Literally 'twist and wrench' — the medical word for a sprain.
T6-0786.t: 염좌 is formal and medical; in daily life people say 발목을 삐었어요 (I sprained my ankle).

T6-0787.x: I hurt a ligament in my knee while playing soccer.
T6-0787.e: Literally 'tough band' — the tissue that ties bones together.

T6-0788.ex: 나이가 들면 무릎 연골이 닳을 수 있어요.
T6-0788.x: As you get older, the cartilage in your knees can wear down.
T6-0788.t: The native Korean equivalent is 물렁뼈, literally 'squishy bone'.

T6-0789.ex: 그는 사고로 척수를 다쳐 걷지 못하게 되었습니다.
T6-0789.x: He injured his spinal cord in an accident and became unable to walk.
T6-0789.t: Pronounced [척쑤]; don't confuse 척수 (spinal cord) with 척추 (the spine bones themselves).

T6-0790.ex: 골다공증을 예방하려면 칼슘을 충분히 먹어야 해요.
T6-0790.x: To prevent osteoporosis, you should get enough calcium.
T6-0790.t: Pronounced [골다공쯩]; -증 means 'symptom or condition' and appears in many illness names.

T6-0791.ex: 통풍이 있으면 술과 고기를 줄이는 게 좋아요.
T6-0791.x: If you have gout, it's good to cut down on alcohol and meat.
T6-0791.e: Literally 'painful wind', an old traditional-medicine name for the disease.
T6-0791.t: Homonym warning: 통풍 (通風) also means 'ventilation', as in 통풍이 잘 되다.

T6-0792.x: The doctor said being overweight is bad for your health.
T6-0792.t: 과체중 is milder than 비만 (obesity); doctors use both as separate categories.

T6-0793.ex: 이 연구의 가장 중요한 목적은 바로 가설검증입니다.
T6-0793.x: The most important purpose of this study is hypothesis testing.
T6-0793.e: Literally 'examining and proving a tentative theory'.
T6-0793.t: Often written with a space, 가설 검증, and used with 하다: 가설을 검증하다.

T6-0794.x: In this experiment, temperature is an important variable.
T6-0794.t: 변인 is common in science education; statistics and math usually say 변수 instead.

T6-0795.x: The independent variable is what the researcher controls directly.

T6-0796.x: The dependent variable in this experiment is the height of the plants.
T6-0796.e: Literally 'subordinate changing factor' — it depends on the independent variable.

T6-0797.ex: 물의 양은 모든 실험에서 같은 통제변인이었어요.
T6-0797.x: The amount of water was a controlled variable, the same in every trial.

T6-0798.ex: 연구팀은 대조군에게 진짜 약 대신 가짜 약을 주었습니다.
T6-0798.x: The research team gave the control group a fake pill instead of the real medicine.

T6-0799.x: The experimental group's results were much better than the control group's.
T6-0799.t: -군 is a reusable research suffix: 실험군, 대조군, 고위험군 (high-risk group).

T6-0800.x: Sampling is important for getting accurate results.

T6-0801.ex: 이 조사의 모집단은 서울에 사는 대학생입니다.
T6-0801.x: The population for this survey is college students living in Seoul.
T6-0801.e: Literally 'mother group' — the whole group a sample comes from.
T6-0801.t: Pronounced [모집딴]; 모- here means 'source' like in 모국 (home country).

T6-0802.x: We split the participants into two groups at random.
T6-0802.e: Literally 'without deliberate action' — nobody chooses on purpose.
T6-0802.t: Most often used as 무작위로 (randomly) or before a noun: 무작위 추출 (random sampling).

T6-0803.forms: 통계적으로 유의하다 (be statistically significant) · 통계적 유의성이 있다/없다
T6-0803.ex: 두 그룹의 차이는 통계적 유의성이 없었습니다.
T6-0803.x: The difference between the two groups was not statistically significant.
T6-0803.t: Papers usually phrase it as 통계적으로 유의한 차이 (a statistically significant difference).

T6-0804.ex: 우리는 회귀분석으로 두 변인의 관계를 살펴보았습니다.
T6-0804.x: We examined the relationship between the two variables using regression analysis.
T6-0804.e: Literally 'returning analysis' — from 'regression toward the mean'.

T6-0805.ex: 표준편차가 작으면 데이터가 평균 근처에 모여 있어요.
T6-0805.x: If the standard deviation is small, the data is clustered near the mean.

T6-0806.ex: 소득은 평균보다 중앙값을 보는 것이 더 정확해요.
T6-0806.x: For income, looking at the median is more accurate than the mean.
T6-0806.t: Pronounced [중앙깝]; 값 after a noun gets a tensed sound, as in 최빈값 [최빈깝].

T6-0807.ex: 이 반에서 가장 자주 나온 점수인 최빈값은 80점이에요.
T6-0807.x: The mode, the score that came up most often in this class, is 80.
T6-0807.e: 최빈 (most frequent) + native 값 (value): 'the most frequent value'.
T6-0807.t: Pronounced [최빈깝] — 값 is tensed after a noun.

T6-0808.ex: 분산이 크다는 것은 자료가 넓게 퍼져 있다는 뜻이에요.
T6-0808.x: A large variance means the data is widely spread out.
T6-0808.t: Outside statistics, 분산 means spreading out, as in 위험을 분산하다 (to spread risk).

T6-0809.ex: 두 후보의 지지율 차이는 오차범위 안에 있습니다.
T6-0809.x: The gap in support between the two candidates is within the margin of error.
T6-0809.t: News reports love the phrase 오차범위 내 접전 — a close race within the margin of error.

T6-0810.ex: 이 설문지는 신뢰도가 높은 도구로 알려져 있어요.
T6-0810.x: This questionnaire is known as a highly reliable instrument.
T6-0810.t: Pronounced [실뢰도] — ㄴ before ㄹ becomes ㄹ (liquidization).

T6-0811.ex: 측정 도구의 타당도를 먼저 확인해야 합니다.
T6-0811.x: We must first check the validity of the measurement tool.
T6-0811.e: Literally 'degree of being proper and fitting'.
T6-0811.t: -도 = 'degree of': 신뢰도, 타당도, 만족도 (satisfaction level), 인지도 (name recognition).

T6-0812.ex: 이번 연구는 정량적 방법으로 자료를 분석했습니다.
T6-0812.x: This study analyzed the data using quantitative methods.
T6-0812.e: Literally 'fixing the amount' — measured in numbers.
T6-0812.t: Pronounced [정냥적] — nasalization; 양적 연구 is a common everyday synonym.

T6-0813.x: We analyzed the interview data using qualitative methods.
T6-0813.e: Literally 'fixing the nature' — describing qualities, not numbers.
T6-0813.t: Don't confuse it with 정성 (精誠), 'sincere effort', as in 정성껏 (wholeheartedly).

T6-0814.ex: 베이킹을 할 때는 재료 계량이 정말 중요해요.
T6-0814.x: When baking, measuring the ingredients is really important.

T6-0815.ex: 세 번 측정한 측정치의 평균을 계산했어요.
T6-0815.x: We calculated the average of three measured values.
T6-0815.t: -치 = value: 측정치, 평균치 (average value), 최고치 (peak value).

T6-0816.x: Happiness and love are concepts that are hard to quantify.

T6-0817.ex: 과학 실험은 재현성이 있어야 믿을 수 있어요.
T6-0817.x: A scientific experiment must be reproducible to be trusted.

T6-0818.ex: 논문을 쓰기 전에 선행연구를 꼼꼼히 읽어야 해요.
T6-0818.x: Before writing a paper, you should read the previous research carefully.
T6-0818.t: Thesis chapters often have a section titled 선행연구 검토 (review of previous studies).

T6-0819.x: This paper was written based on a literature review.

T6-0820.ex: 다음 달 학술대회에서 연구 결과를 발표할 거예요.
T6-0820.x: I'm going to present my research results at an academic conference next month.
T6-0820.t: 학회 is the shorter, more casual word researchers use for both the society and its conference.

T6-0821.ex: 인용한 내용은 반드시 각주로 출처를 밝혀야 해요.
T6-0821.x: For quoted content, you must give the source in a footnote.
T6-0821.e: Literally 'foot note' — a note at the foot of the page.

T6-0822.ex: 이 책은 각주 대신 미주를 사용했어요.
T6-0822.x: This book used endnotes instead of footnotes.
T6-0822.e: Literally 'tail note' — notes at the end of the text.
T6-0822.t: Homonym warning: 미주 (美洲) also means 'the Americas', as in 미주 지역.

T6-0823.ex: 이 논문은 동료평가를 거쳐 학술지에 실렸습니다.
T6-0823.x: This paper was published in a journal after going through peer review.
T6-0823.t: Pronounced [동뇨평까] — nasalization makes 료 sound like [뇨].

T6-0824.ex: 심사위원들이 제 논문에 좋은 점수를 주었어요.
T6-0824.x: The reviewers gave my paper a good score.
T6-0824.t: Also used for judges in contests and TV auditions, not just academic reviewers.

T6-0825.x: Every researcher must follow research ethics.
T6-0825.t: Pronounced [연구율리] — ㄴ before ㄹ becomes ㄹ.

T6-0826.x: Fabricating data is serious research misconduct.
T6-0826.t: 부정 here means 'wrongdoing' (不正), not 'denial' (否定); 부정행위 means cheating.

T6-0827.ex: 언니는 요즘 학위논문을 쓰느라 아주 바빠요.
T6-0827.x: My older sister is very busy these days writing her thesis.

T6-0828.x: He is pursuing a doctoral program in the US.
T6-0828.t: Use the collocation 박사과정을 밟다 (to pursue a doctoral program); a PhD student is 박사과정생.

T6-0829.ex: 정부는 기초과학 연구에 더 많이 투자해야 합니다.
T6-0829.x: The government should invest more in basic science research.

T6-0830.x: Engineering and medicine are typical fields of applied science.

T6-0831.ex: 기후 문제는 학제간 연구가 꼭 필요한 분야입니다.
T6-0831.x: Climate change is a field that really needs interdisciplinary research.
T6-0831.t: Pronounced [학쩨간]; mostly used before nouns like 연구 or 교육.

T6-0832.ex: 양자역학은 아주 작은 입자의 움직임을 설명합니다.
T6-0832.x: Quantum mechanics explains the behavior of very small particles.
T6-0832.t: Pronounced [양자여칵]; 역학 shows up in many physics field names.

T6-0833.x: Einstein is a scientist who is very famous for the theory of relativity.
T6-0833.t: Pronounced [상대썽이론]; often spaced as 상대성 이론.

T6-0834.x: Newton's laws are the foundation of classical mechanics.
T6-0834.t: Pronounced [고전녀칵] — an ㄴ sound is inserted before 역.

T6-0835.ex: 열역학 법칙에 따르면 에너지는 사라지지 않아요.
T6-0835.x: According to the laws of thermodynamics, energy does not disappear.
T6-0835.t: Pronounced [열려칵] — ㄴ insertion, then ㄹ assimilation.

T6-0836.ex: 전자기학은 전기와 자기의 관계를 연구하는 학문이에요.
T6-0836.x: Electromagnetism is the study of the relationship between electricity and magnetism.
T6-0836.e: Literally 'study of electric and magnetic energy'.

T6-0837.x: Airplane wings are designed using fluid mechanics.
T6-0837.t: -체 = state of matter: 고체 (solid), 액체 (liquid), 기체 (gas), 유체 (fluid).

T6-0838.x: She is majoring in astrophysics in graduate school.

T6-0839.ex: 쿼크와 전자는 더 이상 나눌 수 없는 소립자입니다.
T6-0839.x: Quarks and electrons are elementary particles that cannot be divided further.
T6-0839.t: Pronounced [소립짜]; in everyday science writing 기본 입자 is also common.

T6-0840.x: An atomic nucleus is made up of protons and neutrons.

T6-0841.ex: 원자핵 속의 양성자는 양전하를 띠고 있습니다.
T6-0841.x: The protons in an atomic nucleus have a positive charge.
T6-0841.t: The same 양성 'positive' is used for test results, as in 코로나 양성 (testing positive for COVID).

T6-0842.x: A neutron is a particle with no electric charge.

T6-0843.ex: 빛은 광자라는 작은 입자로 이루어져 있어요.
T6-0843.x: Light is made up of tiny particles called photons.
T6-0843.t: -자 = particle: 광자, 전자 (electron), 양성자, 중성자, 입자.

T6-0844.ex: 양성자는 세 개의 쿼크로 이루어져 있습니다.
T6-0844.x: A proton is made up of three quarks.

T6-0845.x: Nuclear power plants generate electricity through nuclear fission.
T6-0845.t: Pronounced [핵뿌녈]; 분열 alone also means a split in a group, like a political party.

T6-0846.ex: 태양은 핵융합으로 엄청난 에너지를 만들어 냅니다.
T6-0846.x: The sun produces enormous energy through nuclear fusion.

T6-0847.ex: 이 물질의 반감기는 약 오천 년입니다.
T6-0847.x: The half-life of this substance is about 5,000 years.

T6-0848.ex: 과학자들은 탄소 동위원소로 화석의 나이를 알아냅니다.
T6-0848.x: Scientists determine the age of fossils using carbon isotopes.
T6-0848.e: Literally 'same-position element' — same spot on the periodic table.

T6-0849.x: We had to memorize the periodic table in chemistry class.

T6-0850.ex: 바닷물은 물과 소금 등이 섞인 혼합물이에요.
T6-0850.x: Seawater is a mixture of water, salt, and other substances.
