T6-0850.t: Pronounced [혼함물]; don't mix up 혼합물 (mixture) with 화합물 (chemical compound).

T6-0851.ex: 우리가 매일 마시는 물의 분자식은 H₂O입니다.
T6-0851.x: The molecular formula of the water we drink every day is H2O.

T6-0852.x: Try writing the chemical formula for carbon dioxide on the board.
T6-0852.t: Pronounced [화학씩]; -식 = formula or style: 공식 (formula), 수식 (equation).

T6-0853.ex: 그 회장은 재산을 사회에 환원하기로 했어요.
T6-0853.x: The chairman decided to give his fortune back to society.
T6-0853.t: In chemistry it pairs with 산화 (oxidation); in daily news, 사회에 환원하다 means giving wealth back to society.

T6-0854.x: Water is the most commonly used solvent.
T6-0854.t: 용매 + 용질 = 용액: solvent + solute = solution.

T6-0855.x: In sugar water, sugar is the solute and water is the solvent.

T6-0856.ex: 이 용액에 소금을 조금 더 넣어 보세요.
T6-0856.x: Try adding a little more salt to this solution.
T6-0856.t: This is only a chemical solution; a solution to a problem is 해결책.

T6-0857.ex: 물에 소금이 더 이상 녹지 않으면 포화 상태입니다.
T6-0857.x: When no more salt dissolves in water, it is in a saturated state.
T6-0857.t: Also used figuratively: 시장이 포화 상태다 means 'the market is saturated'.

T6-0858.ex: 두 용액을 섞자 바닥에 하얀 침전이 생겼어요.
T6-0858.x: When the two solutions were mixed, a white precipitate formed at the bottom.
T6-0858.t: Weather 'precipitation' is 강수, not 침전; 침전 is only for settling particles.

T6-0859.ex: 바닷물을 증류하면 마실 수 있는 물을 얻을 수 있습니다.
T6-0859.x: If you distill seawater, you can get drinkable water.
T6-0859.e: Literally 'steam and trickle': vapor rises, then drips down as liquid.
T6-0859.t: Pronounced [증뉴] — ㄹ after ㅇ becomes ㄴ (nasalization).

T6-0860.ex: 이 물은 여과 과정을 거쳐서 마셔도 안전해요.
T6-0860.x: This water has gone through filtration, so it's safe to drink.
T6-0860.t: 여과 없이 means 'unfiltered' and is also used for uncensored media content.

T6-0861.x: When blood touches the air, clotting begins.

T6-0862.x: Clouds form in the sky through the condensation of water vapor.
T6-0862.t: 응결 is gas to liquid (condensation); 응고 is liquid to solid — don't mix them up.

T6-0863.x: When water boils, vaporization happens quickly.

T6-0864.ex: 액화 천연가스는 큰 배로 다른 나라에 운반합니다.
T6-0864.x: Liquefied natural gas is shipped to other countries on large vessels.
T6-0864.t: Pronounced [애콰] — ㄱ and ㅎ merge into ㅋ (aspiration).

T6-0865.x: The melting of ice happens at zero degrees.
T6-0865.t: Don't confuse it with 용해 (dissolving in a liquid); 융해 is a solid melting from heat.

T6-0866.x: Soap is alkaline, so it feels slippery when you touch it.

T6-0867.ex: 순수한 물은 산성도 알칼리성도 아닌 중성입니다.
T6-0867.x: Pure water is neither acidic nor alkaline; it is neutral.
T6-0867.t: It also describes a gender-neutral look (중성적인 스타일). A homonym 중성, written with different hanja, is the middle vowel of a Hangul syllable.

T6-0868.x: The higher the hydrogen ion concentration, the stronger the acidity.
T6-0868.t: In everyday Korean people usually just say 피에이치 (pH) instead.

T6-0869.ex: 흙 속의 유기물은 식물이 잘 자라게 도와줘요.
T6-0869.x: Organic matter in the soil helps plants grow well.

T6-0870.x: Water and salt are typical inorganic substances.
T6-0870.e: Literally 'things without a living mechanism'. 무- = 'without': 무료, 무기물.
T6-0870.t: Careful: 무기 alone usually means 'weapon', a completely different word.

T6-0871.x: Plastic is a typical polymer material.

T6-0872.x: If you fill a balloon with helium, it floats up into the sky.

T6-0873.x: Ramyeon contains a lot of sodium.
T6-0873.e: From German 'Natrium' (symbol Na) — that's why it isn't 'sodium'.
T6-0873.t: Health news uses 나트륨 for dietary salt: 나트륨 섭취를 줄이세요 'cut down on sodium'.

T6-0875.ex: 마그네슘이 부족하면 눈 밑이 떨릴 수 있어요.
T6-0875.x: If you lack magnesium, the skin under your eyes may twitch.

T6-0876.ex: 뉴턴은 사과가 떨어지는 것을 보고 만유인력을 생각했다고 해요.
T6-0876.x: They say Newton thought of universal gravitation after seeing an apple fall.
T6-0876.e: Literally 'the pulling force of all existing things'.
T6-0876.t: Pronounced [마뉴일력] — ㄴ before ㄹ becomes ㄹ.

T6-0877.x: On a downhill road you pick up speed, so it's dangerous.
T6-0877.t: 가속도가 붙다 is also figurative: things gain momentum and speed up.

T6-0878.ex: 물체의 운동량은 질량과 속도를 곱한 값입니다.
T6-0878.x: An object's momentum is its mass multiplied by its velocity.
T6-0878.t: In daily life it means 'amount of exercise': 운동량이 부족해요 'I don't exercise enough'.

T6-0879.ex: 얼음 위에서는 마찰력이 작아서 미끄러지기 쉬워요.
T6-0879.x: On ice there's little friction, so it's easy to slip.
T6-0879.e: Literally 'rubbing force'. -력 = force, power: 마찰력, 중력, 노력.
T6-0879.t: 마찰 alone also means conflict between people or countries, as in 무역 마찰 'trade friction'.

T6-0880.x: When a ride spins fast, you can feel the centrifugal force.
T6-0880.t: Pronounced [원심녁] — ㄹ after ㅁ becomes ㄴ (nasalization).

T6-0881.ex: 물체가 원을 그리며 돌려면 구심력이 필요합니다.
T6-0881.x: For an object to move in a circle, centripetal force is needed.
T6-0881.t: Figuratively it means a leader's or group's power to hold people together.

T6-0882.ex: 고무줄은 탄성이 좋아서 늘어났다가 다시 돌아와요.
T6-0882.x: A rubber band is very elastic, so it stretches and then snaps back.
T6-0882.e: Literally 'bounce nature'. Homonym warning: 탄성 also means a gasp of admiration.

T6-0883.x: Sound is a wave carried through the air.
T6-0883.t: It's also used for economic shocks: 석유 파동 means 'the oil crisis'.

T6-0884.x: The louder the sound, the bigger the wave's amplitude.

T6-0885.ex: 빛이 물에 들어가면 굴절이 일어나서 막대가 꺾여 보여요.
T6-0885.x: When light enters water it refracts, so a stick looks bent.
T6-0885.t: Pronounced [굴쩔] — ㅈ after ㄹ is tensed in Sino-Korean words.

T6-0886.ex: 소리는 회절 때문에 벽 뒤에서도 들립니다.
T6-0886.x: Because of diffraction, sound can be heard even behind a wall.
T6-0886.e: Literally 'turn and bend' — a wave bending around an obstacle.

T6-0887.ex: 두 파동이 만나면 간섭이 일어나 무늬가 생깁니다.
T6-0887.x: When two waves meet, interference occurs and creates a pattern.
T6-0887.t: In daily life it means meddling: 제 일에 간섭하지 마세요 'Stay out of my business'.

T6-0888.ex: 프리즘을 통과한 빛은 무지개색 스펙트럼으로 나뉘어요.
T6-0888.x: Light passing through a prism splits into a rainbow-colored spectrum.
T6-0888.t: It's also used for a range of views: 다양한 스펙트럼의 의견 'a wide spectrum of opinions'.

T6-0889.x: A remote control uses infrared rays to send signals.
T6-0889.e: Literally 'ray outside the red' — just beyond red on the spectrum.

T6-0890.ex: 사람의 눈은 가시광선만 볼 수 있습니다.
T6-0890.x: The human eye can see only visible light.
T6-0890.e: Literally 'light rays that can be seen'.

T6-0891.x: Cell phones send and receive information using electromagnetic waves.
T6-0891.t: Everyday Korean shortens it to 전자파, as in worries about 전자파 from phones.

T6-0892.x: The longer the wire, the greater the electrical resistance.
T6-0892.t: Outside physics, 저항 means resisting people or power: 저항 운동 'resistance movement'.

T6-0893.x: Copper is a conductor that carries electricity well.
T6-0893.e: Literally 'conducting body'. -체 = body, substance: 도체, 기체, 액체.

T6-0894.x: Rubber is an insulator that doesn't conduct electricity.
T6-0894.t: The prefix 불- becomes 부- before ㄷ and ㅈ: 부도체, 부족, 부정.

T6-0895.ex: 초전도체는 아주 낮은 온도에서 전기 저항이 0이 됩니다.
T6-0895.x: A superconductor's electrical resistance drops to zero at very low temperatures.

T6-0896.ex: 지구에는 나침반 바늘을 움직이는 자기장이 있어요.
T6-0896.x: The Earth has a magnetic field that moves a compass needle.
T6-0896.t: Don't confuse 자기 'magnetism' here with 자기 'oneself' — context makes it clear.

T6-0897.x: An electric field forms around an electric charge.
T6-0897.e: Literally 'electricity field'. -장 = field: 자기장, 전기장, 중력장.

T6-0898.ex: 축전기의 두 금속판 사이에는 유전체가 들어 있습니다.
T6-0898.x: In a capacitor, there is a dielectric between the two metal plates.
T6-0898.t: Homonym alert: in biology 유전체 (with different hanja) means 'genome'.

T6-0899.x: The Human Genome Project was completed in 2003.
T6-0899.e: From German 'Genom'; the Sino-Korean term is 유전체.

T6-0900.e: Literally 'dye-color body' — it stains easily for the microscope.

T6-0901.x: The criminal's DNA was found at the crime scene.
T6-0901.e: The English letters 'DNA' spelled out in Hangul; often simply written DNA.

T6-0902.ex: 유전공학 기술로 병에 강한 작물을 만들 수 있어요.
T6-0902.x: Genetic engineering can create crops that resist disease.

T6-0903.x: Genetically modified foods must be labeled.

T6-0904.forms: 유전자 가위로 + noun + 을/를 편집하다 (edit ... with gene scissors)
T6-0904.ex: 과학자들은 유전자 가위로 병을 일으키는 유전자를 고쳤어요.
T6-0904.x: Scientists fixed a disease-causing gene using gene-editing tools.
T6-0904.e: 유전자 'gene' + native 가위 'scissors' — a nickname for gene-editing technology.

T6-0905.ex: 줄기세포는 여러 종류의 세포로 자랄 수 있습니다.
T6-0905.x: Stem cells can develop into many kinds of cells.
T6-0905.e: Native 줄기 'stem' + 세포 'cell' — a direct translation of 'stem cell'.

T6-0906.ex: 세포분열을 통해 몸이 자라고 상처가 낫습니다.
T6-0906.x: Through cell division, the body grows and wounds heal.

T6-0907.ex: 세포막은 물질이 세포 안팎으로 드나드는 것을 조절합니다.
T6-0907.x: The cell membrane controls what goes in and out of the cell.

T6-0908.ex: 세포핵 안에는 유전 정보가 들어 있습니다.
T6-0908.x: Genetic information is stored inside the cell nucleus.
T6-0908.e: Literally 'cell core'; 핵 also means 'nuclear', as in 핵무기.

T6-0909.ex: 침 속의 효소가 음식물의 소화를 돕습니다.
T6-0909.x: Enzymes in saliva help digest food.

T6-0910.ex: 단백질은 여러 가지 아미노산으로 이루어져 있어요.
T6-0910.x: Proteins are made up of various amino acids.

T6-0911.ex: 식물은 광합성을 통해 스스로 양분을 만듭니다.
T6-0911.x: Plants make their own nutrients through photosynthesis.
T6-0911.e: Literally 'combining with light' — building food using sunlight.
T6-0911.t: Pronounced [광합썽] — ㅅ after ㅂ is tensed.

T6-0912.ex: 식물도 호흡작용을 통해 산소를 쓰고 이산화탄소를 내보냅니다.
T6-0912.x: Plants also use oxygen and release carbon dioxide through respiration.

T6-0913.ex: 먹이사슬의 맨 위에는 사자 같은 포식자가 있어요.
T6-0913.x: At the top of the food chain are predators like lions.

T6-0914.ex: 먹이그물은 여러 먹이사슬이 복잡하게 얽힌 것입니다.
T6-0914.x: A food web is many food chains tangled together.
T6-0914.e: 먹이 'feed' + 그물 'net' — a direct translation of 'food web'.

T6-0915.x: Darwin explained the evolution of living things through natural selection.

T6-0916.ex: 적자생존은 환경에 잘 적응한 생물이 살아남는다는 뜻입니다.
T6-0916.x: Survival of the fittest means organisms well adapted to their environment survive.
T6-0916.e: Literally 'the fit one survives'. -자 = person or one who: 적자, 과학자.
T6-0916.t: Pronounced [적짜생존]; also note 적자 alone usually means 'deficit' — a different word.

T6-0918.x: The tiger is a typical endangered species.
T6-0918.e: Literally 'species in a crisis of extinction'.
T6-0918.t: Pronounced [멸쫑위기종] — ㅈ after ㄹ is tensed in Sino-Korean words.

T6-0919.x: When forests disappear, biodiversity also decreases.

T6-0920.x: Mushrooms reproduce with spores instead of seeds.
T6-0920.e: Literally 'sac seed' — a tiny cell that grows into a new organism.

T6-0921.ex: 기계학습은 많은 데이터를 이용해서 컴퓨터를 학습시킵니다.
T6-0921.x: Machine learning trains computers using large amounts of data.
T6-0921.t: In tech talk, the loanword 머신러닝 is just as common as 기계학습.

T6-0922.ex: 인공 신경망은 사람의 뇌를 흉내 낸 기술입니다.
T6-0922.x: An artificial neural network is a technology that imitates the human brain.

T6-0923.ex: 사물인터넷 덕분에 밖에서도 집 안의 전등을 끌 수 있어요.
T6-0923.x: Thanks to the Internet of Things, you can turn off the lights at home even when you're out.

T6-0924.ex: 블록체인 기술은 거래 기록을 안전하게 보관합니다.
T6-0924.x: Blockchain technology stores transaction records securely.

T6-0925.ex: 암호화된 파일은 비밀번호가 있어야 복호화할 수 있어요.
T6-0925.x: An encrypted file can be decrypted only with the password.
T6-0925.e: Literally 'turning a code back' — the reverse of 암호화.
T6-0925.t: Pronounced [보코화] — ㄱ and ㅎ merge into ㅋ.

T6-0926.ex: 랜섬웨어에 감염되면 컴퓨터 파일을 열 수 없게 돼요.
T6-0926.x: If you're infected with ransomware, you can't open your computer files.

T6-0927.ex: 회사에서는 매년 정보보안 교육을 받아야 합니다.
T6-0927.x: At the company, you must take information security training every year.

T6-0928.x: The government decided to strengthen cybersecurity.

T6-0929.ex: 개인정보유출 사고로 많은 고객이 피해를 입었습니다.
T6-0929.x: Many customers were harmed by the personal data leak.
T6-0929.t: News usually writes it with spaces: 개인 정보 유출.

T6-0930.ex: 방화벽을 설정하면 외부의 공격을 막을 수 있어요.
T6-0930.x: Setting up a firewall can block outside attacks.
T6-0930.e: Literally 'wall that prevents fire' — first a building term, then a computer one.
T6-0930.t: Don't confuse 방화 'fire prevention' with its homonym 방화 'arson'.

T6-0931.ex: 요즘 스마트폰은 생체인식으로 잠금을 풀 수 있어요.
T6-0931.x: These days smartphones can be unlocked with biometrics.

T6-0932.ex: 공항에서 안면인식으로 출국 심사를 받을 수 있습니다.
T6-0932.x: At the airport, you can go through departure screening with facial recognition.
T6-0932.t: 안면 is a formal word for 얼굴; 안면이 있다 means 'to be acquainted'.

T6-0933.ex: 지문인식으로 휴대폰 잠금을 풀 수 있어요.
T6-0933.x: You can unlock your phone with fingerprint recognition.

T6-0934.x: A hydrogen car emits only water while driving.

T6-0935.x: Electric cars use high-capacity rechargeable batteries.
T6-0935.e: Literally 'second-round battery' — it can be recharged and reused.
T6-0935.t: In business news, 이차전지 often refers to the whole EV battery industry.

T6-0936.ex: 집적회로는 작은 칩 안에 수많은 회로를 넣은 것입니다.
T6-0936.x: An integrated circuit packs countless circuits into a small chip.

T6-0937.ex: 이 카드에는 아주 작은 마이크로칩이 들어 있어요.
T6-0937.x: This card has a tiny microchip inside it.
T6-0937.e: From English 'microchip.' Often shortened to just 칩.

T6-0938.ex: 새 노트북은 프로세서 성능이 훨씬 좋아졌어요.
T6-0938.x: The new laptop's processor performance has gotten much better.
T6-0938.t: In formal or technical writing, the CPU is also called 중앙처리장치.

T6-0939.ex: 컴퓨터는 복잡한 연산을 아주 빠르게 처리합니다.
T6-0939.x: Computers process complex calculations very quickly.
T6-0939.t: 연산 is the technical word; in everyday talk about money or numbers, use 계산.

T6-0940.ex: 연산장치는 컴퓨터 안에서 계산을 담당하는 부분이에요.
T6-0940.x: The arithmetic unit is the part of a computer that handles calculations.
T6-0940.e: Literally 'calculation device'; 장치 means a device or apparatus.

T6-0941.ex: 중요한 파일은 외부 저장장치에도 꼭 백업하세요.
T6-0941.x: Be sure to back up important files to an external storage device too.
T6-0941.t: 저장하다 is also the everyday word for saving a file: 파일을 저장하세요.

T6-0942.ex: 회사는 프로그램의 소스코드를 외부에 공개하지 않았습니다.
T6-0942.x: The company did not release the program's source code to the public.

T6-0943.ex: 이 프로그램은 오픈소스라서 누구나 무료로 쓸 수 있어요.
T6-0943.x: This program is open source, so anyone can use it for free.

T6-0944.ex: 새 앱은 인터페이스가 단순해서 쓰기 편해요.
T6-0944.x: The new app has a simple interface, so it's easy to use.
T6-0944.e: From English 'interface'; note the f becomes ㅍ.

T6-0945.ex: 우리 팀은 사용자경험을 개선하기 위해 설문 조사를 했어요.
T6-0945.x: Our team ran a survey to improve the user experience.
T6-0945.e: Literally 'user's experience'; -자 = person who does it: 사용자, 운전자.
T6-0945.t: In tech companies people often just say UX (유엑스) instead.

T6-0946.ex: 이 프로그램은 구형 컴퓨터와 호환성이 떨어져요.
T6-0946.x: This program has poor compatibility with older computers.
T6-0946.t: Pronounced [호환썽]; say 호환성이 좋다/떨어지다 for good or poor compatibility.

T6-0947.x: All of the hospital's records were computerized last year.
T6-0947.e: -화 = '-ization': 전산화, 산업화, 실용화. 전산 means 'electronic computing.'
T6-0947.t: Use 전산화되다 for 'to be computerized' and 전산화하다 for 'to computerize.'

T6-0948.x: My younger sibling is majoring in robotics in college.
T6-0948.t: Pronounced [로볻꽁학] — the final ㅅ sounds as ㄷ and the ㄱ after it becomes tense.

T6-0949.ex: 나노기술은 의료와 전자 분야에서 널리 쓰입니다.
T6-0949.x: Nanotechnology is widely used in medicine and electronics.

T6-0950.ex: 정부는 바이오 산업에 대한 투자를 늘리기로 했습니다.
T6-0950.x: The government decided to increase investment in the biotech industry.
T6-0950.e: From English 'bio-.' Used alone, it usually means the biotech industry.
T6-0950.t: Usually works like a prefix: 바이오 산업, 바이오 기업, 바이오 연료.

T6-0951.ex: 이 자전거는 탄소섬유로 만들어서 아주 가벼워요.
T6-0951.x: This bike is very light because it's made of carbon fiber.

T6-0952.ex: 이 회사는 배터리 원천기술을 많이 가지고 있습니다.
T6-0952.x: This company holds a lot of core original battery technology.
T6-0952.e: Literally 'wellspring technology' — the technology everything else flows from.

T6-0953.ex: 핵심기술이 해외로 유출되지 않도록 보호해야 합니다.
T6-0953.x: Core technologies must be protected so they don't leak overseas.
T6-0953.t: Pronounced [핵씸기술]; 핵심 alone is very common: 핵심 내용 'the main point.'

T6-0954.ex: 두 나라는 기술이전에 관한 협정을 맺었습니다.
T6-0954.x: The two countries signed an agreement on technology transfer.
T6-0954.t: Pronounced [기수리전] — the final ㄹ links to the next vowel.

T6-0955.ex: 선진국과 개발도상국의 기술격차가 점점 커지고 있습니다.
T6-0955.x: The technology gap between developed and developing countries is growing.
T6-0955.e: Literally 'technology level difference'; 격차 means a gap or disparity.
T6-0955.t: 격차가 벌어지다 'a gap widens' and 격차를 줄이다 'narrow a gap' are common collocations.

T6-0956.ex: 이 기술은 아직 실용화 단계에 이르지 못했습니다.
T6-0956.x: This technology hasn't yet reached the stage of practical use.

T6-0957.ex: 새 모델은 내년 초부터 양산에 들어갑니다.
T6-0957.x: The new model goes into mass production early next year.
T6-0957.e: Short for 대량 생산 'large-quantity production.' Homonym warning: 양산 also means a parasol.
T6-0957.t: 양산에 들어가다 'go into mass production' is the standard news phrase.

T6-0958.ex: 회사는 전시회에서 새 로봇의 시제품을 처음 공개했어요.
T6-0958.x: The company unveiled the prototype of its new robot at the exhibition.

T6-0959.x: The city launched a pilot program for self-driving buses.
T6-0959.t: 시범 운영 is a trial run, and 시범 경기 is an exhibition game.

T6-0960.m: patent application, filing for a patent
T6-0960.ex: 연구팀은 새 기술에 대해 특허출원을 마쳤습니다.
T6-0960.x: The research team finished filing a patent for the new technology.

T6-0961.x: Creators' intellectual property should be protected by law.
T6-0961.t: The older term 지적재산 means the same thing; 지식재산 is now the official term.

T6-0962.ex: 탈산업화로 많은 공장 도시가 어려움을 겪었습니다.
T6-0962.x: Many factory towns struggled because of deindustrialization.

T6-0963.x: Korea industrialized rapidly from the 1960s on.
T6-0963.e: Literally 'becoming industrial'; 공업 means manufacturing industry.
T6-0963.t: Pronounced [공어퐈]; 공업화 and 산업화 are near synonyms, but 산업화 is more common today.

T6-0964.ex: 울산은 조선과 자동차 같은 중공업이 발달한 도시예요.
T6-0964.x: Ulsan is a city with developed heavy industries like shipbuilding and cars.
T6-0964.e: Literally 'heavy industry'; the opposite is 경공업.

T6-0965.ex: 1960년대 한국 경제는 섬유 같은 경공업이 중심이었습니다.
T6-0965.x: In the 1960s, Korea's economy centered on light industries like textiles.
T6-0965.e: Literally 'light industry'; the opposite is 중공업.

T6-0966.ex: 정부는 반도체 같은 첨단산업을 적극 지원하고 있습니다.
T6-0966.x: The government is actively supporting high-tech industries like semiconductors.
T6-0966.e: Literally 'pointed-tip industry' — at the very tip of progress.
T6-0966.t: 첨단 works as a prefix too: 첨단 장비 'state-of-the-art equipment.'

T6-0967.ex: 한때 잘나가던 필름 산업은 이제 사양산업이 되었어요.
T6-0967.x: The once-booming film industry has now become a declining industry.
T6-0967.e: Literally 'setting-sun industry' — just like English 'sunset industry.'

T6-0968.x: AI is considered a leading promising industry of the future.
T6-0968.t: 유망 also describes people: 유망한 선수 'a promising athlete.'

T6-0969.x: Steel and power are a nation's typical key industries.
T6-0969.e: Literally 'base-and-trunk industry' — the trunk the rest of the economy grows from.
T6-0969.t: Don't confuse with 기간 期間 'period of time' — same sound, different hanja.

T6-0970.ex: 한국의 조선업은 세계적인 경쟁력을 가지고 있습니다.
T6-0970.x: Korea's shipbuilding industry is globally competitive.
T6-0970.e: Literally 'ship-building business'; -업 = industry, business: 조선업, 제조업.
T6-0970.t: Not related to the Joseon dynasty (朝鮮) — same sound, different hanja.

T6-0971.x: Pohang is a city famous for its steel industry.

T6-0972.x: Most plastic is made from petrochemical products.
T6-0972.e: Literally 'stone-oil chemistry'; 석유 'petroleum' is literally 'rock oil.'
T6-0972.t: Pronounced [서규화학] — the final ㄱ links to the next vowel.

T6-0973.ex: 국제 유가가 오르면서 정유 회사들의 이익이 늘었습니다.
T6-0973.x: As global oil prices rose, oil refiners' profits increased.
T6-0973.e: Literally 'refine oil.' 정유사 means an oil refining company.

T6-0974.x: Daegu has long been a city with a developed textile industry.

T6-0975.ex: 최근 한국의 방위산업 수출이 크게 늘었습니다.
T6-0975.x: Korea's defense industry exports have risen sharply recently.
T6-0975.t: News headlines usually use the short form: 방산 수출, 방산 기업.

T6-0976.ex: 그는 대학원에서 항공우주 공학을 공부하고 있어요.
T6-0976.x: He's studying aerospace engineering in grad school.
T6-0976.t: 항공우주 and 우주항공 mean the same; 항공우주 is more common in engineering and academic names.

T6-0977.ex: 정부는 우주항공 분야에 투자를 확대하고 있습니다.
T6-0977.x: The government is expanding investment in the aerospace sector.
T6-0977.e: Literally 'outer space and sky-sailing' — the same words as 항공우주, reversed.
T6-0977.t: Korea's space agency is 우주항공청, so this order is common in government and news contexts.

T6-0978.ex: 한국은 자체 기술로 만든 발사체를 우주로 쏘아 올렸습니다.
T6-0978.x: Korea launched a rocket built with its own technology into space.
T6-0978.e: Literally 'launched body'; -체 = body, object: 발사체, 물체.
T6-0978.t: Pronounced [발싸체]; in news about missile tests, it also means a fired projectile.

T6-0979.ex: 우주인들은 우주정거장에서 여러 달 동안 생활합니다.
T6-0979.x: Astronauts live on the space station for several months.
T6-0979.e: Literally 'outer-space stop'; 정거장 is an everyday word for a bus or train stop.

T6-0980.ex: 달 탐사선이 달 표면 사진을 보내왔습니다.
T6-0980.x: The lunar probe sent back photos of the moon's surface.

T6-0981.ex: 우리 태양계는 은하계의 가장자리 쪽에 있어요.
T6-0981.x: Our solar system is toward the edge of the galaxy.
T6-0981.e: Literally 'silver river system' — Koreans call the Milky Way 은하수, the 'silver river.'
T6-0981.t: 은하계 often means our own Milky Way; for galaxies in general, 은하 alone is common.

T6-0982.ex: 망원경으로 보면 성운은 희미한 구름처럼 보여요.
T6-0982.x: Through a telescope, a nebula looks like a faint cloud.

T6-0983.m: star (that shines by itself), fixed star
T6-0983.x: The sun is a star that produces its own light.
T6-0983.e: Literally 'constant star' — it seems to stay in place, unlike planets.
T6-0983.t: Easy to confuse: 항성 shines by itself, 행성 (planet) orbits it, and 위성 (moon) orbits a planet.

T6-0984.ex: 큰 소행성이 지구 가까이 지나갈 예정이라고 합니다.
T6-0984.x: They say a large asteroid will pass close to Earth.
T6-0984.e: Literally 'small planet'; 행성 is 'moving star,' i.e. planet.

T6-0985.ex: 작년에 한 시골 마을에 운석이 떨어졌습니다.
T6-0985.x: Last year, a meteorite fell in a rural village.
T6-0985.t: 운석 is the rock that lands; the streak of light in the sky is 유성 or 별똥별.

T6-0986.x: The universe is known to have begun with the Big Bang.

T6-0987.ex: 그 별은 지구에서 약 사 광년 떨어져 있어요.
T6-0987.x: That star is about four light-years from Earth.
T6-0987.t: Like English, it measures distance, not time.

T6-0988.ex: 기업은 가치사슬 전체를 분석해서 비용을 줄였습니다.
T6-0988.x: The company cut costs by analyzing its entire value chain.
T6-0988.t: 공급망 'supply chain' is a related but different term often heard in the news.

T6-0989.ex: 반도체 회사들이 올해 설비투자를 크게 늘렸습니다.
T6-0989.x: Chip companies sharply increased their capital investment this year.

T6-0990.x: Orders dropped, so the factory's operating rate fell to 70 percent.
T6-0990.e: Literally 'running rate'; 가동 means a machine or plant is running.
T6-0990.t: Pronounced [가동뉼]; the suffix 'rate' is written 률 after a consonant, but 율 after a vowel or ㄴ.

T6-0991.ex: 새 공정 덕분에 반도체 수율이 크게 높아졌습니다.
T6-0991.x: Thanks to the new process, the chip yield rose significantly.
T6-0991.e: Literally 'gathered rate' — the share of usable output.
T6-0991.t: A key word in chip-industry news; 수율이 높다 means more good chips per wafer.

T6-0992.ex: 품질 검사를 강화하자 불량률이 절반으로 줄었어요.
T6-0992.x: When they tightened quality checks, the defect rate dropped by half.

T6-0993.x: This factory is known for its strict quality control.
T6-0993.t: Pronounced [품질괄리] — ㄴ before ㄹ becomes ㄹ.

T6-0994.ex: 정부는 도로와 철도 같은 사회기반시설에 투자하고 있습니다.
T6-0994.x: The government is investing in infrastructure such as roads and railways.
T6-0994.t: In speech and news, the loanword 인프라 is used much more often.

T6-0995.ex: 광통신 덕분에 많은 데이터를 빠르게 보낼 수 있어요.
T6-0995.x: Thanks to optical communication, large amounts of data can be sent quickly.
T6-0995.e: Literally 'light communication' — data travels as light through fiber.

T6-0996.ex: 한국은 초고속 인터넷이 일찍 보급된 나라입니다.
T6-0996.x: Korea is a country where high-speed internet spread early.
T6-0996.t: Mostly used before another noun: 초고속 인터넷, 초고속 열차, 초고속 성장.

T6-0997.ex: 동영상을 많이 보면 더 넓은 대역폭이 필요해요.
T6-0997.x: If you watch a lot of videos, you need more bandwidth.
T6-0997.t: Pronounced [대역폭]; bandwidth is 넓다 'wide' or 좁다 'narrow,' not 크다.

T6-0998.x: Smartphones use a variety of wireless communication technologies.
T6-0998.e: Literally 'no-wire communication'; the opposite is 유선 'wired.'

T6-0999.ex: 계산할 때 카드를 단말기에 꽂아 주세요.
T6-0999.x: When you pay, please insert your card into the terminal.
T6-0999.e: Literally 'end-tip machine' — the device at the user's end of a network.
T6-0999.t: Used for phones in telecom contexts and for card readers at stores.

T6-1000.x: These days even young children use smart devices easily.

T6-1001.ex: 스마트워치 같은 웨어러블 기기가 인기를 끌고 있어요.
T6-1001.x: Wearable devices like smartwatches are gaining popularity.
T6-1001.t: Usually followed by 기기 or 기술: 웨어러블 기기.

T6-1002.ex: 이 카메라는 화소가 높아서 사진이 선명해요.
T6-1002.x: This camera has a high pixel count, so photos are sharp.
T6-1002.e: Literally 'picture element' — exactly what 'pixel' stands for.
T6-1002.t: Camera specs use 만 화소: 1200만 화소 means 12 megapixels.

T6-1003.ex: 이 소설은 한국 문학사에서 중요한 작품입니다.
T6-1003.x: This novel is an important work in the history of Korean literature.
T6-1003.e: Literally 'literature history.' Homonym: 문학사 can also mean a Bachelor of Arts degree.

T6-1004.m: literature and the arts; literary arts
T6-1004.ex: 그는 대학 시절 문예 동아리에서 시를 썼어요.
T6-1004.x: He wrote poems in a literary club in college.
T6-1004.t: Pronounced [무녜]; common in compounds like 문예창작과 'creative writing department.'

T6-1005.m: literary movement, trend in literature and art
T6-1005.x: Romanticism is a leading literary movement of 19th-century Europe.
T6-1005.e: Literally 'currents of thought in literature and art.'

T6-1006.ex: 낭만주의 시인들은 자연과 감정을 중요하게 여겼습니다.
T6-1006.x: Romantic poets valued nature and emotion.
T6-1006.e: 낭만 came via Japanese, whose characters were chosen for the sound 'roman,' not their meaning.
T6-1006.t: 낭만적이다 'to be romantic' is everyday Korean, e.g. a romantic evening.

T6-1007.ex: 사실주의 소설은 평범한 사람들의 삶을 그대로 그립니다.
T6-1007.x: Realist novels portray ordinary people's lives just as they are.
T6-1007.e: -주의 = '-ism': 사실주의, 자본주의, 민주주의. 사실 is 'depicting the real.'
T6-1007.t: This 사실 (寫實) is not 사실 (事實) 'fact' — same sound, different hanja.

T6-1008.ex: 자연주의 작가들은 인간을 환경의 영향을 받는 존재로 보았습니다.
T6-1008.x: Naturalist writers saw humans as beings shaped by their environment.

T6-1009.ex: 고전주의 예술은 균형과 질서를 중요하게 생각했습니다.
T6-1009.x: Classicist art placed great value on balance and order.
T6-1009.e: Literally 'old-canon-ism' — modeled on Greek and Roman classics.

T6-1010.ex: 1930년대 한국 시에도 모더니즘이 큰 영향을 주었어요.
T6-1010.x: Modernism also had a big influence on Korean poetry in the 1930s.

T6-1011.x: Dalí's paintings are representative works of surrealism.
T6-1011.e: Literally 'beyond-reality-ism' — a direct match for French 'sur-réalisme.'

T6-1012.ex: 상징주의 시는 의미를 직접 말하지 않고 암시합니다.
T6-1012.x: Symbolist poetry hints at meaning rather than stating it directly.

T6-1013.ex: 표현주의 화가들은 강한 색으로 내면의 감정을 나타냈습니다.
T6-1013.x: Expressionist painters showed their inner feelings with strong colors.

T6-1014.x: Monet is a French painter who represents impressionism.
T6-1014.e: Literally 'impression-ism'; 인상 means an impression, literally 'stamped image.'
T6-1014.t: 주의 is pronounced [주이] in natural speech.

T6-1015.ex: 그 화가는 젊은 시절 아방가르드 운동에 참여했어요.
T6-1015.x: That painter took part in the avant-garde movement when he was young.
T6-1015.t: Often used before another noun: 아방가르드 영화, 아방가르드 패션.

T6-1016.ex: 1960년대에는 많은 젊은 예술가들이 전위예술에 관심을 가졌습니다.
T6-1016.x: In the 1960s, many young artists took an interest in avant-garde art.
T6-1016.e: Literally 'front-guard art' — art that marches ahead of its time.

T6-1017.ex: 그 소설가는 스무 살에 문단의 주목을 받았어요.
T6-1017.x: That novelist caught the attention of the literary world at twenty.
T6-1017.t: Don't confuse it with the homonym 문단 'paragraph'; 문단에 나오다 clearly means the literary world.

T6-1018.m: literary debut, debut as a writer
T6-1018.x: She won the New Year's literary contest and debuted as a poet.
T6-1018.e: Literally 'ascending the platform' — stepping onto the literary stage.
T6-1018.t: Usually used as 등단하다; 'X(으)로 등단하다' means to debut as X, e.g. 시인으로, 소설가로.

T6-1019.m: New Year's literary contest (run by newspapers)
T6-1019.ex: 그는 다섯 번 도전한 끝에 신춘문예에 당선됐어요.
T6-1019.x: After trying five times, he finally won the New Year's literary contest.
T6-1019.e: Literally 'new spring literary arts' — newspapers announce the winners every January.
T6-1019.t: The standard verb is 당선되다: 신춘문예에 당선되다 = to win the New Year's contest.

T6-1020.m: writer, man or woman of letters
T6-1020.ex: 그는 정치인이면서 뛰어난 문필가로도 알려져 있어요.
T6-1020.x: He is a politician but is also known as an outstanding writer.
T6-1020.e: Literally 'writing-brush expert'; -가 marks a professional: 작가, 화가, 소설가.

T6-1021.ex: 이 작품에서는 타협하지 않는 작가정신이 느껴집니다.
T6-1021.x: You can feel an uncompromising artistic integrity in this work.
T6-1021.e: Literally 'writer spirit' — commitment to one's art over money or fame.
T6-1021.t: Pronounced [작까정신]; 작가 always has a tense ㄲ sound.

T6-1022.ex: 작가는 섬세한 필치로 시골 풍경을 그려 냈어요.
T6-1022.x: The author depicted the countryside with a delicate touch.
T6-1022.e: Literally 'brush manner' — the feel of someone's writing or brushstrokes.
T6-1022.t: Usually adjective + 필치로: 섬세한 필치로, 담담한 필치로 '(written) in a delicate / calm style'.

T6-1023.m: writing skill, the power of one's pen
T6-1023.ex: 그 작가는 데뷔작부터 탄탄한 필력을 보여 주었어요.
T6-1023.x: That author showed solid writing skill from the very first book.
T6-1023.e: Literally 'brush power' — how forcefully and skillfully someone writes.
T6-1023.t: ㄹ + ㄹ is pronounced as a clear double L: [필력], pillyeok.

T6-1024.ex: 책을 많이 읽으면 문장력이 자연스럽게 좋아져요.
T6-1024.x: If you read a lot, your writing ability naturally improves.
T6-1024.e: Literally 'sentence power'; -력 = ability: 필력, 표현력, 이해력.
T6-1024.t: Pronounced [문장녁] — ㄹ after ㅇ becomes ㄴ.

T6-1025.ex: 이 소설의 서술자는 주인공의 어린 딸이에요.
T6-1025.x: The narrator of this novel is the main character's young daughter.
T6-1025.e: Literally 'one who narrates'; -자 = person: 관찰자, 화자.
T6-1025.t: Pronounced [서술짜]; for poems, the term is usually 화자 instead.

T6-1026.ex: 이 소설은 일인칭 시점으로 쓰여 있어요.
T6-1026.x: This novel is written from a first-person point of view.
T6-1026.e: Literally 'one person-label'; 인칭 means grammatical person.
T6-1026.t: Common phrase: 일인칭 주인공 시점 'first-person protagonist point of view'.

T6-1027.ex: 삼인칭 시점을 쓰면 여러 인물의 이야기를 보여 줄 수 있어요.
T6-1027.x: With a third-person point of view, you can show several characters' stories.
T6-1027.e: Literally 'three person-label' — he, she or they.

T6-1028.forms: 전지적 작가 시점으로 쓰다 · 전지적 작가 시점의 소설
T6-1028.ex: 전지적 작가 시점에서는 서술자가 인물의 속마음까지 알려 줘요.
T6-1028.x: In the omniscient point of view, the narrator even tells us the characters' inner thoughts.
T6-1028.e: Literally 'all-knowing writer viewpoint' — the narrator knows every character's thoughts.
T6-1028.t: Pronounced [전지적 작까 시쩜]; one of the four 시점 types taught in Korean schools.

T6-1029.ex: 이 소설에서 나는 사건을 지켜보는 관찰자일 뿐이에요.
T6-1029.x: In this novel, 'I' am just an observer watching the events.
T6-1029.e: Literally 'one who views and examines'; 관찰자 시점 = observer point of view.
T6-1029.t: Pronounced [관찰짜] — the ㅈ after ㄹ is tensed.

T6-1030.ex: 호메로스의 일리아스는 서양 문학의 대표적인 서사시입니다.
T6-1030.x: Homer's Iliad is a representative epic of Western literature.
T6-1030.e: Literally 'narrating-events poem' — a long poem that tells a story.

T6-1031.ex: 그의 시에는 고향에 대한 따뜻한 서정이 담겨 있어요.
T6-1031.x: His poems hold a warm lyrical feeling for his hometown.
T6-1031.e: Literally 'pouring out feeling'; contrasts with 서사 'narrative'.
T6-1031.t: Most often used as 서정적: 서정적인 음악, 서정적인 분위기 'lyrical music, a lyrical mood'.

T6-1032.ex: 김소월의 서정시는 지금도 많은 사람에게 사랑받고 있어요.
T6-1032.x: Kim So-wol's lyric poems are still loved by many people today.
T6-1032.e: Literally 'feeling-expressing poem' — short, personal and emotional, unlike an epic.

T6-1033.ex: 산문시는 행을 나누지 않고 문장처럼 이어서 써요.
T6-1033.x: A prose poem is written continuously like sentences, without line breaks.
T6-1033.e: Literally 'scattered-writing poem' — poetry written in paragraphs, not lines.

T6-1034.ex: 이 시는 같은 소리를 반복해서 운율을 만들어요.
T6-1034.x: This poem creates rhythm by repeating the same sounds.
T6-1034.e: Literally 'rhyme and law' — the musical pattern of a poem.
T6-1034.t: Pronounced [우뉼]; after ㄴ or a vowel, 률 is written 율.

T6-1035.ex: 한국 시에서는 영어 시만큼 압운이 중요하지 않아요.
T6-1035.x: In Korean poetry, rhyme is not as important as in English poetry.
T6-1035.e: Literally 'pressing the rhyme' — placing matching sounds at set positions.
T6-1035.t: Pronounced [아분] — the ㅂ links over to the next syllable.

T6-1036.m: metrical foot, beat unit (in Korean verse)
T6-1036.ex: 김소월의 시는 주로 3음보의 리듬을 가지고 있어요.
T6-1036.x: Kim So-wol's poems mostly have a three-beat rhythm.
T6-1036.e: Literally 'sound step' — a beat unit, counted by pauses rather than syllables.
T6-1036.t: Korean verse is described as 3음보 or 4음보; 4음보 is typical of 시조 and 가사.

T6-1037.ex: 시조는 정해진 율격에 맞춰 써야 해요.
T6-1037.x: Sijo must be written to a fixed meter.
T6-1037.e: Literally 'law pattern' — the fixed rhythmic rules of verse.

T6-1038.ex: 시조는 글자 수와 형식이 정해진 한국의 정형시입니다.
T6-1038.x: Sijo is a Korean fixed-form poem with a set syllable count and structure.
T6-1038.e: Literally 'fixed-type poem' — like sonnets, haiku or Korean sijo.

T6-1039.ex: 요즘 시인들은 형식에 얽매이지 않는 자유시를 많이 써요.
T6-1039.x: Poets these days write a lot of free verse that isn't bound by form.
T6-1039.e: Literally 'free poem' — no fixed meter or line length.

T6-1040.ex: 정철의 관동별곡은 조선 시대의 대표적인 가사입니다.
T6-1040.x: Jeong Cheol's Gwandong Byeolgok is a representative gasa of the Joseon era.
T6-1040.e: Literally 'song words' — long verse in four-beat lines, popular in Joseon.
T6-1040.t: Don't confuse it with homonyms 가사 'song lyrics' and 가사 'housework'; context usually makes it clear.

T6-1041.ex: 향가는 신라 시대에 향찰로 기록된 노래예요.
T6-1041.x: Hyangga are songs from the Silla era recorded in hyangchal script.
T6-1041.e: Literally 'hometown songs' — native Korean songs, as opposed to Chinese poetry.

T6-1042.m: Goryeo songs (folk songs of the Goryeo period)
T6-1042.ex: 청산별곡은 널리 알려진 고려가요 중 하나예요.
T6-1042.x: Cheongsan Byeolgok is one of the well-known Goryeo songs.
T6-1042.e: Literally 'Goryeo songs' — folk songs passed down orally and later written in Hangeul.

T6-1043.ex: 춘향전은 지금도 학교에서 많이 읽히는 고전소설이에요.
T6-1043.x: Chunhyangjeon is a classical novel still widely read in schools today.
T6-1043.e: Literally 'old-classic novel'; 소설 originally meant 'petty talk', minor stories.

T6-1044.ex: 민요, 설화, 판소리는 모두 구비문학에 속해요.
T6-1044.x: Folk songs, tales and pansori all belong to oral literature.
T6-1044.e: Literally 'mouth-monument literature' — kept in memory and passed on by word of mouth.

T6-1045.ex: 이 마을에는 산신령에 관한 설화가 전해 내려와요.
T6-1045.x: A tale about the mountain spirit has been handed down in this village.
T6-1045.e: An umbrella term for myths 신화, legends 전설 and folktales 민담.

T6-1046.ex: 어릴 때 할머니께서 도깨비가 나오는 민담을 자주 들려주셨어요.
T6-1046.x: When I was little, my grandmother often told me folktales with goblins in them.
T6-1046.e: Literally 'people's tales' — stories told by ordinary folk.

T6-1047.ex: 이솝 우화에는 동물이 주인공인 이야기가 많아요.
T6-1047.x: Aesop's Fables has many stories where animals are the main characters.
T6-1047.e: Literally 'lodged talk' — a lesson lodged inside a story, often about animals.

T6-1048.m: the comic, comic humor (as an aesthetic)
T6-1048.ex: 판소리에는 슬픔과 함께 골계의 미가 잘 드러나요.
T6-1048.x: Pansori shows the beauty of the comic as well as sorrow.
T6-1048.e: The first syllable is read 골 here, not its usual reading 활 'slippery'.
T6-1048.t: Mostly in literary criticism: 골계미 'comic beauty', alongside 숭고미, 우아미 and 비장미.

T6-1049.ex: 도둑이 도둑을 맞다니 정말 아이러니한 일이에요.
T6-1049.x: A thief getting robbed — how ironic is that?
T6-1049.t: In literature classes the Sino-Korean term 반어 is used; in daily talk people say 아이러니하다.

T6-1050.x: 'A silent clamor' is an expression that uses paradox.
T6-1050.e: Literally 'reverse-talk method'; -법 = rhetorical device: 과장법, 의인법, 도치법.
T6-1050.t: Pronounced [역썰뻡]; '소리 없는 아우성' (a silent clamor) is the textbook example.

T6-1051.x: 'Eyes as clear as a lake' is an expression that uses a simile.
T6-1051.t: Spot it by 처럼, 같이 or 듯이; without those markers, it's usually 은유 (metaphor).

T6-1052.x: 'The wind whispers to the leaves' is a sentence using personification.
T6-1052.e: Literally 'imitate-person method' — treating things as if they were human.
T6-1052.t: Pronounced [의인뻡] — 법 is tensed in these device names.

T6-1053.x: 'I waited till my eyes fell out' is an expression using hyperbole.
T6-1053.e: Literally 'boast-stretch method' — saying more than is true for effect.

T6-1054.ex: '산은 높고 물은 깊다'는 대구법을 활용한 문장이에요.
T6-1054.x: 'The mountains are high and the waters deep' is a sentence using parallelism.
T6-1054.e: Literally 'paired-phrase method' — matching phrases set side by side.

T6-1055.ex: 이 시는 반복법으로 그리움을 강조하고 있어요.
T6-1055.x: This poem emphasizes longing through repetition.
T6-1055.e: Literally 'repeat method' — repeating words or lines to stress a feeling.

T6-1056.ex: 점층법은 뜻을 점점 크고 강하게 표현하는 방법이에요.
T6-1056.x: Climax is a way of expressing meaning in gradually bigger, stronger steps.
T6-1056.e: Literally 'gradual-layer method' — ideas build up step by step.

T6-1057.x: '보고 싶다, 너를' (literally 'I miss, you') is an expression using inversion.
T6-1057.e: Literally 'overturn-place method' — swapping the normal word order for emphasis.
T6-1057.t: Korean normally ends with the verb, so moving the object after it (보고 싶다, 너를) creates strong emphasis.

T6-1058.ex: '이게 사랑이 아니면 무엇이랴'는 설의법이 쓰인 문장이에요.
T6-1058.x: 'If this isn't love, what is?' is a sentence using a rhetorical question.
T6-1058.e: Literally 'set-up-doubt method' — asking a question whose answer is obvious.

T6-1059.ex: '아, 아름다운 우리 강산이여!'는 영탄법이 쓰인 구절이에요.
T6-1059.x: 'Ah, our beautiful land!' is a line that uses exclamation.
T6-1059.e: Literally 'chant-sigh method' — expressing strong feeling with 아, 오 or -여.

T6-1060.ex: 조지 오웰의 동물농장은 정치를 풍자한 알레고리예요.
T6-1060.x: George Orwell's Animal Farm is an allegory satirizing politics.
T6-1060.e: From English 'allegory'; the Korean literary term is 풍유 or 우의.

T6-1061.ex: 이 시는 색깔을 이용해 선명한 심상을 만들어 내요.
T6-1061.x: This poem uses color to create vivid imagery.
T6-1061.e: Literally 'mind image' — a picture formed in the reader's mind.
T6-1061.t: Textbooks sort 심상 by sense: 시각적, 청각적, 촉각적 심상 (visual, auditory, tactile).

T6-1062.m: poetic diction, words of a poem
T6-1062.x: The most important word in this poem is 'sea.'

T6-1063.ex: 시인은 산책을 하다가 시상이 떠올랐다고 해요.
T6-1063.x: The poet says the idea for the poem came to him on a walk.
T6-1063.e: Literally 'poem thought'; a homonym 시상 means 'awarding prizes'.
T6-1063.t: In exams, 시상 전개 means how the poem's ideas unfold; 시상이 떠오르다 = inspiration strikes.

T6-1064.m: poetic speaker, the speaker of a poem
T6-1064.ex: 이 시의 시적 화자는 떠난 사람을 그리워하고 있어요.
T6-1064.x: The speaker of this poem is longing for someone who left.
T6-1064.e: Literally 'poetic speaking person' — the voice in a poem, not necessarily the poet.
T6-1064.t: Pronounced [시쩍 화자]; don't assume the 화자 is the poet themself.

T6-1065.ex: 그는 차분한 어조로 자신의 의견을 말했어요.
T6-1065.x: He stated his opinion in a calm tone.
T6-1065.e: Literally 'word tune' — the attitude a speaker's words carry.

T6-1066.m: thematic awareness, a work's sense of purpose
T6-1066.ex: 이 영화는 감독의 뚜렷한 주제의식이 돋보여요.
T6-1066.x: This film stands out for the director's clear sense of purpose.
T6-1066.e: Literally 'theme consciousness' — what the author deliberately wants to say.

T6-1067.m: an artist's body of work, artistic world
T6-1067.ex: 이 전시회에서 작가의 작품세계를 한눈에 볼 수 있어요.
T6-1067.x: At this exhibition, you can see the artist's whole body of work at a glance.
T6-1067.e: Literally 'works world' — the themes and style running through all of an artist's works.

T6-1068.ex: 첫 장면은 주인공의 비극적인 결말을 암시해요.
T6-1068.x: The first scene hints at the main character's tragic ending.
T6-1068.t: Usually used as 암시하다 'to hint at'; 복선 is the specific term for plot foreshadowing.

T6-1069.ex: 이 드라마는 이야기 전개가 빨라서 지루하지 않아요.
T6-1069.x: This drama's story moves quickly, so it isn't boring.
T6-1069.e: Literally 'unfold and open' — the stage where the story moves forward.
T6-1069.t: The classic plot stages are 발단, 전개, 위기, 절정, 결말.

T6-1070.ex: 드디어 오늘 밤 드라마가 대단원의 막을 내려요.
T6-1070.x: Tonight the drama finally comes to its grand finale.
T6-1070.e: Literally 'great round circle' — everything coming full circle at the end.
T6-1070.t: Set phrase: 대단원의 막을 내리다 'to come to a grand close'.

T6-1071.ex: 이 소설의 갈등구조는 아버지와 아들 사이에서 시작돼요.
T6-1071.x: The conflict structure of this novel begins between a father and son.
T6-1071.e: Literally 'conflict structure'; 갈등 comes from tangled arrowroot and wisteria vines.
T6-1071.t: Pronounced [갈뜽구조]; the ㄷ after ㄹ is tensed.

T6-1072.forms: 내적 갈등을 겪다 · 내적 갈등에 빠지다
T6-1072.ex: 주인공은 사랑과 의무 사이에서 내적 갈등을 겪어요.
T6-1072.x: The main character goes through an internal conflict between love and duty.
T6-1072.e: Literally 'inner conflict' — a struggle inside a character's mind.
T6-1072.t: Pronounced [내쩍 갈뜽]; the usual verb is 겪다 'to go through'.

T6-1073.forms: 외적 갈등이 생기다 · 외적 갈등을 해결하다
T6-1073.ex: 주인공과 사회 사이의 외적 갈등이 점점 커져요.
T6-1073.x: The external conflict between the main character and society keeps growing.
T6-1073.e: Literally 'outer conflict' — a character against other people, society or nature.

T6-1074.ex: 흥부는 착하고 순진한 인물형을 대표하는 주인공이에요.
T6-1074.x: Heungbu is a main character who represents the kind, innocent type.

T6-1075.ex: 이 소설의 주인공은 성격이 변하는 입체적 인물이에요.
T6-1075.x: The main character of this novel is a round character whose personality changes.
T6-1075.e: Literally 'three-dimensional person' — a character who grows or changes.
T6-1075.t: 입체적 alone means 'three-dimensional' in everyday use, e.g. 입체적인 그림.

T6-1076.ex: 동화 속 악당은 처음부터 끝까지 변하지 않는 평면적 인물이에요.
T6-1076.x: Villains in fairy tales are flat characters who never change from start to finish.
T6-1076.e: Literally 'flat-surface person' — a character whose personality never changes.

T6-1077.ex: 주동인물은 이야기를 이끌어 가는 중심 인물이에요.
T6-1077.x: The protagonist is the central character who drives the story.
T6-1077.e: Literally 'main-moving person' — the character who drives the action.
T6-1077.t: 주인공 is the everyday word; 주동인물 is the class term, always paired with 반동인물.

T6-1078.ex: 이 이야기에서 놀부는 흥부와 대립하는 반동인물이에요.
T6-1078.x: In this story, Nolbu is the antagonist who opposes Heungbu.
T6-1078.e: Literally 'counter-moving person' — the character who opposes the protagonist.
T6-1078.t: 반동 on its own also means 'reactionary' in politics.

T6-1079.ex: 액자소설은 이야기 속에 또 다른 이야기가 들어 있는 형식이에요.
T6-1079.x: A frame story is a form with another story inside the story.
T6-1079.e: Literally 'picture-frame novel' — an outer story framing an inner one.

T6-1080.ex: 이 성장소설은 한 소년이 어른이 되는 과정을 그려요.
T6-1080.x: This coming-of-age novel depicts a boy's journey to adulthood.

T6-1081.ex: 괴테의 빌헬름 마이스터는 대표적인 교양소설로 꼽혀요.
T6-1081.x: Goethe's Wilhelm Meister is considered a classic Bildungsroman.
T6-1081.e: A translation of German 'Bildungsroman' — literally 'cultivation novel'.
T6-1081.t: Close to 성장소설, but stresses the hero's intellectual and moral growth; used mostly for European novels.

T6-1082.ex: 이 역사소설은 조선 시대 궁궐을 배경으로 해요.
T6-1082.x: This historical novel is set in a Joseon-era royal palace.

T6-1083.ex: 어릴 때부터 공상과학 영화를 정말 좋아했어요.
T6-1083.x: I've really loved sci-fi movies since I was a kid.
T6-1083.t: Usually modifies a noun: 공상과학 소설, 공상과학 영화; SF (에스에프) is also very common.

T6-1084.ex: 여행을 다녀와서 짧은 기행문을 써 봤어요.
T6-1084.x: After coming back from my trip, I tried writing a short travelogue.
T6-1084.e: Literally 'recording-travel writing' — an account of one's journey.

T6-1085.ex: 그는 소설가이면서 문학평론도 꾸준히 쓰고 있어요.
T6-1085.x: He is a novelist but also steadily writes literary criticism.
T6-1085.t: Pronounced [문학평논]: ㄹ after ㅇ becomes ㄴ (the ㅎ is kept in standard pronunciation).

T6-1086.ex: 신문에 실린 서평을 읽고 그 책을 샀어요.
T6-1086.x: I bought that book after reading a review in the newspaper.
T6-1086.t: 독후감 is a personal book report, usually for school; 서평 evaluates a book for other readers.

T6-1087.m: introductory notes (on a text), bibliographical commentary
T6-1087.ex: 책 뒤에 실린 해제를 읽으면 작품을 더 깊이 이해할 수 있어요.
T6-1087.x: Reading the notes at the back of the book helps you understand the work more deeply.
T6-1087.e: Literally 'explaining the title'; a homonym 해제 means lifting a ban or alert.

T6-1088.ex: 이 고전은 주해가 자세해서 읽기 쉬워요.
T6-1088.x: This classic is easy to read because its annotations are detailed.
T6-1088.e: Literally 'note and explain' — notes that explain a difficult text.

T6-1089.ex: 어려운 단어에는 페이지 아래에 주석이 달려 있어요.
T6-1089.x: Difficult words have notes at the bottom of the page.
T6-1089.e: Literally 'note and interpret'; homonyms mean 'tin' and 'chairman'.
T6-1089.t: Collocation: 주석을 달다 'to add notes'; programmers also use 주석 for a code comment.

T6-1090.ex: 이 소설은 영어 번역본으로 먼저 읽었어요.
T6-1090.x: I first read this novel in its English translation.
T6-1090.e: Literally 'translated copy'; -본 = edition or copy: 원본, 판본.

T6-1091.ex: 이 시집은 판본마다 내용이 조금씩 달라요.
T6-1091.x: The contents of this poetry collection differ slightly from edition to edition.
T6-1091.e: Literally 'print-block copy' — originally a book printed from woodblocks.

T6-1092.x: The first edition of this book was published in 1950.
T6-1092.t: 초판 1쇄 means 'first edition, first printing', the copy collectors want most.

T6-1093.ex: 그 책은 이미 절판되어서 구하기가 어려워요.
T6-1093.x: That book is already out of print, so it's hard to find.
T6-1093.t: Usually used as the verb 절판되다 'to go out of print.'

T6-1094.ex: 할아버지는 조선 시대의 고서를 많이 모으셨어요.
T6-1094.x: My grandfather collected many old books from the Joseon era.

T6-1095.ex: 이 소설의 필사본이 한 박물관에서 발견되었습니다.
T6-1095.x: A handwritten copy of this novel was discovered in a museum.
T6-1095.e: Literally 'brush-copied edition' — copied out by hand.
T6-1095.t: Pronounced [필싸본]; -본 means 'edition, copy,' as in 목판본, 활자본, 번역본.

T6-1096.ex: 이 책은 조선 시대에 찍은 목판본이에요.
T6-1096.x: This book is a woodblock edition printed in the Joseon era.

T6-1097.m: book printed with movable type, movable-type edition
T6-1097.ex: 고려 시대에 이미 금속 활자본이 만들어졌습니다.
T6-1097.x: Books printed with metal movable type were already made in the Goryeo era.
T6-1097.e: Literally 'living-letter edition' — the type pieces move and can be reused.
T6-1097.t: Pronounced [활짜본] — the ㅈ after ㄹ is tensed.

T6-1098.ex: 이 도서관은 장서가 백만 권이 넘어요.
T6-1098.x: This library has a collection of over a million books.

T6-1099.ex: 이 영화는 제작비만 300억 원이 든 대작이에요.
T6-1099.x: This movie is a blockbuster that cost 30 billion won just to make.
T6-1099.e: Literally 'big work' — large in scale or ambition.
T6-1099.t: -작 means 'a work' and builds many words: 대작, 역작, 수작, 졸작, 유작, 습작.

T6-1100.m: work of great effort, labor of love, masterpiece
T6-1100.ex: 이 소설은 작가가 10년 동안 공들여 쓴 역작입니다.
T6-1100.x: This novel is a labor of love the author spent ten years writing.
T6-1100.e: Literally 'strength work' — made with tremendous effort.
T6-1100.t: Pronounced [역짝]; often paired with 심혈을 기울인 'poured heart and soul into.'

T6-1101.x: Many excellent works were entered in this year's film festival.
T6-1101.t: Don't confuse it with 수작 'ploy, come-on' (酬酌), as in 수작을 부리다 'to play tricks.'

T6-1102.x: It's a humble effort, but thank you for reading it to the end.
T6-1102.t: Writers humbly call their own work 졸작; saying it about someone else's work is a harsh insult.

T6-1103.ex: 그는 대학 시절에 습작으로 시를 많이 썼어요.
T6-1103.x: He wrote a lot of poems as practice pieces in college.

T6-1104.ex: 이 그림은 화가가 세상을 떠나기 전에 남긴 유작입니다.
T6-1104.x: This painting is the last work the artist left before passing away.

T6-1105.m: first work, maiden work, debut work
T6-1105.ex: 그의 처녀작은 출간되자마자 큰 인기를 얻었어요.
T6-1105.x: His first work became hugely popular as soon as it was published.
T6-1105.e: 처녀 'maiden' + -작 'work': an author's very first published work.
T6-1105.t: 데뷔작 is the more modern, neutral word for the same idea.

T6-1106.ex: 이 영화는 감독의 데뷔작이라고 믿기 어려울 만큼 훌륭해요.
T6-1106.x: This movie is so good it's hard to believe it's the director's debut.

T6-1107.m: series of linked works, cycle (of stories, poems, paintings)
T6-1107.ex: 그 작가는 바다를 주제로 한 연작 소설을 발표했어요.
T6-1107.x: That writer published a linked series of stories about the sea.
T6-1107.t: 연작 is separate works sharing a theme; 연재 is one work published in installments.

T6-1108.ex: 그는 중편 소설 두 편을 묶어 책으로 냈어요.
T6-1108.x: He put two novellas together and published them as a book.
T6-1108.e: Literally 'medium piece' — between 단편 'short' and 장편 'long.'

T6-1109.m: omnibus, anthology (film or book of separate stories)
T6-1109.ex: 이 영화는 세 감독이 함께 만든 옴니버스 영화예요.
T6-1109.x: This movie is an anthology film made by three directors.
T6-1109.e: From English 'omnibus' — in Korea it mostly means a film or drama of separate short stories.

T6-1110.ex: 이 소설은 고전 작품과의 상호텍스트성이 뚜렷해요.
T6-1110.x: This novel shows clear intertextuality with classic works.
T6-1110.e: 상호 'mutual' + English 'text' + -성 '-ness': texts echoing each other.

T6-1111.ex: 해석학은 텍스트를 이해하는 방법을 연구하는 학문입니다.
T6-1111.x: Hermeneutics is the discipline that studies how texts are understood.
T6-1111.e: Literally 'the study of untying and explaining.'
T6-1111.t: Pronounced [해서칵] — ㄱ and ㅎ merge into an aspirated ㅋ.

T6-1112.ex: 수용미학에서는 독자의 역할을 특히 중요하게 봅니다.
T6-1112.x: Reception aesthetics places special importance on the reader's role.
T6-1112.e: Literally 'aesthetics of receiving' — a work's meaning is completed by its readers.

T6-1113.ex: 독자반응 비평은 독자가 작품의 의미를 만든다고 봅니다.
T6-1113.x: Reader-response criticism holds that readers create a work's meaning.
T6-1113.e: Literally 'reader's response'; -자 = person who does it: 독자, 저자, 작자.
T6-1113.t: Usually seen in the phrase 독자반응 비평 'reader-response criticism'; pronounced [독짜바능].

T6-1114.m: well-written prose, fine piece of writing
T6-1114.x: His speech is still regarded as a fine piece of writing.
T6-1114.t: 명문 also means 'prestigious school or family' (名門), as in 명문대; context tells you which.

T6-1115.x: That writer is famous for ornate, elegant prose.
T6-1115.e: Literally 'beautiful writing' — sometimes hints at style over substance.

T6-1116.x: It's a clumsy piece of writing, but I'd welcome your feedback.
T6-1116.e: Literally 'clumsy writing' — often a humble word for one's own writing.

T6-1117.ex: 작가는 원고를 열 번 넘게 퇴고했어요.
T6-1117.x: The author revised the manuscript more than ten times.
T6-1117.e: From a Chinese poet who agonized over 'push' or 'knock' for a single line of verse.
T6-1117.t: 퇴고 is revising your own writing; 교정 is fixing errors, often by someone else.

T6-1118.m: finishing a manuscript, completing a draft
T6-1118.x: The author finished the manuscript of the novel after three years.
T6-1118.e: Literally 'shedding the manuscript' — finally done with it.

T6-1119.ex: 번역 원고를 출판하기 전에 전문가에게 윤문을 맡겼어요.
T6-1119.x: Before publishing, we had an expert polish the translated manuscript.
T6-1119.e: Literally 'moistening the writing' — making it read smoothly.
T6-1119.t: 윤문 polishes a text's style; 교정 fixes typos and other errors.

T6-1120.ex: 인쇄하기 전에 교정을 꼼꼼히 봐야 해요.
T6-1120.x: You need to proofread carefully before printing.
T6-1120.t: 교정을 보다 means 'to proofread'; another 교정 (矯正) means straightening, as in 치아 교정 'braces.'

T6-1121.m: copyediting, checking a text for errors and accuracy
T6-1121.ex: 이 원고는 교열 과정에서 많은 오류가 고쳐졌어요.
T6-1121.x: Many errors in this manuscript were fixed during copyediting.
T6-1121.e: Literally 'check and review' — goes deeper than proofreading, covering facts and wording.

T6-1122.ex: 그 교수는 은퇴 후에도 활발하게 저술 활동을 하고 있어요.
T6-1122.x: That professor is still actively writing books after retiring.

T6-1123.ex: 그 학자는 자기 저서보다 역서가 더 많아요.
T6-1123.x: That scholar has more translated books than books of his own.
T6-1123.t: Pronounced [역써]; contrast with 저서 'book one wrote.'

T6-1124.m: compiled and written work, edited volume
T6-1124.ex: 이 책은 김 교수의 편저로 출판되었습니다.
T6-1124.x: This book was published as a volume compiled and written by Professor Kim.
T6-1124.e: Literally 'compile and write' — partly the editor's own writing, partly collected material.

T6-1125.ex: 그 선비의 문집에는 시와 편지가 함께 실려 있어요.
T6-1125.x: That scholar's collected writings include both poems and letters.
T6-1125.e: Literally 'writing collection' — traditionally one scholar's collected works.

T6-1126.ex: 이 책은 한국 현대 시 선집이에요.
T6-1126.x: This book is an anthology of modern Korean poetry.
T6-1126.t: 선집 contains selected pieces, while 전집 contains everything.

T6-1127.ex: 대학생 때 셰익스피어 전집을 다 읽었어요.
T6-1127.x: I read the complete works of Shakespeare in college.

T6-1128.ex: 그 출판사는 세계 문학 총서를 100권째 냈어요.
T6-1128.x: That publisher has released the 100th volume of its world literature series.
T6-1128.e: Literally 'cluster of books' — a numbered series from one publisher.

T6-1129.m: life story, chronicle of someone's life
T6-1129.ex: 이 영화는 한 독립운동가의 일대기를 그렸어요.
T6-1129.x: This movie depicts the life story of an independence activist.
T6-1129.t: Pronounced [일때기]; often used with 그리다 'to depict,' as in 일대기를 그리다.

T6-1130.x: I bought a critical biography of a poet at the bookstore.
T6-1130.e: Literally 'critiqued biography' — tells a life while evaluating it.

T6-1131.ex: 어릴 때 위인 전기를 많이 읽었어요.
T6-1131.x: When I was little, I read a lot of biographies of great people.
T6-1131.t: 전기 also means 'electricity' (電氣) and 'first half' (前期); context tells you which.

T6-1132.ex: 그 조각가는 나무와 돌을 이용한 조형 작업으로 유명해요.
T6-1132.x: That sculptor is famous for shaping works out of wood and stone.

T6-1133.x: This pottery is simple, but its beauty of form is outstanding.
T6-1133.e: Literally 'beauty of shaping' — beauty in form and structure.

T6-1134.ex: 회화와 조각, 건축은 모두 대표적인 조형예술입니다.
T6-1134.x: Painting, sculpture and architecture are all typical examples of the visual arts.

T6-1135.ex: 이 수묵화는 먹의 진하고 옅은 정도만으로 산을 표현했어요.
T6-1135.x: This ink-wash painting depicts mountains using only darker and lighter ink.
T6-1135.t: Pronounced [수무콰] — ㄱ and ㅎ merge into an aspirated ㅋ.

T6-1136.x: I viewed Joseon-era landscape paintings at the museum.

T6-1137.m: genre painting, painting of everyday life
T6-1137.ex: 김홍도의 풍속화에는 서민들의 생활이 잘 나타나 있어요.
T6-1137.x: Kim Hong-do's genre paintings vividly show the lives of ordinary people.
T6-1137.e: Literally 'customs painting' — scenes of ordinary daily life.
T6-1137.t: Pronounced [풍소콰]; Kim Hong-do and Shin Yun-bok are the classic Joseon genre painters.

T6-1138.ex: 호랑이와 까치는 민화에 자주 나오는 소재예요.
T6-1138.x: Tigers and magpies are common subjects in Korean folk painting.
T6-1138.e: Literally 'people's painting' — colorful, usually anonymous folk art.

T6-1139.ex: 조선의 선비들은 대나무나 매화를 그린 문인화를 즐겼어요.
T6-1139.x: Joseon scholars enjoyed literati paintings of bamboo and plum blossoms.
T6-1139.e: Literally 'scholar's painting' — done by educated amateurs, not professional painters.

T6-1140.ex: 이 병풍에는 아름다운 화조도가 그려져 있어요.
T6-1140.x: This folding screen has a beautiful bird-and-flower painting on it.

T6-1141.ex: 그 화가는 주로 노인들의 인물화를 그려요.
T6-1141.x: That painter mostly paints portraits of elderly people.

T6-1142.ex: 미술 시간에 사과와 꽃병으로 정물화를 그렸어요.
T6-1142.x: In art class we painted a still life of apples and a vase.

T6-1143.ex: 그 성당 천장에는 유명한 프레스코 벽화가 있어요.
T6-1143.x: That cathedral has a famous fresco on its ceiling.
T6-1143.e: From Italian 'fresco' ('fresh') — painted on wet plaster.

T6-1144.ex: 미대 입시를 준비하면서 매일 소묘를 연습했어요.
T6-1144.x: While preparing for art school entrance exams, I practiced drawing every day.
T6-1144.e: Literally 'plain depiction' — line and shading without color.
T6-1144.t: 소묘 and 데생 mean the same thing; 소묘 sounds a bit more formal.

T6-1145.x: Pencil drawing is the foundation of all painting.

T6-1146.x: Using perspective gives a picture a sense of depth.
T6-1146.t: Pronounced [원근뻡] — the ㅂ of -법 is tensed.

T6-1147.m: light and shade, chiaroscuro; bright and dark sides
T6-1147.ex: 명암을 잘 표현하면 사물이 더 입체적으로 보여요.
T6-1147.x: If you render light and shade well, objects look more three-dimensional.
T6-1147.e: Literally 'bright and dark' — also used for the good and bad sides of something.
T6-1147.t: Figuratively, 명암이 엇갈리다 means 'fortunes diverged' — some came out ahead, others behind.

T6-1148.x: After drawing the sketch, I colored it in with paint.
T6-1148.e: Both syllables mean 'color' — filling a drawing with color.

T6-1149.ex: 이 그림은 전체적으로 따뜻한 색조를 띠고 있어요.
T6-1149.x: This painting has a warm tone overall.
T6-1149.t: Pronounced [색쪼]; in beauty stores, 색조 화장품 means color cosmetics like lipstick and eyeshadow.

T6-1150.ex: 이 화가는 물감을 두껍게 칠해서 거친 질감을 살렸어요.
T6-1150.x: This painter applied paint thickly to bring out a rough texture.

T6-1151.x: Please leave plenty of blank space on the paper.
T6-1151.e: Literally 'leftover white' — the unpainted or unwritten part of the page.

T6-1152.forms: 여백의 미를 살리다 · 여백의 미가 느껴지다
T6-1152.m: beauty of empty space, aesthetic of restraint
T6-1152.ex: 한국 전통 그림은 여백의 미를 잘 살려요.
T6-1152.x: Traditional Korean paintings make good use of the beauty of empty space.
T6-1152.e: A key idea in Korean aesthetics: what's left empty matters as much as what's painted.
T6-1152.t: Used beyond art, too — for design, architecture, even a simply decorated room.

T6-1153.x: The painter captured the scenery of his hometown on canvas.
T6-1153.e: Literally 'painting width' — the cloth or paper a picture is painted on.
T6-1153.t: Common pattern: ~을/를 화폭에 담다 'to capture something on canvas.'

T6-1154.ex: 김 화백은 올해로 화가 생활 50년을 맞았습니다.
T6-1154.x: Master painter Kim marks fifty years as an artist this year.
T6-1154.e: Literally 'painting elder' — a respectful title for an established painter.
T6-1154.t: Used as a title after a name, like 김 화백; never use it about yourself.

T6-1155.ex: 그녀는 젊은 나이에 한국 화단의 주목을 받았어요.
T6-1155.x: She drew the attention of the Korean art world at a young age.
T6-1155.e: Literally 'painting platform' — the community of painters.
T6-1155.t: Homonym: 화단 (花壇) means 'flower bed,' a far more everyday word.

T6-1156.x: On the weekend I saw an exhibition at a gallery in Insa-dong.
T6-1156.t: Not to be confused with 화랑 (花郞), the elite youth corps of ancient Silla.

T6-1157.ex: 국립현대미술관에서 그 화가의 회고전이 열리고 있어요.
T6-1157.x: A retrospective of that painter is being held at the National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art.

T6-1158.ex: 이번 기획전은 한국 근대 미술을 주제로 합니다.
T6-1158.x: This special exhibition focuses on modern Korean art.
T6-1158.e: Literally 'planned exhibition' — organized around a theme.

T6-1159.ex: 광주 비엔날레는 2년마다 열리는 국제 미술 전시예요.
T6-1159.x: The Gwangju Biennale is an international art exhibition held every two years.
T6-1159.t: Pronounced [비엔날레]; Korea's best-known is the Gwangju Biennale, started in 1995.

T6-1160.ex: 전문가들은 그 그림이 진품이라고 결론을 내렸어요.
T6-1160.x: The experts concluded that the painting was genuine.

T6-1161.ex: 미술을 공부하는 학생들은 명화의 모작을 그리며 연습해요.
T6-1161.x: Art students practice by painting copies of famous paintings.
T6-1161.t: 모작 is an open copy made for study; 위작 is a forgery meant to deceive.

T6-1162.ex: 박물관 기념품 가게에서 유명한 그림의 복제품을 팔아요.
T6-1162.x: The museum gift shop sells reproductions of famous paintings.
T6-1162.t: Pronounced [복쩨품] — the ㅈ after ㄱ is tensed.

T6-1163.ex: 할머니가 물려주신 도자기의 감정을 받아 봤어요.
T6-1163.x: I had the pottery my grandmother left me appraised.
T6-1163.t: Different from 감정 'emotion' (感情); appraisal usually appears as 감정을 받다 or 감정을 의뢰하다.

T6-1164.ex: 감정가는 그 그림의 가치를 10억 원으로 평가했어요.
T6-1164.x: The appraiser valued the painting at one billion won.
T6-1164.e: -가 = expert or professional: 감정가, 작가, 화가.
T6-1164.t: 감정가 can also mean 'appraised price' (鑑定價), pronounced [감정까], as in 감정가 1억 원.

T6-1165.ex: 소조는 흙을 붙여 가며 형태를 만드는 기법이에요.
T6-1165.x: Modeling is a technique of building up a form by adding clay.
T6-1165.e: Literally 'molding and making' — building form up, the opposite of carving.
T6-1165.t: 소조 adds material and 조각 carves it away; together they make up 조소 'sculpture.'

T6-1166.ex: 이 탑의 벽면에는 불상이 부조로 새겨져 있어요.
T6-1166.x: Buddha figures are carved in relief on the walls of this pagoda.
T6-1166.e: Literally 'floating carving' — figures rise from a flat surface.
T6-1166.t: Homonym: 부조 (扶助) means a cash gift at weddings or funerals, an everyday word.

T6-1167.ex: 전시장 한가운데에 거대한 설치미술 작품이 놓여 있었어요.
T6-1167.x: A huge installation art piece stood in the middle of the exhibition hall.

T6-1168.ex: 그 작가는 거리에서 행위예술 공연을 펼쳤어요.
T6-1168.x: The artist staged a performance art piece on the street.
T6-1168.e: Literally 'act art' — the artist's actions are the artwork.

T6-1169.ex: 요즘 취미로 도예 수업을 듣고 있어요.
T6-1169.x: These days I'm taking a pottery class as a hobby.

T6-1170.ex: 고려청자는 은은하고 아름다운 푸른빛으로 세계적으로 유명해요.
T6-1170.x: Goryeo celadon is world famous for its subtle, beautiful blue-green color.
T6-1170.e: Literally 'blue-green porcelain' — Goryeo celadon is world famous.
T6-1170.t: Pronounce it [청자]; 고려청자 'Goryeo celadon' and 조선백자 'Joseon white porcelain' are the classic pair.

T6-1171.ex: 조선 시대에는 깨끗하고 단순한 백자가 크게 유행했어요.
T6-1171.x: In the Joseon era, clean and simple white porcelain was hugely popular.
T6-1171.t: Remember the pair: 고려청자 (Goryeo celadon) and 조선백자 (Joseon white porcelain).

T6-1172.m: buncheong ware, gray stoneware coated with white slip
T6-1172.x: Buncheong ware is known for its free, unpretentious patterns.
T6-1172.e: Literally 'powdered blue-green sand vessel': gray clay brushed with white slip.

T6-1173.x: Goryeo celadon is famous for its unique inlay technique.
T6-1173.e: A design is carved into the surface, then filled with clay of another color.
T6-1173.t: Usually appears in compounds: 상감 기법 (inlay technique), 상감청자 (inlaid celadon).

T6-1174.ex: 옻칠을 한 그릇은 오래 써도 쉽게 상하지 않아요.
T6-1174.x: Lacquered bowls don't get damaged easily even after long use.
T6-1174.t: 옻이 오르다 means to get a rash from lacquer sap, a common allergic reaction.

T6-1175.ex: 할머니 댁에는 오래된 나전칠기 장롱이 있어요.
T6-1175.x: My grandmother's house has an old mother-of-pearl lacquered wardrobe.
T6-1175.e: Shell pieces are inlaid into wood, then coated with lacquer.
T6-1175.t: In everyday speech people often say 자개 for the shell inlay, as in 자개장 (inlaid wardrobe).

T6-1176.ex: 요즘 취미로 목공예를 배우는 사람이 많아요.
T6-1176.x: These days many people learn woodworking as a hobby.

T6-1177.ex: 발표 자료에는 읽기 쉬운 서체를 쓰는 게 좋아요.
T6-1177.x: It's best to use an easy-to-read font in presentation slides.
T6-1177.e: Literally 'writing style'; covers both brush styles and computer fonts.
T6-1177.t: For a person's own handwriting, use 필체 or 글씨체; 서체 leans toward designed styles and fonts.

T6-1178.ex: 편지의 필체를 보고 누가 썼는지 바로 알았어요.
T6-1178.x: I knew right away who wrote the letter from the handwriting.
T6-1178.e: Literally 'brush style': the way a person's hand shapes letters.

T6-1179.m: brush calligraphy, writing with a brush
T6-1179.ex: 방학 동안 서예 학원에서 붓글씨를 배웠어요.
T6-1179.x: I learned brush calligraphy at a calligraphy school over the break.
T6-1179.t: Pronounced [붇끌씨]: the batchim ㅅ sounds like ㄷ and tenses the next consonant.

T6-1180.m: the four treasures of the study (brush, ink, paper, inkstone)
T6-1180.ex: 옛날 선비들은 문방사우를 무척 소중히 여겼습니다.
T6-1180.x: Scholars of old treasured the four treasures of the study.
T6-1180.e: Literally 'four friends of the study': brush, ink stick, paper and inkstone.

T6-1181.ex: 이 절은 자연과 어울리는 건축미로 잘 알려져 있어요.
T6-1181.x: This temple is well known for architectural beauty that blends with nature.
T6-1181.e: -미 = a kind of beauty: 건축미, 곡선미, 균형미, 절제미.
T6-1181.t: Pronounced [건충미]: ㄱ before ㅁ becomes ㅇ (nasalization).

T6-1183.ex: 유럽 여행에서 고딕 성당을 여러 곳 구경했어요.
T6-1183.x: I visited several Gothic cathedrals on my trip to Europe.
T6-1183.e: From English 'Gothic'. Surprise: 고딕체 is the Korean name for sans-serif fonts.

T6-1184.x: Bach is the leading composer of the Baroque period.
T6-1184.e: From 'Baroque', via French; note the extra vowel: 바-로-크.

T6-1185.ex: 르네상스 시대에는 미술과 과학이 함께 발전했어요.
T6-1185.x: During the Renaissance, art and science developed together.
T6-1185.e: From French 'Renaissance' (rebirth); also used for any revival or golden age.
T6-1185.t: Used figuratively too: 한국 영화의 르네상스 means a golden age of Korean film.

T6-1186.x: Wearing hanbok gives off a sense of classical beauty.
T6-1186.e: Literally 'classic beauty'; also praises a person's traditional, elegant looks.

T6-1187.ex: 이 탑은 좌우 대칭이 완벽해서 균형미가 뛰어나요.
T6-1187.x: This pagoda has perfect symmetry, so its balance is outstanding.

T6-1188.x: Hanok roofs are beautiful for their soft curves.
T6-1188.t: Said of a person, it praises body shape, so use it carefully outside art contexts.

T6-1189.ex: 그의 시는 감정을 아끼는 절제미가 돋보입니다.
T6-1189.x: His poetry stands out for the beauty of holding emotions back.
T6-1189.e: Literally 'self-control beauty': saying more with less.

T6-1190.ex: 이 그릇은 장식이 없어서 오히려 소박미가 있어요.
T6-1190.x: This bowl has no decoration, which actually gives it a simple charm.
T6-1190.t: Pronounced [소방미]: ㄱ before ㅁ becomes ㅇ (nasalization).

T6-1191.ex: 좋은 작품을 고르려면 뛰어난 심미안이 필요해요.
T6-1191.x: To choose good works, you need a keen eye for beauty.
T6-1191.t: Common collocation: 심미안을 기르다 means to develop an eye for beauty.

T6-1192.ex: 한국 도자기에는 한국인의 미의식이 잘 담겨 있어요.
T6-1192.x: Korean ceramics capture the Korean aesthetic sense well.
T6-1192.e: Literally 'beauty awareness': what a person or culture finds beautiful.

T6-1193.x: Even while ill, the painter poured his whole soul into his art.
T6-1193.e: Literally 'art soul': deep devotion to one's art.
T6-1193.t: Often paired with burning verbs: 예술혼을 불태우다 (to pour one's soul into art).

T6-1194.ex: 그 작가는 나이가 들어도 창작열이 식지 않았어요.
T6-1194.x: That writer's creative passion didn't cool even as he grew older.
T6-1194.e: -열 = fever for something: 창작열, 교육열, 학구열.
T6-1194.t: Pronounced [창장녈]: an ㄴ sound is added before 열, then ㄱ nasalizes to ㅇ.

T6-1195.ex: 이 곡은 단순한 멜로디에 풍부한 화성을 더했어요.
T6-1195.x: This piece adds rich harmony to a simple melody.
T6-1195.e: Literally 'harmonized sounds'. Homonym alert: 화성 is also Mars and the city Hwaseong.

T6-1196.ex: 할아버지는 흥겨운 가락에 맞춰 어깨춤을 추셨어요.
T6-1196.x: Grandpa danced with his shoulders to the cheerful tune.
T6-1196.e: Homonym: 가락 also means a long thin piece, as in 손가락 and 젓가락.
T6-1196.t: Also a counter for thin strands: 국수 한 가락 means one strand of noodles.

T6-1197.m: rhythmic cycle (in Korean traditional music), beat; length (long and short)
T6-1197.ex: 고수가 북으로 장단을 맞추면 소리꾼이 노래를 시작해요.
T6-1197.x: When the drummer sets the rhythm on the drum, the singer begins.
T6-1197.e: Literally 'long and short': the pattern of strong and weak beats.
T6-1197.t: 장단을 맞추다 means to keep the beat, and figuratively to go along with someone.

T6-1198.ex: 한국 전통 음악은 주로 다섯 개의 음으로 된 음계를 사용합니다.
T6-1198.x: Korean traditional music mainly uses a scale made of five notes.
T6-1198.e: Literally 'sound steps', like a staircase of notes.

T6-1199.m: interval; pitch accuracy, being in tune
T6-1199.ex: 노래는 잘하는데 높은 음에서 음정이 자꾸 틀려요.
T6-1199.x: She sings well, but she keeps going off pitch on the high notes.
T6-1199.e: Literally 'sound distance': the gap between two notes.
T6-1199.t: 음정이 불안하다 or 음정이 틀리다 is how Koreans say someone sings off-key.

T6-1200.ex: 그 가수는 맑고 독특한 음색으로 사랑받고 있어요.
T6-1200.x: That singer is loved for her clear, distinctive voice.
T6-1200.e: Literally 'sound color', just like English 'tone color'.

T6-1201.ex: 이 노래는 음역이 넓어서 부르기가 어려워요.
T6-1201.x: This song has a wide range, so it's hard to sing.
T6-1201.e: Literally 'sound territory'. Homonym alert: 음역 also means 'transliteration'.
T6-1201.t: Pronounced [으멱]: the batchim ㅁ links over to the vowel of 역.

T6-1202.ex: 새 정책을 두고 정부 안에서 불협화음이 생겼습니다.
T6-1202.x: Discord arose within the government over the new policy.
T6-1202.t: In the news it usually means friction between people or groups, not music: 불협화음이 나다/생기다.

T6-1203.x: Consonant chords sound stable and comfortable to the ear.

T6-1204.ex: 현대 음악 중에는 조성이 없는 곡도 많아요.
T6-1204.x: Many modern pieces have no tonality at all.
T6-1204.e: Homonym alert: 조성 more often means 'creating', as in 공원 조성.

T6-1205.ex: 장조로 된 곡은 대체로 밝고 경쾌하게 들려요.
T6-1205.x: Pieces in a major key generally sound bright and lively.
T6-1205.e: Keys use Korean letter names: 다장조 = C major, 사장조 = G major.

T6-1206.ex: 이 노래는 단조라서 그런지 조금 슬프게 들려요.
T6-1206.x: Maybe because it's in a minor key, this song sounds a bit sad.
T6-1206.e: Homonym alert: 단조롭다 'monotonous' comes from a different 단조.

T6-1207.ex: 연주자는 익숙한 멜로디에 재미있는 변주를 넣었어요.
T6-1207.x: The performer added fun variations to a familiar melody.
T6-1207.t: Used figuratively for retelling a story in new ways: 같은 이야기의 변주.

T6-1208.x: Mozart wrote variations on 'Twinkle, Twinkle, Little Star.'
T6-1208.e: -곡 = a musical piece: 변주곡, 협주곡, 교향곡.

T6-1209.ex: 오늘 연주회에서 베토벤의 피아노 소나타를 들었어요.
T6-1209.x: At today's concert, I heard a Beethoven piano sonata.

T6-1210.ex: 그 바이올리니스트는 다음 달에 첫 독주회를 엽니다.
T6-1210.x: That violinist is holding her first solo recital next month.
T6-1210.t: For singers, use 독창회; 독주회 is for instrumentalists.

T6-1211.ex: 동아리 친구들과 매주 토요일에 합주를 해요.
T6-1211.x: I play together with my club friends every Saturday.
T6-1211.t: Pair it with its singing twin: 합주 for instruments, 합창 for voices.

T6-1212.m: ensemble with one player per part (duet, trio, quartet...)
T6-1212.ex: 네 명의 연주자가 아름다운 현악 사중주를 들려주었습니다.
T6-1212.x: Four players performed a beautiful string quartet.
T6-1212.e: Add a number: 이중주 duet, 삼중주 trio, 사중주 quartet, 오중주 quintet.

T6-1213.m: performing with (as a soloist with an orchestra), joint performance
T6-1213.ex: 그 피아니스트는 서울시향과 협연을 하게 되었어요.
T6-1213.x: That pianist will be performing with the Seoul Philharmonic.

T6-1214.ex: 이 영화 음악은 웅장한 관현악으로 연주되었어요.
T6-1214.x: This film score was performed as grand orchestral music.
T6-1214.e: Literally 'pipe and string music': winds plus strings.

T6-1215.ex: 시립 관현악단이 공원에서 무료 공연을 합니다.
T6-1215.x: The city orchestra is giving a free performance in the park.
T6-1215.t: In casual speech, 오케스트라 is far more common.

T6-1216.ex: 이번 주말에 교향악단의 정기 공연을 보러 가요.
T6-1216.x: This weekend I'm going to see the symphony orchestra's regular concert.
T6-1216.t: Often shortened in names: 서울시향 is short for 서울시립교향악단.

T6-1217.ex: 작은 공연장에서 듣는 실내악은 특별한 매력이 있어요.
T6-1217.x: Chamber music heard in a small hall has a special charm.
T6-1217.e: Literally 'indoor music', a calque of 'chamber music'.
T6-1217.t: Pronounced [실래악]: ㄴ after ㄹ turns into ㄹ (liquidization).

T6-1218.ex: 저는 대학에서 성악이 아니라 기악을 전공했어요.
T6-1218.x: In college I majored in instrumental music, not voice.
T6-1218.e: Literally 'instrument music'; the opposite of 성악, vocal music.

T6-1219.m: jeongak, Korean court and aristocratic classical music
T6-1219.x: Jeongak is characterized by its slow, graceful style.
T6-1219.e: Literally 'proper music', in contrast to folk music (민속악).

T6-1220.m: sanjo, solo instrumental folk music with drum accompaniment
T6-1220.ex: 가야금 산조는 느린 장단에서 시작해 점점 빨라져요.
T6-1220.x: Gayageum sanjo starts with a slow rhythm and gradually speeds up.
T6-1220.e: Literally 'scattered melodies': a free-flowing solo genre.

T6-1221.ex: 거문고 소리는 낮고 묵직해서 마음을 차분하게 해요.
T6-1221.x: The geomungo's low, heavy sound calms the mind.
T6-1221.e: Probably from an old word 고 'zither', also seen in 가얏고, another name for 가야금.
T6-1221.t: Unlike the finger-plucked 가야금, the 거문고 is struck with a bamboo stick called 술대.

T6-1222.ex: 해금의 애절한 소리가 사람의 목소리처럼 들렸어요.
T6-1222.x: The haegeum's sorrowful sound sounded like a human voice.
T6-1222.e: Named after the Xi, a northern nomadic people; a bowed two-string fiddle.

T6-1223.ex: 대금 연주를 들으면 바람 소리가 떠올라요.
T6-1223.x: Listening to the daegeum reminds me of the sound of the wind.
T6-1223.e: Literally 'big flute'. Homonym alert: 대금 also means 'payment, price'.

T6-1224.m: pungmul, Korean folk percussion music and dance; scenery and customs of a place
T6-1224.ex: 마을 축제에서 사람들이 풍물을 치며 행진했어요.
T6-1224.x: At the village festival, people marched while playing pungmul.
T6-1224.e: Originally 'scenery and things of a place'; later the folk percussion played at village events.
T6-1224.t: The verb is 치다: 풍물을 치다, like 북을 치다 for drums.

T6-1225.x: Nongak was inscribed as UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage in 2014.
T6-1225.e: Literally 'farming music', played to cheer workers and pray for harvest.

T6-1226.m: madangnori, open-air folk theater performed in the round
T6-1226.ex: 연말이 되면 부모님과 함께 마당놀이를 보러 가요.
T6-1226.x: At the end of the year, I go see madangnori with my parents.
T6-1226.e: 마당 'yard' + 놀이 'play': staged in an open space with the audience all around.
T6-1226.t: Audience participation is expected: laughing, shouting back and even joining in are part of the show.

T6-1227.m: changgeuk, Korean traditional opera based on pansori
T6-1227.x: The pansori 'Chunhyangga' was made into a changgeuk and staged.
T6-1227.e: Literally 'sung drama': pansori split among many singers in costume.

T6-1228.m: singing (in pansori and traditional vocal music)
T6-1228.ex: 그는 어릴 때부터 스승에게 창을 배웠습니다.
T6-1228.x: He learned traditional singing from his teacher since childhood.
T6-1228.e: Homonym alert: 창 also means 'window' and 'spear'.
T6-1228.t: Pansori alternates 창 (singing) with 아니리 (spoken narration) and 발림 (gestures).

T6-1229.ex: 소리꾼은 혼자서 여러 인물을 연기하며 노래해요.
T6-1229.x: The pansori singer sings while playing many characters alone.
T6-1229.e: 소리 'sound, song' + -꾼 'person who does it', as in 사냥꾼, 나무꾼.

T6-1230.ex: 고수는 북을 치며 소리꾼의 노래를 이끌어 줍니다.
T6-1230.x: The drummer beats the drum and guides the singer's song.
T6-1230.e: Literally 'drum hand'. Homonym alert: 고수 also means 'expert' and 'cilantro'.
T6-1230.t: A famous saying, 일고수 이명창, ranks the drummer first and the singer second.

T6-1231.m: chuimsae, shouts of encouragement during a performance (like 얼씨구, 좋다)
T6-1231.x: The audience shouted 'Eolssigu!' to cheer the performer on.
T6-1231.e: Probably related to 추어올리다 'to praise, to cheer up'.
T6-1231.t: The verb is 넣다: 추임새를 넣다; it's also used casually for chiming in to cheer a speaker.

T6-1232.ex: 그녀는 오랜 수련 끝에 판소리 명창이 되었어요.
T6-1232.x: After long training, she became a master pansori singer.
T6-1232.e: Literally 'famous singing'; refers to the singer, too.

T6-1233.ex: 가야금 명인의 연주에 관객들은 숨을 죽였어요.
T6-1233.x: The audience held their breath at the gayageum master's performance.
T6-1233.e: Literally 'famous person', but it means a master of a skill or art.
T6-1233.t: Don't confuse with 유명인 (celebrity): 명인 is about mastery, not fame.

T6-1234.ex: 그 안무가는 유명 아이돌의 춤을 많이 만들었어요.
T6-1234.x: That choreographer created many dances for famous idols.
T6-1234.e: -가 = professional in a field: 안무가, 연출가, 작곡가.

T6-1235.ex: 현대무용은 정해진 형식보다 자유로운 표현을 중요하게 생각해요.
T6-1235.x: Modern dance values free expression over fixed forms.

T6-1236.ex: 동생은 어릴 때부터 고전무용을 배워 왔어요.
T6-1236.x: My younger sister has been learning classical dance since she was little.

T6-1237.x: Lighting and costumes are also important parts of stage art.

T6-1238.ex: 연출가는 배우들과 함께 장면 하나하나를 다시 연습했어요.
T6-1238.x: The director rehearsed each scene again with the actors.
T6-1238.e: Literally 'one who brings out the performance'.
T6-1238.t: Theater uses 연출가; for films, 감독 is the usual word.

T6-1239.ex: 셰익스피어의 희곡은 지금도 전 세계에서 공연됩니다.
T6-1239.x: Shakespeare's plays are still performed all over the world.
T6-1239.e: The written script; the performance itself is 연극.
T6-1239.t: Pronounced [히곡]: ㅢ after a consonant, as in 희, is said like ㅣ.

T6-1240.ex: 그 극작가의 새 작품이 다음 주에 초연됩니다.
T6-1240.x: That playwright's new work premieres next week.
T6-1240.t: Pronounced [극짝까]: consonants after ㄱ become tense.

T6-1241.ex: 이 작품은 웃음과 눈물이 섞인 희비극입니다.
T6-1241.x: This work is a tragicomedy mixing laughter and tears.

T6-1242.m: theater of the absurd, absurdist play
T6-1242.x: 'Waiting for Godot' is a classic absurdist play.
T6-1242.t: 부조리 alone often means social injustice or corruption, as in 사회의 부조리.

T6-1243.ex: 주인공의 긴 독백이 이 연극의 가장 감동적인 장면이에요.
T6-1243.x: The hero's long monologue is the most moving scene in this play.

T6-1244.ex: 배우가 방백으로 관객에게 자신의 속마음을 털어놓았어요.
T6-1244.x: In an aside, the actor revealed his true feelings to the audience.
T6-1244.e: Literally 'speaking to the side': other characters supposedly can't hear.

T6-1245.x: This play consists of three acts in total.
T6-1245.e: Literally 'curtain': each act ends as the curtain falls.
T6-1245.t: 막을 내리다 (to lower the curtain) also means any event comes to an end.

T6-1246.x: The main character first appears in Act 1, Scene 2.
T6-1246.e: Literally 'place': a new scene often means a new setting.
T6-1246.t: Always counted with Sino numbers after the act: 2막 3장 = Act 2, Scene 3.

T6-1247.ex: 공연이 끝나자 관객들의 박수 속에 커튼콜이 이어졌어요.
T6-1247.x: When the show ended, curtain calls followed amid the audience's applause.

T6-1248.x: This opera premiered in Rome in 1900.
T6-1248.e: Literally 'first performance'. Homonym alert: 초연하다 also means 'to be aloof, detached'.
T6-1248.t: Often used as a verb: 초연되다 (to be premiered), 세계 초연 (world premiere).

T6-1249.ex: 그 뮤지컬은 관객들의 요청으로 내년에 재연이 결정되었어요.
T6-1249.x: Due to audience demand, the musical's revival has been confirmed for next year.
T6-1249.t: Don't confuse with 재현 (reproduction, re-creation); 재연 is for restaged shows and staged reenactments.

T6-1250.ex: 그녀는 대학에서 공연예술을 전공하고 연출가가 되었어요.
T6-1250.x: She majored in performing arts in college and became a director.

T6-1251.ex: 고조선은 단군왕검이 세운 한국 최초의 국가예요.
T6-1251.x: Gojoseon is Korea's first state, founded by Dangun Wanggeom.
T6-1251.e: 'Old' was added by later historians to tell it apart from the Joseon dynasty (1392–1910).

T6-1252.ex: 삼국시대에는 고구려, 백제, 신라가 서로 경쟁했어요.
T6-1252.x: During the Three Kingdoms period, Goguryeo, Baekje and Silla competed with each other.
T6-1252.t: Pronounced [삼국씨대] — the ㅅ after ㄱ becomes tense.

T6-1253.x: Bulguksa Temple and Seokguram Grotto were built in the Unified Silla period.
T6-1253.e: Silla after it unified the three kingdoms in the 7th century.
T6-1253.t: Pronounced [통일실라] — ㄴ turns into ㄹ next to ㄹ.

T6-1254.m: Samguk Sagi, History of the Three Kingdoms (1145)
T6-1254.ex: 삼국사기는 김부식이 왕의 명령으로 편찬한 역사책이에요.
T6-1254.x: The Samguk Sagi is a history book Kim Busik compiled on the king's orders.
T6-1254.e: Literally 'historical records of the three kingdoms'; Korea's oldest surviving history.
T6-1254.t: 삼국사기 is the official history by Kim Busik; 삼국유사 collects legends gathered by the monk Iryeon.

T6-1255.m: Samguk Yusa, Memorabilia of the Three Kingdoms
T6-1255.ex: 단군 신화는 삼국유사에 처음으로 기록되어 있어요.
T6-1255.x: The Dangun myth was first recorded in the Samguk Yusa.
T6-1255.e: Literally 'leftover stories of the three kingdoms', compiled by the monk Iryeon.

T6-1256.x: The Annals of the Joseon Dynasty were designated UNESCO Memory of the World in 1997.
T6-1256.e: Literally 'true records of the Joseon royal dynasty', written reign by reign.

T6-1257.m: Jiphyeonjeon, Hall of Worthies (royal research institute)
T6-1257.ex: 세종대왕은 집현전 학자들과 함께 한글을 만들었어요.
T6-1257.x: King Sejong created Hangeul together with the scholars of the Jiphyeonjeon.
T6-1257.t: Pronounced [지편전] — ㅂ plus ㅎ becomes ㅍ.

T6-1258.x: The state examination system was first introduced in the Goryeo period.
T6-1258.e: Choosing officials by exam subjects; -제 = system: 과거제, 신분제.
T6-1258.t: 과거 (state exam) is a homonym of 과거 (the past); context makes it clear.

T6-1259.ex: 그는 여러 번의 도전 끝에 과거에 급제했어요.
T6-1259.x: After many attempts, he finally passed the state examination.
T6-1259.e: Literally 'reaching the rank' of successful candidates.
T6-1259.t: Used with 에: 과거에 급제하다; for modern exams say 합격하다.

T6-1260.m: failing an exam (esp. the state exam)
T6-1260.x: He failed the state exam and went back to his hometown.
T6-1260.e: Literally 'falling off the list' of passers posted on a board.

T6-1261.m: first place in the state exam; top scorer
T6-1261.x: He passed the state exam in first place.
T6-1261.t: A different 장원 means a medieval manor; in exam contexts it always means top scorer.

T6-1262.m: jungin, the middle class (technical specialists in Joseon)
