T6-1262.ex: 조선 시대 중인은 통역관이나 의원 같은 일을 했어요.
T6-1262.x: In the Joseon era, the jungin worked as interpreters, doctors and the like.
T6-1262.e: Literally 'middle people', between the yangban aristocrats and commoners.

T6-1263.ex: 상민은 주로 농사를 지으며 세금을 냈어요.
T6-1263.x: Commoners mostly farmed and paid taxes.

T6-1264.m: the lowborn, the lowest social class
T6-1264.ex: 조선 시대에 노비와 백정은 천민으로 취급되었어요.
T6-1264.x: In the Joseon era, slaves and butchers were treated as lowborn.

T6-1265.ex: 사대부들은 유교 경전을 공부하고 관직에 나갔어요.
T6-1265.x: The literati studied the Confucian classics and entered government office.

T6-1266.ex: 고려 시대에는 문신이 무신보다 더 좋은 대우를 받았어요.
T6-1266.x: In the Goryeo period, civil officials were treated better than military officials.
T6-1266.e: Literally 'subject of letters', an official who serves with the pen.
T6-1266.t: Homonym alert: 문신 also means a tattoo, written with different characters.

T6-1267.x: In 1170, military officials staged a coup and seized power.

T6-1268.ex: 그는 과거에 급제해서 높은 벼슬에 올랐어요.
T6-1268.x: He passed the state exam and rose to a high government post.
T6-1268.e: Native word for an official post; colloquially also a rooster's comb (닭 벼슬).
T6-1268.t: The typical collocation is 벼슬에 오르다, 'to rise to an official post'.

T6-1269.ex: 그는 관직에서 물러나 고향에서 책을 썼어요.
T6-1269.x: He retired from office and wrote books in his hometown.

T6-1270.ex: 백성들이 관아 앞에 모여 억울함을 호소했어요.
T6-1270.x: The people gathered in front of the government office to protest their unfair treatment.
T6-1270.e: Literally 'official office', the local magistrate's compound.

T6-1271.x: The magistrate governed the provinces on behalf of the king.
T6-1271.e: Literally 'one who guards and commands' a district.
T6-1271.t: Homonyms: 수령 also means receiving (a package) and a gang leader, each with different characters.

T6-1272.ex: 암행어사는 몰래 지방을 다니며 수령들을 감시했어요.
T6-1272.x: Secret royal inspectors traveled the provinces in disguise, watching the magistrates.
T6-1272.e: Literally 'royal official who travels in secret'.
T6-1272.t: The famous cry 암행어사 출두요! means the inspector is revealing himself, as in The Tale of Chunhyang.

T6-1273.m: power of the ministers (vs. royal power)
T6-1273.ex: 조선 초기에는 왕권과 신권이 서로 대립했어요.
T6-1273.x: In early Joseon, royal power and the ministers' power clashed.
T6-1273.e: Literally 'subjects' power', the counterweight to royal power.
T6-1273.t: Homonym: 신권 also means newly issued banknotes; in history texts it means ministers' power.

T6-1274.t: 왕위에 오르다 means to ascend the throne; 왕위를 물려주다 means to hand it down.

T6-1275.ex: 연산군은 폭정을 일삼다가 결국 신하들에 의해 폐위되었어요.
T6-1275.x: Yeonsangun ruled as a tyrant and was eventually deposed by his own ministers.

T6-1276.ex: 어린 왕 대신 대비가 섭정을 했어요.
T6-1276.x: The queen dowager ruled as regent for the young king.
T6-1276.e: Literally 'taking over government' on someone's behalf.

T6-1277.ex: 세자는 어릴 때부터 왕이 되기 위한 교육을 받았어요.
T6-1277.x: From childhood, the crown prince was trained to become king.
T6-1277.e: Literally 'son of the generation', the heir who continues the line.

T6-1278.ex: 명성황후는 조선의 스물여섯 번째 왕 고종의 왕비였어요.
T6-1278.x: Empress Myeongseong was the queen of Gojong, Joseon's twenty-sixth king.
T6-1278.t: A queen who rules in her own right is 여왕.

T6-1279.x: Jang Hui-bin was King Sukjong's concubine before becoming queen.
T6-1279.e: Literally 'rear palace', the quarters where concubines lived.

T6-1280.ex: 궁녀들은 궁궐 안에서 왕실의 생활을 도왔어요.
T6-1280.x: Court ladies assisted the royal family's daily life inside the palace.

T6-1281.ex: 내시는 왕의 곁에서 궁궐의 여러 일을 돌보았어요.
T6-1281.x: Eunuchs took care of many palace duties at the king's side.

T6-1282.ex: 연산군 때 일어난 사화로 많은 선비가 죽었어요.
T6-1282.x: Many scholars died in the literati purges under Yeonsangun.
T6-1282.e: Literally 'disaster for scholars'; Joseon saw four major purges.

T6-1283.ex: 조선 후기에는 당쟁이 심해서 정치가 혼란스러웠어요.
T6-1283.x: In late Joseon, factional strife was so severe that politics was in chaos.

T6-1284.x: The factions were divided according to their scholarly positions.
T6-1284.e: Literally 'party of friends', groups bound by teacher and school.

T6-1285.ex: 영조는 탕평책을 실시해 인재를 고르게 등용했어요.
T6-1285.x: King Yeongjo carried out the Tangpyeong policy, appointing talent evenly from all factions.
T6-1285.e: From a classic phrase meaning 'broad and level', fair to every side.
T6-1285.t: The dish 탕평채 (mung bean jelly salad) is said to be named after this policy.

T6-1286.ex: 흥선대원군은 서양과의 교류를 막고 쇄국을 고집했어요.
T6-1286.x: Heungseon Daewongun blocked contact with the West and insisted on isolation.

T6-1287.ex: 쇄국정책 때문에 조선의 근대화가 늦어졌다는 의견도 있어요.
T6-1287.x: Some argue that the isolationist policy delayed Joseon's modernization.

T6-1288.m: opening of ports (to foreign trade); opening of a port or airport
T6-1288.ex: 조선은 1876년 강화도 조약으로 개항을 하게 되었어요.
T6-1288.x: Joseon opened its ports in 1876 through the Treaty of Ganghwa.
T6-1288.t: Today it is also used for a new airport opening, e.g. 인천공항 개항.

T6-1289.ex: 개화를 주장한 사람들은 서양의 기술을 배우자고 했어요.
T6-1289.x: Those who called for enlightenment urged learning Western technology.
T6-1289.t: Homonym: 개화 also means flowers blooming, written with different characters.

T6-1290.ex: 개화기에는 신문과 전차 같은 새로운 문물이 들어왔어요.
T6-1290.x: During the Enlightenment period, new things like newspapers and streetcars arrived.

T6-1291.x: The Gabo Reform, carried out in 1894, abolished the class system and the state examinations.
T6-1291.e: Named after 1894, a gabo year in the 60-year cycle.
T6-1291.t: Many events carry their cycle-year names: 임진 (1592), 갑오 (1894), 을사 (1905).

T6-1292.x: Donghak promoted the idea that 'people are heaven.'
T6-1292.e: Literally 'Eastern Learning', founded in 1860 as a response to Western Learning (Catholicism).

T6-1293.x: The Donghak Peasant Revolution broke out in 1894 under Jeon Bong-jun's leadership.
T6-1293.t: Pronounced [동항농미눈동] — ㄱ becomes ㅇ before ㄴ.

T6-1294.m: leader of a righteous army (volunteer militia)
T6-1294.ex: 곽재우는 임진왜란 때 활약한 유명한 의병장이에요.
T6-1294.x: Gwak Jae-u is a famous righteous army leader who fought in the Imjin War.

T6-1295.x: With the Eulsa Treaty, signed in 1905, the Korean Empire was stripped of its diplomatic rights.
T6-1295.e: Named after 1905, an eulsa year in the 60-year cycle.
T6-1295.t: Many Koreans prefer 을사늑약, 'forced treaty', to stress that it was signed under coercion.

T6-1296.ex: 많은 사람들이 빼앗긴 국권을 되찾기 위해 싸웠어요.
T6-1296.x: Many people fought to regain the nation's lost sovereignty.

T6-1297.m: loss of national sovereignty; Japan's annexation of Korea (1910)
T6-1297.x: With the loss of sovereignty in 1910, the Korean Empire became a Japanese colony.
T6-1297.t: Textbooks now prefer 국권피탈 over 한일합병, which sounds like a voluntary merger.

T6-1298.x: Korea was under Japanese colonial rule for 35 years.
T6-1298.t: Pronounced [싱민통치] — ㄱ becomes ㅇ before ㅁ.

T6-1299.ex: 일제는 토지 조사 사업으로 농민들의 땅을 수탈했어요.
T6-1299.x: Imperial Japan seized farmers' land through the land survey project.

T6-1300.ex: 강제징용 피해자들은 지금도 일본의 사과를 요구하고 있어요.
T6-1300.x: Victims of forced labor are still demanding an apology from Japan.

T6-1301.m: forced adoption of Japanese-style names (colonial era)
T6-1301.ex: 일제는 한국인에게 일본식 이름을 쓰도록 창씨개명을 강요했어요.
T6-1301.x: Imperial Japan forced Koreans to adopt Japanese-style names.
T6-1301.e: Literally 'creating a clan name and changing one's given name'.

T6-1302.ex: 삼일운동 때 사람들은 거리에서 대한 독립 만세를 외쳤어요.
T6-1302.x: During the March 1st Movement, people shouted 'Long live Korean independence!' in the streets.
T6-1302.t: Usually written 3·1 운동; the national holiday is 삼일절, pronounced [사밀쩔].

T6-1303.m: provisional government (esp. the one in Shanghai, 1919)
T6-1303.x: The Provisional Government of the Republic of Korea was founded in Shanghai in 1919.
T6-1303.e: Literally 'government for the time at hand'.

T6-1304.ex: 그 독립투사는 평생을 조국의 독립을 위해 바쳤어요.
T6-1304.x: That independence fighter devoted his whole life to his homeland's independence.
T6-1304.e: Literally 'fighter for standing alone', that is, for independence.
T6-1304.t: Pronounced [동닙투사] — ㄱ and ㄹ both shift to nasal sounds.

T6-1305.ex: 유관순 열사는 삼일운동에 참여했다가 감옥에서 세상을 떠났어요.
T6-1305.x: The martyr Yu Gwan-sun took part in the March 1st Movement and died in prison.
T6-1305.t: 열사 resisted without weapons, like 유관순 열사; 의사 used armed action, like 안중근 의사.

T6-1306.m: righteous patriot, martyr (who resisted with arms)
T6-1306.ex: 안중근 의사는 하얼빈에서 이토 히로부미를 저격했어요.
T6-1306.x: The patriot Ahn Jung-geun shot Ito Hirobumi in Harbin.
T6-1306.t: Homonym: 의사 also means a doctor; 안중근 의사 means the patriot, not a physician.

T6-1307.ex: 그는 독립운동을 하다가 서른 살의 나이에 순국했어요.
T6-1307.x: He died for his country at age thirty while fighting for independence.

T6-1308.m: patriotic martyrs (who died for Korea's independence)
T6-1308.ex: 우리는 순국선열의 희생을 절대 잊지 말아야 해요.
T6-1308.x: We must never forget the sacrifice of the patriotic martyrs.
T6-1308.e: Literally 'ardent forebears who died for the country'.
T6-1308.t: 순국선열 died during the struggle; patriots who survived to liberation are called 애국지사.

T6-1309.ex: 광복절에는 애국지사들의 묘역을 찾는 사람이 많아요.
T6-1309.x: On Liberation Day, many people visit the graves of the patriots.
T6-1309.e: Literally 'person of strong will who loves the country'.

T6-1310.ex: 광복 후에도 친일파를 청산하는 일은 쉽지 않았어요.
T6-1310.x: Even after liberation, purging the pro-Japanese collaborators was not easy.
T6-1310.e: Literally 'pro-Japan faction'; -파 = faction or group: 친일파, 개화파.

T6-1311.ex: 을사조약에 찬성한 다섯 대신은 매국노라고 불려요.
T6-1311.x: The five ministers who approved the Eulsa Treaty are called traitors.
T6-1311.t: Pronounced [매궁노] — ㄱ becomes ㅇ before ㄴ.

T6-1312.ex: 우리 할아버지는 육이오 때 부산으로 피란을 가셨어요.
T6-1312.x: My grandfather fled to Busan as a refugee during the Korean War.
T6-1312.e: Named after its start date, June 25, 1950; usually written 6·25.
T6-1312.t: Pronounced [유기오] — the ㄱ batchim links to the next syllable.

T6-1313.ex: 전쟁 중에 수많은 피란민이 부산으로 몰려들었어요.
T6-1313.x: During the war, countless refugees flooded into Busan.
T6-1313.t: 피란 means fleeing war; 피난 means fleeing any disaster, and people often mix them up.

T6-1314.forms: 산업화 시대에 + verb; 산업화 시대를 거치다 (go through the industrial era)
T6-1314.m: the industrialization era, the age of industrialization
T6-1314.ex: 산업화 시대에 많은 사람들이 일자리를 찾아 도시로 왔어요.
T6-1314.x: In the industrialization era, many people came to the cities looking for work.
T6-1314.e: Literally 'era of becoming industrial'; -화 = -ization: 산업화, 민주화, 도시화.

T6-1315.x: The April 19 Revolution finally forced President Syngman Rhee to step down.
T6-1315.e: Named after April 19, 1960, when student-led protests toppled the government; usually written 4·19.

T6-1316.x: In May 1980, a large pro-democracy movement broke out in Gwangju.
T6-1316.e: Literally 'movement to make the people the masters'.

T6-1317.ex: 경주에는 국가가 지정한 사적이 아주 많아요.
T6-1317.x: Gyeongju has a great many state-designated historic sites.
T6-1317.t: Homonym: 사적 also means private or personal, as in 사적인 이야기.

T6-1318.m: intangible cultural heritage, intangible cultural property
T6-1318.x: Pansori is designated and protected as a National Intangible Cultural Property.
T6-1318.e: Literally 'cultural asset without form', such as music, dance and crafts.
T6-1318.t: Since 2024 the official term is 무형유산, but 무형문화재 is still widely used.

T6-1319.ex: 이 절의 오래된 종은 유형문화재로 지정되었어요.
T6-1319.x: This temple's old bell has been designated a tangible cultural property.
T6-1319.e: Literally 'cultural asset with form', such as buildings and objects.

T6-1320.m: living national treasure (master of an intangible heritage)
T6-1320.x: That grandmother was recognized as a living national treasure of pansori.
T6-1320.e: Literally 'human cultural asset'; officially called a holder of intangible heritage.

T6-1321.ex: 경주 시내에는 신라 시대의 큰 고분들이 있어요.
T6-1321.x: Downtown Gyeongju has large tombs from the Silla period.

T6-1322.ex: 고구려 고분벽화에는 사냥하는 모습이 그려져 있어요.
T6-1322.x: Goguryeo tomb murals depict scenes of hunting.

T6-1323.ex: 불국사에는 다보탑과 석가탑이라는 두 석탑이 있어요.
T6-1323.x: Bulguksa Temple has two stone pagodas, Dabotap and Seokgatap.
T6-1323.e: Literally 'stone tower'; 탑 ultimately comes from Sanskrit 'stupa'.

T6-1324.ex: 석굴암은 인공으로 만든 석굴 안에 불상을 모신 곳이에요.
T6-1324.x: Seokguram enshrines a Buddha statue inside a man-made stone grotto.

T6-1325.ex: 그 탑 안에서 부처님의 사리가 발견되었어요.
T6-1325.x: The Buddha's relics were found inside that pagoda.
T6-1325.e: A sound borrowing of Sanskrit 'sarira' (body), so the characters' meanings don't help.
T6-1325.t: Don't confuse it with native 사리, a coil of noodles added to a stew, as in 라면 사리.

T6-1326.ex: 이 금동 불상은 삼국시대에 만들어진 거예요.
T6-1326.x: This gilt-bronze Buddha statue was made in the Three Kingdoms period.
T6-1326.e: Literally 'gold and copper': bronze covered with gold.

T6-1327.x: Comb-pattern pottery is the representative artifact of the Neolithic era.
T6-1327.e: 빗살 (comb teeth) + 무늬 (pattern) + 토기 (earthenware): pottery with comb-like lines.
T6-1327.t: 무늬 is spelled with ㅢ but pronounced [무니]; 빗살 sounds like [빋쌀].

T6-1328.m: bronze ware, bronze tools; the Bronze Age
T6-1328.x: Social classes began to appear in the Bronze Age.
T6-1328.e: Literally 'blue-green copper tools' — bronze turns greenish as it ages.
T6-1328.t: Used alone it often means the Bronze Age, but 청동기 시대 is the full, clearer form.

T6-1329.m: iron tools, ironware; the Iron Age
T6-1329.ex: 철기가 보급되면서 농업 생산량이 크게 늘었습니다.
T6-1329.x: As iron tools spread, agricultural output increased greatly.

T6-1330.m: Paleolithic stone tools; the Paleolithic (Old Stone Age)
T6-1330.ex: 이 동굴에서 구석기 시대의 유물이 발견되었어요.
T6-1330.x: Paleolithic artifacts were found in this cave.
T6-1330.e: Literally 'old stone tools' — chipped stone, before polished tools.

T6-1331.m: Neolithic stone tools; the Neolithic (New Stone Age)
T6-1331.ex: 신석기 시대 사람들은 농사를 짓기 시작했어요.
T6-1331.x: People in the Neolithic era began farming.
T6-1331.e: Literally 'new stone tools' — polished stone tools.
T6-1331.t: Watch the pronunciation: 신석기 sounds like [신석끼].

T6-1332.ex: 선사시대에는 문자가 없어서 기록이 남아 있지 않아요.
T6-1332.x: There was no writing in prehistoric times, so no records remain.
T6-1332.e: Literally 'the era before history' — before written records.

T6-1333.m: the historical period (era with written records)
T6-1333.x: The historical period began when written records appeared.
T6-1333.e: The era of written history, as opposed to 선사시대 (prehistory).

T6-1334.ex: 그는 대학에서 한국 고대사를 연구하고 있어요.
T6-1334.x: He is researching ancient Korean history at the university.

T6-1335.m: early modern times, the early modern period
T6-1335.x: The Joseon period is often classified as the early modern era.
T6-1335.e: Literally 'the near age' — the period just before modern times.
T6-1335.t: Order of eras: 고대 → 중세 → 근세 → 근대 → 현대; 근세 and 근대 are easily confused.

T6-1336.x: The Korean War was a great tragedy in modern Korean history.

T6-1337.x: The view used to interpret history differs from era to era.
T6-1337.e: Literally 'history view.' -관 = outlook: 역사관, 가치관, 세계관.
T6-1337.t: 사관 also means 'court historian' or 'military officer' (different hanja); context decides.

T6-1338.m: history (as an academic field), historical studies
T6-1338.x: I majored in Korean history in college.
T6-1338.t: A homonym 사학 means 'private school (system)', as in 사학 재단.

T6-1339.ex: 여러 사학자들이 그 기록의 신뢰성을 의심했어요.
T6-1339.x: Several historians doubted the reliability of that record.
T6-1339.e: -자 = person who does it: 과학자, 사학자, 운전자.

T6-1340.x: It is important to have a sound view of history.
T6-1340.t: A homonym 역사관 means 'history museum hall'; you'll often see that one on signs.

T6-1341.m: colonial view of history (Japanese colonial historiography of Korea)
T6-1341.ex: 많은 학자들이 식민사관을 비판하고 극복하려고 노력했어요.
T6-1341.x: Many scholars criticized the colonial view of history and tried to overcome it.
T6-1341.e: Literally 'colony history view' — a framing that portrayed Korea as stagnant and dependent.

T6-1342.m: historical research, verification by evidence; period accuracy
T6-1342.ex: 이 사극은 시대 고증이 정확하기로 유명해요.
T6-1342.x: This historical drama is famous for its accurate period detail.
T6-1342.e: Literally 'examine and prove' — checking facts against old sources.
T6-1342.t: Common in reviews: 고증이 잘 됐다 / 고증 오류 (historical inaccuracy) for dramas and films.

T6-1343.ex: 이 책은 조선 왕조의 연대기를 쉽게 정리했어요.
T6-1343.x: This book neatly summarizes the chronicle of the Joseon dynasty.
T6-1343.e: Literally 'a record of years and eras' in time order.

T6-1344.x: King Gwanggaeto used his own era name, Yeongnak.
T6-1344.e: Literally 'year name' — monarchs named eras to count years.
T6-1344.t: Japan still uses era names today, such as 레이와 (Reiwa).

T6-1345.m: clan, family lineage (descendants of one ancestor)
T6-1345.ex: 추석에는 문중 사람들이 모여서 성묘를 해요.
T6-1345.x: On Chuseok, members of the clan gather to visit ancestral graves.
T6-1345.e: Literally 'within the gate' — everyone belonging to the same family house.

T6-1346.m: head family (main line of a clan), head house
T6-1346.ex: 이 마을에는 오백 년 된 종가가 있어요.
T6-1346.x: There is a five-hundred-year-old head family house in this village.
T6-1346.e: Literally 'main-line house' — the eldest son's line of a clan.
T6-1346.t: Often heard as 종갓집, especially when talking about traditional recipes passed down.
rel: eldest grandson of the main line

T6-1347.m: eldest grandson of the main line, heir of the head family
T6-1347.x: He's the main-line heir, so he is responsible for the ancestral rites.

T6-1348.m: clan seat, ancestral home of a family name
T6-1348.ex: 같은 김씨라도 본관이 다를 수 있어요.
T6-1348.x: Even people with the same surname Kim can have different clan seats.
T6-1348.e: The place your clan's founder came from, e.g., 김해 김씨.
T6-1348.t: Ask politely with 본관이 어디세요? A homonym 본관 also means 'main building.'

T6-1349.x: That family is known for its tradition of frugality.
T6-1349.e: Literally 'house wind' — the atmosphere and customs of a family.

T6-1350.x: Our family motto is 'Let's live honestly.'
T6-1350.t: Korean schoolkids are often asked to write their 가훈; it's typically framed and hung at home.

T6-1351.ex: 명절 아침에 가족이 함께 제사상을 차려요.
T6-1351.x: On holiday mornings, the family sets the ancestral rite table together.
T6-1351.t: Pronounced [제사쌍]; the verb is 차리다: 제사상을 차리다.

T6-1352.ex: 할머니는 명절 전에 제기를 깨끗이 닦으셨어요.
T6-1352.x: Grandma cleaned the ritual dishes before the holiday.
T6-1352.t: Don't mix it up with 제기차기, the native shuttlecock-kicking game; 제기 there is a different word.

T6-1353.m: tidying ancestral graves (cutting the grass), grave weeding
T6-1353.ex: 추석 전에 가족들과 벌초를 하러 시골에 가요.
T6-1353.x: Before Chuseok, I go to the countryside with my family to tidy the graves.
T6-1353.e: Literally 'cutting grass' — done on family graves before Chuseok.
T6-1353.t: News often warns about bee stings and snakes during 벌초 season in late August and September.

T6-1354.x: Traditional funeral rites had very complicated procedures.
T6-1354.t: Pronounced [상녜] — ㄹ becomes ㄴ after ㅇ.

T6-1355.ex: 장례식장에 가서 상주에게 위로의 말을 전했어요.
T6-1355.x: I went to the funeral hall and offered words of comfort to the chief mourner.
T6-1355.e: Literally 'mourning host' — usually the eldest son of the deceased.
T6-1355.t: 상주 also has a homonym meaning 'stationed, resident,' as in 상주 인원; context makes it clear.

T6-1356.ex: 유족들은 검은 상복을 입고 손님을 맞았어요.
T6-1356.x: The bereaved family wore black mourning clothes and greeted the guests.
T6-1356.e: Literally 'mourning clothes.' Traditionally rough hemp; today usually black.

T6-1357.m: condolence call, paying respects to the bereaved
T6-1357.ex: 회사 동료의 아버지가 돌아가셔서 문상을 다녀왔어요.
T6-1357.x: A coworker's father passed away, so I went to pay my respects.
T6-1357.e: Literally 'visiting the mourning' — calling on a grieving family.
T6-1357.t: Common phrase: 문상을 가다. 조문 means nearly the same and is more common in news.

T6-1358.ex: 흰 봉투에 조의금을 넣어서 접수대에 냈어요.
T6-1358.x: I put the condolence money in a white envelope and handed it in at the reception desk.
T6-1358.t: Odd amounts such as 30,000, 50,000 or 70,000 won are customary; 조의금 and 부의금 are used interchangeably.

T6-1359.ex: 봉투 앞면에 부의라고 쓰고 부의금을 넣었어요.
T6-1359.x: I wrote 'condolence' on the front of the envelope and put the money in.
T6-1359.e: Literally 'funeral-gift money' — help for the family's funeral costs.

T6-1360.m: departure of the funeral procession, carrying out the coffin
T6-1360.ex: 발인은 내일 아침 일곱 시에 있을 예정입니다.
T6-1360.x: The funeral procession will depart tomorrow at 7 a.m.
T6-1360.e: The moment the coffin leaves for burial or cremation, usually on day three.
T6-1360.t: Funeral notices list 발인 with a date and time, so guests know when the procession leaves.

T6-1361.ex: 장례를 마친 뒤 가족끼리 삼우제를 지냈어요.
T6-1361.x: After the funeral, the family held the third-day memorial rite on their own.
T6-1361.e: Literally 'third repose rite' — held at the grave three days after burial.
T6-1361.t: The verb is 지내다: 삼우제를 지내다, just like 제사를 지내다.

T6-1362.ex: 요즘은 사십구재를 마치고 탈상하는 경우가 많아요.
T6-1362.x: These days, many families end mourning after the forty-ninth-day rite.
T6-1362.e: Literally 'taking off mourning' — once meant removing mourning clothes after three years.

T6-1363.x: The two held a traditional wedding at a hanok.
T6-1363.t: Pronounced [전통홀례] — ㄴ before ㄹ becomes ㄹ. The verb is 올리다: 혼례를 올리다.

T6-1364.m: pyebaek (bride's formal greeting to the groom's family after the wedding)
T6-1364.ex: 결혼식이 끝나고 신랑 부모님께 폐백을 드렸어요.
T6-1364.x: After the wedding, we performed pyebaek for the groom's parents.
T6-1364.e: Literally 'silk offerings' — the gifts once presented; parents toss dates and chestnuts for children.
T6-1364.t: The verb is 드리다: 폐백을 드리다.

T6-1365.m: wedding gift box (sent by the groom's family to the bride's)
T6-1365.ex: 결혼식 전날 밤에 신랑 친구들이 함을 지고 왔어요.
T6-1365.x: The night before the wedding, the groom's friends came carrying the gift box.
T6-1365.e: A box with the marriage letter and silk; friends carry it shouting '함 사세요!'
T6-1365.t: Collocations: 함을 지다 (carry it on the back) and 함을 받다 (receive it).

T6-1366.m: the four rites of passage (coming of age, marriage, funeral, ancestral rites)
T6-1366.ex: 관혼상제는 유교 문화에서 가장 중요한 의례였어요.
T6-1366.x: The four rites of passage were the most important rituals in Confucian culture.
T6-1366.e: Capping (coming of age), wedding, funeral, ancestral rite.

T6-1367.ex: 설날에 떡국을 먹는 것은 대표적인 세시풍속이에요.
T6-1367.x: Eating rice cake soup on Lunar New Year is a typical seasonal custom.

T6-1368.m: seasonal division (one of the 24 solar terms)
T6-1368.ex: 입춘은 일 년의 첫 번째 절기예요.
T6-1368.x: Ipchun is the first solar term of the year.
T6-1368.e: The year split into 24 'sections of climate,' used to time farm work.

T6-1369.m: Ipchun, the start of spring (solar term, around Feb 4)
T6-1369.x: On Ipchun, people write 'Great luck at spring's start' and post it on the gate.

T6-1370.ex: 하지에는 일 년 중 낮이 가장 길어요.
T6-1370.x: On the summer solstice, the day is the longest of the year.
T6-1370.t: Don't confuse with the verb ending -하지, as in 하지 마세요 ('don't do it').

T6-1371.ex: 춘분에는 낮과 밤의 길이가 거의 같아요.
T6-1371.x: On the spring equinox, day and night are almost the same length.
T6-1371.e: Literally 'spring division' — day and night split evenly.

T6-1372.x: After the autumn equinox, the nights get longer and longer.

T6-1373.m: Jeongwol Daeboreum, the first full moon of the lunar year
T6-1373.x: On the first full moon of the lunar year, people usually eat five-grain rice and seasoned greens.
T6-1373.e: 정월 (first lunar month) + 대 (great) + native 보름 (full-moon day, 15th).

T6-1374.m: nuts cracked on Jeongwol Daeboreum (walnuts, peanuts, chestnuts, etc.)
T6-1374.x: On the morning of Daeboreum, I cracked walnuts with my teeth as bureom.
T6-1374.e: Cracking these nuts was believed to prevent 부스럼 (skin boils) all year.
T6-1374.t: The set phrase is 부럼을 깨다 or 부럼을 깨물다.

T6-1375.m: jwibul-nori (swinging fire cans and burning field edges on Daeboreum)
T6-1375.x: The kids played jwibul-nori, swinging cans of fire around.
T6-1375.e: 쥐 (rat) + 불 (fire) + 놀이 (game): burning field edges to drive out rats and pests.
T6-1375.t: Pronounced [쥐불로리] — ㄹ followed by ㄴ becomes ㄹㄹ.

T6-1376.m: swinging (traditional swing contest, especially on Dano)
T6-1376.x: When Dano came, women enjoyed swinging contests.
T6-1376.e: 그네 (swing) + 뛰기 (jumping): you 'jump' a swing in Korean, 그네를 뛰다.
T6-1376.t: Today, for playground swings, people say 그네를 타다.

T6-1377.ex: 할아버지는 설날에 한복 위에 두루마기를 입으셨어요.
T6-1377.x: Grandpa wore a durumagi over his hanbok on Lunar New Year.
T6-1377.e: Probably from 두루 (all around) + 막다 (block): a coat closed all around, without slits.

T6-1378.ex: 조선 시대 양반들은 외출할 때 갓을 썼어요.
T6-1378.x: Joseon aristocrats wore a gat when they went out.
T6-1378.e: Homonym warning: 갓 also means 'just, freshly' (갓 구운 빵) and is a mustard leaf.
T6-1378.t: Hats use 쓰다: 갓을 쓰다. Pronounced [갇]; 갓이 sounds like [가시].

T6-1379.x: In the old days, married men tied their hair into a topknot.
T6-1379.e: Boys wore a long braid until marriage, then tied a topknot as a sign of adulthood.
T6-1379.t: The verb is 틀다: 상투를 틀다. Slang 상투를 잡다 means buying a stock at its peak.

T6-1380.ex: 할머니는 머리를 쪽 찌고 비녀를 꽂으셨어요.
T6-1380.x: Grandma put her hair up in a bun and slid in a hairpin.
T6-1380.e: A married woman's hairpin, worn through the chignon (쪽머리); jade and silver were prized.
T6-1380.t: The verb is 꽂다 (stick in): 비녀를 꽂다.

T6-1381.ex: 한복을 입을 때는 하얀 버선을 신어요.
T6-1381.x: When you wear hanbok, you put on white beoseon socks.
T6-1381.e: Its upturned toe, 버선코, is a classic image for the curved eaves of hanok roofs.
T6-1381.t: Like 양말, it takes 신다: 버선을 신다.

T6-1382.ex: 민속촌에 가면 옛날 초가를 볼 수 있어요.
T6-1382.x: At the folk village, you can see old thatched-roof houses.
T6-1382.e: Literally 'grass house' — roofed with rice straw.
T6-1382.t: In speech, 초가집 is more common; it contrasts with 기와집, the wealthier tile-roofed house.

T6-1383.m: gudeul, ondol (underfloor heating system); heated floor
T6-1383.ex: 구들은 아궁이의 열로 방바닥을 데우는 난방 방식이에요.
T6-1383.x: Gudeul is a heating method that warms the floor with heat from the fireplace.
T6-1383.e: The native word for the heated-floor system; 온돌 is the Sino-Korean equivalent.
rel: flat stone of the heated floor

T6-1384.m: main wooden-floored hall (central room of a hanok)
T6-1384.x: In summer, we sat in the wooden-floored hall and ate watermelon.
T6-1384.e: 대청 (great hall) + native 마루 (wooden floor): the open, breezy center of a hanok.

T6-1385.m: sarangbang (the master's study and guest room in a hanok); gathering place
T6-1385.x: Grandpa chatted with guests in the sarangbang.
T6-1385.e: Not 'love room': this 사랑 is a Sino word for outer quarters, unrelated to native 사랑 (love).
T6-1385.t: Figuratively it means a local hangout, e.g., 동네 사랑방 for a neighborhood gathering spot.

T6-1386.m: inner quarters (women's and family living building of a hanok)
T6-1386.x: The inner quarters were mainly where the women lived.
T6-1386.e: 안 (inside) + 채 (counter for buildings): the inner building; compare 사랑채, 바깥채.

T6-1387.m: platform for sauce jars (where crocks of soy sauce, gochujang, etc. are kept)
T6-1387.ex: 할머니 집 장독대에는 된장 항아리가 가득했어요.
T6-1387.x: The jar platform at Grandma's house was full of doenjang crocks.
T6-1387.t: Pronounced [장똑때] — both 독 and 대 are tensed.

T6-1388.m: unforgettable gratitude, a kindness one will never forget
T6-1388.ex: 어려울 때 도와주신 은혜는 정말 각골난망입니다.
T6-1388.x: I will never forget the kindness you showed me in hard times.
T6-1388.e: Literally 'carved into the bone, hard to forget.'
T6-1388.t: Pronounced [각꼴란망]; used in formal thanks, often with 은혜 (a favor received).
rel: repaying a kindness even after death

T6-1389.ex: 두 사람은 견원지간이라서 만나기만 하면 싸워요.
T6-1389.x: Those two fight like cats and dogs whenever they meet.
T6-1389.e: Literally 'the relationship between a dog and a monkey.'
T6-1389.t: English says 'cats and dogs'; Korean pairs a dog with a monkey.

T6-1390.m: repaying a kindness even after death, eternal gratitude
T6-1390.ex: 이 은혜는 결초보은의 마음으로 꼭 갚겠습니다.
T6-1390.x: I will repay this kindness without fail, even beyond the grave.
T6-1390.e: Literally 'tie grass to repay kindness' — a ghost tied grass to trip his benefactor's enemy.

T6-1391.x: Don't act rashly until the situation becomes clear.
T6-1391.t: Usually appears in warnings: 경거망동하지 말라 / 경거망동을 삼가다.

T6-1392.m: twisting scholarship to flatter the powerful
T6-1392.ex: 그 교수는 권력에 아부하는 곡학아세로 비판을 받았어요.
T6-1392.x: That professor was criticized for bending his scholarship to please those in power.
T6-1392.e: Literally 'bend learning to flatter the world.'

T6-1393.m: a cure worse than the disease, ruining the whole by fixing a small flaw
T6-1393.ex: 작은 문제를 고치려다 교각살우의 잘못을 저지르면 안 돼요.
T6-1393.x: Don't make the mistake of ruining everything while fixing a small problem.
T6-1393.e: Literally 'straighten the horns and kill the cow.'

T6-1394.m: a drop in the bucket, a tiny fraction
T6-1394.ex: 그의 재산에 비하면 이 돈은 구우일모에 불과해요.
T6-1394.x: Compared to his fortune, this money is just a drop in the bucket.
T6-1394.t: Typical pattern: N에 불과하다 ('is nothing more than'). Casual speech prefers 새 발의 피.
rel: a drop in the bucket (lit. bird-foot blood)

T6-1395.m: a narrow escape from death, a miraculous comeback
T6-1395.ex: 우리 팀은 마지막 일 분에 골을 넣어 기사회생했어요.
T6-1395.x: Our team scored in the last minute and made a miraculous comeback.
T6-1395.e: Literally 'rise from death, return to life.'
T6-1395.t: Common in sports and business news: 기사회생하다 means a team or company that seemed finished revived.

T6-1396.m: no take-backs, what's done can't be undone
T6-1396.ex: 한번 낸 카드는 낙장불입이니까 다시 가져갈 수 없어요.
T6-1396.x: Once a card is played, there are no take-backs, so you can't pick it up again.
T6-1396.e: Literally 'a dropped card doesn't come back in' — a rule from the card game hwatu.
T6-1396.t: Used jokingly beyond games, meaning a decision or statement can't be reversed.

T6-1397.x: That castle was famous as an impregnable fortress.
T6-1397.t: Pronounced [난공불락]; also used for unbeatable champions or tough markets: 난공불락의 시장.

T6-1398.m: wandering as refugees with all one's belongings
T6-1398.ex: 전쟁이 나자 사람들은 남부여대하여 피난을 떠났어요.
T6-1398.x: When war broke out, people fled carrying everything they owned.
T6-1398.e: Literally 'men carry on their backs, women on their heads.'

T6-1399.m: troubles at home and abroad, internal and external crises
T6-1399.ex: 그 회사는 지금 내우외환에 시달리고 있습니다.
T6-1399.x: That company is now suffering from both internal and external troubles.
T6-1399.t: Common news collocations: 내우외환에 시달리다 / 내우외환을 겪다.

T6-1400.m: flying into a rage, being furious
T6-1400.x: My father flew into a rage when he heard the news.
T6-1400.e: Literally 'anger bursts out, bursts out big.'
T6-1400.t: Often used with honorifics about elders or bosses: 사장님이 노발대발하셨다.

T6-1401.m: an extremely precarious situation, imminent danger
T6-1401.x: At that time, the country was in an extremely precarious situation.

T6-1402.m: same bed, different dreams; sharing a situation but having different goals
T6-1402.ex: 두 회사는 손을 잡았지만 사실은 동상이몽이에요.
T6-1402.x: The two companies joined hands, but in reality they want different things.
T6-1402.t: Very common in politics and business news about partners with conflicting aims.

T6-1403.m: shutting oneself in, staying at home and not going out
T6-1403.ex: 그는 시험 준비를 위해 한 달 동안 두문불출했어요.
T6-1403.x: He shut himself in for a month to prepare for the exam.
T6-1403.e: Literally 'shut the gate and don't go out.'

T6-1404.m: it's darkest under the lamp; missing what's right under one's nose
T6-1404.ex: 등하불명이라더니 안경이 바로 책상 위에 있었네요.
T6-1404.x: Talk about missing what's right in front of you — my glasses were right on the desk.
T6-1404.e: Literally 'under the lamp it isn't bright.'
T6-1404.t: The native proverb 등잔 밑이 어둡다 means the same and is more common in everyday speech.

T6-1405.m: being stunned and at a loss, dazed with shock
T6-1405.x: The family was stunned by the sudden news of the accident.
T6-1405.e: Literally 'blankly losing oneself' — too shocked to think.
T6-1405.t: Usually 망연자실하다 or 망연자실한 표정, describing a reaction to sudden loss or disaster.

T6-1406.m: outward obedience with inner defiance, two-faced compliance
T6-1406.ex: 그는 상사 앞에서만 순종하는 면종복배의 태도를 보였어요.
T6-1406.x: He showed a two-faced attitude, obedient only in front of his boss.
T6-1406.e: Literally 'the face obeys, the belly turns away' — agreeing outwardly, opposing inside.

T6-1407.m: living up to one's reputation, fame that is well deserved
T6-1407.ex: 역시 명불허전이네요. 이 집 냉면은 정말 맛있어요.
T6-1407.x: It really lives up to its name. This place's naengmyeon is amazing.
T6-1407.e: Literally 'a name is not passed on in vain' — fame has a reason.
T6-1407.t: Often said alone as praise: 역시 명불허전! means 'Just as good as they say!'

T6-1408.m: being true to the name, living up to one's title in reality
T6-1408.x: He is truly Korea's best pianist, in name and in fact.
T6-1408.e: Literally 'name and reality match each other'.
T6-1408.t: Almost always used as 명실상부한 + noun, meaning 'undisputed, true'.

T6-1409.m: a crowd of visitors, being swamped with customers
T6-1409.ex: 그 식당은 방송에 나온 뒤로 문전성시를 이루고 있어요.
T6-1409.x: Since it was on TV, that restaurant has been packed with customers.
T6-1409.e: Literally 'a market forms in front of the gate' — so many visitors.
T6-1409.t: Common collocation: 문전성시를 이루다 'to be swamped with visitors'.

T6-1410.ex: 미사여구만 늘어놓지 말고 핵심을 말해 주세요.
T6-1410.x: Don't just string together fancy words; get to the point.
T6-1410.t: Usually negative: 미사여구를 늘어놓다 'to pile on flowery words' without substance.

T6-1411.m: rooting out completely, eradicating at the source
T6-1411.ex: 정부는 공직 사회의 부정부패를 반드시 발본색원하겠다고 발표했습니다.
T6-1411.x: The government announced it would completely root out corruption in public service.
T6-1411.e: Literally 'pull up the root, block the source'.
T6-1411.t: A favorite in news and politics: 비리를 발본색원하다 'to root out corruption'.

T6-1412.m: eternal gratitude, a kindness never forgotten even after death
T6-1412.ex: 어려울 때 도와주신 은혜는 정말 백골난망입니다.
T6-1412.x: I will never forget how you helped me in hard times, even after I die.
T6-1412.e: Literally 'hard to forget even as white bones' — gratitude that outlasts death.
T6-1412.t: Very formal and old-fashioned; used to thank someone deeply for a great favor.

T6-1413.m: a couple growing old happily together
T6-1413.x: I sincerely hope you two will grow old happily together.
T6-1413.e: Literally 'a hundred years, growing old together'.
T6-1413.t: A classic wedding wish; pronounced [뱅년해로] — nasalization.

T6-1414.m: an even match, neck and neck
T6-1414.ex: 두 후보의 지지율이 백중지세를 보이고 있습니다.
T6-1414.x: The two candidates are neck and neck in approval ratings.
T6-1414.e: Literally 'like first and second brothers' — hard to tell who's ahead.
T6-1414.t: The synonym 막상막하 is more common in speech; 백중지세 suits news and sports commentary.

T6-1415.m: blindly following others, going along with the crowd
T6-1415.ex: 남의 말에 부화뇌동하지 말고 스스로 판단하세요.
T6-1415.x: Don't just blindly follow what others say; judge for yourself.
T6-1415.e: Literally 'echoing along when thunder sounds' — agreeing without thinking.

T6-1416.m: doing one's utmost, working oneself to the bone
T6-1416.x: From now on, I will give everything I have for the company's growth.
T6-1416.e: Literally 'grinding bones to powder and crushing the body'.
T6-1416.t: A set phrase in formal pledges and speeches, like a new employee's or an official's vow.

T6-1417.m: sacrificing oneself for others or a just cause
T6-1417.ex: 그 소방관은 살신성인의 정신으로 아이를 구했습니다.
T6-1417.x: The firefighter saved the child in a spirit of self-sacrifice.
T6-1417.e: From Confucius: 'give up one's body to fulfill benevolence'.
T6-1417.t: Pronounced [살씬성인]; common in news about heroes who died saving others.

T6-1418.m: earnestly seeking someone out again and again, persistently courting talent
T6-1418.ex: 사장님은 삼고초려 끝에 그 전문가를 영입했어요.
T6-1418.x: After repeated earnest visits, the CEO finally recruited that expert.
T6-1418.e: From the Three Kingdoms: Liu Bei visited Zhuge Liang's thatched hut three times.
T6-1418.t: Typically 삼고초려 끝에 'after earnest persistence', used when recruiting talent.

T6-1419.m: a complete transformation, drastic change over time
T6-1419.x: This neighborhood has changed beyond recognition in ten years.
T6-1419.e: Literally 'mulberry fields turned into blue sea' — the world changed completely.
T6-1419.t: Pronounced [상전벼캐]; often describes cities or neighborhoods redeveloped beyond recognition.

T6-1420.m: an inseparable relationship, as close as fish and water
T6-1420.ex: 두 사람은 어릴 때부터 수어지교 같은 사이예요.
T6-1420.x: The two have been as inseparable as fish and water since childhood.
T6-1420.e: Literally 'the friendship of water and fish' — Liu Bei's words about Zhuge Liang.

T6-1421.m: interdependence; when one falls, the other suffers
T6-1421.ex: 두 나라는 순망치한의 관계라서 서로 도와야 합니다.
T6-1421.x: The two countries depend on each other, so they must help each other.
T6-1421.e: Literally 'without lips, the teeth get cold'.
T6-1421.t: Often used for neighboring countries or partner businesses: 순망치한의 관계.

T6-1422.ex: 그 결과를 판단하기에는 아직 시기상조인 것 같아요.
T6-1422.x: I think it's still too early to judge the results.

T6-1423.m: pandemonium, a hellish scene of chaos and screaming
T6-1423.ex: 지진이 일어난 거리는 순식간에 아비규환이 되었습니다.
T6-1423.x: The street hit by the earthquake instantly turned into a hellish scene.
T6-1423.e: From Buddhism: the Avici hell and the screaming hell; the first two syllables just spell a Sanskrit name.

T6-1424.ex: 어린 아이들을 이용해 돈을 벌다니 정말 언어도단입니다.
T6-1424.x: Using young children to make money is simply outrageous.
T6-1424.e: Literally 'the path of words is cut off'.
T6-1424.t: Originally a Buddhist term for truth beyond words; today it means 'outrageous'.

T6-1425.m: walking on thin ice, acting with extreme caution
T6-1425.x: He ran the company as though walking on thin ice.
T6-1425.t: Note 박빙 alone means 'neck and neck': 박빙의 승부 'a razor-thin contest'.

T6-1426.m: a futile attempt, looking for something in the wrong place
T6-1426.ex: 노력 없이 성공을 바라는 것은 연목구어예요.
T6-1426.x: Hoping for success without effort is like climbing a tree to catch fish.
T6-1426.e: From Mencius: 'climbing a tree to look for fish'.

T6-1427.m: a suspicious coincidence, unlucky timing that invites blame
T6-1427.ex: 오비이락이라고, 내가 들어가자마자 컴퓨터가 고장 났어요.
T6-1427.x: Talk about bad timing — the computer broke the moment I walked in.
T6-1427.e: Literally 'the crow flies off, the pear falls' — so the crow gets blamed.
T6-1427.t: The native proverb version is 까마귀 날자 배 떨어진다.

T6-1428.m: enduring hardship to get revenge or reach a goal
T6-1428.ex: 작년의 패배 이후 그는 와신상담 끝에 우승했어요.
T6-1428.x: After last year's defeat, he endured hardship and finally won the title.
T6-1428.e: Literally 'sleeping on firewood, tasting gall' — ancient kings keeping their grudge alive.
T6-1428.t: Common in sports news for a comeback after a painful loss.

T6-1429.ex: 우공이산의 마음으로 매일 조금씩 공부하고 있어요.
T6-1429.x: I study a little every day, believing persistence can move mountains.
T6-1429.e: From the fable of 'the foolish old man who moved mountains' by digging stubbornly.

T6-1430.m: patiently holding back, enduring quietly with self-restraint
T6-1430.ex: 그는 기회가 올 때까지 은인자중하며 때를 기다렸어요.
T6-1430.x: He held back patiently and waited until the opportunity came.
T6-1430.e: Literally 'hide feelings, endure, and carry oneself with dignity'.

T6-1431.m: human nature, what anyone would naturally feel
T6-1431.ex: 어려운 사람을 돕고 싶은 것은 인지상정이에요.
T6-1431.x: Wanting to help people in need is only human.
T6-1431.t: Used to call a feeling natural: -는 것은 인지상정이다 'it's only human to …'.

T6-1432.m: a single word (usually 'not even a word')
T6-1432.x: He left without a single word, let alone an apology.
T6-1432.t: Almost always negative: 일언반구도 없다 'to not say a single word'.

T6-1433.x: He caught the ball as fast as lightning.
T6-1433.e: Literally 'a lightning flash, a spark from struck stone'.

T6-1434.m: unprecedented and never to be repeated, one of a kind
T6-1434.x: That athlete set a record never seen before and likely never again.
T6-1434.t: Usually 전무후무한 + noun, especially 기록 or 사건.

T6-1435.m: gnashing one's teeth with resolve, burning determination after a defeat
T6-1435.ex: 지난 대회에서 진 뒤 그는 절치부심하며 연습했어요.
T6-1435.x: After losing the last tournament, he practiced with fierce determination.
T6-1435.e: Literally 'grinding teeth and rotting the heart' — seething anger turned into resolve.

T6-1436.m: getting better and better; (ironically) going from bad to worse
T6-1436.ex: 드라마가 갈수록 점입가경이라 다음 회가 기다려져요.
T6-1436.x: The drama keeps getting better, so I can't wait for the next episode.
T6-1436.t: Often sarcastic today: 갈수록 점입가경이다 'it just keeps getting more absurd'.

T6-1437.ex: 정부 정책이 조변석개하니 국민들이 크게 혼란스러워해요.
T6-1437.x: Government policies change from day to day, so citizens are very confused.
T6-1437.e: Literally 'change in the morning, alter in the evening'.

T6-1438.m: a narrow view of the world, like a frog in a well
T6-1438.ex: 좌정관천에서 벗어나려면 다양한 경험을 해 봐야 해요.
T6-1438.x: To escape a narrow view of the world, you need diverse experiences.
T6-1438.e: Literally 'sitting in a well, looking at the sky'.
T6-1438.t: The everyday equivalent is 우물 안 개구리 'a frog in a well'.

T6-1439.m: skimming superficially, looking at things in a rush
T6-1439.x: I didn't have time, so I just rushed through the museum.
T6-1439.e: Literally 'viewing mountains from a galloping horse'.

T6-1440.m: twisting the truth through power, deliberately calling black white
T6-1440.x: No one dared object when the powerful man twisted the truth.
T6-1440.e: Literally 'pointing at a deer and calling it a horse' — a Qin minister testing loyalty.

T6-1441.m: a world of difference, night and day
T6-1441.ex: 같은 가격인데도 두 제품의 품질은 천양지차예요.
T6-1441.x: Even at the same price, the quality of the two products is night and day.
T6-1441.e: Literally 'the gap between heaven and earth'.
T6-1441.t: The everyday version is 하늘과 땅 차이.

T6-1442.m: divine help, a stroke of providence
T6-1442.ex: 천우신조로 큰 사고에서 가족 모두 무사했어요.
T6-1442.x: By a miracle, the whole family came through the serious accident unharmed.
T6-1442.t: Typically 천우신조로 'by the grace of heaven'.

T6-1443.m: perfect composure, staying calm and unruffled
T6-1443.ex: 그는 위기 속에서도 태연자약한 모습을 보였어요.
T6-1443.x: He stayed perfectly calm even in the middle of the crisis.

T6-1444.m: being discarded once one's usefulness is over
T6-1444.x: Once the election was over, he was tossed aside.
T6-1444.e: Literally 'when the rabbit dies, the hunting dog gets cooked'.
T6-1444.t: Usually 토사구팽을 당하다 'to be used and then thrown away'.

T6-1445.m: a precarious situation, hanging by a thread
T6-1445.x: Because of the war, the nation's fate hung by a thread.
T6-1445.e: Literally 'a lamp flame in front of the wind'.

T6-1446.m: there must be a reason behind it
T6-1446.ex: 그가 갑자기 그만둔 데에는 필유곡절이 있을 거예요.
T6-1446.x: There must be some reason why he suddenly quit.
T6-1446.e: Literally 'there must be twists and turns' behind it.
T6-1446.t: 곡절 is common on its own too, as in 우여곡절 'ups and downs'.

T6-1447.m: success through diligent study despite hardship
T6-1447.x: He studied hard against all odds and became a doctor.
T6-1447.e: Literally 'achievement by firefly light and snow glow' — poor scholars reading at night.

T6-1448.m: borrowing someone else's power to throw one's weight around
T6-1448.ex: 사장 아들이라고 호가호위하는 사람은 아무도 좋아하지 않아요.
T6-1448.x: Nobody likes someone who throws his weight around for being the boss's son.
T6-1448.e: Literally 'the fox borrows the tiger's might'.
T6-1448.t: Often a verb: 호가호위하다 'to lord it over others with borrowed power'.

T6-1449.m: a vast, free spirit; broad-minded vigor
T6-1449.ex: 산에 올라 호연지기를 기르는 것도 좋아요.
T6-1449.x: Climbing mountains is also a good way to nurture a broad, free spirit.
T6-1449.e: From Mencius: a vast, upright energy that fills heaven and earth.
T6-1449.t: Set phrase: 호연지기를 기르다 'to cultivate a great spirit'.

T6-1450.m: being scared out of one's wits
T6-1450.ex: 골목에서 갑자기 큰 개가 짖어서 혼비백산했어요.
T6-1450.x: A big dog suddenly barked in the alley, and I was scared out of my wits.
T6-1450.e: Literally 'the soul flies off, the spirit scatters'.
T6-1450.t: Common as 혼비백산하다, or 혼비백산하여 달아나다 'to flee in terror'.

T6-1451.ex: 회자정리라지만 친구와 헤어지는 건 늘 슬퍼요.
T6-1451.x: They say all who meet must part, but leaving friends is always sad.
T6-1451.e: A Buddhist teaching: 'those who meet are bound to part'.
T6-1451.t: Pronounced [회자정니]; often paired with 거자필반 'those who leave will return'.

T6-1452.x: Pushing his own mistake onto others — how shameless!

T6-1453.m: joy ends and sorrow follows; life's ups and downs
T6-1453.ex: 흥진비래라더니 좋은 일 뒤에 힘든 일이 생겼어요.
T6-1453.x: Just as they say, after joy comes sorrow — hard times followed the good ones.
T6-1453.e: Literally 'when joy is used up, sorrow comes'.
T6-1453.t: Its opposite pair is 고진감래 'after bitterness comes sweetness'.

T6-1454.m: deep gratitude, being thankful for whatever one gets
T6-1454.ex: 요즘 같은 때에 일자리가 있는 것만도 감지덕지예요.
T6-1454.x: In times like these, just having a job is something to be grateful for.
T6-1454.e: Literally 'feel it, count it a blessing' — humble gratitude.
T6-1454.t: Often -만 해도 감지덕지다 'I'd be grateful for even …'; can sound self-deprecating.

T6-1455.m: thinking of what is right when seeing profit
T6-1455.x: Public officials must put what is right before profit.
T6-1455.e: From Confucius: 'when you see gain, think of what is right'.
T6-1455.t: Pronounced [결리사의]; famous as calligraphy by independence fighter Ahn Jung-geun.

T6-1456.m: being isolated and helpless, alone with no support
T6-1456.x: He ended up isolated at work, with no one to support him.

T6-1457.m: fairness and impartiality, with no personal bias
T6-1457.x: A judge must always rule fairly and impartially.
T6-1457.e: Literally 'fair and even, without private interest'.

T6-1458.m: remarkable progress; seeing someone in a new light
T6-1458.ex: 그의 한국어 실력이 1년 만에 괄목상대할 만큼 늘었어요.
T6-1458.x: His Korean improved remarkably in just one year.
T6-1458.e: Literally 'rubbing one's eyes to look again' at someone who has improved.
T6-1458.t: The news phrase 괄목할 만한 성장 'remarkable growth' uses just the first half.

T6-1459.m: flattering words and an ingratiating face, sweet talk
T6-1459.x: Don't be fooled by sweet talk; look at what people do.
T6-1459.e: From Confucius: smooth talk and a fawning face rarely come with true virtue.

T6-1460.m: you become like the company you keep
T6-1460.ex: 근묵자흑이라고, 나쁜 친구는 멀리하는 게 좋아요.
T6-1460.x: You become like the company you keep, so it's best to avoid bad friends.
T6-1460.e: Literally 'whoever stays near ink turns black'.

T6-1461.x: He won a gold medal at the Olympics and returned home in glory.
T6-1461.e: Literally 'returning home in silk robes' — coming back a success.
T6-1461.t: Usually 금의환향하다; here 금 means 'silk brocade', not 'gold'.

T6-1462.x: That movie is famous for its utterly unexpected twist.
T6-1462.e: Literally 'a strange idea from beyond the sky'.
T6-1462.t: Usually 기상천외한 + noun, e.g. 기상천외한 아이디어 'a wild idea'.

T6-1463.m: being eventful and full of difficulties
T6-1463.x: An eventful year is drawing to a close.
T6-1463.t: A year-end cliché: 다사다난했던 한 해를 보내며 'saying goodbye to an eventful year'.

T6-1464.ex: 단도직입적으로 말할게요. 그 계획은 안 돼요.
T6-1464.x: I'll be blunt: that plan won't work.
T6-1464.e: Literally 'charging straight in with a single sword'.
T6-1464.t: Most common as 단도직입적으로 묻다/말하다 'to ask/say directly'.

T6-1465.m: a hopeless fight against a far stronger opponent
T6-1465.ex: 작은 가게가 대기업과 경쟁하는 건 당랑거철 같아요.
T6-1465.x: A small shop competing with a big corporation is like a mantis facing a chariot.
T6-1465.e: Literally 'a praying mantis trying to block a chariot wheel'.
T6-1465.t: Pronounced [당낭거철] — the ㄹ becomes ㄴ after ㅇ.

T6-1466.m: elation and triumph, being puffed up with pride
T6-1466.ex: 시험에 합격한 동생이 득의양양한 표정을 지었어요.
T6-1466.x: My younger sibling, having passed the exam, looked triumphant.
T6-1466.e: Literally 'having gotten one's wish, spirits soaring high'.

T6-1467.m: regret that it is too late, a belated lament
T6-1467.ex: 지금 대책을 세워도 만시지탄이라는 비판이 있어요.
T6-1467.x: Critics say that even if measures are taken now, it's too little, too late.
T6-1467.e: Literally 'a sigh over the lateness of the hour'.
T6-1467.t: Pattern: 만시지탄의 감이 있다 'it feels belated', common in editorials.
rel: fixing the barn after losing the cow

T6-1468.m: a sight too awful to look at, an unbearable scene
T6-1468.x: The beach full of trash was a truly unbearable sight.
T6-1468.e: Literally 'the eyes cannot bear to see it'.

T6-1469.ex: 졸업 후에 무위도식하며 지낼 수는 없어요.
T6-1469.x: I can't just sit around doing nothing after graduation.

T6-1470.m: a last stand, fighting with no way to retreat
T6-1470.ex: 그는 이번 시험에 배수진을 치고 모든 것을 걸었어요.
T6-1470.x: He burned his bridges and staked everything on this exam.
T6-1470.e: Literally 'a battle line with water at its back' — no retreat possible.
T6-1470.t: Set phrase: 배수진을 치다 'to burn one's bridges, make a last stand'.

T6-1471.x: Countless people have given up on this work.
T6-1471.t: Used as a predicate: -은/는 부지기수다 'there are countless …'.

T6-1472.m: foolishly waiting for luck to repeat, clinging to old ways
T6-1472.ex: 옛날 방식만 고집하는 건 수주대토와 같아요.
T6-1472.x: Sticking only to old methods is like waiting by the stump for another rabbit.
T6-1472.e: A farmer saw a rabbit hit a stump, then waited there forever for another.

T6-1473.m: a fresh start, turning over a new leaf
T6-1473.x: Let's put the failure behind us and start again with a fresh mind.
T6-1473.e: Literally 'the workings of the heart turn completely around'.
T6-1473.t: Common as 심기일전하다, often at New Year or after a setback.

T6-1474.x: My grandmother lives happily in the countryside, content with what she has.
T6-1474.e: Literally 'at ease with one's lot, knowing what is enough'.

T6-1475.m: practicing what one preaches, words matching actions
T6-1475.ex: 국민의 신뢰를 얻으려면 지도자에게는 언행일치가 중요합니다.
T6-1475.x: To earn the public's trust, a leader must practice what they preach.

T6-1476.m: having nothing to say for oneself
T6-1476.x: It's all my fault, so I really have nothing to say for myself.
T6-1476.e: Literally 'having a mouth but no words'.
T6-1476.t: Used in apologies to humbly admit fault, especially in formal settings.

T6-1477.m: a mudslinging fight, a dirty and ugly struggle
T6-1477.x: The election is turning into a mudslinging fight.
T6-1477.e: Literally 'dogs fighting in a muddy field'.
T6-1477.t: Common in political news; 진흙탕 싸움 is the everyday equivalent.

T6-1478.m: being caught in one's own trap
T6-1478.x: He kept lying and ended up trapped by his own words.
T6-1478.e: Literally 'binding oneself with one's own rope'.

T6-1479.m: tossing and turning, being unable to sleep
T6-1479.x: I was so worried about tomorrow's exam that I tossed and turned all night.
T6-1479.e: From an ancient Chinese poem: rolling from side to side, unable to sleep.

T6-1480.m: orders that change constantly, inconsistent policy
T6-1480.ex: 조령모개식 정책 때문에 시민들의 불만이 커지고 있습니다.
T6-1480.x: Citizens are growing frustrated with policies that change constantly.
T6-1480.e: Literally 'an order in the morning, changed by evening'.
T6-1480.t: Usually criticism of government: 조령모개식 정책 'flip-flopping policy'.

T6-1481.m: the Seven Sages of the Bamboo Grove
T6-1481.ex: 죽림칠현은 세상을 피해 숲에서 술과 시를 즐겼어요.
T6-1481.x: The Seven Sages of the Bamboo Grove fled the world to enjoy wine and poetry in the woods.
T6-1481.e: Seven third-century Chinese scholars who quit politics; a symbol of carefree retreat.

T6-1482.m: an outrage that angers heaven and people alike
T6-1482.ex: 어린이를 노린 그 사건은 천인공노할 범죄입니다.
T6-1482.x: That crime targeting children is an outrage to heaven and humanity alike.
T6-1482.e: Literally 'heaven and people are angry together'.
T6-1482.t: Fixed pattern: 천인공노할 + noun (범죄, 만행) for atrocities.

T6-1483.m: thoroughness, being thorough from start to finish
T6-1483.ex: 그는 일을 할 때 항상 철두철미하게 준비합니다.
T6-1483.x: He always prepares thoroughly when he works.
T6-1483.e: Literally 'thorough at the head, thorough at the tail' — complete from start to finish.
T6-1483.t: Mostly used as 철두철미하다 or 철두철미하게 to praise careful, flawless work.

T6-1484.m: full of ups and downs, eventful (life or history)
T6-1484.x: My grandmother lived a life full of ups and downs.
T6-1484.e: Literally 'billows ten thousand jang high' (a jang is about ten feet) — a life tossed by enormous waves.
T6-1484.t: Almost always appears as 파란만장한 삶, 인생, or 역사.

T6-1485.m: bluster, empty bravado, putting on a show of strength
T6-1485.x: His confidence was nothing but empty bluster.
T6-1485.e: Literally 'puffing up emptiness, inflating one's voice and power.'
T6-1485.t: Often paired with 부리다: 허장성세를 부리다 means to bluster or put on airs.

T6-1486.m: to state, to express (an opinion formally)
T6-1486.x: At the meeting, everyone freely expressed their opinions.
T6-1486.e: Literally 'open up and lay out' one's thoughts.
T6-1486.t: Almost always used with 의견 or 견해: 의견을 개진하다.

T6-1487.m: to maintain, to hold firmly (a position or view)
T6-1487.x: The government said it would maintain its existing position.

T6-1488.m: to devote, to pour (effort or energy into)
T6-1488.ex: 회사는 신제품 개발에 모든 노력을 경주했습니다.
T6-1488.x: The company devoted all its efforts to developing the new product.
T6-1488.e: Literally 'tilt and pour' — pouring all your energy into one thing.
T6-1488.t: Don't confuse with 경주 'race' (競走) or the city 경주; this one goes with 노력을.

T6-1489.m: to stick to, to adhere firmly to
T6-1489.ex: 그 식당은 전통 방식을 고수하고 있어요.
T6-1489.x: That restaurant sticks to the traditional way of doing things.
T6-1489.e: Literally 'firmly guard' — refusing to let go.
T6-1489.t: Homonym alert: 고수 can also mean an expert (高手) or cilantro.

T6-1490.m: to inspire, to instill, to boost (spirit or awareness)
T6-1490.x: This campaign stirred up citizens' patriotism.
T6-1490.e: Literally 'beat the drum and blow the horn' to rouse people.

T6-1491.m: to carry through, to push through (a demand or will) to the end
T6-1491.x: The union finally got its demands accepted.
T6-1491.t: Common pattern: 요구를 관철하다 or 뜻을 관철하다, meaning to get one's way in the end.

T6-1492.m: to look down on, to treat with contempt, to slight
T6-1492.x: You shouldn't look down on people just because they're poor.
T6-1492.e: Literally 'look at someone indifferently' — treating them as unimportant.
T6-1492.t: Pronounced [괄씨] — tensing after ㄹ in Sino-Korean words.

T6-1493.m: to enjoy (to the fullest), to bask in (prosperity, success)
T6-1493.ex: 그 회사는 최근 최고의 호황을 구가하고 있습니다.
T6-1493.x: The company is currently enjoying its best boom ever.
T6-1493.e: Literally 'sing praises' — singing about your good times.
T6-1493.t: Typical objects: 자유, 전성기, 호황, 인기 — something good you are enjoying.

T6-1494.m: to study thoroughly, to investigate deeply
T6-1494.x: He spent his whole life deeply studying human nature.
T6-1494.e: Literally 'exhaust and investigate' — studying until nothing is left.

T6-1495.m: to come to (a conclusion), to end up in, to result in
T6-1495.ex: 결국 모든 논의는 비용 문제로 귀결됐습니다.
T6-1495.x: In the end, every discussion came down to the issue of cost.
T6-1495.e: Literally 'return and tie up' — everything ends up at one point.
T6-1495.t: Usually used with -(으)로: N(으)로 귀결되다 = to boil down to N.

T6-1496.m: to reveal, to expose (a weakness or problem)
T6-1496.ex: 이번 사고는 안전 관리의 허점을 노정했습니다.
T6-1496.x: This accident exposed the holes in safety management.
T6-1496.e: Literally 'show openly' — something hidden comes out.
T6-1496.t: Homonym: 노정 (路程) means route or journey; this verb is about exposing flaws.

T6-1497.m: to toy with, to manipulate, to make a fool of
T6-1497.e: Literally 'basket and rope' — catching and controlling someone like an animal.
T6-1497.t: Pronounced [농나카다] — ㄹ becomes ㄴ after ㅇ.

T6-1498.m: to carry out (decisively), to push ahead with
T6-1498.x: The government pushed ahead with large-scale restructuring.
T6-1498.t: Used for bold moves: 개혁, 인사, 구조 조정을 단행하다.

T6-1500.forms: 미연에 방지해요 · 미연에 방지했어요 · 미연에 방지하세요
T6-1500.m: to prevent beforehand, to nip in the bud
T6-1500.ex: 정기 점검으로 사고를 미연에 방지할 수 있습니다.
T6-1500.x: Regular inspections can prevent accidents before they happen.
T6-1500.e: Literally 'prevent while it is not yet so.'
T6-1500.t: 미연 is almost never used alone; it appears in 미연에 방지하다 or 미연에 막다.

T6-1501.m: to deprive of, to strip of (rights, a title)
T6-1501.x: That athlete was stripped of his medal for doping.
T6-1501.t: Often passive with 당하다: 자격을 박탈당하다 = to be stripped of one's qualification.

T6-1502.m: to overflow, to flood; to be flooded with (a glut of something)
T6-1502.x: The river overflowed because of the heavy rain.
T6-1502.e: Both syllables carry the water radical — water spreading everywhere.
T6-1502.t: Pronounced [범남하다] — ㄹ becomes ㄴ after ㅁ.

T6-1503.m: to do side by side, to combine, to do in parallel
T6-1503.x: He is balancing work and study at the same time.

T6-1504.m: to be highlighted, to come to the fore, to stand out
T6-1504.ex: 최근 환경 문제가 크게 부각되고 있습니다.
T6-1504.x: Environmental issues have recently come to the fore.
T6-1504.e: Literally 'carved in relief' — something raised so it stands out.

T6-1505.m: to erupt, to spew, to gush out; to burst out (emotions, demands)
T6-1505.t: Also figurative: 불만이 분출하다 = discontent bursts out.

T6-1506.m: to dispel, to wipe out (doubts, concerns)
T6-1506.x: The company tried to dispel consumers' anxiety.
T6-1506.t: Typical objects: 우려, 의혹, 불안, 편견 — negative feelings or doubts.

T6-1507.m: to shield, to protect (often wrongly), to cover for
T6-1507.ex: 그 정치인은 비리 공무원을 비호했다는 의혹을 받았습니다.
T6-1507.x: The politician was suspected of covering for a corrupt official.
T6-1507.t: Usually negative: shielding someone who doesn't deserve protection.

T6-1508.m: to use as a pretext, to do under the pretense of
T6-1508.x: He went on a trip under the pretext of a business trip.
T6-1508.e: Literally 'lean on and rely on' — leaning on an excuse.
T6-1508.t: Common pattern: N을/를 빙자하여 or N을/를 빙자한 사기 (fraud).

T6-1509.m: to instigate, to put someone up to (a wrongdoing)
T6-1509.ex: 경찰은 누가 범행을 사주했는지 조사하고 있습니다.
T6-1509.x: The police are investigating who instigated the crime.
T6-1509.e: Literally 'make someone do it by egging them on.'
T6-1509.t: Homonym: 사주 (四柱) is fortune-telling by birth date; 사주 (社主) is a company owner.

T6-1510.x: Rising exports offset weak domestic demand.
T6-1510.e: Literally 'mutually cancel' — two forces wiping each other out.
T6-1510.t: The second syllable is read 쇄, not 살 — a classic reading trap for this hanja.

T6-1511.m: to read extensively, to range widely over (books, fields)
T6-1511.ex: 그는 젊었을 때 고전을 두루 섭렵했어요.
T6-1511.x: When he was young, he read widely through the classics.
T6-1511.e: Literally 'wade through and hunt' — roaming widely through a field.

T6-1512.m: to go back (to), to apply retroactively
T6-1512.x: This law applies retroactively from January of last year.
T6-1512.t: Very common in legal and pay contexts: 소급 적용, 소급하여 지급하다.

T6-1513.m: to explain, to justify, to vindicate (oneself officially)
T6-1513.x: He explained himself regarding the allegations at the hearing.
T6-1513.e: Literally 'clear up and make bright' — clarifying the facts.
T6-1513.t: Homonym: 소명 (召命) means a calling or vocation, as in 소명 의식.

T6-1514.m: to jump to conclusions, to judge hastily
T6-1514.x: It's too early to jump to conclusions about the result.
T6-1514.t: Set phrase: 속단하기는 이르다 = it's too early to tell.

T6-1515.m: to pour in, to flood in, to rush
T6-1515.x: Orders for the new product are pouring in.
T6-1515.e: Literally 'arrive intensely' — everything rushes in at once.

T6-1516.m: to guard, to defend, to protect

T6-1517.x: I'll decide after giving it careful thought.
T6-1517.e: Literally 'ripe thinking' — thoughts left to mature.
T6-1517.t: Often appears as the idiom 심사숙고하다 = to think long and hard.

T6-1518.m: to be damaged, to fall (of reputation, authority)
T6-1518.ex: 이번 사건으로 회사의 이미지가 크게 실추됐습니다.
T6-1518.x: The company's image was badly damaged by this incident.
T6-1518.t: Collocates with 명예, 위신, 신뢰, 이미지.

T6-1519.m: to abuse, to misuse, to exploit (for bad ends)
T6-1519.ex: 개인 정보를 악용하는 범죄가 늘고 있습니다.
T6-1519.x: Crimes that misuse personal information are increasing.

T6-1520.m: to settle down; to be complacent, to rest on one's laurels
T6-1520.x: Don't settle for where you are now; keep challenging yourself.
T6-1520.t: Homonym: 안주 (按酒) means snacks eaten with alcohol.

T6-1521.m: to mass-produce; to produce in large numbers (often of bad things)
T6-1521.x: The misguided policy produced large numbers of unemployed people.
T6-1521.t: Homonym: 양산 (陽傘) is a parasol.

T6-1522.m: to appeal (to), to attract; to make one's case
T6-1522.ex: 이 광고는 젊은 층에게 어필하고 있어요.
T6-1522.x: This ad appeals to young people.
T6-1522.e: From English 'appeal.' Mostly means 'to attract' or 'to show off one's strengths.'
T6-1522.t: 자신을 어필하다 means to sell yourself, as in a job interview.

T6-1523.m: to speculate (groundlessly), to make wild guesses
T6-1523.x: Don't speculate about things that aren't certain.
T6-1523.e: Literally 'guess by one's own thoughts' — guessing without evidence.
T6-1523.t: More often used as a noun: 억측이 난무하다 = wild speculation runs rampant.

T6-1524.m: to strictly observe, to keep strictly (time, rules)
T6-1524.x: Please strictly observe the exam time.

T6-1525.m: to lead (a life), to run, to carry on (a business or activity)
T6-1525.ex: 누구나 인간다운 삶을 영위할 권리가 있습니다.
T6-1525.x: Everyone has the right to lead a decent human life.
T6-1525.t: Most common object: 삶 or 생활 — 삶을 영위하다 = to lead a life.

T6-1526.m: to talk about, to mention (dismissively), to say this and that
T6-1526.x: Before going on about responsibility, let's check the facts first.
T6-1526.e: Literally 'say, say' — 'and so on and so forth.'
T6-1526.t: Often slightly critical: someone keeps bringing something up inappropriately.

T6-1527.m: to violate, to go against (rules, principles)
T6-1527.x: That decision goes against the constitution.
T6-1527.e: Literally 'go against and turn one's back.'
T6-1527.t: Pattern: N에 위배되다 — note the particle 에, not 을.

T6-1528.m: to bear in mind, to keep in mind
T6-1528.x: Please keep the following points in mind.

T6-1529.m: to infer by analogy, to deduce
T6-1529.ex: 앞뒤 문맥으로 단어의 뜻을 유추해 보세요.
T6-1529.x: Try to infer the word's meaning from the surrounding context.

T6-1530.m: to punish, to chastise, to retaliate against
T6-1530.ex: 정부는 테러 세력을 강력히 응징하겠다고 밝혔습니다.
T6-1530.x: The government vowed to punish the terrorist groups severely.

T6-1531.m: to shout (a rebuke), to roar out, to rebuke sharply
T6-1531.x: The teacher sharply rebuked the noisy students.
T6-1531.e: Literally 'one shout' — a single loud, sharp rebuke.

T6-1532.m: to be consistent, to stick to one approach throughout
T6-1532.x: He remained silent to the very end.
T6-1532.t: Pattern: N(으)로 일관하다, e.g. 침묵으로 일관하다 = to stay silent throughout.

T6-1533.m: to entrust entirely, to leave (something) completely to someone
T6-1533.x: We left all the decisions entirely to the team leader.
T6-1533.e: Literally 'one entrusting' — handing over the whole thing.
T6-1533.t: Pronounced [이림하다] — the ㄹ links to the next vowel.

T6-1534.m: to take on oneself (a role), to consider oneself as
T6-1534.ex: 그는 스스로 환경 운동의 대변인을 자임했습니다.
T6-1534.x: He took it upon himself to be the spokesperson for the environmental movement.

T6-1535.m: to call oneself, to pose as; to bring on oneself
T6-1535.e: Literally 'place oneself' in a role or situation.
T6-1535.t: 고생을 자처하다 means to choose hardship voluntarily.

T6-1536.m: to encroach on, to eat into, to erode gradually
T6-1536.ex: 외국 기업들이 국내 시장을 잠식하고 있습니다.
T6-1536.x: Foreign companies are eating into the domestic market.
T6-1536.e: Literally 'silkworm eating' — nibbling away bit by bit like a silkworm on a leaf.

T6-1537.x: That plan needs to be reconsidered.
T6-1537.t: Homonym: 재고 (在庫) means stock or inventory, and 제고 means to raise.

T6-1538.m: to hinder, to impede, to hamper
T6-1538.ex: 지나친 규제는 경제 성장을 저해할 수 있습니다.
T6-1538.x: Excessive regulation can hinder economic growth.

T6-1539.m: to shift (blame or burden) onto someone, to pass the buck
T6-1539.x: Don't shift the blame for your mistakes onto others.
T6-1539.e: Literally 'transfer and pass off' — the second syllable originally meant marrying a daughter off into another family, hence sending something over to someone else.
T6-1539.t: Fixed collocation: 책임을 전가하다 or 부담을 전가하다.

T6-1540.m: to be dotted with, to be marked by (a series of events)
T6-1540.x: His life was marked by failure and frustration.
T6-1540.e: Literally 'dotted and stitched together' — a life strung with events.
T6-1540.t: Pattern: N(으)로 점철되다, usually with negative things like 실패, 갈등, 고난.

T6-1541.m: to raise, to enhance, to improve (efficiency, awareness)
T6-1541.ex: 정부는 국가 경쟁력을 제고하기 위해 노력하고 있습니다.
T6-1541.x: The government is working to enhance national competitiveness.
T6-1541.t: Don't confuse with 재고하다 (to reconsider) — they sound almost the same.

T6-1542.m: to create, to build (an atmosphere, environment, fund); to develop (a park, site)
T6-1542.x: The city created a park along the riverbank.
T6-1542.t: Common objects: 분위기, 환경, 공원, 기금 — creating something that wasn't there.

T6-1543.m: to urge, to press (someone to do something)
T6-1543.x: The company pressured employees to resign.
T6-1543.t: Usually implies pressure, as in 사퇴를 종용하다 = to push someone to step down.

T6-1544.m: to be based on, to conform to (a standard)
T6-1544.ex: 이 평가는 국제 기준에 준거하여 실시됩니다.
T6-1544.x: This assessment is conducted based on international standards.
T6-1544.e: Literally 'follow and rely on' a standard.

T6-1545.m: to avoid, to refrain from, to move away from
T6-1545.e: From Hegel's 'Aufheben,' literally 'stop and raise'; in everyday Korean it simply means to avoid.
T6-1545.t: Opposite-looking pair: 지양 = avoid, 지향 = aim toward. Learners mix them up constantly.

T6-1546.m: to boost, to stimulate, to raise (morale, an economy)
T6-1546.ex: 정부는 내수를 진작하기 위한 대책을 발표했습니다.
T6-1546.x: The government announced measures to boost domestic demand.
T6-1546.t: Homonym: the adverb 진작 means 'earlier, long before' as in 진작 말하지.

T6-1547.m: to rebuke, to castigate, to scold sharply
T6-1547.x: The lawmakers castigated the minister's irresponsible attitude.
T6-1547.e: Literally 'shout and scold' — both syllables mean to yell at.

T6-1548.m: to create, to generate (jobs, value, profits)
T6-1548.ex: 새 공장은 많은 일자리를 창출할 것입니다.
T6-1548.x: The new factory will create many jobs.

T6-1549.m: to delve into, to dig deeply into (a subject)
T6-1549.ex: 그 작가는 평생 인간의 고독에 천착했습니다.
T6-1549.x: The writer delved into human loneliness all his life.
T6-1549.e: Literally 'pierce and chisel' — boring deep into a subject.

T6-1550.m: to trigger, to spark, to set off
T6-1550.x: That remark sparked a huge controversy.
T6-1550.e: Literally 'touch and set off' — a touch that sets something off.

T6-1551.m: to revere, to look up to, to venerate
T6-1551.x: The people revered him as a hero.
T6-1551.e: Literally 'push up and look up to.'
T6-1551.t: Pattern: N을/를 N(으)로 추앙하다 = to revere someone as...

T6-1552.m: to put emphasis on, to focus (too much) on
T6-1552.x: Don't focus only on looks; take care of your inner self too.
T6-1552.t: Often implies imbalance: N에 치중하다 = to overemphasize N.

T6-1553.m: to break down, to abolish, to do away with (customs, prejudice)
T6-1553.x: We must do away with outdated customs.

T6-1554.m: to emerge, to begin to stir, to be born (of a movement or era)
T6-1554.ex: 이 시기에 새로운 예술 운동이 태동했습니다.
T6-1554.x: A new art movement began to stir in this period.
T6-1554.e: Literally 'fetal movement' — the first kicks of something not yet born.

T6-1555.m: to feel keenly, to be painfully aware of
T6-1555.ex: 저는 이번 사태에 대해 책임을 통감합니다.
T6-1555.x: I keenly feel my responsibility for this situation.
T6-1555.t: A staple of public apologies: 책임을 통감합니다.

T6-1556.m: to project, to reflect (one's feelings or ideas onto something)
T6-1556.x: The author projected his own experiences onto the main character.
T6-1556.e: Literally 'throw a shadow' — casting an image onto something.

T6-1557.m: to spread, to ripple out, to have a knock-on effect
T6-1557.x: The financial crisis spread across the whole world.
T6-1557.e: Literally 'waves reaching' — ripples spreading across water.
T6-1557.t: Most common as the noun phrase 파급 효과 (ripple effect).

T6-1558.m: to ride on, to jump on the bandwagon, to take advantage of (a trend)
T6-1558.ex: 일부 업체가 유행에 편승해 가격을 올렸습니다.
T6-1558.x: Some businesses took advantage of the trend and raised prices.
T6-1558.e: Literally 'convenient ride' — hitching a ride on someone else's vehicle.
T6-1558.t: Pattern: N에 편승하다; usually slightly negative, implying opportunism.

T6-1559.m: to belittle, to disparage, to play down
T6-1559.ex: 남의 노력을 폄하하는 것은 좋지 않아요.
T6-1559.x: It's not good to belittle other people's efforts.
T6-1559.e: Literally 'lower the rank' of someone or something.

T6-1560.m: to discard, to dispose of; to abolish, to scrap (a law, plan)
T6-1560.ex: 유통 기한이 지난 식품은 모두 폐기했습니다.
T6-1560.x: We disposed of all the food past its expiration date.

T6-1561.ex: 독서는 학생들의 사고력을 함양하는 데 큰 도움이 됩니다.
T6-1561.x: Reading greatly helps cultivate students' thinking skills.
T6-1561.e: Literally 'soak and nourish' — building qualities slowly over time.
T6-1561.t: Typical objects are 인성, 사고력 and 시민 의식 — a staple of education policy writing.

T6-1562.ex: 시험이 끝난 뒤 학생들의 분위기가 많이 해이해졌어요.
T6-1562.x: After the exams ended, the students' attitude became quite lax.
T6-1562.e: Literally 'untied and slackened' — like a loosened bowstring.
T6-1562.t: Usually appears as 해이해지다 'to become lax', often with 기강 'discipline'.

T6-1563.m: to gloss over, to misrepresent, to mislead
T6-1563.ex: 정부가 사실을 호도하고 있다는 비판이 나왔습니다.
T6-1563.x: Criticism arose that the government was misrepresenting the facts.
T6-1563.e: Literally 'paste and smear' — plastering over the truth.
T6-1563.t: Common collocations: 사실을 호도하다 and 여론을 호도하다 'to mislead public opinion'.

T6-1564.ex: 평론가들은 그 영화의 지루한 줄거리를 혹평했어요.
T6-1564.x: Critics panned the movie's boring plot.
T6-1564.t: 혹평을 받다 'to be panned' is very common; the opposite is 호평을 받다.

T6-1565.m: to coexist in a mix, to be mixed together
T6-1565.ex: 이 도시에는 전통과 현대가 혼재해 있어요.
T6-1565.x: In this city, tradition and modernity exist side by side.
T6-1565.e: Literally 'exist mixed' — different things present side by side.

T6-1566.m: to look back on, to recall, to reminisce
T6-1566.ex: 그는 어린 시절을 회고하며 책을 썼어요.
T6-1566.x: He wrote a book looking back on his childhood.

T6-1567.m: to return (to an origin), to revert
T6-1567.ex: 연어는 알을 낳기 위해 태어난 강으로 회귀합니다.
T6-1567.x: Salmon return to the river where they were born to lay eggs.
T6-1567.e: Literally 'turn and go home' — like salmon heading upstream.

T6-1568.m: to damage, to deface; to defame (reputation)
T6-1568.ex: 문화재를 훼손하면 법에 따라 처벌을 받습니다.
T6-1568.x: Damaging cultural heritage is punishable by law.
T6-1568.t: 명예를 훼손하다 'to defame' — 명예 훼손 is the legal term for defamation.

T6-1569.x: Dilute this detergent with water before using it.
T6-1569.t: Figurative use is common too: 의미가 희석되다 'the meaning gets watered down'.

T6-1570.m: to replace (with), to substitute, to let stand in place of
T6-1570.x: I will let this brief introduction stand in place of today's greeting.
T6-1570.e: From 갈다 'to change, to replace' plus the noun ending -음.
T6-1570.t: Don't confuse it with 가름하다 'to divide, to decide' — both are pronounced [가름].

T6-1571.m: to downgrade, to demote, to lower in status
T6-1571.x: The government downgraded the agency's status.

T6-1572.m: to link, to connect, to tie (to)
T6-1572.ex: 그 사건을 정치 문제와 결부해서 생각하면 안 돼요.
T6-1572.x: You shouldn't link that incident to political issues.

T6-1573.m: to become fixed, to become entrenched
T6-1573.ex: 성 역할에 대한 고정관념이 사회에 고착되었습니다.
T6-1573.x: Stereotypes about gender roles have become entrenched in society.

T6-1574.ex: 그는 이번 선거에서 꼭 이기겠다고 공언했어요.
T6-1574.x: He publicly declared that he would definitely win this election.

T6-1575.m: to be bound by, to be constrained by
T6-1575.ex: 나이에 구애되지 않고 누구나 지원할 수 있습니다.
T6-1575.x: Anyone can apply regardless of age.
T6-1575.t: Almost always negative: -에 구애되지 않고 'regardless of'; unrelated to 구애 'courtship'.

T6-1576.m: to yield, to submit, to give in
T6-1576.x: He never gave in to the pressure, right to the end.

T6-1577.ex: 정부는 학교 폭력을 근절하기 위해 노력하고 있습니다.
T6-1577.x: The government is working to root out school violence.

T6-1578.ex: 그 회사는 허위 광고로 소비자를 기만했습니다.
T6-1578.x: The company deceived consumers with false advertising.

T6-1580.ex: 회사 기밀을 누설하면 법적 책임을 져야 합니다.
T6-1580.x: If you leak company secrets, you will face legal liability.

T6-1581.m: to assert, to state flatly, to declare with certainty
T6-1581.ex: 그 계획이 성공할 거라고 단언하기는 어려워요.
T6-1581.x: It's hard to say for certain that the plan will succeed.
T6-1581.e: Literally 'decisive words' — saying it with full certainty.
T6-1581.t: Often negative: -다고 단언할 수 없다 'one can't say for sure that ...'.

T6-1582.m: to be cut off, to be severed, to be disconnected
T6-1582.ex: 폭설로 그 마을과의 교통이 완전히 단절되었습니다.
T6-1582.x: Heavy snow completely cut off transportation to the village.
T6-1582.t: Useful phrases: 세대 단절 'generational disconnect' and 경력 단절 'career break'.

T6-1583.m: to arrive, to come (an era, a time)
T6-1583.ex: 이제 우리 사회에도 인공지능 시대가 도래했습니다.
T6-1583.x: The age of artificial intelligence has now arrived in our society too.

T6-1584.m: to hush up, to smooth over, to appease
T6-1584.x: The company tried to hush up the incident with money.
T6-1584.e: Literally 'stroke and rub' — soothing a problem until it quiets down.
T6-1584.t: Usually has a negative ring: 사건을 무마하다 'to hush up an incident'.

T6-1585.m: to ruminate, to reflect on; to chew the cud
T6-1585.x: He quietly reflected on past events.
T6-1585.e: Literally 'bring fodder back' — how cows chew the cud.
rel: to reflect on, to mull over

T6-1586.m: to reject, to exclude, to ostracize
T6-1586.ex: 다른 문화를 무조건 배척해서는 안 됩니다.
T6-1586.x: We should not reject other cultures out of hand.

T6-1588.m: to be indignant, to resent, to be outraged
T6-1588.x: Citizens were outraged by the government's decision.

T6-1589.m: to belittle, to disparage, to demean
T6-1589.ex: 다른 사람의 외모를 비하하는 말은 하지 마세요.
T6-1589.x: Don't make remarks that belittle other people's looks.
T6-1589.t: Common phrases: 비하 발언 'derogatory remark' and 자기 비하 'self-deprecation'.

T6-1590.m: to submit (a bill) to the agenda, to table
T6-1590.x: The National Assembly put the bill on the plenary session agenda.
T6-1590.t: A homonym 상정하다 (想定) means 'to assume, to suppose', mostly in academic writing.

T6-1591.m: to exceed, to be above (a figure)
T6-1591.x: This year's sales far exceeded expectations.
T6-1591.e: Literally 'go around above' — running higher than a mark.
T6-1591.t: A news word for numbers; the native synonym is 웃돌다.

T6-1592.m: to fall below, to be lower than (a figure)
T6-1592.ex: 이번 분기 실적이 시장 기대치를 하회했습니다.
T6-1592.x: This quarter's earnings fell short of market expectations.
T6-1592.e: Literally 'go around below' — running under a mark.
T6-1592.t: The native equivalent 밑돌다 is more common in everyday news.

T6-1593.m: to select, to screen, to sort out
T6-1593.ex: 회사는 지원자 중에서 우수한 인재를 선별했어요.
T6-1593.x: The company selected top talent from among the applicants.
T6-1593.t: 선별 진료소 'screening clinic' became a familiar term during COVID-19.

T6-1594.m: to expound, to preach, to argue persuasively
T6-1594.x: He preached the importance of peace all his life.
T6-1594.e: Literally 'speak and break through' — explaining until others are convinced.

T6-1595.m: to be prevalent, to be rampant, to flourish
T6-1595.x: Online scams are rampant these days.

T6-1596.ex: 그는 마라톤 후반에 체력을 모두 소진했어요.
T6-1596.x: He used up all his stamina in the second half of the marathon.

T6-1597.m: to agree, to accept, to nod in assent
T6-1597.x: After hearing his explanation, everyone agreed.
T6-1597.e: Literally 'head consenting' — a nod of agreement.

T6-1598.m: to be gathered, to be incorporated (opinions); to converge
T6-1598.ex: 시민들의 의견이 새 정책에 충분히 수렴되었습니다.
T6-1598.x: Citizens' opinions were fully incorporated into the new policy.
T6-1598.t: Active 의견을 수렴하다 'to collect opinions' is very common; in math, 수렴 means 'convergence'.

T6-1599.m: to adapt, to conform, to comply
T6-1599.x: People live by adapting to new environments.
T6-1599.t: 순응 suggests passively going along; 적응 is the neutral word for adjusting.

T6-1600.m: to correct, to rectify, to redress
T6-1600.x: The government announced it would correct the unfair system.
T6-1600.t: Don't confuse it with 시정 (市政) 'city administration' — same sound, different word.

T6-1601.m: to train, to cultivate, to foster (people)
T6-1601.ex: 이 학교는 전문 요리사를 양성하고 있습니다.
T6-1601.t: Homonyms: 양성 (陽性) 'positive test result' and 양성 (兩性) 'both sexes'.

T6-1602.m: to go against, to run counter to
T6-1602.ex: 그 정책은 시대의 흐름에 역행한다는 비판을 받았어요.
T6-1602.x: The policy was criticized for going against the trend of the times.
T6-1602.t: Set phrase: 시대에 역행하다 'to go against the times'.

T6-1603.ex: 그는 그 계획의 문제점을 하나씩 열거했어요.
T6-1603.x: He listed the problems with the plan one by one.
T6-1603.e: Literally 'line up and raise' — holding items up one by one.

T6-1604.m: to come over, to seize (fear, cold); to attack suddenly
T6-1604.ex: 혼자 집에 있으니 갑자기 두려움이 엄습했어요.
T6-1604.x: Being home alone, I was suddenly gripped by fear.
T6-1604.e: Literally 'cover and attack' — a surprise assault.
T6-1604.t: The subject is usually a feeling or weather: 공포, 불안감, 한파가 엄습하다.

T6-1605.m: to mistake (A for B), to misidentify
T6-1605.x: At first, the police mistook him for the criminal.
T6-1605.t: Pattern: A를 B로 오인하다 'to mistake A for B'.

T6-1606.m: to tolerate, to allow, to accept
T6-1606.ex: 이런 부정행위는 절대 용납할 수 없습니다.
T6-1606.x: This kind of cheating can never be tolerated.
T6-1606.t: Mostly negative: 용납할 수 없다 or 용납되지 않는다.

T6-1607.m: to give preferential treatment, to favor
T6-1607.ex: 이 회사는 신입 사원을 뽑을 때 경력자를 우대합니다.
T6-1607.x: When hiring new employees, this company gives preference to experienced applicants.
T6-1607.t: Job ads often say 경력자 우대 'experience preferred'.

T6-1608.x: The dictatorship trampled on the people's human rights.
T6-1608.t: 인권 유린 'human rights abuse' is the most common collocation.

T6-1609.m: to flow in, to be brought in
T6-1609.ex: 해외 자본이 국내 시장에 대거 유입되었습니다.
T6-1609.x: Foreign capital flowed into the domestic market in large amounts.

T6-1610.m: to conceal, to hide (assets, a criminal)
T6-1610.ex: 그는 재산을 해외에 은닉한 혐의를 받고 있습니다.
T6-1610.x: He is suspected of hiding assets overseas.
T6-1610.t: Pronounced [은니카다]; legal phrases include 재산 은닉 and 범인 은닉죄 'harboring a criminal'.

T6-1611.m: to recognize, to be aware of, to perceive
T6-1611.ex: 그는 문제의 심각성을 제대로 인지하지 못했어요.
T6-1611.x: He didn't properly recognize the seriousness of the problem.

T6-1612.ex: 그의 연구는 의학 발전에 크게 일조했습니다.
T6-1612.x: His research contributed greatly to medical progress.
T6-1612.t: Pattern -에 일조하다; it can also be ironic, as in contributing to a problem.

T6-1613.m: to become aware of, to realize (about oneself)
T6-1613.x: He belatedly realized his own mistake.
T6-1613.t: 자각 증상 means symptoms the patient can notice, e.g. 자각 증상이 없다 'no noticeable symptoms'.

T6-1614.m: to seize control of, to take over, to dominate
T6-1614.ex: 그 회사는 국내 시장을 빠르게 장악했어요.
T6-1614.x: The company quickly took over the domestic market.
T6-1614.e: Literally 'grasp in the palm' — holding something firmly in hand.

T6-1615.m: to decline, to deteriorate, to drop
T6-1615.ex: 잠이 부족하면 업무 집중력이 크게 저하됩니다.
T6-1615.x: When you lack sleep, your concentration at work declines significantly.

T6-1616.m: to occupy, to hold, to possess
T6-1616.ex: 그 회사가 국내 시장의 절반을 점유하고 있어요.
T6-1616.x: That company holds half of the domestic market.
T6-1616.t: 시장 점유율 'market share' is the phrase you'll see most.

T6-1617.m: to restrict, to limit, to constrain
T6-1617.ex: 예산 부족이 연구 활동을 제약하고 있어요.
T6-1617.x: A lack of budget is restricting research activities.
T6-1617.t: Don't confuse it with 제약 (製藥) 'pharmaceuticals', as in 제약 회사.

T6-1618.m: to view (a landscape) from above; to survey (a field)
T6-1618.ex: 이 책은 한국 현대사를 폭넓게 조망합니다.
T6-1618.x: This book offers a broad survey of modern Korean history.
T6-1618.t: Real estate ads boast 한강 조망 'Han River view'.
