T6-1619.x: He was the scholar who first advocated gender equality.
T6-1619.e: Literally 'lead the chant' — the first to call out an idea.

T6-1620.e: Literally 'flick with the finger' — pointing at someone in blame.
T6-1620.t: Most often passive in meaning: 사회적 지탄을 받다 'to face public condemnation'.

T6-1621.x: The doctor diagnosed his illness as gastritis.
T6-1621.t: Also figurative: experts 경제 상황을 진단하다 'assess the economic situation'.

T6-1622.m: to condense, to summarize, to concentrate
T6-1622.ex: 이 보고서는 연구 결과를 한 장으로 집약했어요.
T6-1622.x: This report condensed the research findings into one page.

T6-1623.m: to take into account, to consider
T6-1623.ex: 판사는 피고인의 나이를 참작해서 형량을 줄였어요.
T6-1623.x: The judge took the defendant's age into account and reduced the sentence.
T6-1623.t: 정상 참작 'extenuating circumstances' is a common legal phrase.

T6-1624.m: to root out, to eradicate (corruption, evils)
T6-1624.ex: 새 정부는 부정부패를 반드시 척결하겠다고 약속했습니다.
T6-1624.x: The new government promised to root out corruption without fail.
T6-1624.e: Literally 'gouge and pick out' — cutting out something rotten.
T6-1624.t: Mainly used with social evils: 비리, 부패, 적폐를 척결하다.

T6-1625.m: to settle, to pay off (debts); to break with (the past)
T6-1625.ex: 그는 빚을 모두 청산하고 새 출발을 했어요.
T6-1625.x: He paid off all his debts and made a fresh start.
T6-1625.t: Also 과거를 청산하다 'to make a clean break with the past'.

T6-1626.m: to learn through experience, to master by doing
T6-1626.x: He mastered the skills by working on site.
T6-1626.e: Literally 'gain with the body' — learning by doing.

T6-1627.x: Experts estimated the damage at about 10 billion won.

T6-1628.m: to presume, to estimate, to infer
T6-1628.ex: 경찰은 사고 원인을 운전자의 부주의로 추정하고 있습니다.
T6-1628.x: Police presume the cause of the accident was driver carelessness.
T6-1628.t: 추산 is for numbers; 추정 covers any inference — causes, ages, identities.

T6-1629.m: to sound out, to feel out; to percuss (medical)
T6-1629.ex: 그 회사는 해외 진출 가능성을 타진하고 있어요.
T6-1629.x: The company is sounding out the possibility of expanding overseas.
T6-1629.e: Literally 'tap and examine' — like a doctor tapping a patient's chest.

T6-1630.m: to be in common use, to be accepted, to circulate
T6-1630.x: The euro is used in many European countries.
T6-1630.e: Literally 'pass through in use' — accepted everywhere.

T6-1631.m: to be forced out, to be expelled, to be removed
T6-1631.x: The player who cheated was kicked out of the league.
T6-1631.t: 퇴출 means being forced out; leaving voluntarily is 탈퇴.

T6-1632.m: to break (a contract); to destroy (documents); to overturn (a ruling)
T6-1632.x: The company unilaterally broke the contract.
T6-1632.t: In court news, 원심 파기 means 'reversal of the lower court's ruling'.

T6-1633.m: to decide, to determine (an outcome), to settle
T6-1633.ex: 이번 경기가 우승 팀을 판가름할 거예요.
T6-1633.x: This game will decide the championship team.
T6-1633.e: From 판 'round, match' plus 가름 'dividing' — splitting winners from losers.
T6-1633.t: Intransitive 판가름이 나다 'to be settled' is just as common as the verb.

T6-1634.m: to capture, to catch (a moment, signs), to detect
T6-1634.x: The photographer captured the moment the child smiled.

T6-1635.ex: 정부는 그 사건에 대해 유감을 표명했습니다.
T6-1635.x: The government expressed regret over the incident.
T6-1635.t: Formulaic phrases: 유감을 표명하다, 입장을 표명하다, 사의를 표명하다 'to offer to resign'.

T6-1636.x: People's lives were devastated by the long war.

T6-1637.m: to dazzle, to bewilder, to lure (deceptively)
T6-1637.ex: 사기꾼들은 높은 수익을 약속하며 사람들을 현혹했어요.
T6-1637.x: The scammers lured people in by promising high returns.
T6-1637.t: The passive is very common: 광고에 현혹되지 마세요 'Don't be fooled by ads'.

T6-1638.m: to threaten, to intimidate, to blackmail
T6-1638.ex: 그 남자는 돈을 주지 않으면 비밀을 폭로하겠다고 협박했어요.
T6-1638.x: The man threatened to reveal the secret if he wasn't paid.

T6-1639.m: to embody, to give concrete form to, to depict
T6-1639.x: This work gives concrete form to the pain of war.
T6-1639.e: Literally 'turn into shape and image' — making the abstract visible.
T6-1639.t: Common in art and literary criticism: 고통을 형상화하다 'to portray suffering in concrete form'.

T6-1640.ex: 그 소문은 인터넷을 통해 빠르게 확산되었습니다.
T6-1640.x: The rumor spread quickly through the internet.
T6-1640.t: Typical in news about diseases, rumors and trends: 감염이 확산되다 'infections spread'.

T6-1641.ex: 두 사람은 어릴 때부터 각별한 사이였어요.
T6-1641.x: The two of them have been especially close since childhood.
T6-1641.e: Literally 'each set apart' — treated as special.

T6-1642.x: He asked for help in an earnest voice.
T6-1642.e: Literally 'earnest and thorough' — pleading with full sincerity.
T6-1642.t: Almost always with requests: 간곡히 부탁드립니다 'I earnestly ask you'. Pronounced [간고카다].

T6-1643.x: It's best to write reports concisely.

T6-1644.ex: 선생님은 어려운 개념을 간명하게 설명해 주셨어요.
T6-1644.x: The teacher explained the difficult concept simply and clearly.
T6-1644.t: 간명하다 stresses clarity, 간결하다 stresses brevity — both praise good writing.

T6-1645.x: My grandfather is over eighty but still strong and healthy.

T6-1646.ex: 그는 강직한 성품으로 많은 존경을 받았어요.
T6-1646.x: He was greatly respected for his upright character.
T6-1646.e: Literally 'firm and straight' — someone who won't bend.

T6-1647.ex: 그는 한국 문학사에서 가장 걸출한 시인 중 한 명이에요.
T6-1647.x: He is one of the most outstanding poets in Korean literary history.
T6-1647.e: Literally 'a hero who stands out' from the crowd.

T6-1649.ex: 그런 고루한 생각은 이제 버려야 해요.
T6-1649.x: You need to let go of that old-fashioned way of thinking.
T6-1649.e: Literally 'rigid and crude' — stuck in old ways.
T6-1649.t: It criticizes stubbornly outdated thinking, not age: 고루한 사고방식 'a fusty mindset'.

T6-1650.m: lofty, noble, exalted (of character or ideals)
T6-1650.x: Everyone respected the teacher's noble character.
T6-1650.t: Mostly in set phrases praising others: 고매한 인품, 고매한 뜻.

T6-1651.x: That person is very refined in speech and manner.

T6-1652.x: As evening fell, the mountain temple grew quiet and still.
T6-1652.e: A favorite word for calm, still places like old temples or villages at dusk.

T6-1653.ex: 두 후보의 입장 차이가 극명하게 드러났어요.
T6-1653.x: The difference between the two candidates' positions became starkly clear.
T6-1653.e: Literally 'thoroughly clear' — often used for stark contrasts.
T6-1653.t: Pronounced [긍명하다] — nasalization; usually with 드러나다 or 대비되다.

T6-1654.x: The judge read the ruling with a stern expression.

T6-1655.x: The government must respond swiftly to the crisis.
T6-1655.t: Usually with 대응하다 or 움직이다: 기민하게 대응하다 'to respond swiftly'.

T6-1656.ex: 이 철학책은 너무 난해해서 읽기 힘들어요.
T6-1656.x: This philosophy book is so abstruse that it's hard to read.

T6-1657.m: easy, pushover (usually negated: not easy, tough)
T6-1657.ex: 요즘 취업 시장은 결코 녹록하지 않아요.
T6-1657.x: The job market these days is by no means easy.
T6-1657.e: From a word meaning 'ordinary, mediocre'; today almost always used negatively.
T6-1657.t: Nearly always negative: 녹록지 않다 'it's no easy matter'. Pronounced [농노카다].

T6-1658.ex: 군복을 입은 아들의 모습이 정말 늠름했어요.
T6-1658.x: My son looked truly dignified in his military uniform.
T6-1658.e: A doubled syllable for emphasis — 'imposing, imposing'.
T6-1658.t: Pronounced [늠늠하다] — ㄹ becomes ㄴ after ㅁ; often used for boys, men or soldiers.

T6-1659.m: considerable, quite a lot (esp. of likelihood)
T6-1659.x: There's a good chance that plan will fail.
T6-1659.t: Typically 가능성이 다분하다 or 소지가 다분하다 — 'there's a good chance of (something bad)'.

T6-1660.x: She turned her head away with a haughty look.
T6-1660.e: Homonym warning: another 도도하다 means 'surging, sweeping' (of rivers or historical trends).
T6-1660.t: Can be half-complimentary for a chic, aloof woman, closer to 'aloof' than plainly 'rude'.

T6-1661.m: close, strong, deep (of friendship or ties)
T6-1661.ex: 두 나라는 오랫동안 돈독한 관계를 유지해 왔습니다.
T6-1661.x: The two countries have maintained close ties for a long time.
T6-1661.t: Used for bonds, not people: 우정이 돈독하다, 돈독한 관계. Pronounced [돈도카다].

T6-1662.ex: 그 팀은 올해 막강한 전력을 갖추었어요.
T6-1662.x: That team has assembled a formidable lineup this year.

T6-1663.x: His explanation was short but clear.
T6-1663.t: Pronounced [명뇨하다] — ㄹ becomes ㄴ after ㅇ.

T6-1664.ex: 그는 명철한 판단으로 회사를 위기에서 구했어요.
T6-1664.x: He saved the company from crisis with his wise judgment.

T6-1665.ex: 아이들의 무구한 눈빛을 보면 마음이 맑아져요.
T6-1665.x: Seeing the innocent eyes of children makes my heart feel clear.

T6-1666.x: This technology has endless potential for development.
T6-1666.e: Literally 'without end'; the national flower 무궁화 is the 'endless flower'.
T6-1666.t: Common in the four-syllable phrase 무궁무진하다 'inexhaustible, limitless'.

T6-1667.x: The people were outraged by the king's wicked conduct.
T6-1667.e: Literally 'without the Way' — lacking all morality.

T6-1668.ex: 준비 없이 겨울 산에 오르는 것은 무모해요.
T6-1668.x: Climbing a mountain in winter without preparation is reckless.

T6-1669.ex: 그의 실력은 프로 선수가 무색할 정도예요.
T6-1669.x: His skills would put a pro athlete to shame.
T6-1669.e: Literally 'colorless' — something looks pale beside something better.
T6-1669.t: Often in ~이/가 무색할 정도로 'so much that it puts ~ to shame'. Pronounced [무새카다].

T6-1670.x: Countless stars are shining in the night sky.

T6-1671.x: The preparation was still lacking, so we postponed the presentation.
T6-1671.t: A humble set phrase: 미흡하지만 최선을 다했습니다 'It's not perfect, but I did my best'.

T6-1672.ex: 그 교수님은 역사에 대해 정말 박식하세요.
T6-1672.x: That professor is truly knowledgeable about history.

T6-1673.ex: 그 아이는 어릴 때부터 재능이 범상치 않았어요.
T6-1673.x: That child's talent was out of the ordinary from an early age.
T6-1673.t: Mostly negated: 범상치 않다 means 'remarkable, out of the ordinary'.

T6-1674.ex: 이해를 돕기 위해 비근한 예를 하나 들어 보겠습니다.
T6-1674.x: To help you understand, let me give a familiar example.
T6-1674.e: Literally 'low and near' — everyday, close to home.
T6-1674.t: Almost always in 비근한 예 'a familiar, everyday example'.

T6-1675.ex: 그는 돈 때문에 비루한 행동을 서슴지 않았어요.
T6-1675.x: He didn't hesitate to act basely for money.

T6-1676.x: This paper's evidence is far too thin.
T6-1676.t: Common with 근거, 내용, 체격: 근거가 빈약하다 'the evidence is thin'.

T6-1677.x: The results of the two studies differ from each other.
T6-1677.t: A formal, written synonym of 다르다, common in reports and academic writing.

T6-1678.ex: 오랜만에 돌아온 고향 풍경이 생경하게 느껴졌어요.
T6-1678.x: Back after so long, my hometown scenery felt strangely unfamiliar.
T6-1678.e: Literally 'raw and hard' — not yet softened by familiarity.

T6-1679.x: After I moved, my friend and I gradually drifted apart.
T6-1679.t: Usually 소원해지다 or 관계가 소원하다; don't confuse it with the noun 소원 'a wish'.

T6-1680.ex: 속된 말로 하면 그 사람은 금수저예요.
T6-1680.x: To put it in slang, he was born with a silver spoon.
T6-1680.t: 속된 말로 'to put it crudely' is a common way to introduce slang. Pronounced [속뙤다].

T6-1681.m: beautiful, handsome, fine (of scenery or looks)
T6-1681.ex: 이 지역은 산과 물이 수려하기로 유명해요.
T6-1681.x: This area is famous for its beautiful mountains and rivers.

T6-1682.x: Being sick for a long time has made his face very gaunt.

T6-1683.ex: 그는 나라를 위해 숭고한 희생을 했어요.
T6-1683.x: He made a noble sacrifice for his country.

T6-1684.ex: 그 영화는 평론가들에게 신랄한 비판을 받았어요.
T6-1684.x: The film received scathing criticism from critics.
T6-1684.e: Literally 'spicy and pungent' — criticism that stings.
T6-1684.t: Pronounced [실랄하다] — ㄴ becomes ㄹ before ㄹ.

T6-1685.ex: 그 의사는 신묘한 의술로 이름이 났어요.
T6-1685.x: That doctor became famous for his marvelous healing skills.

T6-1686.ex: 이 시에는 삶에 대한 심오한 의미가 담겨 있어요.
T6-1686.x: This poem contains a profound meaning about life.

T6-1687.m: far off, distant, faint; at a loss
T6-1687.x: The summit still looked far, far away.
T6-1687.e: Also 눈앞이 아득하다 'to feel faint, at a loss' — distance turned into a feeling.
T6-1687.t: Also for time and memory: 아득한 옛날 'long, long ago'. Pronounced [아드카다].

T6-1688.ex: 문제를 너무 안이하게 생각하면 안 돼요.
T6-1688.x: You shouldn't think about the problem so complacently.
T6-1688.e: Literally 'comfortable and easy' — too relaxed about something serious.
T6-1688.t: Critical in tone: 안이한 대처 'a complacent response'; don't confuse with 용이하다 'easy to do'.

T6-1689.x: After my business failed, the future looked bleak.

T6-1690.ex: 법원은 이번 사건을 엄정하게 처리해야 합니다.
T6-1690.x: The court must handle this case strictly and fairly.
T6-1690.t: Common in official statements: 엄정하게 대처하겠습니다 'we will deal with it firmly'.

T6-1691.ex: 그 소설에는 전쟁의 참상이 여실하게 그려져 있어요.
T6-1691.x: That novel depicts the horrors of war true to life.
T6-1691.t: Mostly as the adverb 여실히 with 드러나다 or 보여 주다 'to show plainly'.

T6-1692.x: The workings of nature are truly profound and mysterious.

T6-1693.t: Usually with refusal or denial: 완강히 거부하다, 완강히 부인하다.

T6-1694.m: distant, far off, remote (of a goal)
T6-1694.x: Complete peace still seems far off.
T6-1694.t: Used for goals rather than places: 해결은 아직 요원하다 'a solution is still a long way off'.

T6-1695.x: He meticulously prepared for every situation.
T6-1695.e: Literally 'attention used, reaching all around' — nothing overlooked.
T6-1695.t: Can sound sinister: 용의주도한 범인 'a meticulous criminal'.

T6-1696.m: simple and honest, honest to a fault
T6-1696.x: He has steadfastly walked a single path.
T6-1696.e: Literally 'foolishly straight' — honest to a fault.

T6-1697.ex: 그는 세계적인 기업을 만들겠다는 원대한 꿈을 품었어요.
T6-1697.x: He cherished the grand dream of building a world-class company.

T6-1698.x: Korea is a country with a long history.

T6-1699.m: flowing, fluent, graceful (of writing or style)
T6-1699.x: His sentences are flowing and beautiful.

T6-1700.ex: 그는 성격이 너무 유약해서 결정을 잘 못 내려요.
T6-1700.x: He's so soft-natured that he struggles to make decisions.

T6-1701.x: He smiled on the outside, but inside he was sinister.

T6-1702.ex: 노력 없이 성공할 수 없다는 것은 자명한 사실이에요.
T6-1702.x: It's a self-evident fact that you can't succeed without effort.
T6-1702.t: Typically 자명한 사실 or 자명한 이치 'a self-evident truth'.

T6-1703.ex: 산 위에서 본 일출은 정말 장엄했어요.
T6-1703.x: The sunrise we saw from the mountaintop was truly majestic.
T6-1703.e: Literally 'solemn and stern' — grandeur that commands awe.

T6-1704.ex: 그 선수는 절묘한 타이밍에 골을 넣었어요.
T6-1704.x: That player scored a goal with perfect timing.
T6-1704.t: Great for timing and balance: 절묘한 타이밍, 절묘한 조화.

T6-1705.x: Grandma laid out a neat, carefully prepared meal for us.
T6-1705.e: A native Korean word, not built from hanja; a classic word for neat, lovingly prepared food.
T6-1705.t: Very common in food reviews: 정갈한 한정식 'a neat, carefully presented Korean set meal'.

T6-1706.x: You must stay quiet inside the exam hall.
T6-1706.e: Literally 'quiet and solemn'. A homonym means 'chaste, virtuous'.
T6-1706.t: Signs reading 정숙 mean 'Quiet, please' in libraries, hospitals and exam halls. Pronounced [정수카다].

T6-1707.ex: 그의 주장은 논리가 정연해서 설득력이 있어요.
T6-1707.x: His argument is logically well-organized, so it's persuasive.
T6-1707.t: Common as 논리 정연하다 'logically coherent' and 질서 정연하다 'in perfect order'.

T6-1708.x: The product was as shoddy as it was cheap.

T6-1709.m: coarse, crude, unrefined (of manners or style)
T6-1709.x: His way of speaking was coarse, but his heart was warm.
T6-1709.t: 조악하다 describes poor-quality goods; 조야하다 describes unrefined manners or style.

T6-1710.ex: 상대의 약점을 이용하는 것은 졸렬한 방법이에요.
T6-1710.x: Exploiting your opponent's weakness is a petty tactic.

T6-1711.ex: 국민들은 선거를 통해 준엄한 심판을 내렸습니다.
T6-1711.x: Through the election, the people delivered a stern verdict.
T6-1711.t: News collocations: 준엄한 심판, 준엄한 경고 'a stern verdict/warning'.

T6-1712.ex: 어머니의 지순한 사랑은 무엇과도 바꿀 수 없어요.
T6-1712.x: A mother's utterly pure love can't be traded for anything.

T6-1713.ex: 이 도자기는 질박한 아름다움을 지니고 있어요.
T6-1713.x: This pottery has a plain, unadorned beauty.
T6-1713.e: Literally 'all substance, plainly made' — beauty without decoration.

T6-1714.x: That civil servant was famous for being incorruptible.
T6-1714.e: Literally 'clear and honest' — taking no bribes.
T6-1714.t: Pronounced [청념하다]; typically describes officials and public servants.

T6-1715.m: clear and elegant (of a voice or sound)
T6-1715.x: That singer's voice is clear and elegant.

T6-1716.ex: 그는 세상의 평가에 초연한 태도를 보였어요.
T6-1716.x: He showed an attitude of detachment toward the world's opinion.
T6-1716.t: Often ~에 초연하다 'to be above ~': 결과에 초연하다 'to be unbothered by the outcome'.

T6-1717.m: rough, crude, coarse; blunt, unpolished (speech or manner)
T6-1717.ex: 할아버지는 말투가 투박하지만 정이 정말 많으세요.
T6-1717.x: My grandfather talks bluntly, but he's really warm-hearted.
T6-1717.e: Used for objects and manners that look clumsy but are often sturdy and honest.

T6-1718.ex: 두 형제는 얼굴은 닮았지만 성격은 판이하게 달라요.
T6-1718.x: The two brothers look alike, but their personalities are completely different.
T6-1718.t: Very common in the pattern 판이하게 다르다 'utterly different', even though it sounds redundant.

T6-1719.ex: 그런 편협한 생각은 버리는 게 좋겠어요.
T6-1719.x: You'd better get rid of such narrow-minded thinking.
T6-1719.t: Common collocations: 편협한 시각 (narrow perspective), 편협한 사고방식 (narrow-minded way of thinking).

T6-1720.ex: 이번 시험 문제는 작년보다 평이하게 출제됐어요.
T6-1720.x: This year's exam questions were easier than last year's.
T6-1720.e: Literally 'flat and easy': nothing steep to climb.

T6-1721.ex: 동화 속 포악한 거인이 마을 사람들을 괴롭혔어요.
T6-1721.x: In the fairy tale, a brutal giant tormented the villagers.
T6-1721.t: The first syllable is read 포 here, but the same character is read 폭 in 폭력 (violence).

T6-1722.ex: 피상적인 이해만으로는 이 문제를 해결할 수 없어요.
T6-1722.x: You can't solve this problem with only a superficial understanding.
T6-1722.e: Literally 'skin-appearance': looking only at the surface.

T6-1723.x: He traveled a rough road before he succeeded.

T6-1724.ex: 무대 위의 현란한 조명 때문에 눈이 부셨어요.
T6-1724.x: The dazzling lights on the stage nearly blinded me.
T6-1724.t: Pronounced [혈란하다]: ㄴ becomes ㄹ next to ㄹ.

T6-1725.ex: 주차 공간이 협소해서 차를 세우기가 힘들어요.
T6-1725.x: The parking area is cramped, so it's hard to park.

T6-1726.ex: 그는 성격이 호방해서 주변에 친구가 많아요.
T6-1726.x: He's bold and big-hearted, so he has lots of friends around him.

T6-1727.ex: 우리는 호젓한 산길을 따라 천천히 걸었어요.
T6-1727.x: We walked slowly along a quiet, secluded mountain path.
T6-1727.e: Describes a peaceful, out-of-the-way spot, or being pleasantly alone there.
T6-1727.t: Pronounced [호저타다]: the ㅅ batchim sounds like ㄷ and merges with ㅎ into ㅌ.

T6-1728.m: flustered, in a frantic hurry; sudden and shocking (news of a death)
T6-1728.ex: 친구 아버님의 황망한 부고를 듣고 말을 잃었어요.
T6-1728.x: I was speechless when I heard the sudden news of my friend's father's passing.
T6-1728.e: Literally 'hurried and busy': so rushed you lose your composure.
T6-1728.t: Common in condolences: 황망한 소식, 황망한 마음 for a sudden, shocking loss.
rel: to have no time to think

T6-1729.x: My grandmother has a kind, generous face and is always smiling.

T6-1730.m: restless and uneasy, ominous (public mood); turbulent
T6-1730.ex: 그 사건 이후 마을 분위기가 흉흉해졌어요.
T6-1730.x: After that incident, the mood in the village became tense and uneasy.
T6-1730.e: Originally waves surging noisily; now a restless, fearful public mood.
T6-1730.t: Typical subjects: 민심 (public sentiment), 분위기 (mood), 소문 (rumors).

T6-1731.x: At the mountaintop the air is thin, so it's hard to breathe.
T6-1731.t: Classic collocation: 가능성이 희박하다 'the chances are slim'.

T6-1732.x: I had a really weird dream last night.
T6-1732.e: Literally 'rare, rare': something you almost never see.
T6-1732.t: Common spelling mistake: 희안하다 is wrong; the correct form is 희한하다.

T6-1733.m: absurd, preposterous, out of the question
T6-1733.ex: 그런 가당찮은 요구는 들어줄 수 없어요.
T6-1733.x: I can't accept such an absurd demand.
T6-1733.e: Contraction of 가당하지 않다, 'not proper or reasonable'.
T6-1733.t: Pronounced [가당찬타]: the ㅎ in ㄶ makes the next ㄷ aspirated.

T6-1734.ex: 하루 종일 일했더니 몸이 너무 고단해요.
T6-1734.x: I worked all day, so I'm completely worn out.
T6-1734.e: Covers both a tired body and a hard life: 고단한 삶 'a hard life'.

T6-1735.ex: 오래된 쓰레기통에서 정말 고약한 냄새가 나요.
T6-1735.x: A really foul smell is coming from the old trash can.
T6-1735.e: Unrelated to the noun 고약, a traditional herbal ointment.
T6-1735.t: Works for smells, tempers and weather: 고약한 냄새, 성미가 고약하다, 날씨가 고약하다.

T6-1736.ex: 이제 와서 그런 변명을 하는 건 너무 구차해요.
T6-1736.x: Making that kind of excuse now is just too undignified.
T6-1736.e: Literally 'makeshift, just for now': lacking dignity.
T6-1736.t: Common pattern: 구차한 변명 'a lame excuse'.

T6-1737.ex: 그는 질문을 받고 궁색한 변명만 늘어놓았어요.
T6-1737.x: When questioned, he just rattled off feeble excuses.
T6-1737.e: Literally 'destitute and blocked': no way out, in money or in words.
T6-1737.t: Two uses: 살림이 궁색하다 'to be hard up' and 궁색한 변명 'a lame excuse'.

T6-1738.ex: 그 집에서 손님들을 정말 극진하게 대접했어요.
T6-1738.x: That family treated their guests with the utmost hospitality.
T6-1738.e: Literally 'going to the extreme, using everything up': giving all you have.

T6-1739.m: sly, coy; acting innocent with a straight face
T6-1739.ex: 그는 아무것도 모르는 척 능청스럽게 웃었어요.
T6-1739.x: He smiled slyly, pretending he didn't know anything.
T6-1739.t: Not always negative: a 능청스러운 actor plays a role smoothly and naturally.

T6-1740.m: easygoing, good-natured, tolerant; fairly good, decent
T6-1740.ex: 그 친구는 성격이 무던해서 누구하고나 잘 지내요.
T6-1740.x: That friend is so easygoing that he gets along with anyone.
T6-1740.e: Adverb 무던히 shifts meaning to 'quite a lot': 무던히 애쓰다 'to try really hard'.

T6-1741.ex: 형은 대학을 졸업하고 버젓한 회사에 들어갔어요.
T6-1741.x: My brother graduated from college and got a job at a respectable company.
T6-1741.e: Close in sound and meaning to 번듯하다 'decent, presentable'.
T6-1741.t: The adverb 버젓이 is usually negative: 버젓이 거짓말하다 'to lie brazenly'.

T6-1742.ex: 요즘 너무 바빠서 변변한 식사도 못 했어요.
T6-1742.x: I've been so busy lately that I haven't had a proper meal.
T6-1742.e: Mostly used with negatives: 변변한 ~이 없다, 변변치 않다.
T6-1742.t: Humble phrase when serving food: 변변치 않지만 많이 드세요 'It's nothing special, but please eat up'.

T6-1743.ex: 이미 지난 일을 후회해 봐야 부질없어요.
T6-1743.x: It's pointless to regret what's already past.
T6-1743.e: Often used about regrets and wishes: 부질없는 욕심, 부질없는 생각.
T6-1743.t: Pronounced [부지럽따]: the ㄹ links to the next syllable.

T6-1744.ex: 어머니는 적은 월급으로 살림을 살뜰하게 꾸려 가셨어요.
T6-1744.x: My mother managed the household thriftily on a small salary.
T6-1744.e: Two kinds of care: careful with money, and attentive to people (살뜰히 챙기다).

T6-1745.x: That employee answered the customer coldly.
T6-1745.e: From 쌀쌀하다 'chilly' + -맞다 'having that quality': chilly in attitude.

T6-1746.ex: 그 사람 말이 사실인지 아직도 아리송해요.
T6-1746.x: I'm still not sure whether what he said is true.
T6-1746.e: Related to the livelier form 알쏭달쏭하다, which also means 'puzzling, hard to pin down'.

T6-1747.ex: 화가 난다고 애꿎은 동생한테 소리 지르지 마세요.
T6-1747.x: Don't yell at your innocent little brother just because you're angry.
T6-1747.e: Almost always 애꿎은 + noun: the innocent bystander who takes the hit.

T6-1748.x: He speaks haltingly, but you can feel his sincerity.
T6-1748.t: Also used for a learner's Korean: 어눌한 한국어 'halting Korean'.

T6-1749.ex: 그는 어수룩해 보여도 사실 아주 똑똑해요.
T6-1749.x: He may look naive, but he's actually very smart.
T6-1749.t: 어리숙하다 is an accepted standard variant with the same meaning.

T6-1750.ex: 얄궂은 운명 때문에 두 사람은 헤어져야 했어요.
T6-1750.x: Because of a cruel twist of fate, the two had to part.
T6-1750.e: Signature collocation: 얄궂은 운명 'a cruel twist of fate'.

T6-1751.ex: 그런 작은 일로 화를 내다니 너무 옹졸해요.
T6-1751.x: Getting angry over such a small thing is really petty.
T6-1751.e: Literally 'blocked and clumsy': a cramped, petty heart.

T6-1752.ex: 그는 모르는 척하지만 사실 꽤 의뭉스러운 사람이에요.
T6-1752.x: He pretends not to know, but he's actually quite a sly person.
T6-1752.e: From 의뭉 'simple outside, scheming inside' + -스럽다 'having that quality'.

T6-1753.ex: 그 아이는 어른들 앞에서 늘 조신하게 행동해요.
T6-1753.x: That child always behaves politely in front of adults.
T6-1753.e: Literally 'controlling one's body': careful in conduct and manners.

T6-1754.m: advanced in years, mature; patient, steady
T6-1754.x: An elderly gentleman asked me for directions.
T6-1754.e: Mainly in 나이가 지긋하다 'of mature age'; the adverb 지긋이 means 'patiently'.
T6-1754.t: A respectful way to say 'old': 연세가 지긋하신 분 'an elderly person'.

T6-1755.m: nonchalant, poker-faced, acting perfectly natural (as if nothing happened)
T6-1755.x: Even after lying, he smiled as if nothing had happened.
T6-1755.e: Built on 천연 'natural': acting as natural as can be.
T6-1755.t: Usually after a lie or mischief: 천연덕스럽게 시치미를 떼다 'to play innocent with a straight face'.

T6-1756.ex: 할머니 집에 가면 언제나 마음이 푸근해져요.
T6-1756.x: Whenever I go to my grandma's house, I feel warm and at ease.
T6-1756.e: Works for weather, blankets and people: soft, mild and comforting.

T6-1757.ex: 친구들이 다 떠나고 나니 마음이 헛헛해요.
T6-1757.x: Now that all my friends have left, I feel empty inside.
T6-1757.e: Probably related to 헛- 'empty, in vain', as in 헛수고 'wasted effort'.
T6-1757.t: Also means slightly hungry: 배가 헛헛하다, close to 출출하다.

T6-1758.ex: 같은 영화를 봐도 사람마다 느낌이 각기 달라요.
T6-1758.x: Even watching the same movie, each person feels differently.

T6-1759.m: absolutely, by no means, never (with negatives)
T6-1759.e: From 결단 'firm decision' + intensifying -코: as if decided once and for all.
T6-1759.t: Like 결코, it's mostly used with negatives, but sounds even stronger and more dramatic.

T6-1760.m: in a rush, frantically, with no time to think
T6-1760.ex: 이사 준비로 한 주를 경황없이 보냈어요.
T6-1760.x: I spent the week in a frantic rush getting ready to move.
T6-1760.e: 경황 'leeway, presence of mind' + 없이: with no room to think.
T6-1760.t: Common apology: 경황이 없어서 연락을 못 드렸어요 'I was so swamped I couldn't get in touch'.

T6-1761.ex: 모든 사람은 죽습니다. 고로 소크라테스도 죽습니다.
T6-1761.x: All men are mortal. Therefore, Socrates is mortal too.
T6-1761.t: Famous line: 나는 생각한다, 고로 존재한다 'I think, therefore I am'.

T6-1762.ex: 그 회사의 문제는 업계에서 공공연히 알려져 있어요.
T6-1762.x: That company's problems are openly known in the industry.
T6-1762.e: Literally 'public, public-ly': done right out in the open.

T6-1763.ex: 그는 강해 보이지만 기실 마음이 여린 사람이에요.
T6-1763.x: He looks tough, but in fact he's a soft-hearted person.
T6-1763.e: Literally 'its truth': the real fact behind appearances.
T6-1763.t: Very literary; in speech, say 사실은 or 실은.

T6-1764.ex: 선생님은 안전 수칙을 지키라고 누차 강조하셨어요.
T6-1764.x: The teacher repeatedly stressed that we follow the safety rules.

T6-1765.m: in large numbers, en masse, on a large scale
T6-1765.ex: 이번 축제에 젊은 관객들이 대거 몰렸습니다.
T6-1765.x: Young audiences flocked to this festival in large numbers.
T6-1765.e: Literally 'a big move': moving all at once, in force.

T6-1766.ex: 세 사람이 낸 돈은 도합 십만 원이에요.
T6-1766.x: The money the three people chipped in comes to 100,000 won in total.

T6-1767.x: He thinks and acts carefully in everything.
T6-1767.t: Most often as 매사에: 매사에 긍정적이다 'positive about everything'.

T6-1768.ex: 이 전통은 수백 년 동안 면면히 이어져 왔습니다.
T6-1768.x: This tradition has continued unbroken for hundreds of years.
T6-1768.e: Literally 'like a thread, on and on': never breaking.
T6-1768.t: Don't confuse with the noun 면면 'faces, line-up': 참석자의 면면 'the line-up of attendees'.

T6-1769.m: generally, as a rule (opening a general truth)
T6-1769.x: As a rule, people should live honestly.
T6-1769.e: A literary opener for universal statements, like English 'As a rule' or 'In general'.

T6-1770.m: no less than, a whopping (before a surprising number)
T6-1770.ex: 그 그림은 경매에서 물경 백억 원에 팔렸습니다.
T6-1770.x: That painting sold at auction for a whopping ten billion won.
T6-1770.e: Literally 'don't be surprised': said right before a shocking figure.
T6-1770.t: Old-fashioned; modern Korean usually says 무려 instead.

T6-1771.m: now (at last), just now, at this very moment
T6-1771.x: The age of artificial intelligence has now truly arrived.
T6-1771.e: A grand, literary 'now' used to announce a new era or season.
T6-1771.t: Typical frame: 바야흐로 ~의 계절이다/시대다 'it is now the season/age of ~'.

T6-1772.x: Guests are arriving at the venue one after another.

T6-1773.ex: 그는 인터뷰 동안 시종 진지한 태도를 보였어요.
T6-1773.x: He kept a serious attitude from start to finish during the interview.

T6-1774.m: consistently, unwaveringly, all the way through
T6-1774.x: He consistently maintained his innocence throughout the trial.
T6-1774.e: Literally 'beginning and end pierced by one thread'.

T6-1775.m: before one knows it, already (time passing)
T6-1775.ex: 한국에 온 지 어언 십 년이 되었어요.
T6-1775.x: Before I knew it, it's been ten years since I came to Korea.
T6-1775.e: Built from two classical function syllables; used for time slipping by unnoticed.
T6-1775.t: Almost always with a span of time: 어언 30년 'a good thirty years already'.

T6-1776.ex: 주말에는 오롯이 저만을 위한 시간을 보내요.
T6-1776.x: On weekends, I spend time entirely for myself.
T6-1776.e: Adverb of 오롯하다 'whole, complete, with nothing missing'.
T6-1776.t: Pronounced [오로시]; popular in writing: 오롯이 집중하다 'to focus completely'.

T6-1777.m: naturally, rightly, as a matter of course
T6-1777.x: If you did something wrong, you naturally ought to apologize.

T6-1778.ex: 아이는 한참 울다가 이내 잠이 들었어요.
T6-1778.x: The child cried for a while and soon fell asleep.
T6-1778.e: Homonym warning: the noun 이내 means 'within' (일주일 이내 'within a week').

T6-1779.m: at one stroke, in one go, all at once
T6-1779.ex: 그 정책으로 여러 문제를 일거에 해결할 수 있습니다.
T6-1779.x: That policy can solve several problems at one stroke.
T6-1779.e: 일거 'one move' + 에: everything in a single stroke.

T6-1780.m: a trace, a touch, a shred (of)
T6-1780.x: I wish he had at least a shred of conscience.
T6-1780.e: Literally 'one brushstroke': just a faint trace.
T6-1780.t: Fixed pattern: 일말의 희망/양심/기대 'a shred of hope/conscience/expectation'.

T6-1781.m: not at all, never, absolutely not
T6-1781.ex: 이 건물 안에서는 흡연을 일절 금지합니다.
T6-1781.x: Smoking is strictly prohibited inside this building.
T6-1781.e: Literally 'one cut': cutting something off completely.
T6-1781.t: Same characters as 일체 'all'; use 일절 with negatives or bans, 일체 for 'everything'.

T6-1782.x: The company covers all travel expenses.
T6-1782.t: 일체 = all (positive), 일절 = not at all (negative): 일체 무료 vs 일절 금지.

T6-1783.x: Is this truly our last chance?
T6-1783.e: Used in heartfelt questions and vows: 'is it really so?'
T6-1783.t: Dramatic and literary; common in historical dramas and song lyrics.

T6-1784.m: more than half, the greater part, most
T6-1784.x: More than half of the attendees opposed that opinion.
T6-1784.e: Literally 'a big half': most of it.
T6-1784.t: Homonym alert: 태반 also means 'placenta', a completely different word.

T6-1785.ex: 우리 학교를 통틀어 그가 키가 제일 커요.
T6-1785.x: He's the tallest in our whole school.

T6-1786.m: in the end, after all; surely
T6-1786.ex: 이렇게 서두르다가는 필경 실수하게 될 거예요.
T6-1786.x: If you rush like this, you'll surely end up making a mistake.
T6-1786.e: Literally 'finish-end': in the end, after all is said and done.

T6-1787.ex: 연락이 없는 걸 보니 필시 무슨 일이 생긴 거예요.
T6-1787.x: Since there's no word from him, something must have happened.
T6-1787.t: Signals a strong guess, usually with -ㄹ 것이다 or -ㄴ 게 틀림없다.

T6-1788.x: That rumor was nothing but a lie.
T6-1788.e: From 한 'one' + 낱 'single piece' (as in 낱개): just one single thing.
T6-1788.t: Typical frame: 한낱 ~에 불과하다/지나지 않다 'nothing but a mere ~'.

T6-1789.ex: 친구는 돈을 받지 않겠다고 한사코 거절했어요.
T6-1789.x: My friend stubbornly refused to take the money.
T6-1789.e: Literally 'to the limit of death': resisting with all one's might.

T6-1790.ex: 혹자는 그 계획이 실패할 거라고 말합니다.
T6-1790.x: Some say that plan will fail.
T6-1790.e: Literally 'some person'; -자 = person, as in 과학자, 운전자.
T6-1790.t: Formal, mostly in writing as 혹자는 ~라고 한다 'some say …'.

T6-1791.ex: 그는 어느 날 홀연히 마을을 떠났어요.
T6-1791.x: One day, he suddenly left the village.
T6-1791.e: Literally 'suddenly so': appearing or vanishing without warning.

T6-1792.m: just like, exactly as if, closely resembling
T6-1792.ex: 그 바위는 흡사 사람 얼굴처럼 생겼어요.
T6-1792.x: That rock looks just like a human face.

T6-1793.ex: 그는 상을 받는 것을 극구 사양했어요.
T6-1793.x: He firmly declined to accept the award.
T6-1793.e: Literally 'with all one's mouth': using every word to insist.

T6-1794.ex: 그의 발언에는 다분히 정치적인 의도가 있어 보여요.
T6-1794.x: His remarks seem to have a largely political motive.

T6-1795.x: He has lived thinking solely of his family.
T6-1795.e: An old native adverb that survives mostly in literature and formal writing.
T6-1795.t: Very literary; in conversation use 오로지 or 오직 instead.

T6-1796.forms: 연거푸 + verb: 연거푸 마시다, 연거푸 실패하다
T6-1796.m: repeatedly, in a row, again and again
T6-1796.ex: 그는 물을 연거푸 세 잔이나 마셨어요.
T6-1796.x: He drank three glasses of water in a row.
T6-1796.e: Built from 연 'in a row' + native 거푸 'again'; 거푸 alone means the same.

T6-1797.x: He revealed his true feelings without realizing it.
T6-1797.e: Literally 'in the midst of hiddenness': something that shows without anyone noticing.
T6-1797.t: Usually followed by 에: 은연중에 드러나다 means 'to show through unintentionally'.

T6-1798.m: deliberately, on purpose (putting on an act)
T6-1798.x: She smiled, deliberately pretending not to know.
T6-1798.e: Native adverb that almost always pairs with 척하다 or 체하다 'to pretend'.
T6-1798.t: Unlike plain 일부러, 짐짓 implies putting on a show or feigning an attitude.

T6-1799.m: helplessly, with no other choice; unmistakably
T6-1799.ex: 버스를 놓친 우리는 하릴없이 걸어서 집에 갔어요.
T6-1799.x: Having missed the bus, we had no choice but to walk home.
T6-1799.e: From 하릴없다 'to have no way out'; not the same as 할 일 없이 'with nothing to do'.
T6-1799.t: Pronounced [하리럽씨]; many people misuse it as 'idly', but the dictionary sense is 'helplessly'.

T6-1800.forms: 허투루 + 쓰다/듣다/보다, usually with 않다 or 말다: 허투루 듣지 마세요
T6-1800.ex: 할머니는 돈을 한 푼도 허투루 쓰지 않으세요.
T6-1800.x: My grandmother never wastes even a single penny.
T6-1800.e: Mostly appears in negative warnings, like 허투루 듣지 마 'don't take it lightly'.

T6-1801.forms: 호젓이 + verb; adjective 호젓하다 → 호젓한 길
T6-1801.m: quietly and alone, in peaceful solitude
T6-1801.x: On the weekend I walked a mountain path in peaceful solitude.
T6-1801.e: Adverb of 호젓하다 'secluded and quiet'; a lonely but peaceful feeling.

T6-1802.m: super-aged society (20% or more of people aged 65+)
T6-1802.x: Korea became a super-aged society at the end of 2024.
T6-1802.e: Literally 'beyond-high-age society': over a fifth of people are 65 or older.
T6-1802.t: Official tiers: 고령화사회 at 7%, 고령사회 at 14%, 초고령사회 at 20% aged 65+.

T6-1803.ex: 저출생 문제를 해결하기 위해 정부가 새 대책을 발표했습니다.
T6-1803.x: The government announced new measures to solve the low birth rate problem.
T6-1803.t: Same meaning as 저출산; 저출생 is newer and seen as more neutral, since it doesn't focus on mothers.

T6-1804.ex: 인구절벽으로 문을 닫는 학교가 늘고 있습니다.
T6-1804.x: More and more schools are closing because of the population cliff.
T6-1804.e: Literally 'population sheer cliff': numbers drop as if falling off a cliff.

T6-1805.ex: 인구구조의 변화는 경제에 큰 영향을 미칩니다.
T6-1805.x: Changes in population structure have a big impact on the economy.
T6-1805.e: Literally 'population construction': the age and gender makeup of a society.

T6-1806.ex: 요즘 일인가구를 위한 소포장 식품이 인기예요.
T6-1806.x: These days, small-package foods for single-person households are popular.
T6-1806.e: Literally 'one-person household'; 가구 is the unit for counting households.
T6-1806.t: Usually written 1인 가구; pronounced [이린가구] with the ㄹ linking over.

T6-1807.ex: 이 지역에는 다양한 나라에서 온 이주민이 살고 있어요.
T6-1807.x: Migrants from many different countries live in this area.

T6-1808.x: Protecting the human rights of migrant workers is an important task.
T6-1808.e: -자 = person who does it: 노동자, 소비자, 운전자.
T6-1808.t: Media increasingly prefer 이주노동자 to 외국인 노동자 as a more neutral term.

T6-1809.ex: 온라인 혐오표현을 규제해야 한다는 목소리가 높습니다.
T6-1809.x: There are growing calls to regulate online hate speech.
T6-1809.e: Literally 'hatred expression'; the 오 here is the 'hate' reading of the character for 악 'evil'.

T6-1810.ex: 성소수자에 대한 차별을 금지하는 법이 논의되고 있습니다.
T6-1810.x: A law banning discrimination against sexual minorities is being discussed.
T6-1810.e: Literally 'sexual-minority person'; 소수 means 'small number, minority'.

T6-1811.ex: 정부는 사회적 약자를 위한 지원을 늘렸습니다.
T6-1811.x: The government increased support for the socially disadvantaged.

T6-1812.ex: 폭염 때는 취약계층을 위한 무더위 쉼터가 운영됩니다.
T6-1812.x: During heat waves, cooling shelters are run for vulnerable people.

T6-1813.ex: 이 단체는 소외계층 아이들에게 무료 교육을 제공합니다.
T6-1813.x: This organization provides free education to underprivileged children.
T6-1813.e: Literally 'kept-outside stratum': people left out of society's benefits.

T6-1814.x: Mostly upper-class people live in that neighborhood.
T6-1814.t: Pronounced [상뉴층]: ㄹ becomes ㄴ after ㅇ.

T6-1815.x: Education is called the ladder of social mobility.
T6-1815.t: Common phrase: 계층이동 사다리가 끊어졌다, 'the ladder of social mobility is broken'.

T6-1816.m: rise in social status, climbing the social ladder
T6-1816.ex: 드라마에서는 결혼을 통한 신분상승 이야기가 자주 나와요.
T6-1816.x: Stories of climbing the social ladder through marriage often appear in dramas.
T6-1816.e: Literally 'status ascent'; 신분 is one's place in society.

T6-1817.m: hereditary succession, passing down (wealth, power, status)
T6-1817.ex: 부의 세습이 사회 불평등을 키운다는 지적이 많습니다.
T6-1817.x: Many point out that inherited wealth deepens social inequality.
T6-1817.t: Used for power, wealth or poverty passed down; 상속 is the legal word for inheriting property.

T6-1818.ex: 특권층만 누리는 혜택에 대한 비판이 커졌어요.
T6-1818.x: Criticism grew over benefits that only the privileged enjoy.

T6-1819.ex: 그 정치인은 엘리트주의적인 태도로 비판을 받았습니다.
T6-1819.x: The politician was criticized for his elitist attitude.
T6-1819.e: From English 'elite' + -주의 '-ism', a highly productive suffix: 개인주의, 민주주의.
T6-1819.t: Pronounced [엘리트주이]; add -적 for the adjective: 엘리트주의적인 태도.

T6-1820.m: academic elitism, judging people by their school background
T6-1820.ex: 한국 사회의 학벌주의는 입시 경쟁을 더 심하게 만들어요.
T6-1820.x: Korean society's obsession with school pedigree makes entrance exam competition even fiercer.
T6-1820.e: 학벌 is one's school pedigree, i.e. which university one graduated from.

T6-1821.m: favoritism based on personal ties, cronyism
T6-1821.ex: 인사에서 연고주의를 없애야 한다는 목소리가 높습니다.
T6-1821.x: Many say favoritism based on personal ties must be removed from hiring.
T6-1821.e: 연고 means old ties of region, school or family: 지연, 학연, 혈연.

T6-1822.m: regional ties, bonds from a shared hometown
T6-1822.ex: 선거 때마다 지연에 따라 표가 갈리는 경향이 있습니다.
T6-1822.x: In every election, votes tend to split along regional ties.
T6-1822.e: Literally 'land tie': bonds between people from the same hometown.
T6-1822.t: Don't confuse it with its homonym 지연 'delay', as in 열차 지연 'train delay'.

T6-1823.x: Debates about feminism are heated online.

T6-1824.ex: 가부장제의 영향은 아직도 명절 문화에 남아 있어요.
T6-1824.x: The influence of patriarchy still remains in holiday customs.

T6-1825.m: the idea that men are superior to women
T6-1825.ex: 남존여비 사상은 이제 시대에 맞지 않습니다.
T6-1825.x: The idea that men are superior to women no longer fits the times.
T6-1825.e: Literally 'men honored, women lowly', an old Confucian-era social idea.
T6-1825.t: Pronounced [남존녀비]: an ㄴ sound is added before 여.

T6-1826.ex: 그녀는 유리천장을 깨고 회사의 첫 여성 사장이 되었어요.
T6-1826.x: She broke the glass ceiling and became the company's first female president.
T6-1826.e: A word-for-word translation of English 'glass ceiling': an invisible barrier to promotion.
T6-1826.t: Usually paired with 깨다: 유리천장을 깨다 'to break the glass ceiling'.

T6-1827.m: career break, career interruption (esp. women leaving work for childcare)
T6-1827.ex: 출산 후 경력단절을 겪는 여성이 많습니다.
T6-1827.x: Many women experience a career break after giving birth.
T6-1827.t: Pronounced [경녁딴절]; the slang 경단녀 is short for 경력단절여성.

T6-1828.forms: 일과 삶의 균형을 맞추다 / 찾다 / 지키다; casual: 워라밸
T6-1828.ex: 요즘 직장인들은 연봉보다 일과 삶의 균형을 더 중요하게 생각해요.
T6-1828.x: These days, office workers value work-life balance more than salary.
T6-1828.t: In speech, 워라밸 is far more common; the full phrase sounds formal or official.

T6-1829.ex: 택배 기사의 과로사가 사회 문제가 되었습니다.
T6-1829.x: Delivery drivers dying from overwork has become a social issue.

T6-1830.ex: 한국의 자살률은 OECD 국가 중에서 높은 편입니다.
T6-1830.x: Korea's suicide rate is relatively high among OECD countries.
T6-1830.e: -률/-율 = rate, a very productive suffix: 출산율, 실업률, 합격률.
T6-1830.t: Write 률 after consonants but 율 after vowels or ㄴ, as in 비율 and 할인율.

T6-1831.ex: 청소년비행을 막기 위해 학교와 가정이 함께 노력해야 합니다.
T6-1831.x: Schools and families must work together to prevent juvenile delinquency.
T6-1831.e: 비행 here means 'wrongful conduct', literally 'not-proper deeds'.
T6-1831.t: Don't confuse this 비행 'misconduct' with 비행 'flight', as in 비행기.

T6-1832.x: Reports of elder abuse are increasing every year.

T6-1833.x: Systems that protect victims of sexual violence have been strengthened.
T6-1833.t: Pronounced [성퐁녁]: nasalization turns ㄱ into ㅇ and ㄹ into ㄴ.

T6-1834.ex: 악성 댓글 같은 사이버폭력은 심각한 범죄입니다.
T6-1834.x: Cyberbullying such as malicious comments is a serious crime.

T6-1835.m: doxxing, digging up and exposing someone's personal info
T6-1835.ex: 신상털기는 사생활 침해이며 처벌받을 수 있습니다.
T6-1835.x: Doxxing is an invasion of privacy and can be punished.
T6-1835.e: 신상 'personal details' + 털기 'shaking out', from 털다 'to shake out; to rob'.
T6-1835.t: The verb form is 신상을 털다; being doxxed is 신상이 털리다.

T6-1836.x: False information spread rapidly during the election period.

T6-1837.ex: 신문사는 잘못된 기사에 대해 정정보도를 냈습니다.
T6-1837.x: The newspaper published a correction for the inaccurate article.
T6-1837.t: Typical collocations: 정정보도를 내다 'to run a correction', 정정보도를 요청하다 'to request one'.

T6-1838.ex: 그 회사는 기사에 대한 반론보도를 요구했습니다.
T6-1838.x: The company demanded a right-of-reply report on the article.
T6-1838.e: Literally 'counter-argument report': the subject of a story gets to tell their side.
T6-1838.t: Pronounced [발론보도]: ㄴ becomes ㄹ next to ㄹ.

T6-1839.x: Freedom of the press is the foundation of democracy.
T6-1839.t: Pronounced [얼론자유]: ㄴ becomes ㄹ next to ㄹ.

T6-1840.x: In the 1980s, the government controlled the press with reporting directives.
T6-1840.e: Literally 'reporting compass needle'; recalls the secret press orders of the 1980s military regime.

T6-1841.ex: 기자들은 외부 압력 때문에 자기검열을 하게 되었습니다.
T6-1841.x: Under outside pressure, reporters ended up censoring themselves.

T6-1842.m: press arbitration, mediation of media disputes
T6-1842.ex: 보도로 피해를 입은 사람은 언론중재를 신청할 수 있습니다.
T6-1842.x: People harmed by news reports can apply for press arbitration.
T6-1842.e: 중재 is literally 'standing in the middle to judge'.
T6-1842.t: Korea has an official body for this, the 언론중재위원회 (Press Arbitration Commission).

T6-1843.ex: 아버지는 매일 아침 일간지 두 개를 읽으세요.
T6-1843.x: My father reads two daily newspapers every morning.
T6-1843.t: 일간지 uses the 지 for 'paper', while 주간지 and 월간지 use a different 지 meaning 'record'.

T6-1844.ex: 그 사건은 한 시사 주간지가 처음 보도했어요.
T6-1844.x: That incident was first reported by a weekly current-affairs magazine.

T6-1845.ex: 저는 여행 월간지를 정기 구독하고 있어요.
T6-1845.x: I have a subscription to a monthly travel magazine.

T6-1846.ex: 그 소식은 오늘 조간에 크게 실렸습니다.
T6-1846.x: That news ran prominently in this morning's papers.
T6-1846.e: Short for 조간신문 'morning newspaper'; the opposite is 석간 'evening paper'.

T6-1847.ex: 요즘은 석간을 발행하는 신문사가 많지 않아요.
T6-1847.x: These days, not many newspaper companies publish an evening paper.

T6-1849.x: Thanks to a whistleblower, the company's corruption came to light.
T6-1849.e: Literally 'inside-reporting person'; the official legal term is 공익신고자.

T6-1850.ex: 그 신문은 장관의 비리 의혹을 단독보도했습니다.
T6-1850.x: The newspaper ran an exclusive on the minister's alleged corruption.
T6-1850.e: Literally 'solo report': only one outlet has the story.
T6-1850.t: Headlines often just mark these stories with [단독].

T6-1851.ex: 회사는 신제품 출시에 맞춰 보도자료를 배포했습니다.
T6-1851.x: The company distributed a press release timed to the new product launch.
T6-1851.e: Literally 'reporting materials' handed out to journalists.
T6-1851.t: Usual verbs: 보도자료를 내다 or 배포하다 'to issue a press release'.

T6-1852.x: The crowd protested the referee's biased call.
T6-1852.t: Mostly used before a noun or with -적: 편파 판정, 편파 방송, 편파적이다 'to be biased'.

T6-1853.x: Viewers protested the broadcaster's biased reporting.

T6-1854.ex: 국민의 알권리를 위해 정보를 공개해야 합니다.
T6-1854.x: Information must be disclosed for the sake of the public's right to know.
T6-1854.e: 알 'to know' (modifier form of 알다) + 권리 'right'.
T6-1854.t: Pronounced [알꿜리]: tensing plus ㄴ becoming ㄹ after ㄹ.

T6-1855.ex: 연예인 집 앞에서 기다리는 것은 사생활침해입니다.
T6-1855.x: Waiting in front of a celebrity's home is an invasion of privacy.

T6-1856.x: The media play a big role in shaping public opinion.
T6-1856.e: 여론 is 'public opinion', literally 'the crowd's discussion'.

T6-1857.m: agenda-setting, putting an issue on the agenda
T6-1857.ex: 시민단체가 기후 문제를 의제화하는 데 성공했습니다.
T6-1857.x: Civic groups succeeded in putting climate issues on the agenda.
T6-1857.e: -화 = '-ization', a very productive suffix: 고령화, 세계화, 민주화.

T6-1858.ex: 젊은 세대는 주로 뉴미디어를 통해 뉴스를 접합니다.
T6-1858.x: Younger generations mostly get their news through new media.

T6-1859.x: Public broadcasters must protect their fairness and independence.
T6-1859.e: Literally 'publicly run broadcasting', funded mainly by license fees, like KBS.

T6-1860.x: Commercial broadcasters depend heavily on advertising revenue.
T6-1860.e: Literally 'privately run broadcasting', funded by ads, like SBS.

T6-1861.m: general programming cable channel (e.g. JTBC, MBN)
T6-1861.x: General programming channels first went on the air in 2011.
T6-1861.e: Literally 'comprehensive-programming channel'; 채널 is from English 'channel'.
T6-1861.t: Almost everyone says 종편; the four are JTBC, TV조선, 채널A and MBN.

T6-1862.ex: 추천 알고리즘은 필터버블을 만들 수 있습니다.
T6-1862.x: Recommendation algorithms can create filter bubbles.

T6-1863.ex: 사람들은 확증편향 때문에 믿고 싶은 정보만 찾습니다.
T6-1863.x: Because of confirmation bias, people look only for information they want to believe.

T6-1864.ex: 노인과 젊은 세대 사이의 정보격차가 커지고 있습니다.
T6-1864.x: The information gap between seniors and young people is growing.

T6-1865.x: As kiosks spread, the digital divide became a serious problem.
T6-1865.e: From English 'digital' + 격차 'gap'; a translation of 'digital divide'.

T6-1866.ex: 학교에서 미디어리터러시 교육이 점점 중요해지고 있어요.
T6-1866.x: Media literacy education is becoming more and more important in schools.
T6-1866.e: From English 'media literacy'; also called 미디어 문해력.

T6-1867.x: Hip-hop started as a subculture and became mainstream.

T6-1868.ex: 한때 비주류였던 웹툰이 이제는 주류문화가 되었습니다.
T6-1868.x: Webtoons, once on the fringe, have now become mainstream culture.
T6-1868.e: Literally 'main-stream culture', just like the English image.
T6-1868.t: Don't confuse 주류 'mainstream' with its homonym 주류 'alcoholic beverages'.

T6-1869.x: The hippie movement of the 1960s was a classic counterculture.

T6-1870.ex: 문화상대주의는 다른 문화를 그 사회의 맥락에서 이해하는 태도입니다.
T6-1870.x: Cultural relativism is the attitude of understanding other cultures in their own social context.
T6-1870.e: 상대 means 'relative': each culture is understood on its own terms.

T6-1871.ex: 자문화중심주의는 다른 문화를 낮게 보게 만듭니다.
T6-1871.x: Ethnocentrism makes people look down on other cultures.

T6-1872.m: cultural toadyism, blind worship of foreign culture
T6-1872.ex: 외국 것이라면 무조건 좋다고 보는 것은 문화사대주의입니다.
T6-1872.x: Seeing anything foreign as automatically better is cultural toadyism.
T6-1872.e: 사대 means 'serving the great', from Joseon's tributary relationship with China.
T6-1872.t: The mirror image of 자문화중심주의: one overvalues foreign culture, the other one's own.

T6-1873.ex: 기술 발전을 제도가 따라가지 못하면 문화지체가 생깁니다.
T6-1873.x: When institutions can't keep up with technological progress, cultural lag occurs.
T6-1873.e: Literally 'culture delayed': values and rules lag behind new technology.

T6-1874.ex: 이민자들은 새로운 사회에서 문화접변을 겪게 됩니다.
T6-1874.x: Immigrants go through acculturation in a new society.
T6-1874.e: Literally 'culture touches and changes': two cultures meet and both shift.
T6-1874.t: Pronounced [문화접뼌]: the ㅂ becomes tense (the ㅎ is kept in standard pronunciation).

T6-1875.ex: 소수 민족에게 동화를 강요해서는 안 됩니다.
T6-1875.x: Ethnic minorities should not be forced to assimilate.
T6-1875.t: Homonym warning: 동화 (童話) also means 'fairy tale'; context tells you which.

T6-1876.ex: 가치관 차이 때문에 세대갈등이 점점 심해지고 있어요.
T6-1876.x: Generational conflict is getting worse because of differing values.
T6-1876.e: Literally 'generations tangled like vines': 갈등 pictures twisted vines.
T6-1876.t: Pronounced [세대갈뜽]: ㄷ after ㄹ becomes tense in Sino words.

T6-1877.x: As the baby boomers retire, the workforce is shrinking.
T6-1877.e: From English 'baby boom' plus 세대 'generation'; in Korea, people born roughly 1955–1963.

T6-1878.ex: 재난 상황에서 사람들의 공동체의식이 더 강해졌어요.
T6-1878.x: People's sense of community grew stronger during the disaster.
T6-1878.e: Literally 'shared-body awareness': feeling you belong to one group.

T6-1879.ex: 집단주의 문화에서는 개인보다 조직의 이익이 중요합니다.
T6-1879.x: In a collectivist culture, the group's interests matter more than the individual's.
T6-1879.t: Pronounced [집딴주의] or [집딴주이]; the final 의 is usually said like 이.

T6-1880.ex: 같은 어려움을 겪으면서 노동자들 사이에 연대의식이 생겼어요.
T6-1880.x: Going through the same hardship created a sense of solidarity among the workers.
T6-1880.e: Literally 'linked-belt awareness': people bound together by a shared cause.

T6-1881.x: The audience's civic-mindedness stood out as they took their trash home.
T6-1881.t: Korean news often praises or criticizes 시민의식 after big public events.

T6-1882.m: law-abiding spirit, respect for the law
T6-1882.x: Following traffic rules is a basic part of respecting the law.
T6-1882.t: Pronounced [준뻡쩡신]: 법 is tensed in 준법 [준뻡], and ㅈ after ㅂ becomes tense.

T6-1883.ex: 그 간호사는 투철한 봉사정신으로 환자들을 돌봤어요.
T6-1883.x: That nurse cared for patients with a deep spirit of service.
T6-1883.e: Literally 'serving spirit'; 봉사 alone also means volunteer work.

T6-1884.ex: 연말이 되면 기부문화를 확산하자는 캠페인이 많아요.
T6-1884.x: At the end of the year there are many campaigns to spread a culture of giving.

T6-1885.m: social contribution, corporate social responsibility (CSR) activities
T6-1885.ex: 많은 기업이 사회공헌 활동에 적극적으로 참여하고 있습니다.
T6-1885.x: Many companies actively take part in social contribution activities.
T6-1885.t: Usually followed by 활동 or 사업: 사회공헌 활동 'CSR activities'.

T6-1886.forms: 사회적 기업을 세우다 · 사회적 기업에서 일하다
T6-1886.ex: 그는 장애인을 고용하는 사회적 기업을 운영하고 있어요.
T6-1886.x: He runs a social enterprise that employs people with disabilities.
T6-1886.e: -적 turns a noun into 'related to X': 사회적 'social', 경제적 'economic'.

T6-1887.ex: 농민들이 협동조합을 만들어 농산물을 직접 팔고 있어요.
T6-1887.x: The farmers formed a cooperative and sell their produce directly.
T6-1887.t: Pronounced [협똥조합]: ㄷ after ㅂ becomes tense.

T6-1888.ex: 그녀는 아동을 돕는 비영리단체에서 일하고 있어요.
T6-1888.x: She works at a nonprofit organization that helps children.
T6-1888.t: Pronounced [비영니단체]: ㄹ after ㅇ turns into ㄴ (nasalization).

T6-1889.ex: 그 사회운동은 여성의 권리를 높이는 데 큰 역할을 했어요.
T6-1889.x: That social movement played a big role in advancing women's rights.

T6-1890.ex: 수많은 시민이 광장에 모여 촛불집회를 열었습니다.
T6-1890.x: Countless citizens gathered in the square and held a candlelight rally.
T6-1890.e: 촛불 'candlelight' (초 + 불) plus 집회 'rally'; iconic peaceful protests in modern Korea.

T6-1891.ex: 그 의원은 법안 통과를 요구하며 단식농성에 들어갔습니다.
T6-1891.x: The lawmaker began a hunger strike demanding the bill be passed.
T6-1891.e: Literally 'cut off food and hold the fort'.
T6-1891.t: Pronounced [단싱농성]: ㄱ before ㄴ becomes ㅇ (nasalization).

T6-1892.ex: 주민들이 공원을 지키기 위해 서명운동을 벌였어요.
T6-1892.x: Residents launched a petition drive to save the park.
T6-1892.t: Collocation: 서명운동을 벌이다 'to launch a petition drive'.

T6-1893.ex: 시민들은 국회에 법 개정을 요구하는 청원을 냈습니다.
T6-1893.x: Citizens submitted a petition to the National Assembly calling for a change in the law.

T6-1894.ex: 그 국민청원은 한 달 만에 이십만 명의 동의를 받았어요.
T6-1894.x: That public petition got 200,000 signatures in a month.
T6-1894.e: Literally 'the people's petition'; known from Korea's online presidential petition site.
T6-1894.t: Pronounced [궁민청원]: ㄱ before ㅁ becomes ㅇ (nasalization).

T6-1895.ex: 기후위기에 대응하려면 모든 나라가 함께 노력해야 합니다.
T6-1895.x: To respond to the climate crisis, every country must work together.

T6-1896.x: The methane from cows' burps is also a greenhouse gas.

T6-1897.x: The government announced it would greatly cut carbon emissions by 2030.
T6-1897.t: Collocation: 탄소배출을 줄이다 or 감축하다 'to cut carbon emissions'.

T6-1898.ex: 그 회사는 남은 탄소배출권을 다른 기업에 팔았어요.
T6-1898.x: That company sold its leftover carbon credits to another company.
T6-1898.t: Pronounced [탄소배출꿘]: 권 becomes tense after ㄹ.

T6-1899.ex: 대중교통을 이용하면 탄소발자국을 줄일 수 있어요.
T6-1899.x: Using public transportation can reduce your carbon footprint.
T6-1899.e: A direct calque: 탄소 'carbon' + native 발자국 'footprint' (발 'foot' + 자국 'mark').

T6-1900.ex: 우리 회사는 2040년까지 넷제로를 달성하는 것이 목표예요.
T6-1900.x: Our company's goal is to reach net zero by 2040.
T6-1900.t: News often uses the Sino-Korean term 탄소중립 instead; both mean the same goal.

T6-1901.ex: 파리협정은 지구 평균 기온 상승을 2도보다 훨씬 낮게, 가능하면 1.5도 이내로 제한하는 것을 목표로 합니다.
T6-1901.x: The Paris Agreement aims to keep global warming well below 2 degrees, ideally within 1.5 degrees.
T6-1901.t: Pronounced [파리협쩡]: ㅈ after ㅂ becomes tense.

T6-1902.ex: 해수면 상승으로 섬나라들이 사라질 위기에 놓였습니다.
T6-1902.x: Island nations are in danger of disappearing because of sea-level rise.

T6-1903.ex: 히말라야의 만년설이 빠른 속도로 녹고 있습니다.
T6-1903.x: The permanent snow of the Himalayas is melting fast.

T6-1904.ex: 영구동토층이 녹으면 메탄이 대기 중으로 나옵니다.
T6-1904.x: When permafrost thaws, methane is released into the atmosphere.

T6-1905.ex: 오늘은 초미세먼지 농도가 높으니 마스크를 쓰세요.
T6-1905.x: Ultrafine dust levels are high today, so wear a mask.
T6-1905.e: 초- 'super' + 미세 'tiny' + native 먼지 'dust'; 미세먼지 is PM10, 초미세먼지 PM2.5.
T6-1905.t: Collocation: 초미세먼지 농도 'ultrafine dust level', 초미세먼지 경보 'ultrafine dust alert'.

T6-1906.ex: 도시 전체가 짙은 스모그에 덮여 있어요.
T6-1906.x: The whole city is covered in thick smog.
T6-1906.e: From English 'smog' (smoke + fog); the extra vowels make it three syllables.

T6-1907.x: Using a lot of pesticide makes soil pollution worse.

T6-1908.ex: 플라스틱 쓰레기는 해양오염의 주요 원인 중 하나입니다.
T6-1908.x: Plastic waste is one of the main causes of ocean pollution.

T6-1909.x: Microplastics were even found in fish caught in the sea.

T6-1910.ex: 적조 때문에 양식장 물고기들이 떼죽음을 당했습니다.
T6-1910.x: Fish at the fish farm died en masse because of the red tide.
T6-1910.e: Literally 'red tide', just like the English term.
T6-1910.t: Pronounced [적쪼]: ㅈ after ㄱ becomes tense.

T6-1911.ex: 생활 하수가 강으로 흘러들어 부영양화가 일어났어요.
T6-1911.x: Household sewage flowed into the river and caused eutrophication.

T6-1912.ex: 이 시설은 도시 전체의 하수처리를 담당합니다.
T6-1912.x: This facility handles sewage treatment for the entire city.

T6-1913.x: Pollutants released from the factory flowed into the river.
T6-1913.t: Pronounced [오염물찔]: 질 becomes tense after ㄹ.

T6-1914.x: No hazardous substances were detected in this product.
T6-1914.t: Pronounced [유해물찔]: 질 becomes tense after ㄹ.

T6-1915.ex: 플라스틱 용기를 데우면 환경호르몬이 나올 수 있어요.
T6-1915.x: Heating plastic containers can release endocrine disruptors.
T6-1915.e: 환경 'environment' + German-derived 호르몬 'hormone'; a Japanese-coined term.
T6-1915.t: Not literally 'environmental hormones' in English; say 'endocrine disruptors' when translating.

T6-1916.x: A company that illegally dumped industrial waste was caught.

T6-1917.x: I upcycled old jeans into a bag.
T6-1917.e: Native 새 'new' + 활용 'use'; the recommended Korean replacement for 업사이클링.
T6-1917.t: Pronounced [새화룡]: the ㄹ links into the next syllable.

T6-1918.ex: 버려진 현수막으로 업사이클링 가방을 만드는 회사가 있어요.
T6-1918.x: There's a company that makes upcycled bags from discarded banners.
T6-1918.e: From English 'upcycling'; purists prefer the Korean term 새활용.

T6-1919.ex: 이 봉투는 땅속에서 생분해가 되는 소재로 만들었어요.
T6-1919.x: This bag is made of a material that biodegrades in the ground.
T6-1919.e: Literally 'life breaking apart': broken down by living microbes.
T6-1919.t: Common pattern: 생분해 플라스틱 'biodegradable plastic', 생분해되다 'to biodegrade'.

T6-1920.ex: 요즘 기업들은 지속가능성을 경영의 핵심으로 삼고 있습니다.
T6-1920.x: These days companies make sustainability central to their management.
T6-1920.e: Literally 'the quality of being able to continue'; -성 = '-ness, -ity'.
T6-1920.t: Pronounced [지속까능썽]: 가 and 성 become tense.

T6-1921.forms: 지속가능한 발전을 추구하다 · 지속가능한 발전 목표 (SDGs)
T6-1921.ex: 유엔은 지속가능한 발전을 위해 17개의 목표를 세웠습니다.
T6-1921.x: The UN set 17 goals for sustainable development.
T6-1921.t: Pronounced [지속까능한 발쩐]; 발전 here means 'development', not 'power generation'.

T6-1922.ex: 정부는 녹색성장을 국가 발전 전략으로 내세웠습니다.
T6-1922.x: The government put forward green growth as its national development strategy.
T6-1922.e: Literally 'green-colored growth': growth that is eco-friendly.

T6-1923.x: The government said it would increase the share of new and renewable energy.
T6-1923.e: 신 'new' (hydrogen, fuel cells) + 재생 'renewable' (solar, wind) + English 'energy'.

T6-1924.ex: 이 마을은 필요한 전기를 모두 재생에너지로 만듭니다.
T6-1924.x: This village produces all the electricity it needs from renewable energy.

T6-1925.ex: 시화호에는 세계적인 규모의 조력 발전소가 있습니다.
T6-1925.x: Sihwa Lake has a world-class tidal power plant.
T6-1925.t: Homonym: 조력 (助力) also means 'help, assistance'; 조력자 is 'helper'.

T6-1926.ex: 아이슬란드는 지열을 이용해 난방을 많이 합니다.
T6-1926.x: Iceland uses a lot of geothermal heat for heating.

T6-1927.m: thermal power (from burning fuel); firepower; heat of a fire
T6-1927.ex: 석탄을 쓰는 화력 발전소는 탄소배출이 많아요.
T6-1927.x: Coal-fired thermal power plants produce a lot of carbon emissions.
T6-1927.t: In cooking, 화력 means the strength of the flame: 화력이 세다 'the heat is high'.

T6-1928.ex: 탈원전 정책을 두고 찬반 논쟁이 뜨거웠습니다.
T6-1928.x: There was a heated debate over the nuclear phase-out policy.
T6-1928.e: 탈- = 'escaping from': 탈원전, 탈플라스틱; 원전 is short for 원자력 발전(소).
T6-1928.t: Pronounced [타뤈전]: the ㄹ links into the next syllable.

T6-1929.x: We need to reduce our dependence on fossil fuels.
T6-1929.t: Pronounced [화성녈료]: ㄴ is inserted, then nasalization and ㄹ assimilation.

T6-1930.ex: 미국은 셰일가스 덕분에 에너지 수출국이 되었습니다.
T6-1930.x: The United States became an energy exporter thanks to shale gas.

T6-1931.ex: 에너지전환을 위해 태양광 발전에 대한 투자가 늘고 있어요.
T6-1931.x: Investment in solar power is growing for the energy transition.

T6-1932.x: A refrigerator with a first-grade energy efficiency rating uses less electricity.
T6-1932.t: Korean appliances carry 에너지소비효율 등급 labels from grade 1 (best) to 5.

T6-1933.ex: 태풍으로 배전 설비가 고장 나서 정전이 됐어요.
T6-1933.x: The typhoon damaged power distribution facilities, causing a blackout.

T6-1934.m: amount of power generated, power output
T6-1934.ex: 흐린 날에는 태양광 발전량이 크게 줄어들어요.
T6-1934.x: On cloudy days, solar power output drops sharply.
T6-1934.t: Pronounced [발쩐냥]: 전 becomes tense and ㄹ turns into ㄴ.

T6-1935.ex: 그녀는 대학원에서 해양 생태학을 전공하고 있어요.
T6-1935.x: She is majoring in marine ecology in graduate school.

T6-1936.m: inhabiting, living (of animals and plants); habitat
T6-1936.ex: 이 습지에는 멸종위기종 여러 종이 서식하고 있어요.
T6-1936.x: Several endangered species live in this wetland.
T6-1936.t: Homonym: 서식 (書式) also means 'form, format' for documents.

T6-1937.m: population (number of individuals of a species)
T6-1937.ex: 보호 활동 덕분에 반달가슴곰의 개체수가 늘었어요.
T6-1937.x: Thanks to conservation efforts, the Asiatic black bear population has grown.

T6-1938.x: Ladybugs are known as natural enemies of aphids.
T6-1938.t: Also used for people: 그 팀은 우리의 천적이야 'that team is our nemesis'.

T6-1939.ex: 황소개구리 같은 외래종이 토종 생물을 위협하고 있습니다.
T6-1939.x: Non-native species like the bullfrog are threatening native wildlife.
T6-1939.e: Literally 'species that came from outside'; -종 = 'kind, species'.

T6-1940.ex: 토종 씨앗을 지키려는 농부들이 늘고 있어요.
T6-1940.x: More and more farmers are trying to preserve native seeds.
T6-1940.e: Literally 'soil kind': born of this land.
T6-1940.t: Also figurative: 토종 기업 'homegrown company', 토종 한국인 'born-and-raised Korean'.

T6-1941.ex: 고속도로 위에 동물들을 위한 생태통로를 만들었습니다.
T6-1941.x: A wildlife crossing for animals was built over the highway.
T6-1941.t: Pronounced [생태통노]: ㄹ after ㅇ turns into ㄴ.

T6-1942.ex: 이곳은 철새 보호구역이라서 사냥이 금지돼 있어요.
T6-1942.x: This is a migratory bird reserve, so hunting is banned.
T6-1942.t: On Korean roads, 어린이 보호구역 marks a school zone with strict speed limits.

T6-1943.ex: 울창한 삼림이 산 전체를 덮고 있어요.
T6-1943.x: Dense forest covers the whole mountain.
T6-1943.e: Literally 'dense trees and woods'; both syllables picture trees.
T6-1943.t: Pronounced [삼님]: ㄹ after ㅁ turns into ㄴ.

T6-1944.x: Reckless logging has left the mountains barren.

T6-1945.x: Deforestation makes the climate crisis even more serious.
T6-1945.t: Pronounced [살림파괴]: ㄴ before ㄹ becomes ㄹ.

T6-1946.x: The Amazon rainforest is called the lungs of the Earth.
T6-1946.t: Pronounced [열때우림]: 대 becomes tense after ㄹ.

T6-1947.ex: 올해는 이상기온 때문에 벚꽃이 일찍 피었어요.
T6-1947.x: Cherry blossoms bloomed early this year because of abnormal temperatures.
T6-1947.t: Homonym: 이상 (以上) also means 'more than'; 이상기온 always uses the 'abnormal' sense.

T6-1948.ex: 화산재 때문에 공항의 모든 비행기가 결항됐어요.
T6-1948.x: All flights at the airport were canceled because of volcanic ash.
T6-1948.t: Pronounced [화산째]: 재 becomes tense in this compound.

T6-1949.ex: 엘니뇨가 발생하면 세계 곳곳에 이상기온이 나타납니다.
T6-1949.x: When El Niño occurs, abnormal temperatures appear all over the world.
T6-1949.e: From Spanish 'El Niño' ('the boy', referring to the Christ child).

T6-1950.ex: 라니냐 때문에 올겨울은 더 추울 것으로 예상됩니다.
T6-1950.x: This winter is expected to be colder because of La Niña.
T6-1950.e: From Spanish 'La Niña' ('the girl'), named as the opposite of El Niño.

T6-1951.m: to add, to season with; to incorporate (an element)
T6-1951.ex: 이 영화는 역사적 사실에 상상력을 가미했습니다.
T6-1951.x: This film added imagination to historical facts.
T6-1951.e: Literally 'add flavor': first to food, then to ideas or styles.
T6-1951.t: Used figuratively in writing: A에 B를 가미하다 means 'to add a touch of B to A.'

T6-1952.m: to declare boldly, to point out incisively
T6-1952.x: In his speech, he forcefully pointed out the importance of education.
T6-1952.e: Literally 'shout and break through': cutting through false views to state the truth.

T6-1953.m: to venture, to dare to carry out, to risk
T6-1953.x: Even in the heavy rain, they went ahead with the climb.
T6-1953.e: Literally 'dare to act': doing something despite risk or opposition.
T6-1953.t: Collocates with bold acts: 파업을 감행하다, 공격을 감행하다, 탈출을 감행하다.

T6-1954.m: to be drawn toward, to lean heavily toward (an idea); to be captivated
T6-1954.ex: 그는 젊은 시절 급진적인 사상에 경도되었습니다.
T6-1954.x: In his youth, he was drawn heavily toward radical ideas.
T6-1954.e: Literally 'lean and topple': being so attracted to an idea you tilt toward it.
T6-1954.t: Usually A에 경도되다, often with a critical tone about ideologies or trends.

T6-1955.m: to replace, to dismiss and replace (an official)
T6-1955.ex: 대통령은 사고의 책임을 물어 장관을 경질했습니다.
T6-1955.x: The president replaced the minister, holding him responsible for the accident.
T6-1955.e: Literally 'change and alternate': swapping out a person in office.
T6-1955.t: A news word for firing high officials, coaches or executives; 경질되다 is the passive.

T6-1956.m: to decline firmly, to turn down politely
T6-1956.x: He ultimately declined the offer of a minister's post.
T6-1956.e: Literally 'firmly decline': refusing an honor or offer, usually out of modesty.
T6-1956.t: Homonyms: 고사하다 can also mean 'to wither' (枯死); -는 고사하고 means 'let alone.'

T6-1958.m: to flow through, to run through
T6-1958.x: This river flows right through the middle of the city.
T6-1958.e: Literally 'pierce-flow': a river or a theme running all the way through.
T6-1958.t: Pronounced [괄류하다] — ㄴ becomes ㄹ before ㄹ.

T6-1959.m: to disturb, to disrupt, to throw into confusion
T6-1959.ex: 적의 통신망을 교란하는 것이 작전의 목표였습니다.
T6-1959.x: The goal of the operation was to disrupt the enemy's communication network.

T6-1960.m: to investigate thoroughly, to get to the bottom of
T6-1960.ex: 과학자들은 질병의 원인을 구명하기 위해 노력하고 있습니다.
T6-1960.x: Scientists are working to get to the bottom of the disease's cause.
T6-1960.t: Homonym: 구명 (救命) means 'lifesaving,' as in 구명조끼 (life jacket).

T6-1961.m: to use skillfully, to command (a language or technique)
T6-1961.x: She speaks English and Chinese fluently.
T6-1961.e: Literally 'drive and employ': wielding a skill as if commanding it.

T6-1962.m: to reign, to dominate, to lord it over
T6-1962.ex: 그 팀은 10년 동안 리그의 최강자로 군림했어요.
T6-1962.x: That team reigned as the league's strongest for ten years.
T6-1962.e: Literally 'the ruler presides': ruling from above.
T6-1962.t: Pronounced [굴림하다] — ㄴ becomes ㄹ before ㄹ.

T6-1963.m: to rise up, to rally (in protest)
T6-1963.x: Citizens rose up against the rigged election.
T6-1963.e: Literally 'spring to one's feet': rising up together for a cause.

T6-1964.forms: 귀감이 돼요 · 귀감이 됐어요 · 귀감이 될 거예요; formal: 귀감이 됩니다
T6-1964.m: to be a model, to serve as an example
T6-1964.ex: 그분의 봉사 정신은 많은 사람들에게 귀감이 됩니다.
T6-1964.x: His spirit of service is a model for many people.
T6-1964.e: Turtle shells (used in divination) and mirrors were guides; 귀감 means a model to follow.
T6-1964.t: Pattern: A가 B에게 귀감이 되다 (A sets an example for B).

T6-1965.ex: 회사는 이익을 극대화하기 위해 비용을 줄였습니다.
T6-1965.x: The company cut costs to maximize profits.
T6-1965.e: Literally 'make extremely big'. -화 = '-ize': 극대화, 최소화, 세계화.

T6-1966.ex: 안전 장비는 사고 피해를 극소화하는 데 도움이 됩니다.
T6-1966.x: Safety gear helps minimize damage from accidents.

T6-1967.m: to be described, to be written (in a text)
T6-1967.ex: 그 사건은 교과서에 자세히 기술되어 있어요.
T6-1967.x: That event is described in detail in the textbook.
T6-1967.t: Homonym warning: 기술 (技術) means 'technology, skill.' Context tells them apart.

T6-1968.m: to appoint, to put in (a person) for a role
T6-1968.x: The coach put the rookie in as a starter.
T6-1968.e: Literally 'raise up and use': giving someone a chance in a role.

T6-1969.m: to entrust, to deposit; to donate (to an organization)
T6-1969.ex: 그는 평생 모은 재산을 장학 재단에 기탁했습니다.
T6-1969.x: He donated the wealth he had saved all his life to a scholarship foundation.
T6-1969.t: In news, 성금을 기탁하다 means to hand over a donation to a charity or public body.

T6-1970.m: to brand, to stigmatize, to label
T6-1970.e: Literally 'press a branding iron': marking someone with a lasting stigma.
T6-1970.t: Pattern: A를 B(으)로 낙인찍다. The passive 낙인찍히다 is very common.

T6-1971.m: to spring up in disorderly numbers, to proliferate
T6-1971.x: Ahead of the election, small parties sprang up everywhere.
T6-1971.e: Literally 'stand in disorder': too many of something popping up chaotically.
T6-1971.t: Pronounced [날리파다] — ㄴ becomes ㄹ before ㄹ.

T6-1972.m: to issue recklessly, to overuse, to throw around (promises)
T6-1972.x: Politicians throw around campaign promises every election.
T6-1972.e: Literally 'issue in excess', like printing too much money.

T6-1973.m: to be inherent, to be intrinsic

T6-1974.x: History will condemn the dictator's crimes.
T6-1974.e: Literally 'judge a crime': passing a guilty sentence, legally or morally.

T6-1975.m: to pour in, to flood in (letters, donations, aid)
T6-1975.ex: 수재민을 돕기 위한 성금이 전국에서 답지했습니다.
T6-1975.x: Donations to help flood victims poured in from across the country.
T6-1975.t: Pronounced [답찌하다]. Subjects are things arriving: 성금, 편지, 문의, 격려.

T6-1976.m: to steal and use, to misappropriate (an identity or idea)
T6-1976.ex: 누군가 제 이름을 도용해서 계정을 만들었어요.
T6-1976.x: Someone stole my name and made an account.
T6-1976.t: Common in phrases like 명의 도용 (identity theft) and 아이디어 도용.

T6-1977.m: to be fascinated, to be captivated, to be charmed
T6-1977.x: The audience was completely captivated by her voice.

T6-1978.m: to evade, to escape (duty or responsibility)
T6-1978.x: He was caught trying to evade military service.
T6-1978.e: Literally 'escape and slip out of' an obligation.
T6-1978.t: Almost always in 병역 면탈 or 책임 면탈 — legal and news language.

T6-1979.m: to ignore entirely, to lose sight of
T6-1979.x: That policy is armchair theorizing that completely ignores reality.
T6-1979.e: Literally 'sink and discard': losing track of something essential.

T6-1980.m: to depict vividly, to portray incisively
T6-1980.ex: 이 소설은 당시 서민의 삶을 생생하게 묘파했습니다.
T6-1980.x: This novel vividly portrayed the lives of ordinary people of the time.
T6-1980.e: Literally 'depict and break through': portraying something to its core.

T6-1981.m: to disprove, to refute; to show (indirectly), to be a sign of
T6-1981.ex: 새로운 실험 결과가 기존 이론을 반증했습니다.
T6-1981.x: The new experimental results disproved the existing theory.
T6-1981.t: In news, 이는 ~을 반증한다 often means 'this shows (indirectly) that…', not just 'disproves.'

T6-1982.m: to show itself, to be expressed, to manifest
T6-1982.ex: 그의 행동은 깊은 애국심이 발로한 것입니다.
T6-1982.x: His actions were an expression of deep patriotism.
T6-1982.e: Literally 'emerge and be exposed': a hidden feeling coming to the surface.
T6-1982.t: Mostly used as a noun: ~의 발로 (an expression of ~). Pronounced [발로하다].

T6-1983.m: to select, to pick out (for a position)
T6-1983.x: The director picked an unknown actor for the lead role.
T6-1983.e: Literally 'pull out and pick': choosing a talent from many.

T6-1984.forms: 방불해요 · 방불했어요 · 방불한 (+noun); usually: ~을 방불케 하다
T6-1984.m: to closely resemble, to be reminiscent of
T6-1984.ex: 오늘 경기장 분위기는 결승전을 방불케 했습니다.
T6-1984.x: The stadium atmosphere today was like a final.
T6-1984.e: Both syllables mean 'resembling'; an old pair for 'looking just like'.
T6-1984.t: Almost always in the pattern A를 방불케 하다 (to make one think of A).

T6-1985.m: to double, to be doubled; to increase greatly
T6-1985.x: Doing it with a friend doubled the fun.

T6-1986.m: to reject, to denounce, to repudiate
T6-1986.x: We reject all forms of violence.

T6-1987.m: to discriminate, to distinguish, to tell apart
T6-1987.ex: 아기는 생후 몇 달 만에 엄마 목소리를 변별할 수 있어요.
T6-1987.x: A baby can tell its mother's voice apart within a few months of birth.
T6-1987.t: 변별력 is common in test talk: a test 'with good 변별력' separates strong and weak students.

T6-1988.m: to coexist, to exist side by side
T6-1988.x: Tradition and modernity coexist in this city.

T6-1989.x: He assisted the president closely for ten years.
T6-1989.t: Used only for helping someone higher up; 보좌관 is a lawmaker's aide.

T6-1990.m: to patch up (a conflict); to suture
T6-1990.x: The two parties temporarily patched up their conflict.
T6-1990.e: Literally 'sew together': first a wound, then a rift.
T6-1990.t: Often implies a surface fix: 갈등을 봉합하다 suggests the problem may come back.

T6-1991.m: to add (a remark), to say further

T6-1992.ex: 공기 중에 미세 먼지가 부유하고 있습니다.
T6-1992.x: Fine dust is floating in the air.
T6-1992.t: Homonym: the adjective 부유하다 means 'wealthy'; this verb is the scientific 'to float, drift'.

T6-1993.ex: 이 도로는 시청 앞에서 두 갈래로 분기합니다.
T6-1993.x: This road branches into two in front of city hall.
T6-1993.t: Homonyms: 분기하다 (奮起) 'to rise up,' and 분기 (分期) 'quarter (of a year).'

T6-1994.m: to split, to divide; to break up (a group)
T6-1994.ex: 당 내부 갈등으로 조직이 둘로 분열했어요.
T6-1994.x: Due to internal conflict, the organization split in two.
T6-1994.t: Pronounced [부녈하다] — the batchim ㄴ links to the next vowel.

T6-1995.m: to boil; to surge, to be in uproar (public opinion)
T6-1995.ex: 정부의 결정에 대한 비판 여론이 비등하고 있습니다.
T6-1995.x: Public criticism of the government's decision is boiling over.
T6-1995.t: Homonym: 비등하다 (比等) as an adjective means 'evenly matched.'

T6-1996.x: Water accidents occur frequently in summer.

T6-1997.m: to lie unused, to be shelved, to go to waste
T6-1997.x: A good idea was shelved due to a lack of budget.
T6-1997.e: Literally 'stored dead': kept away where it is never used.
T6-1997.t: Homonym warning: 사장 (社長) is 'company president.' 사장되다 has nothing to do with bosses.

T6-1998.ex: 보험료는 나이와 건강 상태를 기준으로 산출합니다.
T6-1998.x: Insurance premiums are calculated based on age and health.
T6-1998.t: Homonym: 산출하다 (産出) means 'to produce (goods or resources).'

T6-1999.m: to be stationed permanently, to reside permanently
T6-1999.x: A guard is stationed in this building 24 hours a day.

T6-2000.m: to have in common, to be in line with; to communicate mutually
T6-2000.ex: 두 사람의 생각은 여러 면에서 상통해요.
T6-2000.x: The two of them think alike in many ways.

T6-2001.m: to promote, to enhance, to exalt (a nation's honor)
T6-2001.x: The athlete raised the nation's prestige at the Olympics.
T6-2001.t: Nearly fixed in 국위를 선양하다. Pronounced [서냥하다].

T6-2002.m: to circle, to turn around; to shift (a policy)
T6-2002.ex: 정부는 강경한 입장에서 대화 쪽으로 선회했습니다.
T6-2002.x: The government shifted from a hard-line stance toward dialogue.
T6-2002.e: Literally 'revolve and turn', like a plane circling.

T6-2003.m: to set, to set up, to establish
T6-2003.x: Try setting specific goals for this year.
T6-2003.t: Pronounced [설쩡하다]. You'll see 설정 on every Korean phone menu: 'Settings.'

T6-2004.x: Our forces annihilated the enemy's main unit.
T6-2004.e: Literally 'annihilate and destroy': leaving nothing behind.

T6-2005.m: to denounce publicly, to condemn (in a group)
T6-2005.x: Residents loudly denounced the development plan at the public hearing.
T6-2005.e: Literally 'attack with voices': a group criticizing something loudly.

T6-2006.m: to inherit, to pass down (by heredity)
T6-2006.x: That family passed power down over three generations.

T6-2007.m: to be retroactive, to apply retroactively
T6-2007.ex: 이번 법 개정은 작년 1월로 소급되어 적용됩니다.
T6-2007.x: This legal amendment applies retroactively to last January.
T6-2007.e: Literally 'go back and reach' an earlier point in time.
T6-2007.t: Pronounced [소급뙤다]. Usually in 소급 적용 (retroactive application).

T6-2008.m: to alienate, to exclude, to leave out
T6-2008.ex: 우리 사회가 노인들을 소외하고 있지는 않은지 생각해 봐야 합니다.
T6-2008.x: We need to consider whether our society is leaving the elderly out.
T6-2008.t: The passive 소외되다 and noun 소외감 are much more common than 소외하다.

T6-2009.m: to exploit, to plunder, to extort
T6-2009.x: Imperial Japan plundered rice from its colony.

T6-2010.x: The dictator brutally purged the opposition.
T6-2010.e: Literally 'sternly cleanse': removing rivals from power.

T6-2011.m: to manifest, to show, to demonstrate
T6-2011.ex: 이 작품은 작가의 예술 세계를 잘 시현하고 있습니다.
T6-2011.x: This work clearly manifests the artist's artistic world.
T6-2011.t: Don't confuse with 시연하다 (試演), 'to give a demo' of a product.

T6-2012.m: to fall from power, to lose one's position
T6-2012.x: That politician fell from power because of a corruption scandal.

T6-2013.m: to be absorbed in, to be infatuated with
T6-2013.ex: 그는 요즘 클래식 음악에 심취해 있어요.
T6-2013.x: He's really absorbed in classical music these days.
T6-2013.e: Literally 'heart-drunk': intoxicated by something you love.

T6-2014.m: to arrange, to mediate, to broker
T6-2014.x: The school helps graduates find jobs.
T6-2014.e: Literally 'turn and revolve': moving things around to connect two sides.
T6-2014.t: Pronounced [알썬하다]. Neutral (취업 알선) or negative (불법 알선) depending on context.

T6-2015.m: to compress; to condense, to narrow down
T6-2015.x: Please compress the file and send it by email.
T6-2015.t: Figurative too: 후보를 세 명으로 압축하다 (narrow the candidates to three).

T6-2016.m: to make great strides, to advance rapidly
T6-2016.ex: 그 기업은 해외 시장에서 크게 약진했습니다.
T6-2016.x: The company made great strides in overseas markets.

T6-2017.x: It's not easy for work and child-rearing to go hand in hand.
T6-2017.e: Literally 'both stand': two things that can exist together.
T6-2017.t: Pronounced [양니파다]. Often negative: A와 B는 양립할 수 없다.

T6-2018.m: to punish severely, to deal strictly with
T6-2018.x: The government announced it would crack down hard on drunk driving.

T6-2019.m: to have served (successively) as, to have held (a post)
T6-2019.x: He served as foreign minister and prime minister.
T6-2019.e: Literally 'pass through offices': listing posts held in a career.

T6-2020.m: to hone, to polish, to cultivate (a skill)
T6-2020.ex: 그는 매일 몇 시간씩 기술을 연마했어요.
T6-2020.x: He honed his skills for several hours every day.
T6-2020.e: Literally 'grind and polish', like sharpening a blade.

T6-2021.m: to barely survive, to eke out a living; to prolong life
T6-2021.x: He barely scraped by doing manual labor.
T6-2021.t: 연명 치료 (life-sustaining treatment) is a common term in medical and ethics debates.

T6-2022.m: to make a soft landing (also of an economy)
T6-2022.ex: 정부는 부동산 시장이 연착륙하기를 기대하고 있습니다.
T6-2022.x: The government hopes the housing market will make a soft landing.
T6-2022.e: Literally 'soft land-touching'; also used for economies cooling without a crash.

T6-2023.m: to read, to view, to look over (records)
T6-2023.ex: 도서관에서는 옛날 신문을 무료로 열람할 수 있어요.
T6-2023.x: You can view old newspapers for free at the library.

T6-2024.m: to cater to, to pander to
T6-2024.ex: 일부 언론은 대중의 취향에 영합하는 기사만 씁니다.
T6-2024.x: Some media only write articles that pander to public tastes.
T6-2024.e: Literally 'welcome and fit in': bending yourself to please others.

T6-2025.x: It's hard to predict the election results right now.

T6-2026.ex: 그 광고는 소비자를 오도할 수 있습니다.

T6-2027.m: to be misreported, to be distorted (in passing along)
T6-2027.x: My words got twisted along the way, and a misunderstanding arose.
T6-2027.e: Literally 'transmitted with errors', like a game of telephone.

T6-2028.ex: 설탕은 따뜻한 물에 더 빨리 용해됩니다.
T6-2028.x: Sugar dissolves faster in warm water.
T6-2028.t: A science word; in daily speech, 녹다 is used: 설탕이 물에 녹아요.

T6-2029.m: to gather in great numbers, to throng, to flock
T6-2029.x: Tens of thousands of citizens thronged the plaza.
T6-2029.e: Literally 'gather like clouds' — people massing thickly together.

T6-2030.m: to postpone, to defer, to suspend (a decision, payment or sentence)
T6-2030.ex: 정부는 세금 납부 기한을 석 달 유예하기로 했습니다.
T6-2030.x: The government decided to defer the tax payment deadline by three months.
T6-2030.e: Literally 'hesitate and delay' — putting something off for a set time.
T6-2030.t: 집행유예 'suspended sentence' and 유예 기간 'grace period' are the most common collocations.

T6-2031.m: to collude, to be in cozy ties (with); to adhere (medical)
T6-2031.ex: 일부 공무원이 기업과 유착해 특혜를 준 사실이 드러났습니다.
T6-2031.x: It came to light that some officials had colluded with companies and granted them favors.
T6-2031.e: Literally 'heal and stick together' — tissues fusing, then figuratively improper ties.
T6-2031.t: 정경유착 'cozy ties between government and business' is a fixed news term.

T6-2032.m: to embellish, to embroider, to dress up (a story or text)
T6-2032.ex: 그는 자신의 경험을 조금 윤색해서 이야기했어요.
T6-2032.x: He embellished his experience a little when he told the story.
T6-2032.e: Literally 'add luster and color' — making a story shinier than the facts.
T6-2032.t: Unlike 과장하다, 윤색하다 suggests polishing the wording, not necessarily inflating the facts.

T6-2033.m: to condense, to compress, to concentrate
T6-2033.ex: 이 시에는 시인의 삶이 짧은 문장 속에 응축되어 있어요.
T6-2033.x: In this poem, the poet's life is condensed into short lines.
T6-2033.e: Literally 'congeal and shrink' — vapor turning to liquid, or ideas packed tightly.

T6-2034.m: to turn away from, to become alienated from (support, loyalty)
T6-2034.x: After a string of policy failures, public sentiment turned away from the government.
T6-2034.e: Literally 'leave and rebel' — loyalty or support drifting away.
T6-2034.t: Almost always in 민심 이반 or 민심이 이반하다 'public sentiment turns away'.

T6-2035.m: to relax, to loosen, to become slack
T6-2035.x: Your muscles relax when you get into warm water.
T6-2035.e: Literally 'loosen and slacken' — muscles, discipline or tension letting go.

T6-2036.ex: 발표할 때 전문가의 말을 인용하면 설득력이 높아져요.
T6-2036.x: Quoting an expert in your presentation makes it more persuasive.
T6-2036.e: Literally 'pull in and use' — borrowing someone else's words.
T6-2036.t: Pronounced [이뇽하다] — ㄴ links to the next vowel.

T6-2037.m: to sweep away, to wipe out, to eradicate completely
T6-2037.x: The new mayor promised to wipe out corruption.
T6-2037.e: Literally 'one sweep' — clearing something away in a single stroke.
T6-2037.t: Homonym warning: 일소 can also mean 'a laugh' as in 일소에 부치다 'to laugh off'.

T6-2038.m: to act on, to work, to have an effect, to play a role
T6-2038.ex: 이번 결정에는 여러 요인이 복합적으로 작용했습니다.
T6-2038.x: Several factors worked together in this decision.
T6-2038.e: Literally 'make use' — a force or factor having an effect.

T6-2039.m: to lie dormant, to be latent, to be hidden within
T6-2039.ex: 모든 아이에게는 무한한 가능성이 잠재해 있어요.
T6-2039.x: Limitless potential lies hidden in every child.
T6-2039.e: Literally 'exist submerged' — present but not yet visible.
