T6-2040.m: to reorganize, to restructure, to realign
T6-2040.ex: 회사는 시장 변화에 맞춰 조직을 재편했습니다.
T6-2040.x: The company reorganized its structure to keep up with market changes.
T6-2040.e: Literally 'organize again' — reshaping a structure or lineup.

T6-2041.m: to point out, to specify, to state explicitly
T6-2041.x: The report specifically pointed out the cause of the problem.
T6-2041.e: Literally 'pick out and show' — naming a fact clearly.
T6-2041.t: Legal term 사실 적시 명예훼손 means defamation by stating facts; don't confuse with 적시 適時 'timely'.

T6-2042.m: to be inverted, to be turned upside down, to be reversed
T6-2042.x: As money became the goal, values were turned upside down.
T6-2042.e: Literally 'topple and fall over' — order or priorities flipped.
T6-2042.t: 주객전도 'host and guest switched' describes the tail wagging the dog.

T6-2043.m: to overturn, to capsize; to overthrow (a regime)
T6-2043.x: A small fishing boat capsized in the storm.
T6-2043.e: Literally 'topple and overturn' — boats, cars, or governments.
T6-2043.t: Homonym warning: 전복 is also the noun 'abalone' (a different word).

T6-2044.m: to divert (funds or land) to another use, to repurpose
T6-2044.ex: 예산을 다른 곳에 전용한 것이 감사에서 적발됐습니다.
T6-2044.x: The audit caught that the budget had been diverted elsewhere.
T6-2044.e: Literally 'shift the use' — moving money or land to a purpose not intended.
T6-2044.t: Don't confuse with 전용 專用 'exclusive use', as in 버스 전용 차로 'bus-only lane'.

T6-2045.m: to compromise, to strike a middle ground, to blend
T6-2045.ex: 두 회사는 오랜 협상 끝에 가격을 절충했습니다.
T6-2045.x: After long negotiations, the two companies settled on a compromise price.
T6-2045.e: Literally 'break toward the middle' — meeting halfway between positions.
T6-2045.t: 절충안 'compromise proposal' is the most frequent derivative.

T6-2046.m: to ignite, to light; to spark off (a controversy)
T6-2046.ex: 개막식에서 성화를 점화하는 순간 관중이 환호했습니다.
T6-2046.x: The crowd cheered the moment the Olympic torch was lit at the opening ceremony.
T6-2046.e: Literally 'light a fire' — from cauldrons to debates.

T6-2047.m: to devote oneself to, to strive diligently
T6-2047.ex: 그는 은퇴 후에도 연구에 정진하고 있어요.
T6-2047.x: Even after retiring, he is devoting himself to his research.
T6-2047.e: Literally 'advance with purity' — originally Buddhist striving toward enlightenment.

T6-2048.m: to advocate, to propose, to put forward (an idea or theory)
T6-2048.ex: 그 학자는 새로운 경제 이론을 처음 제창했습니다.
T6-2048.x: That scholar was the first to propose a new economic theory.
T6-2048.e: Literally 'raise and call out' — putting forward a new idea.
T6-2048.t: Homonym: 제창 齊唱 means singing in unison, as in 애국가 제창 at ceremonies.

T6-2049.m: to tune (an instrument); to coordinate, to adjust (views or schedules)
T6-2049.ex: 두 나라는 정상회담 일정을 조율하고 있습니다.
T6-2049.x: The two countries are coordinating the schedule for the summit.
T6-2049.e: Literally 'adjust the pitch' — tuning a piano, then tuning opinions.
T6-2049.t: Very common for diplomacy and business: 의견을 조율하다, 일정을 조율하다.

T6-2050.m: to end, to bring to an end, to put a stop to
T6-2050.ex: 전 세계가 전쟁을 종식하기 위해 힘을 모았습니다.
T6-2050.x: The whole world joined forces to bring the war to an end.
T6-2050.e: Literally 'end and extinguish' — like a fire dying out.

T6-2051.m: to watch closely, to keep an eye on, to monitor
T6-2051.ex: 정부는 국제 유가의 움직임을 주시하고 있습니다.
T6-2051.x: The government is closely watching movements in international oil prices.
T6-2051.e: Literally 'pour one's gaze' — focused, careful watching.
T6-2051.t: 예의 주시하다 'to watch intently' is a set phrase in news.

T6-2052.m: to apply mutatis mutandis, to apply correspondingly (law or rule)
T6-2052.x: We apply this regulation correspondingly to contract employees as well.
T6-2052.e: Literally 'use by analogy' — applying a rule to a similar case.
T6-2052.t: A legal-document word: you'll see it as '제○조를 준용한다' in statutes.

T6-2053.m: to overlap, to pile up, to be layered
T6-2053.ex: 여러 기관의 업무가 중첩되어 예산이 낭비됩니다.
T6-2053.x: The duties of several agencies overlap, so the budget is wasted.
T6-2053.e: Literally 'doubled and piled' — layers on top of layers.

T6-2054.m: to be amplified, to grow, to escalate (doubts, conflict)
T6-2054.x: As the explanation was delayed, the suspicions grew even more.
T6-2054.e: Literally 'widen the range' — signals, doubts, or anger getting bigger.
T6-2054.t: Typical collocations: 의혹이 증폭되다, 갈등이 증폭되다, 불안이 증폭되다.

T6-2055.m: to continue, to sustain, to last
T6-2055.ex: 정부는 경기 부양 정책을 당분간 지속하기로 했습니다.
T6-2055.x: The government decided to continue its economic stimulus policy for the time being.
T6-2055.e: Literally 'hold and continue' — keeping something going over time.
T6-2055.t: In everyday writing 지속되다 is more common for situations; 지속 가능한 발전 means 'sustainable development'.

T6-2056.m: to lead from the front, to personally take command
T6-2056.ex: 사장이 직접 현장에서 복구 작업을 진두지휘했습니다.
T6-2056.x: The CEO personally led the recovery work on site.
T6-2056.e: Literally 'directing from the head of the battle line'.

T6-2057.m: to do one's utmost, to devote all one's energy
T6-2057.x: The government said it would do its utmost to recover from the damage.
T6-2057.e: Literally 'exhaust one's strength' — giving everything to a task.
T6-2057.t: Pronounced [질려카다] — ㄴ before ㄹ becomes ㄹ.

T6-2058.m: to compile into a comprehensive whole, to synthesize, to systematize
T6-2058.ex: 이 책은 조선 시대 의학 지식을 집대성했습니다.
T6-2058.x: This book compiles the medical knowledge of the Joseon era into one comprehensive work.
T6-2058.e: Literally 'gather into a great completion' — bringing scattered work into one system.

T6-2059.m: to requisition, to commandeer (goods or people by the state)
T6-2059.ex: 전쟁 중 군대는 민간 차량을 징발했습니다.
T6-2059.x: During the war, the army requisitioned civilian vehicles.
T6-2059.e: Literally 'levy and send out' — the state taking property or labor in emergencies.

T6-2060.x: Korean borrowed many words from Chinese.
T6-2060.e: Literally 'borrow and use' — loans of money, words, or styles.
T6-2060.t: 차용증 is the written IOU you sign when borrowing money privately.

T6-2061.m: to exploit, to squeeze (labor or resources)
T6-2061.ex: 그 공장은 어린 노동자들을 착취해 비판을 받았습니다.
T6-2061.x: That factory was criticized for exploiting young workers.
T6-2061.e: Literally 'squeeze and take' — wringing value out of people.
rel: to use, to take advantage of

T6-2062.m: to falsely assume a title, to usurp a name
T6-2062.ex: 그는 스스로 왕을 참칭하며 반란을 일으켰습니다.
T6-2062.x: He falsely proclaimed himself king and started a rebellion.
T6-2062.e: Literally 'overstep in calling oneself' — claiming a title one has no right to.
T6-2062.t: Compare 사칭하다 'to impersonate' (e.g. a police officer); 참칭 is for titles like king or emperor.

T6-2063.m: to promote, to foster, to develop freely (culture, speech)
T6-2063.ex: 정부는 민족 문화를 창달하기 위해 노력해야 합니다.
T6-2063.x: The government must work to foster the nation's culture.
T6-2063.e: Literally 'flourish and reach far' — letting culture grow freely.

T6-2064.ex: 스승은 가장 뛰어난 제자를 왕에게 천거했습니다.
T6-2064.x: The teacher recommended his most outstanding disciple to the king.
T6-2064.e: Literally 'recommend and raise up' — putting a person forward for office.

T6-2065.m: to give up hope, to resign oneself (to)
T6-2065.ex: 그는 합격을 체념하고 다른 길을 찾았어요.
T6-2065.x: He gave up hope of passing and looked for another path.
T6-2065.e: Originally Buddhist 'seeing the truth'; now accepting that something can't be changed.
T6-2065.t: 체념하다 stresses quiet acceptance; 포기하다 simply means stopping an effort.

T6-2066.m: to invite (an expert or guest), to recruit
T6-2066.x: The school invited a famous writer as a lecturer.
T6-2066.e: Literally 'invite and summon' — formally bringing in an expert.
T6-2066.t: 초빙 is for experts and professionals; use 초대하다 for friends and parties.

T6-2067.m: to elect or install (someone as leader), to set up as head
T6-2067.x: The members unanimously installed him as president.
T6-2067.e: Literally 'push up and hold overhead' — raising someone to lead.

T6-2068.m: to confer posthumously (a rank or decoration)
T6-2068.x: The government posthumously awarded a medal to the firefighter who died on duty.
T6-2068.e: Literally 'confer afterward' — honoring someone after death.
rel: death in the line of duty

T6-2069.m: to ratify after the fact, to approve retroactively
T6-2069.x: The board ratified the CEO's decision after the fact.
T6-2069.e: Literally 'approve afterward' — giving official consent to something already done.

T6-2070.m: to expel, to oust, to drive out
T6-2070.x: The party expelled the corrupt lawmaker.
T6-2070.e: Literally 'chase out' — forcing someone from a group or position.

T6-2071.m: to commend, to praise (a subordinate's work)
T6-2071.x: The president commended the rescue workers for their hard work.
T6-2071.e: Literally 'convey congratulations' — a superior praising effort.
T6-2071.t: Used by a superior toward subordinates; you wouldn't 치하 your boss. 노고를 치하하다 is a set phrase.

T6-2072.m: to immerse oneself (in thought or study); to sink deep
T6-2072.ex: 그는 몇 년 동안 연구에 침잠했습니다.
T6-2072.x: He immersed himself in his research for several years.
T6-2072.e: Literally 'sink and submerge' — going deep into thought, away from the world.

T6-2073.m: to indulge in, to be addicted to (pleasure)
T6-2073.x: He was once addicted to drinking and gambling.
T6-2073.e: Literally 'indulge and drown' — sinking into a pleasure.

T6-2074.m: to integrate, to unify (different fields of knowledge)
T6-2074.ex: 이 강의는 인문학과 과학을 통섭하려는 시도입니다.
T6-2074.x: This course is an attempt to integrate the humanities and science.
T6-2074.e: Literally 'unite and encompass'; popularized as the Korean term for E.O. Wilson's 'consilience'.

T6-2075.m: to see into, to gain insight into
T6-2075.ex: 그는 사회 문제의 본질을 정확히 통찰했습니다.
T6-2075.x: He accurately saw into the essence of the social problem.
T6-2075.e: Literally 'see through and examine' — grasping the core of something.

T6-2076.m: to fall into decay, to decline, to become dilapidated
T6-2076.ex: 한때 번성했던 그 마을은 이제 퇴락했습니다.
T6-2076.x: That once-thriving village has now fallen into decay.
T6-2076.e: Literally 'crumble and fall' — buildings or families losing former glory.

T6-2077.m: to project (light, image or feelings onto)
T6-2077.ex: 사람들은 종종 자신의 불안을 남에게 투사합니다.
T6-2077.x: People often project their own anxieties onto others.
T6-2077.e: Literally 'throw and shoot' — casting light or emotions onto something.
T6-2077.t: Homonym warning: 투사 鬪士 is a noun meaning 'fighter, activist'.

T6-2078.x: The government dispatched medical teams to the disaster area.
T6-2078.e: Literally 'send out and dispatch' — sending people on official duty.

T6-2079.m: to collapse, to break down, to go bankrupt (finances, marriage)
T6-2079.x: Reckless investments caused the company's finances to collapse.
T6-2079.e: Literally 'break and split at the seams' plus native 나다 'to happen'.
T6-2079.t: Also spelled 파탄 나다 with a space; 파탄에 이르다 is a more formal alternative.

T6-2080.m: to compile, to edit (a dictionary, history or anthology)
T6-2080.ex: 학자들은 십 년에 걸쳐 국어사전을 편찬했습니다.
T6-2080.x: Scholars spent ten years compiling the Korean dictionary.
T6-2080.e: Literally 'edit and compile' — assembling large reference works.

T6-2081.m: to subdue, to put down (a rebellion), to pacify; to dominate (a field)
T6-2081.x: The general put down the rebellion and returned to the capital.
T6-2081.e: Literally 'level and settle' — bringing disorder back to calm.
T6-2081.t: Also used figuratively in sports news: 세계를 평정하다 'to conquer the world'.

T6-2082.forms: 폐부를 찌르는 말 · 폐부를 찔렀다 (르 irregular)
T6-2082.m: to cut to the quick, to strike home, to pierce the heart
T6-2082.x: My teacher's single remark cut me to the quick.
T6-2082.e: Literally 'to pierce the lungs and innards' — words that reach your deepest feelings.
rel: to hit the nail on the head

T6-2083.m: to win over, to recruit (to one's side); to subsume
T6-2083.ex: 그들은 내부 직원을 포섭해 정보를 빼냈습니다.
T6-2083.x: They won over an insider and extracted the information.
T6-2083.e: Literally 'wrap and take in' — drawing someone into your group.

T6-2084.m: to embrace, to accept (with tolerance), to be inclusive toward
T6-2084.ex: 우리 사회는 다양한 문화를 포용해야 합니다.
T6-2084.x: Our society should embrace diverse cultures.
T6-2084.e: Literally 'wrap and contain' — making room for differences.

T6-2085.m: to dominate, to sweep (an era), to be all the rage
T6-2085.x: That singer dominated the pop music scene of the 1990s.
T6-2085.e: Literally 'grass bending before the wind' — everything yielding to one trend.
T6-2085.t: Homonym warning: 풍미 風味 is 'flavor', as in 풍미가 좋다.

T6-2086.m: to pass down (orders), to issue (instructions to subordinates)
T6-2086.ex: 본부는 각 지점에 새로운 지침을 하달했습니다.
T6-2086.x: Headquarters passed down new guidelines to every branch.
T6-2086.e: Literally 'send down to reach' — orders flowing from the top.

T6-2087.m: to set aside, to devote, to spare (time or space)
T6-2087.ex: 그는 바쁜 중에도 봉사 활동에 시간을 할애했습니다.
T6-2087.x: Despite being busy, he set aside time for volunteer work.
T6-2087.e: Literally 'cut away something cherished' — giving up precious time or space.

T6-2088.m: to meet again (unexpectedly or after a long separation)
T6-2088.ex: 두 친구는 삼십 년 만에 공항에서 해후했습니다.
T6-2088.x: The two friends met again at the airport after thirty years.
T6-2088.e: A pair of characters both meaning 'meet by chance' — a touching reunion.

T6-2089.m: to waste, to squander (time, money or energy)
T6-2089.x: Don't waste your time on pointless things.
T6-2089.e: Literally 'spend emptily' — using something up for nothing.

T6-2090.m: to display, to make manifest, to show clearly
T6-2090.ex: 그 기념비는 국가의 권위를 현시하기 위해 세워졌습니다.
T6-2090.x: That monument was erected to display the nation's authority.
T6-2090.e: Literally 'make manifest and show' — putting something on clear display.

T6-2091.m: to loathe, to detest, to abhor
T6-2091.x: He detests violence more than anything.
T6-2091.e: Literally 'dislike and hate' — strong, visceral aversion.
T6-2091.t: 혐오 시설 means facilities people don't want nearby, like landfills — a NIMBY term.

T6-2092.m: to confuse, to mix up (one thing with another)
T6-2092.ex: 많은 학생들이 두 단어의 뜻을 혼동합니다.
T6-2092.x: Many students confuse the meanings of the two words.
T6-2092.e: Literally 'mix as the same' — mistaking one thing for another.
T6-2092.t: Pattern: A를 B와 혼동하다; don't mix it up with 혼란 'chaos, disorder'.

T6-2093.m: to use together, to mix (in use)
T6-2093.x: Old newspapers used Hangul and Chinese characters together.
T6-2093.e: Literally 'mix in use' — using two things side by side.
T6-2093.t: Pronounced [호뇽하다] — ㄴ links to the next vowel.

T6-2094.m: to be in harmony, to unite; to combine (chemistry)
T6-2094.ex: 모든 세대가 화합하는 사회를 만들어야 합니다.
T6-2094.x: We must build a society where all generations live in harmony.
T6-2094.e: Literally 'harmonize and join' — people coming together peacefully.

T6-2095.m: to give back, to return; to reduce (to a simpler form or in chemistry)
T6-2095.ex: 그 기업가는 재산의 절반을 사회에 환원했습니다.
T6-2095.x: The entrepreneur gave half of his fortune back to society.
T6-2095.e: Literally 'return to the origin' — giving back or restoring.
T6-2095.t: 사회에 환원하다 'give back to society' is the classic collocation for philanthropy.

T6-2096.m: to coax, to conciliate, to win over (with soft words or favors)
T6-2096.x: He tried to win the witness over with money.
T6-2096.e: Literally 'embrace softly' — persuading through gentleness instead of force.
T6-2096.t: Often paired with its opposite: 회유와 협박 'carrots and sticks'.

T6-2097.ex: 회계 담당자가 회사 자금을 횡령해 구속됐습니다.
T6-2097.x: The accountant was arrested for embezzling company funds.
T6-2097.e: Literally 'take sideways' — diverting money that isn't yours.
T6-2097.t: Pronounced [횡녕하다] — ㄹ becomes ㄴ after ㅇ.

T6-2098.m: to admire, to adore, to look up to
T6-2098.x: Many young people admired that independence activist.
T6-2098.e: Literally 'revere and long for' — deep, respectful admiration.

T6-2099.m: very similar, closely resembling, just like
T6-2099.ex: 두 사람의 목소리가 흡사해서 구별하기 어려워요.
T6-2099.x: Their voices are so similar that it's hard to tell them apart.
T6-2099.t: The adverb 흡사 means 'just like': 흡사 꿈을 꾸는 것 같았다.

T6-2100.m: to long for, to earnestly seek, to aspire to
T6-2100.x: The people earnestly long for peaceful reunification.
T6-2100.e: Literally 'hope and seek' — an earnest wish.

T6-2101.m: to reprimand, to rebuke, to take to task
T6-2101.x: The boss rebuked the employee who kept repeating mistakes.
T6-2101.e: Literally 'interrogate and blame' — demanding answers while scolding.

T6-2102.m: to store away, to put away neatly; to wrap up, to finish off (work)
T6-2102.x: Grandma stored away the harvested grain in the storehouse.
T6-2102.e: From 갈무리 'putting things away in order' — now also 'wrapping up' a project or text.

T6-2103.m: to ferment fully, to mellow with age; (of cloth) to wear thin
T6-2103.ex: 잘 곰삭은 젓갈은 깊은 맛이 나요.
T6-2103.x: Well-fermented salted seafood has a deep flavor.
T6-2103.e: Built on 삭다 'to ferment, to break down' — think slow, deep aging, like jeotgal or old memories.
T6-2103.t: Pronounced [곰삭따]; also figurative: 곰삭은 정 'affection deepened over years'.

T6-2104.m: to look down on (from above); to look kindly down upon
T6-2104.x: I stood on the mountaintop and looked down on the village.
T6-2104.e: 굽다 'to bend' + 보다 'to look' — bending down to look below.

T6-2105.forms: 깃들어요 · 깃들었어요 · 깃들 거예요 · 깃든 (+noun) (ㄹ drops)
T6-2105.m: to dwell in, to be imbued with (spirit, feeling); to settle in (dusk, quiet)
T6-2105.ex: 이 작품에는 작가의 정성이 깃들어 있어요.
T6-2105.x: The artist's devotion dwells in this work.
T6-2105.e: Probably from 깃 'nest' + 들다 'to enter' — something settling in as if into a nest.
T6-2105.t: Don't confuse with 깃들이다 'to nest, to settle in' (birds, people); 깃들다 is for spirit, feelings, or dusk.

T6-2106.forms: 넘나들어요 · 넘나들었어요 · 넘나들 거예요 · 넘나드세요 (ㄹ drops)
T6-2106.m: to go back and forth (across), to cross freely between
T6-2106.ex: 그 배우는 영화와 연극을 자유롭게 넘나들어요.
T6-2106.x: That actor moves freely between film and theater.
T6-2106.e: 넘다 'cross over' + 나다 'go out' + 들다 'come in' — crossing back and forth.
T6-2106.t: Common with 경계 'boundary': 장르의 경계를 넘나들다 'to cross genre boundaries'.

T6-2107.m: to tie up tightly, to bind
T6-2107.ex: 넘어진 아이의 상처를 붕대로 단단히 동여맸어요.
T6-2107.x: I tightly bound the fallen child's wound with a bandage.

T6-2108.m: to repeat over and over, to keep saying (to oneself)
T6-2108.ex: 그는 그 말을 속으로 몇 번이나 되뇌었어요.
T6-2108.x: He repeated those words to himself over and over.
T6-2108.e: 되- (again) + 뇌다 (to say again): saying the same words again and again.
T6-2108.t: Spelled 되뇌다, not 되뇌이다 — the -이- version is a very common mistake.

T6-2109.m: to hang down, to let down (a curtain); to cast (a shadow)
T6-2109.ex: 오래된 나무가 길 위에 긴 그림자를 드리웠어요.
T6-2109.x: The old tree cast a long shadow over the road.
T6-2109.e: Built from an old verb 드리다 'to let hang' (as in 발을 드리다) plus causative -우-.

T6-2110.m: to lift and look under; to dig up, rake up (the past, faults); to leaf through
T6-2110.ex: 이미 끝난 지난 일을 자꾸 들추지 마세요.
T6-2110.x: Please stop dragging up things from the past that are already over.
T6-2110.e: Probably related to 들다 'to lift' — you lift something to see what's underneath.
T6-2110.t: Most common figuratively: 약점을 들추다, 과거를 들추다 — to dig up someone's weak points or past.

T6-2111.m: to hold in the mouth; to hold back (tears); to wear (a faint smile)
T6-2111.ex: 그녀는 눈물을 머금고 작별 인사를 했어요.
T6-2111.x: Holding back her tears, she said goodbye.
T6-2111.e: Something kept inside, neither swallowed nor released — like petals holding dew (이슬을 머금다).
T6-2111.t: Classic pairs: 미소를 머금다 'to wear a faint smile' and 눈물을 머금다 'to fight back tears'.

T6-2112.ex: 햇볕에 오래 둔 사진이 누렇게 바랬어요.
T6-2112.x: The photo left in the sun for a long time has faded to yellow.
T6-2112.e: Homonym warning: another 바래다 means 'to see someone off' (바래다주다).
T6-2112.t: Don't confuse with 바라다 'to hope': correct is 바라요 'I hope', though many people say 바래요.

T6-2113.m: to mix, to toss (food with seasoning); to blend
T6-2113.ex: 절인 배추를 고춧가루 양념에 골고루 버무려요.
T6-2113.x: Toss the salted cabbage evenly in the red pepper seasoning.
T6-2113.e: A kimchi-making verb — picture hands tossing cabbage in red seasoning.

T6-2114.m: to sharpen (a blade by heating and hammering); to hone, to steel (one's resolve)
T6-2114.ex: 대장장이가 무딘 칼을 불에 달궈 다시 벼렸어요.
T6-2114.x: The blacksmith heated the dull knife and sharpened it again.
T6-2114.e: A blacksmith's word: reforging a blade with fire and hammer, unlike 갈다 (grinding on stone).

T6-2115.m: to be jostled, to rub shoulders with; to be harassed, to be troubled; (stomach) to feel unsettled
T6-2115.ex: 출근길 지하철에서 사람들에게 부대껴서 너무 피곤해요.
T6-2115.x: I'm exhausted from being jostled by people on the subway to work.
T6-2115.e: Pictures bodies bumping against each other in a crowd.

T6-2116.x: The coach tried to boost the players' morale.
T6-2116.e: 북 (soil heaped around a plant's roots) + 돋우다 (to raise): helping a plant grow.

T6-2117.m: to pierce deeply (into the heart), to be deeply felt
T6-2117.ex: 고향에 계신 어머니가 뼈에 사무치게 그리워요.
T6-2117.x: I miss my mother back home so much it aches in my bones.
T6-2117.e: From an old verb meaning 'to get through' — a feeling that goes all the way through.
T6-2117.t: Fixed patterns: 뼈에 사무치다, 한이 사무치다, 사무치게 그립다 — for feelings that cut to the core.

T6-2118.m: (steam) to fog up, to form; (feelings, spirit) to be steeped in, to linger
T6-2118.ex: 추운 날 밖에서 들어오니 안경에 김이 서렸어요.
T6-2118.x: When I came in from the cold, my glasses fogged up.
T6-2118.e: Homonym warning: another 서리다 means 'to coil up', like a snake; 서리 alone is 'frost'.
T6-2118.t: Literary use: 한이 서린 노래 'a song steeped in sorrow' — the modifier 서린 is very common.

T6-2119.m: to vanish, to fade away, to die out
T6-2119.ex: 해가 지자 붉은 노을이 천천히 스러졌어요.
T6-2119.x: As the sun went down, the red glow slowly faded away.
T6-2119.e: Sounds like 사라지다 'to disappear' and means something close, but more poetic.
T6-2119.t: Don't confuse with 쓰러지다 'to collapse' — 스러지다 is softer, things melting quietly away.

T6-2120.m: to seep in little by little, to sink in gradually without one noticing
T6-2120.ex: 그 노래는 어느새 내 마음에 시나브로 스며들었어요.
T6-2120.x: Before I knew it, that song had gradually seeped into my heart.
T6-2120.e: 시나브로 = little by little, unnoticed; 스며들다 = 스미다 (to soak) + 들다 (to enter).

T6-2121.forms: 에둘러요 · 에둘렀어요 · 에두를 거예요 · 에두르세요 (르 irregular)
T6-2121.m: to go around, to surround; to beat around the bush, to say indirectly
T6-2121.e: Related to 두르다 'to wrap around' and 에우다 'to go around' — talking around the point.
T6-2121.t: Mostly 에둘러 말하다/표현하다 'to say in a roundabout way'; the opposite is 직설적으로 'bluntly'.

T6-2122.ex: 바람이 너무 차서 코트 깃을 여몄어요.
T6-2122.x: The wind was so cold that I pulled my coat collar together.
T6-2122.e: Pictures overlapping the front flaps of a hanbok and fastening them neatly.

T6-2123.m: to tie up tightly; to ensnare, to bind (with rules or false charges)
T6-2123.x: Excessive rules are tying the employees' hands.
T6-2123.e: 옭다 (to tie in a knot) + 매다 (to tie).
T6-2123.t: Pronounced [올가매다] — the ㄱ of ㄺ moves over to the next syllable.

T6-2124.forms: 움터요 · 움텄어요 · 움틀 거예요 · 움튼 (+noun) (ㅡ drops)
T6-2124.m: to sprout, to bud; (feelings) to begin to grow
T6-2124.x: When spring came, new shoots sprouted on every branch.
T6-2124.e: 움 (a fresh sprout) + 트다 (to break open): a sprout breaking through.
T6-2124.t: Figurative: 사랑이 움트다, 희망이 움트다 — love or hope beginning to bud.

T6-2125.m: to slice thin; (heart) to ache as if cut
T6-2125.ex: 마늘을 얇게 저며서 고기 위에 올리세요.
T6-2125.x: Slice the garlic thin and put it on top of the meat.
T6-2125.e: A kitchen verb for thin slicing, borrowed for heartache — a heart being sliced.
T6-2125.t: Emotional use: 가슴을 저미는 슬픔 'heart-wrenching sorrow'.

T6-2126.forms: 짓눌러요 · 짓눌렀어요 · 짓누를 거예요 · 짓누르세요 (르 irregular)
T6-2126.m: to press down hard, to crush; to weigh on, to oppress
T6-2126.x: The pressure of the exam weighed heavily on me.
T6-2126.t: Pronounced [진누르다] — nasalization; the passive 짓눌리다 'to be crushed' is very common.

T6-2127.m: to examine thoroughly, to comb through
T6-2127.ex: 이번 보고서에서는 사고의 원인을 하나하나 톺아봅니다.
T6-2127.x: This report examines the causes of the accident one by one.
T6-2127.e: 톺다 (to grope through every nook and gap) + 보다 (to look).
T6-2127.t: A revived native word, popular in media headlines as a pure-Korean alternative to 분석하다.

T6-2128.m: to wind around, to coil around, to wrap
T6-2128.x: Ivy is winding all around the old wall.

T6-2129.m: to scatter in the wind, to flutter
T6-2129.x: Cherry blossom petals are scattering like snow in the spring breeze.
T6-2129.e: 흩다 (to scatter) + 날리다 (to fly, blow away).

T6-2130.m: to engrave intricately; to engrave in one's memory
T6-2130.x: I engraved my teacher's words deep in my heart.
T6-2130.e: 새기다 (to carve) + 아로-, suggesting fine, intricate detail (compare 아롱아롱).

T6-2131.forms: 얼러요 · 얼렀어요 · 어를 거예요 · 어르세요 (르 irregular)
T6-2131.m: to soothe, to humor (a baby); to coax
T6-2131.x: The mom gently soothed the crying baby.

T6-2132.x: The enemy surrounded the fortress layer upon layer and attacked.
T6-2132.e: The root of 에워싸다 'to surround'; probably related to 에두르다.

T6-2133.m: to sway, to roll (waves), to flicker; (feelings) to stir
T6-2133.ex: 바람이 불자 호수의 물결이 잔잔하게 일렁였어요.
T6-2133.x: When the wind blew, the lake's ripples gently swayed.
T6-2133.e: From the mimetic word 일렁일렁 (gently swaying) + -이다.
T6-2133.t: Feelings can 일렁이다 too: 마음이 일렁이다 'my heart stirs'.

T6-2134.ex: 시험 준비 때문에 어젯밤을 꼬박 지새웠어요.
T6-2134.x: I stayed up all last night preparing for the exam.
T6-2134.e: Contains 새우다 'to stay up until dawn' — think of 날이 새다 'day breaks'.
T6-2134.t: Almost always with 밤: 밤을 지새우다; the everyday version is 밤을 새우다.

T6-2135.m: to crush, to mash, to trample
T6-2135.ex: 마늘을 칼등으로 잘게 짓이겨서 찌개에 넣으세요.
T6-2135.x: Crush the garlic finely with the back of a knife and add it to the stew.
T6-2135.e: 짓- (roughly, hard) + 이기다 (to knead, mash) — not 이기다 'to win'.
T6-2135.t: Pronounced [진니기다] — an added ㄴ plus nasalization.

T6-2136.m: to spread out, to unfold; to stretch out before one's eyes
T6-2136.ex: 산 정상에 오르자 멋진 풍경이 눈앞에 펼쳐졌어요.
T6-2136.x: When we reached the summit, a stunning view unfolded before our eyes.
T6-2136.e: Passive of 펼치다 'to spread out' with -어지다.

T6-2137.m: to pour out one's troubles, to plead one's case, to complain (to someone)
T6-2137.ex: 친구에게 회사 일의 어려움을 한참 하소연했어요.
T6-2137.x: I poured out my troubles about work to my friend for a long time.
T6-2137.e: Looks Sino-Korean but is native; it means asking to be heard, not just griping.

T6-2138.ex: 그녀는 편지를 읽고 어깨를 들썩이며 조용히 흐느꼈어요.
T6-2138.x: After reading the letter, she sobbed quietly, her shoulders shaking.
T6-2138.t: 흐느끼다 is quiet, shaking sobs; loud crying is 엉엉 울다.

T6-2139.forms: 움츠러들어요 · 움츠러들었어요 · 움츠러들 거예요 · 움츠러든 (+noun) (ㄹ drops)
T6-2139.m: to shrink back, to huddle, to cower; to lose confidence
T6-2139.x: In the cold weather my body huddled up on its own.
T6-2139.t: Spelled 움츠-, not 움추-; also mental: 실수 후 마음이 움츠러들다 'to lose confidence'.

T6-2140.m: to be contorted, to be distorted, to be warped
T6-2140.x: The fallen child's face twisted in pain.

T6-2141.m: to toss and turn; to rummage through
T6-2141.ex: 걱정이 많아서 밤새 잠을 못 이루고 뒤척였어요.
T6-2141.x: I was so worried that I tossed and turned all night without sleeping.
T6-2141.e: From the mimetic word 뒤척뒤척, turning over and over.

T6-2142.m: to pace up and down, to hang around restlessly
T6-2142.ex: 그는 결과를 기다리며 초조하게 복도를 서성였어요.
T6-2142.x: He paced the hallway nervously, waiting for the results.

T6-2143.ex: 그는 간교한 꾀로 순진한 사람들을 속였어요.
T6-2143.x: He deceived innocent people with crafty tricks.

T6-2144.ex: 그 가수의 감미로운 목소리에 완전히 빠졌어요.
T6-2144.x: I completely fell for that singer's sweet, mellow voice.
T6-2144.e: Literally 'sweet and beautiful'; -롭다 turns it into an adjective.
T6-2144.t: Used for music, voices and moods; for food, say 달콤하다 or 달다 instead.

T6-2145.x: Grandpa became more cantankerous as he got older.
T6-2145.e: Literally 'hard and willful' — refusing all advice.
T6-2145.t: Pronounced [강퍄카다] — ㄱ and ㅎ merge into ㅋ.

T6-2146.m: lofty and aloof, noble and solitary
T6-2146.ex: 그는 평생 돈과 권력을 멀리하며 고고하게 살았어요.
T6-2146.x: He lived a lofty life, keeping money and power at a distance.
T6-2146.e: Literally 'alone and high' — standing above worldly concerns.

T6-2147.m: time-honored, timeworn, with an antique look
T6-2147.ex: 고색창연한 절이 산속에 조용히 자리하고 있어요.
T6-2147.x: A timeworn old temple sits quietly in the mountains.

T6-2148.ex: 그는 곡진한 편지로 감사의 마음을 전했어요.
T6-2148.x: He expressed his gratitude in a heartfelt letter.
T6-2148.e: Literally 'covering every bend fully' — attentive to every detail.

T6-2149.ex: 공교롭게도 우리는 같은 날 같은 옷을 입고 왔어요.
T6-2149.x: As luck would have it, we showed up in the same outfit on the same day.
T6-2149.e: Originally 'skillfully made'; now 'oddly well-timed', as if someone arranged it.
T6-2149.t: Usually as the adverb 공교롭게도 'as luck would have it', often for awkward coincidences.

T6-2150.m: more than one deserves, undeserved, too generous
T6-2150.ex: 이렇게 큰 상은 저에게 정말 과분해요.
T6-2150.x: Such a big award is really more than I deserve.
T6-2150.t: A humble set phrase: 과분한 칭찬이에요 'You're too kind', when accepting praise.

T6-2151.x: An endless, vast desert spread out before our eyes.

T6-2152.x: Grandpa sang a folk song in a soulful voice.

T6-2153.ex: 그는 궁벽한 산골 마을에서 태어나 자랐어요.
T6-2153.x: He was born and raised in a remote mountain village.
T6-2153.e: Literally 'at the very end and off to the side'.

T6-2154.ex: 할머니는 전쟁을 겪으며 기구한 삶을 사셨어요.
T6-2154.x: Grandma lived a life full of hardship through the war.
T6-2154.e: Literally 'rugged and steep', like a mountain trail.
T6-2154.t: Almost always with 운명, 삶 or 인생: 기구한 운명 'a cruel fate'.

T6-2155.x: After lunch, I feel all drowsy and sluggish.

T6-2156.x: The child read the poem in a clear, ringing voice.
T6-2156.e: Literally 'bright, bright' — a voice as clear as light.
T6-2156.t: Pronounced [낭낭하다] — ㄹ becomes ㄴ after ㅇ.

T6-2157.ex: 그녀는 단아한 한복 차림으로 손님들을 맞았어요.
T6-2157.x: She welcomed the guests dressed in an elegant hanbok.

T6-2158.ex: 도대체 이런 망측한 소문이 어디서 나온 거예요?
T6-2158.x: Where on earth did such an outrageous rumor come from?
T6-2158.e: Literally 'beyond measuring' — too absurd to believe.
T6-2158.t: The exclamation 망측해라! is what an older person says at something shocking or indecent.

T6-2159.x: His writing is clear, with short sentences.
T6-2159.e: Literally 'bright and clear', like still water.

T6-2160.x: I took cold medicine, and now my head feels a bit hazy.
T6-2160.e: Both syllables picture a dim, hazy moon.
T6-2160.t: Pronounced [몽농하다] — ㄹ becomes ㄴ after ㅇ.

T6-2161.ex: 어른께 그렇게 무람없이 굴면 안 돼요.
T6-2161.x: You shouldn't act so disrespectfully toward your elders.
T6-2161.e: Built with 없다 'lacking' — lacking proper reserve and modesty.

T6-2162.ex: 세월이 흐르니 인생이 참 무상하게 느껴져요.
T6-2162.x: As time goes by, life feels so fleeting.
T6-2162.e: Literally 'nothing constant' — the Buddhist idea of impermanence.
T6-2162.t: Homonym: 무상 'free of charge', as in 무상 급식 'free school meals', is a different word.

T6-2163.x: Their dreams were brutally crushed by the war.
T6-2163.e: Literally 'beyond misery'; the 'no' syllable intensifies rather than negates.
T6-2163.t: Mostly as 무참히: 무참히 짓밟히다/무너지다 'to be crushed mercilessly'.

T6-2164.x: That poet is famous for his beautiful prose.

T6-2165.ex: 어려울 때 도와주지 않다니 너무 박정해요.
T6-2165.x: Not helping me when I was struggling is so heartless.
T6-2165.t: Often 박정하게 굴다 'to treat someone coldly'; the opposite is 다정하다.

T6-2166.x: He behaved insolently even in front of his superiors.

T6-2167.x: This area is famous for its outstanding scenery.
T6-2167.e: Probably 빼다 (to pull out) + 나다: pulled out from the crowd.

T6-2168.ex: 정상 회담장 주변은 경비가 매우 삼엄했습니다.
T6-2168.x: Security around the summit venue was extremely tight.
T6-2168.e: Literally 'dense and strict', like a forest of guards.
T6-2168.t: Classic news collocation: 경비가 삼엄하다 'security is tight'.

T6-2169.x: Now that it's fall, the wind has turned cool in the mornings and evenings.
T6-2169.e: A softer cousin of 싸늘하다 'icy cold'; compare 선선하다 'pleasantly cool'.
T6-2169.t: Figurative: 등골이 서늘하다 'a chill runs down my spine' from fear.

T6-2170.m: vivid, clear (as if seen right now)
T6-2170.x: The memory of that day is still vivid before my eyes.
T6-2170.e: Literally 'fresh-looking' — as vivid as if it were happening now.

T6-2171.x: Leaves fall one by one in the bleak autumn wind.

T6-2172.ex: 그 아이는 나이에 비해 생각이 무척 숙성해요.
T6-2172.x: That child thinks in a very mature way for her age.
T6-2172.t: Homonym: 숙성 'aging, fermenting', as in 숙성된 김치 or 고기, is far more common.

T6-2173.m: bleak, dreary, chilly and gloomy; (mind) unsettled
T6-2173.ex: 비 오는 밤이라 골목길 분위기가 스산했어요.
T6-2173.x: It was a rainy night, so the alley felt bleak and eerie.

T6-2174.x: He meddles in even the most trivial things.
T6-2174.e: Probably built on 시시하다 'petty, dull', doubled up for rhythm.
T6-2174.t: The adverb is common too: 시시콜콜 따지다/묻다 'to nitpick, ask about every little thing'.

T6-2175.ex: 뜻밖의 소식에 모두 아연한 표정을 지었어요.
T6-2175.x: Everyone looked dumbfounded at the unexpected news.
T6-2175.t: Usually in 아연실색하다 'to turn pale with shock'; the homonym 아연 means 'zinc'.

T6-2176.ex: 높은 다리 위에서 아래를 내려다보니 아찔했어요.
T6-2176.x: Looking down from the high bridge made me dizzy.
T6-2176.e: From the mimetic 아찔 (a sudden dizzy jolt); 어찔하다 is a variant.

T6-2177.ex: 경기 침체로 청년들의 미래가 암울해 보여요.
T6-2177.x: Because of the recession, young people's future looks bleak.

T6-2178.x: The poignant violin melody moved my heart.
T6-2178.e: Probably linked to 애 'heart, anxious feeling', as in 애타다 and 애틋하다.

T6-2179.ex: 그는 나를 보며 야릇한 미소를 지었어요.
T6-2179.x: He looked at me with a strange smile.
T6-2179.t: Can hint at something sexual (야릇한 분위기), so use 이상하다 or 묘하다 for plain 'strange'.

T6-2180.ex: 날이 어스름해지자 거리에 불이 하나둘 켜졌어요.
T6-2180.x: As dusk fell, the lights came on one by one along the street.

T6-2181.ex: 그가 규칙을 어긴 것은 엄연한 사실이에요.
T6-2181.x: It's an undeniable fact that he broke the rules.
T6-2181.e: Originally 'solemn and dignified'; now mostly 'undeniably so'.
T6-2181.t: Fixed uses: 엄연한 사실 'undeniable fact', 엄연히 존재하다 'to clearly exist'.

T6-2182.ex: 아침 햇살에 풀잎의 이슬이 영롱하게 빛났어요.
T6-2182.x: The dew on the grass sparkled brilliantly in the morning sun.
T6-2182.e: Both syllables picture tinkling, glittering jade.
T6-2182.t: Pronounced [영농하다] — ㄹ becomes ㄴ after ㅇ.

T6-2183.e: Literally 'blocked and clogged' — no room to move.
T6-2183.t: Common: 옹색한 변명 'a lame excuse' and 살림이 옹색하다 'to be hard up'.

T6-2184.ex: 그 배우는 영화에서 요염한 눈빛 연기로 화제가 됐어요.
T6-2184.x: The actress became the talk of the town for her seductive gaze in the film.

T6-2185.ex: 그 선수는 어깨가 우람하고 키도 아주 커요.
T6-2185.x: That athlete has massive shoulders and is very tall, too.

T6-2186.ex: 우매한 결정 때문에 회사가 큰 손해를 입었습니다.
T6-2186.x: The company suffered a huge loss because of a foolish decision.

T6-2187.x: This mountain has a dense pine forest.
T6-2187.t: Almost always describes forests or trees: 울창한 숲, 나무가 울창하다.

T6-2188.m: deep, profound (of character or thought); deep and hollow
T6-2188.ex: 할아버지의 말씀에는 웅숭깊은 뜻이 담겨 있어요.
T6-2188.x: Grandpa's words carry a profound meaning.

T6-2189.x: The river flows on, long and unhurried, to the sea.

T6-2190.ex: 지구의 자원은 유한하니까 아껴 써야 해요.
T6-2190.x: Earth's resources are finite, so we have to use them sparingly.
T6-2190.t: A homonym 유한하다 (有閑) means 'leisured', as in 유한계급, but 'finite' is far more common.

T6-2191.m: subtle, quiet, understated; warm in a low-key way
T6-2191.ex: 그 사람은 말은 없지만 정이 은근해요.
T6-2191.x: He doesn't talk much, but he's quietly warm-hearted.
T6-2191.e: From hanja meaning 'earnest, attentive'; now 'quiet and understated'.
T6-2191.t: The adverb 은근히 is very common in speech: 은근히 기대돼요 'I'm secretly looking forward to it.'

T6-2192.ex: 비가 계속 와서 거리 분위기가 음울해요.
T6-2192.x: It keeps raining, so the mood on the streets is gloomy.

T6-2193.x: The mother looked at her child with loving eyes.
T6-2193.e: Literally 'merciful love'; -롭다 turns it into an adjective.
T6-2193.t: Typically describes parents, grandparents or rulers looking down with kindness.

T6-2194.x: The ceremony began with solemn music.

T6-2195.x: As night deepened, the mountain temple grew utterly still.
T6-2195.t: A literary word; in everyday speech say 고요하다.

T6-2196.ex: 편지에는 고향을 그리는 마음이 절절하게 담겨 있었어요.
T6-2196.x: The letter was filled with a heartfelt longing for home.

T6-2197.m: hale and hearty (of an elderly person)
T6-2197.x: Grandpa is over ninety but still very hale and hearty.
T6-2197.e: From hanja describing a tree standing tall and straight.
T6-2197.t: Used only for older people; homonym 정정하다 (訂正) is a verb meaning 'to correct'.

T6-2198.x: We had a small, simple birthday party with just the family.
T6-2198.t: Common with gatherings and meals: 조촐한 식사, 조촐한 결혼식.

T6-2199.m: handsome and talented, outstanding; decent, quite good
T6-2199.x: He's good-looking and has a great personality too.
T6-2199.t: Don't confuse with the verb 준수하다 (遵守) 'to obey', as in 법을 준수하다.

T6-2200.ex: 협상은 지난한 과정을 거쳐 마침내 타결되었습니다.
T6-2200.x: After an arduous process, the negotiations were finally concluded.
T6-2200.t: Unrelated to 지난 'last, past' (지난주); it is formal and mostly written.

T6-2201.m: soggy, wet and muddy; broad and flat; lavish (of a party)
T6-2201.x: It rained a lot, so the road is soggy and muddy.

T6-2202.ex: 비를 맞고 서 있는 모습이 처량해 보였어요.
T6-2202.x: Standing there in the rain, he looked forlorn.

T6-2203.ex: 흰 원피스를 입은 그녀가 참 청초해 보였어요.
T6-2203.x: She looked so pure and lovely in her white dress.

T6-2204.ex: 새해를 맞아 희망이 충만한 한 해가 되기를 바랍니다.
T6-2204.x: As the new year begins, I hope it will be a year full of hope.
T6-2204.t: Used with abstract things: 자신감이 충만하다, 행복이 충만하다.

T6-2205.ex: 내일이 시험인데 동생은 태평하게 게임만 해요.
T6-2205.x: The exam is tomorrow, but my brother is just playing games without a care in the world.
T6-2205.t: About people it often criticizes: 태평하다 = too relaxed when you should worry.

T6-2206.ex: 그 영화는 퇴폐적인 분위기 때문에 비판을 받았어요.
T6-2206.x: That movie was criticized for its decadent atmosphere.
T6-2206.t: Pronounced [퇴페적]; before nouns, everyday speech prefers 퇴폐적인.

T6-2207.ex: 새벽이 되자 하늘이 푸르스름하게 밝아 왔어요.
T6-2207.x: As dawn came, the sky grew light with a bluish tint.

T6-2208.ex: 평일 오전이라서 그런지 백화점이 아주 한산해요.
T6-2208.x: Maybe because it's a weekday morning, the department store is very quiet.
T6-2208.t: Describes places with few people: 거리가 한산하다, 도로가 한산하다.

T6-2209.ex: 그는 젊은 시절을 허랑하게 보낸 것을 후회해요.
T6-2209.x: He regrets having spent his youth frivolously.
T6-2209.t: Most often found in the set phrase 허랑방탕하다 'to live a dissolute life'.

T6-2210.ex: 그 배우는 키가 헌칠하고 얼굴도 잘생겼어요.
T6-2210.x: That actor is tall and strapping, and handsome too.
T6-2210.t: 훤칠하다 is the more common near-synonym.

T6-2211.ex: 동양 철학에는 현묘한 이치가 담겨 있다고 해요.
T6-2211.x: They say Eastern philosophy holds profound and subtle truths.
T6-2211.e: Literally 'dark and wondrous' — too deep to fully grasp.

T6-2212.m: murky, turbid; corrupt, chaotic (of society or politics)
T6-2212.x: The river became murky because of factory wastewater.
T6-2212.t: Pronounced [혼타카다]; also used figuratively: 혼탁한 선거 'a dirty election'.

T6-2213.x: It's spring, so I bought clothes in bright, pretty colors.

T6-2214.ex: 이렇게 큰 상을 주시니 황공할 따름입니다.
T6-2214.x: I am deeply honored that you would give me such a great award.
T6-2214.e: Literally 'fear and fear' — awe before a superior.
T6-2214.t: Very humble; you'll hear 황공하옵니다 from courtiers in historical dramas.

T6-2215.x: With all our stuff moved out, the house feels empty.

T6-2216.x: Spring has come, and the cherry blossoms are in full bloom.

T6-2217.x: After working out, my back is soaked with sweat.
T6-2217.t: Used with sweat, water, blood or tears: 땀이 흥건하다, 바닥에 물이 흥건하다.

T6-2218.m: vanished without a trace, completely gone
T6-2218.ex: 그 많던 돈이 어느새 가뭇없이 사라졌어요.
T6-2218.x: All that money has vanished without a trace.
T6-2218.t: Pronounced [가무덥따]; mostly used as the adverb 가뭇없이 사라지다.

T6-2219.x: I'm always grateful for my parents' boundless love.

T6-2220.m: flawless, seamless (so no one can tell)
T6-2220.x: The repair is so seamless that nobody can tell.
T6-2220.t: The adverb 감쪽같이 is very common: 감쪽같이 속았어요 'I was completely fooled.'

T6-2221.ex: 그들은 나라를 위해 거룩한 희생을 했습니다.
T6-2221.x: They made a noble sacrifice for their country.
T6-2221.t: Pronounced [거루카다]; common in religious and patriotic language.

T6-2222.m: very far off, distant (in time or space); hopeless, at a loss
T6-2222.ex: 학교를 졸업한 게 까마득한 옛날 같아요.
T6-2222.x: Graduating from school feels like ages ago.
T6-2222.e: A stronger cousin of 아득하다 'distant, faint'.
T6-2222.t: Also means 'clueless what to do': 앞날이 까마득해요 'The future looks hopeless.'

T6-2223.m: rather low; low and soft (of a voice)
T6-2223.ex: 그는 나지막한 목소리로 비밀을 말해 주었어요.
T6-2223.x: He told me the secret in a low, soft voice.

T6-2224.x: The spring sunshine is so warm that it's perfect for a walk.
T6-2224.e: A cousin of 따스하다 and 따뜻하다 'warm'.
T6-2224.t: Mostly poetic, and typically paired with 햇살 or 햇볕.

T6-2225.ex: 인사를 했는데 아무도 대답을 안 해서 머쓱했어요.
T6-2225.x: I said hello but nobody answered, so I felt awkward.
T6-2225.t: Pronounced [머쓰카다]; often in 머쓱하게 웃다 'to laugh sheepishly'.

T6-2226.x: I simmered the soup over low heat for a long time.

T6-2227.ex: 갓 태어난 아기의 볼이 정말 보드라워요.
T6-2227.x: The newborn baby's cheeks are so soft.

T6-2228.x: She stepped onto the stage with light steps.
T6-2228.e: Related to the adverb 사뿐 'lightly', as in 사뿐사뿐.

T6-2229.m: prim, coy, aloof (pretending not to care)
T6-2229.ex: 그 아이는 새침한 표정으로 고개를 돌렸어요.
T6-2229.x: The child turned her head away with a prim look.

T6-2230.m: plump and pleasing to look at, generous and appetizing
T6-2230.x: I served the rice in a nicely heaped bowl.

T6-2231.ex: 멀리 산봉우리가 안개 속에 아스라하게 보여요.
T6-2231.x: Far away, the mountain peaks look faint through the fog.
T6-2231.t: Used for distant sights and old memories: 아스라한 추억.

T6-2232.ex: 길에서 떨고 있는 강아지가 너무 애처로웠어요.
T6-2232.x: The puppy shivering on the street was heartbreaking.

T6-2233.ex: 할머니는 손녀를 보며 참 어여쁘다고 하셨어요.
T6-2233.x: Looking at her granddaughter, Grandma said how lovely she was.
T6-2233.e: An older, poetic form of 예쁘다 'pretty'.

T6-2234.ex: 그 아이는 마음이 여려서 잘 울어요.
T6-2234.x: That child is so soft-hearted that she cries easily.

T6-2235.x: We spent some cozy time together as a family over the weekend.
T6-2235.t: Pronounced [오부타다]; it praises a small, close group, not a place.

T6-2236.ex: 우리 선생님은 평생 올곧게 살아오신 분이에요.
T6-2236.x: Our teacher is someone who has lived an upright life.
T6-2236.e: Contains 곧다 'straight'; 올 probably means 'a strand of thread'.

T6-2237.x: The scenery of the country village is so warm and homey.
T6-2237.t: Often describes familiar sights and sounds: 정겨운 사투리, 정겨운 골목.

T6-2238.x: The child looked up at me with sparkling eyes.

T6-2239.x: Grandma laid out a generous spread of food.
T6-2239.t: 푸짐하다 is the more common everyday synonym.

T6-2240.x: I can hear the children's innocent laughter from the playground.
T6-2240.t: Pronounced [해막따]; typical with 웃음, 얼굴, 미소.

T6-2241.ex: 그동안 열심히 한 노력이 헛되지 않았어요.
T6-2241.x: All the hard work I put in was not in vain.
T6-2241.e: 헛- 'empty, in vain' (as in 헛소리) + 되다.
T6-2241.t: Pronounced [헏뙤다]; common in 헛된 꿈 'a vain dream'.

T6-2242.forms: 무던히 + verb: 무던히 애쓰다 · 무던히 참다
T6-2242.m: patiently, steadily; quite a lot, considerably
T6-2242.ex: 그는 그 일을 끝내려고 무던히 애를 썼어요.
T6-2242.x: He tried really hard to finish that work.

T6-2243.x: Sure enough, it turned out that he was right.
T6-2243.t: Rare and bookish; in conversation say 아닌 게 아니라 or 과연.

T6-2244.forms: 바투 + verb: 바투 앉다 · 바투 다가서다 · 날짜를 바투 잡다
T6-2244.ex: 의자를 책상 쪽으로 바투 당겨 앉으세요.
T6-2244.x: Pull your chair in close to the desk and sit down.
T6-2244.t: With time it means 'tight, soon': 결혼 날짜를 바투 잡았어요 'They set an early wedding date.'

T6-2245.forms: 부득불 + action: 부득불 취소하다 ≈ 어쩔 수 없이 (casual)
T6-2245.ex: 급한 일이 생겨서 부득불 약속을 취소했습니다.
T6-2245.x: Something urgent came up, so I had no choice but to cancel.
T6-2245.e: Literally 'cannot get to not do it' — no choice.
T6-2245.t: Pronounced [부득뿔]; in everyday speech 어쩔 수 없이 sounds more natural.

T6-2246.m: in every single matter, at every turn
T6-2246.x: My younger sibling meddles in every little thing I do.
T6-2246.t: Pronounced [사사껀껀]; almost always negative, with meddling or opposing.

T6-2247.forms: 삼가 + humble verb: 삼가 명복을 빕니다 · 삼가 아룁니다
T6-2247.ex: 갑작스러운 비보에 고인의 명복을 삼가 빕니다.
T6-2247.x: At this sudden sad news, I humbly pray for the repose of the deceased.
T6-2247.t: 삼가 고인의 명복을 빕니다 is the standard condolence message.

T6-2248.ex: 사진을 보니 옛 추억이 새록새록 떠올라요.
T6-2248.x: Looking at the photos, old memories keep coming back fresh.
T6-2248.e: Probably built on 새 'new' — things keep feeling new.

T6-2249.ex: 그날의 기억이 아직도 선연히 남아 있어요.
T6-2249.x: The memory of that day still remains vivid.

T6-2250.ex: 저는 그분의 입장을 십분 이해할 수 있습니다.
T6-2250.x: I can fully understand their position.
T6-2250.e: Literally 'ten parts out of ten' — completely.
T6-2250.t: Pronounced [십뿐]; don't mix it up with 십 분 'ten minutes'.

T6-2251.ex: 친구를 도와주려다가 외려 일을 더 망쳤어요.
T6-2251.x: I tried to help my friend but made things even worse instead.

T6-2252.x: I was quite relieved at the news that my family was safe.
T6-2252.t: Literary; most common in 적이 안심하다. Don't confuse with 적이 'the enemy (subject)'.

T6-2253.ex: 해 보기도 전에 지레 포기하지 마세요.
T6-2253.x: Don't give up before you've even tried.
T6-2253.t: Usually negative — acting too early: 지레 겁먹다 'to get scared beforehand'.

T6-2254.forms: 차차 + change verb: 차차 나아지다 · 차차 알게 되다
T6-2254.m: gradually, little by little; later, in due time
T6-2254.ex: 삼월이 되니 날씨가 차차 따뜻해지고 있어요.
T6-2254.x: Now that it's March, the weather is gradually getting warmer.
T6-2254.e: Literally 'next and next' — step by step.
T6-2254.t: Also means 'later': 그 얘기는 차차 하자 'Let's talk about that later.'

T6-2255.m: nonchalantly, as if nothing happened, naturally
T6-2255.x: Even after lying, he smiled as if nothing had happened.

T6-2256.forms: 추호도 + negative: 추호도 없다 · 추호도 …지 않다
T6-2256.x: I did not lie in the slightest.
T6-2256.e: Literally 'autumn hair' — an animal's fine new fur, so the tiniest bit.
T6-2256.t: Always paired with a negative: 추호도 의심하지 않아요.

T6-2257.m: in layers, tier upon tier; on every floor
T6-2257.x: The boxes are stacked in layers in the warehouse.

T6-2258.m: layer upon layer, in thick layers
T6-2258.ex: 책상 위에 먼지가 켜켜이 쌓여 있어요.
T6-2258.x: Dust has piled up in layers on the desk.

T6-2259.x: He laughed calmly even in a dangerous situation.

T6-2260.ex: 다들 우는 걸 보니 시험이 퍽이나 어려웠나 봐요.
T6-2260.x: Seeing everyone cry, the exam must have been really hard.
T6-2260.t: In casual speech it's often sarcastic: 퍽이나 잘도 하겠다 'Yeah, as if you'd do it.'

T6-2262.x: Grandma smiled and looked at her grandson with satisfaction.
T6-2262.t: Pronounced [흡쪼키]; the adjective 흡족하다 is more common.

T6-2263.ex: 그 문제에 대해 밤새 곰곰이 생각해 봤어요.
T6-2263.x: I thought that problem over carefully all night.
T6-2263.e: Almost always paired with thinking verbs like 생각하다 or 따져 보다.
T6-2263.t: Spelled 곰곰이, not 곰곰히 — a very common spelling mistake.

T6-2264.m: rather late, quite late (in the day)
T6-2264.x: On weekends I get up rather late and have brunch.
T6-2264.e: Built on 늦다 'to be late'; the adjective is 느지막하다 'rather late'.

T6-2265.x: He knew full well, yet pretended not to know.
T6-2265.t: Most common in 번연히 알면서(도) 'even while knowing full well'.

T6-2266.ex: 안개 속에서 멀리 산이 어슴푸레 보였어요.
T6-2266.x: The mountain was faintly visible far off in the fog.
T6-2266.e: Also as the adjective 어슴푸레하다; used for dim light, blurry sight and hazy memories.

T6-2267.m: for a long time, for long
T6-2267.ex: 그 영화는 오래도록 기억에 남을 거예요.
T6-2267.x: That movie will stay in my memory for a long time.

T6-2268.ex: 그는 눈을 지그시 감고 음악을 들었어요.
T6-2268.x: He gently closed his eyes and listened to the music.
T6-2268.e: Don't mix up with 지긋이 'maturely, patiently', as in 나이가 지긋하다.
T6-2268.t: Common collocations: 눈을 지그시 감다, 입술을 지그시 깨물다, 지그시 누르다.

T6-2269.x: The students all like that teacher, without exception.
T6-2269.t: Pronounced [하나가치] — palatalization of ㅌ before 이.

T6-2270.m: hurriedly, in a frantic rush; greedily (eating)
T6-2270.ex: 너무 배가 고파서 밥을 허겁지겁 먹었어요.
T6-2270.x: I was so hungry that I wolfed down my food.
T6-2270.t: Very often with eating: 허겁지겁 먹다 = to wolf down food.

T6-2271.m: suddenly, all of a sudden, unexpectedly
T6-2271.ex: 그는 어느 날 홀연 자취를 감췄어요.
T6-2271.x: One day he suddenly vanished without a trace.
T6-2271.e: Literally 'in a sudden manner'; a literary word from stories and essays.
T6-2271.t: Literary; in everyday speech say 갑자기 instead.

T6-2272.ex: 그는 전화를 받고 황급히 밖으로 나갔어요.
T6-2272.x: He took the call and rushed outside in a hurry.
T6-2272.t: Pronounced [황그피] — ㅂ and ㅎ merge into ㅍ.

T6-2273.m: at once, right away, in one go
T6-2273.ex: 그는 내 목소리를 듣고 대번에 알아봤어요.
T6-2273.x: He recognized me at once when he heard my voice.
T6-2273.e: Usually with recognizing or succeeding verbs: 대번에 알아보다, 대번에 붙다.

T6-2274.m: inevitably, unavoidably, having no choice but
T6-2274.ex: 사정이 생겨서 불가불 일정을 바꿔야 했어요.
T6-2274.x: Something came up, so I had no choice but to change the schedule.
T6-2274.e: Literally 'cannot not' — a double negative meaning 'must'.

T6-2275.m: anyway, at any rate, in any case
T6-2275.ex: 여하간 이번 주 안에는 꼭 끝내야 해요.
T6-2275.x: At any rate, we have to finish it within this week.
T6-2275.t: Synonyms 어쨌든, 아무튼, 하여간; 여하간 sounds a bit more formal and old-fashioned.

T6-2276.m: resolutely, calmly and firmly, with composure
T6-2276.x: He handled it calmly and firmly even in a difficult situation.

T6-2277.m: taking all the trouble (only to be disappointed), with great effort
T6-2277.ex: 일껏 음식을 준비했는데 아무도 오지 않았어요.
T6-2277.x: I went to all the trouble of making food, but nobody came.
T6-2277.e: Usually sets up a letdown: 일껏 ~했는데 = went to all that trouble, but...

T6-2278.m: from of old, since ancient times
T6-2278.x: Since olden times, people have said health comes first.
T6-2278.e: Literally 'from ancient times'; it introduces proverbs and old wisdom.

T6-2279.m: these days, the present time, recently
T6-2279.x: The current economic situation is very difficult.
T6-2279.t: Mostly in formal writing and news as 작금의 + noun 'the present ~'.

T6-2280.ex: 그는 종내 아무 말도 하지 않았어요.
T6-2280.x: In the end, he didn't say a word.
T6-2280.e: Literally 'at the end, then'; a literary word for 끝내.

T6-2281.ex: 종래의 방식으로는 이 문제를 해결할 수 없습니다.
T6-2281.x: This problem can't be solved with the conventional method.
T6-2281.e: Literally 'coming from back then (up to now)'.

T6-2282.m: on this occasion, while we're at it
T6-2282.x: Let's take this opportunity to overhaul the company rules.
T6-2282.t: Usually followed by a suggestion or decision: 차제에 ~합시다.

T6-2283.m: let alone, much less, all the more
T6-2283.ex: 어른도 힘든 일인데 항차 아이가 어떻게 하겠어요?
T6-2283.x: It's hard even for adults, let alone a child — how could a child do it?
T6-2283.e: A variant of literary 황차; both mean the same as 하물며 'let alone'.

T6-2284.x: I left early in case I might be late.
T6-2284.e: Literally 'perhaps, if'; a more literary 혹시.
T6-2284.t: Often in 혹여 ~(으)ㄹ까 봐 'in case ~'; 혹여나 adds emphasis.

T6-2285.x: Scientists try to avoid value judgments in their research.

T6-2286.ex: 교육은 학생 한 명 한 명의 개별성을 존중해야 합니다.
T6-2286.x: Education should respect the individuality of each student.
T6-2286.t: Pronounced [개별썽] — 성 is tensed after ㄹ.

T6-2287.x: In philosophy, the subject and the object are distinguished.
T6-2287.e: Literally 'guest body' — the thing outside the 'host' self, 주체.

T6-2288.ex: 이 문제는 거시적 관점에서 볼 필요가 있어요.
T6-2288.x: This issue needs to be seen from a big-picture perspective.
T6-2288.e: -적 = '-ic, -al', turning nouns into descriptors: 거시적, 미시적, 유기적.

T6-2289.ex: 미시적 분석만으로는 전체 흐름을 알기 어렵습니다.
T6-2289.x: It's hard to grasp the overall trend with micro-level analysis alone.

T6-2290.m: rallying, concentration, mobilization (of people or forces)
T6-2290.ex: 위기 때는 국민의 힘을 결집하는 것이 중요합니다.
T6-2290.x: In a crisis, it's important to rally the strength of the people.

T6-2291.m: genealogy, lineage; line (of tradition or thought)
T6-2291.ex: 이 작가는 한국 현대 문학의 계보를 잇고 있어요.
T6-2291.x: This writer carries on the lineage of modern Korean literature.
T6-2291.t: Common collocation: 계보를 잇다 'to carry on the line of'.

T6-2292.ex: 각 지역 문화의 고유성을 지켜야 합니다.
T6-2292.x: We must preserve the unique character of each regional culture.

T6-2293.m: synchronic (looking at one point in time)
T6-2293.ex: 언어를 공시적으로 연구하면 한 시대의 모습을 알 수 있어요.
T6-2293.x: Studying a language synchronically shows what it was like in one era.
T6-2293.e: Literally 'same-time'; it freezes one moment for study.

T6-2294.ex: 통시적 연구는 언어의 변화 과정을 살펴봅니다.
T6-2294.x: Diachronic research examines how a language changes over time.
T6-2294.e: Literally 'through-time'; it follows change across history.

T6-2295.ex: 교조주의에 빠지면 새로운 생각을 받아들이기 어렵습니다.
T6-2295.x: If you fall into dogmatism, it's hard to accept new ideas.
T6-2295.t: Pronounced [교조주이] — 의 after the first syllable usually sounds like 이.

T6-2296.x: All eyes are on how these negotiations will turn out.
T6-2296.t: Almost always in the news phrase 귀추가 주목되다 'all eyes are on the outcome'.

T6-2297.ex: 이 정책의 기저에는 평등이라는 가치가 깔려 있습니다.
T6-2297.x: Underlying this policy is the value of equality.
T6-2297.t: Typical pattern: ~의 기저에는 ~이/가 깔려 있다 'underlying ~ is ~'.

T6-2298.ex: 그 단체는 환경 보호를 기치로 내걸었습니다.
T6-2298.x: The group raised environmental protection as its banner.
T6-2298.e: Literally 'flag and banner'; used figuratively for a cause.
T6-2298.t: Collocation: ~을/를 기치로 내걸다 'to raise the banner of ~'.

T6-2299.ex: 이번 사건은 행정의 난맥상을 그대로 보여 줍니다.
T6-2299.x: This incident clearly shows the chaos in the administration.
T6-2299.e: Literally 'tangled-veins appearance' — everything running in disorder.

T6-2300.ex: 이 오래된 그릇에는 특별한 내력이 있어요.
T6-2300.x: This old bowl has a special history.
T6-2300.e: Literally 'coming and passing through' — how something got here.
T6-2300.t: Also used for inherited traits: 우리 집안 내력이에요 'it runs in my family'.

T6-2301.ex: 환경 보호는 선택이 아니라 당위의 문제입니다.
T6-2301.x: Protecting the environment isn't a choice but a matter of necessity.

T6-2302.x: Good and evil are a classic pair of opposites.
T6-2302.t: Pronounced [대리팡] — ㅂ and ㅎ merge into ㅍ.

T6-2303.ex: 두 사람의 생각은 완전히 대척점에 서 있어요.
T6-2303.x: The two people's views stand at completely opposite poles.
T6-2303.e: Literally 'soles-facing point' — the spot on the other side of the Earth.
T6-2303.t: Pronounced [대척쩜]; common pattern: ~의 대척점에 서다 'to be the opposite of ~'.

T6-2304.x: They showed the complicated process in a simple diagram.

T6-2305.ex: 현실을 지나치게 도식화하면 중요한 부분을 놓칠 수 있습니다.
T6-2305.x: If you oversimplify reality too much, you can miss important parts.

T6-2306.ex: 기술 발전은 사회 변화의 중요한 동인입니다.
T6-2306.x: Technological progress is an important driving force of social change.
T6-2306.t: Don't confuse with the homonym 동인 'fellow members', as in 동인지 'coterie magazine'.

T6-2307.ex: 이 작은 모임이 지금 회사의 모태가 되었어요.
T6-2307.x: This small group became the origin of the current company.
T6-2307.t: Fun collocations: 모태 신앙 'faith from birth', slang 모태 솔로 'never dated'.

T6-2308.x: This novel took an old folktale as its motif.
T6-2308.e: From French 'motif'; the variant spelling 모티브 is also common.
T6-2308.t: Collocation: ~을/를 모티프로 하다/삼다 'to be based on ~'.

T6-2309.x: A lack of understanding about disability breeds discrimination.

T6-2310.x: All the effort so far ended up coming to nothing.
T6-2310.e: Literally 'no doing'; also the Taoist ideal of effortless non-action.
T6-2310.t: Common pattern: 무위로 돌아가다/끝나다 'to come to nothing'.

T6-2311.m: awareness of an issue, critical sense of a problem
T6-2311.x: This research started from a clear awareness of the problem.
T6-2311.t: Collocation: 문제의식을 가지다/느끼다 'to see something as a real problem'.

T6-2312.ex: 사람들은 정보를 범주화해서 기억하는 경향이 있습니다.
T6-2312.x: People tend to remember information by categorizing it.

T6-2313.ex: 이 사건은 한국 역사의 중요한 변곡점이 되었습니다.
T6-2313.x: This event became an important turning point in Korean history.

T6-2314.x: Watching over power is the true mission of the press.
T6-2314.t: Pronounced [볼령] — ㄴ becomes ㄹ before ㄹ.

T6-2315.ex: 이 회사는 고객 본위의 서비스를 제공합니다.
T6-2315.e: Literally 'base position'; 금본위제 = the gold standard.

T6-2316.ex: 이 기술은 우주 개발 과정에서 나온 부산물입니다.
T6-2316.x: This technology is a by-product of space development.

T6-2317.ex: 이번 회담이 두 나라 관계의 분수령이 될 것입니다.
T6-2317.x: This summit will be a watershed in relations between the two countries.
T6-2317.e: Literally 'water-dividing ridge' — where rain flows to different sides.

T6-2318.ex: 건강과 생활 습관은 불가분의 관계에 있습니다.
T6-2318.x: Health and lifestyle habits are inseparably linked.
T6-2318.t: Nearly always in the set phrase 불가분의 관계 'an inseparable relationship'.

T6-2319.m: leap, rapid progress; leap in logic
T6-2319.ex: 그 주장은 논리적 비약이 너무 심해요.
T6-2319.x: That argument makes too big a leap in logic.
T6-2319.t: Two senses: 비약적 발전 'dramatic progress' is positive, 논리적 비약 'logical leap' is a criticism.

T6-2320.ex: 수면 시간과 성적 사이에 상관성이 있습니다.
T6-2320.x: There is a correlation between sleep time and grades.

T6-2321.ex: 두 이론은 서로 상보성을 지니고 있습니다.
T6-2321.x: The two theories complement each other.

T6-2322.ex: 아이들은 친구와의 상호작용을 통해 많이 배웁니다.
T6-2322.x: Children learn a lot through interaction with friends.

T6-2323.m: prerequisite task, issue to resolve first
T6-2323.x: Jobs are the most urgent issue to resolve first.

T6-2324.ex: 봄이 오면 꽃이 피는 것은 자연의 섭리입니다.
T6-2324.x: Flowers blooming when spring comes is the law of nature.
T6-2324.t: Pronounced [섬니] — nasalization; often in 자연의 섭리 or 신의 섭리.

T6-2325.ex: 이 작품은 작가의 오랜 노력의 소산입니다.
T6-2325.x: This work is the fruit of the author's long effort.

T6-2326.ex: 이번 선거는 새 정부에 대한 시금석이 될 것입니다.
T6-2326.x: This election will be an acid test for the new government.
T6-2326.e: Literally 'gold-testing stone' — once used to check real gold.

T6-2327.ex: 작은 질문 하나가 이 연구의 시발점이 되었어요.
T6-2327.x: One small question became the starting point of this research.
T6-2327.t: Pronounced [시발쩜]; in casual speech 출발점 or 시작점 is more common.

T6-2328.ex: 이 문제에 대해서는 심층 분석이 필요합니다.
T6-2328.t: Often used before a noun: 심층 분석, 심층 면접, 심층 취재.

T6-2329.ex: 숙련된 기술자의 암묵지는 글로 전하기 어렵습니다.
T6-2329.x: A skilled technician's tacit knowledge is hard to pass on in writing.
T6-2329.e: Literally 'hidden silent knowing'; opposite of 형식지 'explicit knowledge'.

T6-2330.x: As society changed, the forms of family became more diverse.

T6-2331.x: The internet has both positive and negative effects.
T6-2331.t: Usually paired: 순기능과 역기능 'the pros and cons, the good and bad effects'.

T6-2332.x: It's important to make the most of competition's positive effects.

T6-2333.ex: 최근 두 나라의 역학관계가 크게 변했습니다.
T6-2333.x: The power dynamics between the two countries have changed greatly recently.

T6-2334.ex: 이 풍습의 연원은 삼국 시대로 거슬러 올라갑니다.
T6-2334.x: The origin of this custom goes back to the Three Kingdoms period.
T6-2334.e: Literally 'deep pool and spring' — where water begins.
T6-2334.t: Collocation: 연원이 ~(으)로 거슬러 올라가다 'to date back to ~'.

T6-2335.ex: 복지 정책의 외연이 점점 넓어지고 있습니다.
T6-2335.x: The scope of welfare policy is gradually widening.
T6-2335.e: Literally 'outward extension'; the counterpart of 내포.
T6-2335.t: Collocation: 외연을 넓히다/확장하다 'to broaden the scope'.

T6-2336.ex: 이 단어는 부정적인 의미를 내포하고 있어요.
T6-2336.x: This word carries a negative connotation.

T6-2337.x: The heart of this policy is job creation.

T6-2338.ex: 이 이야기는 영웅 신화의 원형을 보여 줍니다.
T6-2338.x: This story shows the archetype of the hero myth.
T6-2338.e: Literally 'original mold'; homonym warning: 원형 also means 'circle, round shape'.
T6-2338.t: Collocation: 원형을 보존하다/유지하다 'to preserve the original form'.

T6-2339.ex: 각 부서가 유기적으로 협력해야 성과가 납니다.
T6-2339.x: Results come only when each department cooperates closely.
T6-2339.e: Literally 'having a mechanism' — parts working together like a living body.

T6-2341.ex: 모든 일에는 원인이 있다는 인과율을 믿어요.
T6-2341.x: I believe in the law of causality: everything has a cause.

T6-2342.x: We must clear away the remnants of the Japanese colonial period.
T6-2342.t: Usually negative; a common collocation is 잔재를 청산하다, 'to clear away the vestiges.'

T6-2343.m: base, foundation; grassroots, broad base (of support or participation)
T6-2343.ex: 생활 체육의 저변이 점점 넓어지고 있어요.
T6-2343.x: The base of everyday sports participation is gradually widening.
T6-2343.e: Literally 'bottom side', like the base of a triangle.
T6-2343.t: Common collocation: 저변을 확대하다, 'to broaden the base (of participation).'

T6-2344.ex: 많은 사람들은 그를 성공한 사업가의 전형으로 생각해요.
T6-2344.x: Many people see him as the very model of a successful businessman.
T6-2344.t: Don't confuse it with the homonym 전형 (screening, selection), as in 대학 입시 전형.

T6-2345.forms: 제반 + noun: 제반 사항 · 제반 비용
T6-2345.m: all kinds of, various, all related (things)
T6-2345.ex: 계약에 필요한 제반 서류를 준비해 주세요.
T6-2345.x: Please prepare all the documents required for the contract.
T6-2345.t: Almost always used directly before a noun: 제반 사항, 제반 비용, 제반 문제.

T6-2346.ex: 그 작가는 시대의 조류를 잘 읽어요.
T6-2346.x: That writer reads the currents of the times well.
T6-2346.e: Literally 'tidal flow': the current of the times.
T6-2346.t: Homonyms: 조류 also means 'birds' or 'algae'; context tells you which.

T6-2347.m: existence, survival (of a nation, organization, etc.)
T6-2347.ex: 이번 위기는 회사의 존립을 위협하고 있어요.
T6-2347.x: This crisis is threatening the company's very existence.
T6-2347.t: Pronounced [졸립]: ㄴ becomes ㄹ before ㄹ.

T6-2348.ex: 그 연구는 과학의 새로운 지평을 열었어요.
T6-2348.x: That research opened new horizons for science.
T6-2348.e: Literally 'flat earth': where the land meets the sky; 지평선 is the horizon line.
T6-2348.t: Common collocation: 새로운 지평을 열다, 'to open new horizons.'

T6-2349.m: shackles, fetters, yoke (of oppression or hardship)
T6-2349.x: They struggled to break free from the shackles of poverty.
T6-2349.t: Typical pattern: N의 질곡에서 벗어나다, 'to break free from the yoke of N.'

T6-2350.m: sharpening, intensification (of a conflict or issue)
T6-2350.ex: 두 나라 사이의 갈등이 첨예화되고 있어요.
T6-2350.x: The conflict between the two countries is intensifying.

T6-2351.ex: 흩어진 자료를 체계화하는 데 시간이 많이 걸렸어요.
T6-2351.x: It took a long time to systematize the scattered data.

T6-2352.ex: 문화는 한 사회의 생활 방식의 총체입니다.
T6-2352.x: Culture is the totality of a society's way of life.
T6-2352.t: 총체적(인) is common: 총체적 난국, 'an all-around crisis.'

T6-2353.ex: 이 문제는 여러 층위에서 분석해야 해요.
T6-2353.x: This issue needs to be analyzed on several levels.

T6-2354.ex: 타자를 이해하려면 먼저 자신을 알아야 해요.
T6-2354.x: To understand the other, you must first know yourself.
T6-2354.t: Homonyms: 타자 also means 'batter' in baseball and 'typing'.

T6-2355.x: We need to break away from outdated ways of thinking.
T6-2355.e: Literally 'shedding skin', like a snake molting.
T6-2355.t: Pattern: N에서 탈피하다, 'to break out of N.'

T6-2357.ex: 이번 정책은 경제 전반에 큰 파급효과를 가져올 거예요.
T6-2357.x: This policy will have a big ripple effect across the economy.
T6-2357.e: Literally 'an effect that spreads like waves'.
T6-2357.t: Pronounced [파그표과]: ㅂ and ㅎ merge into ㅍ.

T6-2358.ex: 인터넷은 사람들이 소통하는 방식의 패러다임을 완전히 바꿨어요.
T6-2358.x: The internet completely changed the paradigm of how people communicate.

T6-2359.m: glimpse, fragment, small part (of a larger whole)
T6-2359.ex: 이 편지에서 그의 성격의 편린을 엿볼 수 있어요.
T6-2359.x: In this letter, you can catch a glimpse of his character.
T6-2359.e: Literally 'a single fish scale' that hints at the whole creature.
T6-2359.t: Pronounced [펼린]; usually in 편린을 엿보다, 'to catch a glimpse of.'

T6-2360.ex: 하얀 비둘기는 오래전부터 평화의 표상으로 여겨져 왔어요.
T6-2360.x: The white dove has long been regarded as a symbol of peace.

T6-2361.ex: 요즘 외모를 지나치게 중시하는 풍조가 있어요.
T6-2361.x: These days there's a trend of placing too much value on looks.
T6-2361.e: Literally 'wind and tide': which way society is blowing.
T6-2361.t: Often negative: 잘못된 풍조, 사회 풍조.

T6-2362.ex: 모든 행정 절차는 합목적성을 갖춰야 합니다.
T6-2362.x: Every administrative procedure must serve its intended purpose.
T6-2362.e: Literally 'the quality of fitting the purpose (목적)'.

T6-2363.ex: 흡연의 해악은 이미 잘 알려져 있어요.
T6-2363.x: The harms of smoking are already well known.

T6-2364.ex: SNS 속 화려한 삶은 허상일 때가 많아요.
T6-2364.x: The glamorous lives on social media are often an illusion.

T6-2365.m: current state, where something stands now; current address
T6-2365.ex: 이 통계는 한국 교육의 현주소를 보여 줘요.
T6-2365.x: These statistics show where Korean education stands today.
T6-2365.e: Literally 'present address': figuratively, where something stands right now.

T6-2366.x: In the narrow sense, culture means the arts and scholarship.
T6-2366.t: Homonym 협의 also means 'consultation'; 협의의 N or 협의로 signals the 'narrow sense' meaning.

T6-2367.x: In the broad sense, education also includes upbringing at home.
T6-2367.t: Usually 광의의 N, or 광의로 보면, 'broadly speaking.'

T6-2368.m: hollowing out, becoming an empty shell (of a system or law)
T6-2368.ex: 감시 기능이 없으면 그 제도는 형해화될 수 있어요.
T6-2368.x: Without oversight, that system could become an empty shell.
T6-2368.e: Literally 'turning into a skeleton': the form remains but the substance is gone.

T6-2369.ex: 모든 행동을 유전자로 설명하는 것은 환원주의라는 비판을 받아요.
T6-2369.x: Explaining all behavior by genes is criticized as reductionism.
T6-2369.t: -주의 means '-ism' (민주주의, 자본주의) and is usually pronounced [주이].

T6-2370.m: beginning, forerunner, the first of its kind
T6-2370.ex: 이 소설은 한국 현대 소설의 효시로 평가받아요.
T6-2370.x: This novel is regarded as the forerunner of modern Korean fiction.
T6-2370.e: Literally 'whistling arrow', once shot to signal the start of a battle.
T6-2370.t: Pattern: N의 효시로 꼽히다/평가받다, 'to be considered the first N.'

T6-2371.ex: 그 영화는 따뜻한 휴머니즘을 담고 있어요.
T6-2371.x: That movie is full of warm humanity.
T6-2371.e: From English 'humanism'; in Korean it often just means warm-hearted compassion.

T6-2372.ex: 날씨의 가변성 때문에 계획을 세우기 어려워요.
T6-2372.x: The changeability of the weather makes it hard to plan.
T6-2372.t: Pronounced [가변썽]: -성 is often tensed after a Sino noun.

T6-2373.ex: 정부 정책의 효과가 점점 가시화되고 있어요.
T6-2373.x: The effects of the government's policy are gradually becoming visible.
T6-2373.t: 가시화되다 means results become visible; for data visualization, 시각화 is more common.

T6-2374.ex: 이상과 현실 사이에는 큰 간극이 있어요.
T6-2374.x: There's a big gap between ideals and reality.

T6-2375.ex: 새로운 현상을 개념화하는 것은 쉽지 않아요.
T6-2375.x: Conceptualizing a new phenomenon isn't easy.

T6-2376.m: entrenchment, becoming fixed or locked in
T6-2376.ex: 한국에서는 저출산 현상이 점점 고착화되고 있어요.
T6-2376.x: In Korea, the low birth rate is becoming more and more entrenched.
T6-2376.t: Pronounced [고차콰]; mostly used for negative trends, e.g. 양극화가 고착화되다.

T6-2377.ex: 정치인과 국민의 생각 사이에 괴리가 커요.
T6-2377.x: There's a big disconnect between what politicians and citizens think.

T6-2378.ex: 글을 쓰기 전에 생각을 구조화해 보세요.
T6-2378.x: Try structuring your thoughts before you write.

T6-2379.m: trajectory, track, path (of a life or career)
T6-2379.ex: 이 책은 한 예술가의 삶의 궤적을 따라가요.
T6-2379.x: This book follows the trajectory of an artist's life.

T6-2380.ex: 그런 행동은 결국 실패로 귀결될 거예요.
T6-2380.x: That kind of behavior will end in failure.
T6-2380.e: Literally 'returning to a conclusion': where things end up.
T6-2380.t: Pattern: N(으)로 귀결되다, 'to end up in N.'

T6-2381.m: crack, fissure; rift (in a relationship or alliance)
T6-2381.ex: 지진 후에 오래된 다리에 큰 균열이 생겼어요.
T6-2381.x: After the earthquake, large cracks formed in the old bridge.
T6-2381.e: Cracks like the pattern on a turtle shell; the first character normally means 'turtle'.
T6-2381.t: Pronounced [규녈]; also figurative: 동맹에 균열이 생기다, 'a rift opens in the alliance.'

T6-2382.x: Children naturally internalize their parents' values.

T6-2383.x: A democratic society is founded on pluralism.

T6-2384.ex: 사회가 다원화되면서 사람들의 가치관도 훨씬 다양해졌어요.
T6-2384.x: As society has become more pluralistic, people's values have become much more diverse.

T6-2385.m: advent, arrival (of an era or age)
T6-2385.ex: 인공지능 시대의 도래로 일자리가 변하고 있어요.
T6-2385.x: With the advent of the AI era, jobs are changing.
T6-2385.t: Used for eras and ages (새 시대가 도래하다), not for people arriving.

T6-2386.x: His argument shows a lot of contradictions.
T6-2386.e: From an old tale of a seller praising an unstoppable spear and an unbreakable shield.

T6-2387.m: materialism, the belief that money can do anything
T6-2387.ex: 물질만능주의가 여러 사회 문제를 낳고 있다는 비판이 많아요.
T6-2387.x: Many criticize materialism for causing various social problems.
T6-2387.e: Literally 'the doctrine that material things can do everything'.
T6-2387.t: Pronounced [물찔만능주의]: ㄹ followed by ㅈ in Sino words is tensed.

T6-2388.ex: 그 집단의 배타성 때문에 새로운 사람이 적응하기 힘들어요.
T6-2388.x: Because the group is so exclusive, it's hard for newcomers to fit in.
T6-2388.e: Literally 'the quality of pushing others away'.

T6-2389.m: history of changes, evolution (of something over time)
T6-2389.ex: 이 박물관에서 한국 옷의 변천사를 볼 수 있어요.
T6-2389.x: At this museum you can see how Korean clothing has changed over time.

T6-2390.ex: 청소년 자살은 우리 사회의 심각한 병리현상입니다.
T6-2390.x: Youth suicide is a serious pathology of our society.
T6-2390.t: Pronounced [병니현상]: ㄹ becomes ㄴ after ㅇ.

T6-2391.m: original nature, true or inherent role
T6-2391.ex: 학교는 교육이라는 본연의 역할에 충실해야 해요.
T6-2391.x: Schools should be faithful to their true role of education.
T6-2391.t: Almost always 본연의 N: 본연의 임무, 본연의 모습.

T6-2392.ex: 우리 회사에서는 선배보다 먼저 퇴근하지 않는 것이 불문율이에요.
T6-2392.x: At our company, it's an unwritten rule not to leave before your seniors.

T6-2393.ex: 광화문은 서울의 역사적 상징성을 지니고 있어요.
T6-2393.x: Gwanghwamun carries historical symbolic significance for Seoul.
T6-2393.e: Literally 'the quality of being an image-sign (상징)'.

T6-2394.ex: 대학 서열화는 입시 경쟁을 심하게 만들어요.
T6-2394.x: Ranking universities makes the admissions race fiercer.

T6-2397.x: The dynamism of Korean society impresses foreigners.

T6-2398.x: Innovation is necessary for a company to last.

T6-2399.ex: 위정자들은 국민의 목소리에 귀를 기울여야 합니다.
T6-2399.x: Those in power must listen to the voice of the people.
T6-2399.e: -자 = person who does it: 과학자, 운전자, 위정자.
T6-2399.t: Formal and literary; often used with a critical edge toward people in power.

T6-2400.x: The outline of the new project has started to emerge.
T6-2400.e: Literally 'rim and outer wall': the outer edge of something.

T6-2401.ex: 세상을 선과 악의 이분법으로 볼 수는 없어요.
T6-2401.x: You can't see the world as a simple split between good and evil.
T6-2401.e: Literally 'the method of dividing in two'.

T6-2402.ex: 강물은 스스로 깨끗해지는 자정 작용을 해요.
T6-2402.x: River water cleans itself through self-purification.
T6-2402.e: Literally 'self-cleaning'; used for nature and for organizations reforming themselves.
T6-2402.t: Homonym: 자정 meaning 'midnight' is far more common in daily life.

T6-2403.ex: 언론이 자정능력을 잃었다는 비판이 나오고 있어요.
T6-2403.x: There is criticism that the press has lost its ability to correct itself.
T6-2403.e: Literally 'the power to clean oneself', said of rivers and of institutions.
T6-2403.t: Pronounced [자정능녁]: ㄹ becomes ㄴ after ㅇ.

T6-2404.m: essence, quintessence, the very best part
T6-2404.ex: 이 음식은 한국 전통 요리의 정수를 보여 줘요.
T6-2404.x: This dish shows the essence of traditional Korean cooking.
T6-2404.t: Homonyms: 정수 also means 'integer' and 'purified water.'

T6-2405.ex: 정형화된 답변보다 자신만의 생각을 말해 보세요.
T6-2405.x: Rather than a formulaic answer, try saying what you really think.

T6-2406.x: In many countries, parental leave has been institutionalized by law.

T6-2407.ex: 건물의 디자인이 주변 자연과 잘 조응해요.
T6-2407.x: The building's design harmonizes well with the surrounding nature.

T6-2408.ex: 이번 개혁의 주안점은 교육의 질을 높이는 거예요.
T6-2408.x: The main focus of this reform is raising the quality of education.
T6-2408.e: Literally 'the point where the main eye rests'.
T6-2408.t: Common pattern: N에 주안점을 두다, 'to focus on N.'

T6-2409.ex: 이 소설은 중층적인 구조를 가지고 있어요.
T6-2409.x: This novel has a multilayered structure.

T6-2410.m: true face, true character, real worth
T6-2410.ex: 그는 위기 상황에서 진면목을 보여 주었어요.
T6-2410.x: He showed his true character in a crisis.

T6-2411.ex: 위키백과는 집단지성을 보여 주는 대표적인 사례예요.
T6-2411.x: Wikipedia is a prime example of collective intelligence at work.

T6-2412.ex: 천부인권 사상은 근대 민주주의의 바탕이 되었어요.
T6-2412.x: The idea of natural rights became the foundation of modern democracy.

T6-2413.m: stirrings, early beginnings (of a movement); fetal movement
T6-2413.x: In the 1920s, a new literary movement began to stir.
T6-2413.e: Literally 'movement in the womb': the first signs of something about to be born.

T6-2414.x: The population is overly concentrated in the capital region.

T6-2415.ex: 이 연구는 문제의 표층만 다루고 있어요.
T6-2415.x: This study only deals with the surface of the problem.

T6-2416.x: Many people think of competition as a necessary evil.
T6-2416.e: Literally 'needed evil', matching the English phrase.
T6-2416.t: Pronounced [피료악]: the ㄹ links to the next syllable.

T6-2417.x: The reporter exposed the falseness of the rumor.
T6-2417.e: Literally 'the quality of being built from nothing'.

T6-2418.ex: 구름이 마치 용의 형상을 하고 있어요.
T6-2418.x: The cloud is shaped just like a dragon.
T6-2418.t: 형상화하다 means 'to give concrete form to' an idea, common in art and literature.

T6-2419.ex: 정권이 무너지자 나라 전체가 혼돈에 빠졌습니다.
T6-2419.x: When the regime collapsed, the whole country fell into chaos.
T6-2419.e: Literally 'mixed and murky', the formless state before order.

T6-2420.ex: 발표 내용이 자주 바뀌어서 현장에 혼선이 생겼습니다.
T6-2420.x: The announcement kept changing, which caused confusion on site.
T6-2420.e: Literally 'mixed lines', like crossed telephone wires; now any mix-up in communication.
T6-2420.t: Common collocations: 혼선을 빚다 and 혼선이 생기다 'cause/have a mix-up'.

T6-2421.m: standardization, uniformity, making everything the same
T6-2421.ex: 교육의 획일화는 학생들의 창의성을 떨어뜨릴 수 있습니다.
T6-2421.x: Uniformity in education can lower students' creativity.
T6-2421.e: Literally 'becoming drawn as one': forcing everything into a single mold.
T6-2421.t: Usually negative in tone, unlike 표준화, which is a neutral 'standardization'.

T6-2422.m: harsh taxation and extortion of the people
T6-2422.ex: 조선 후기 백성들은 관리들의 가렴주구에 시달렸습니다.
T6-2422.x: In the late Joseon period, the people suffered from officials' harsh extortion.
T6-2422.e: Literally 'collect harshly, demand by force': greedy officials squeezing the people.

T6-2423.m: foolishly sticking to outdated ways, failing to adapt
T6-2423.ex: 시대가 바뀌었는데 옛 방식만 고집하는 건 각주구검이에요.
T6-2423.x: Insisting on old methods when times have changed is like marking the boat.
T6-2423.e: A man dropped his sword from a boat, marked the boat, and searched there after landing.

T6-2424.ex: 두 사람은 간담상조하는 사이라 비밀이 없어요.
T6-2424.x: The two are such close friends that they keep no secrets.
T6-2424.e: Literally 'liver and gall shown to each other': revealing your innermost self.

T6-2425.m: taking what suits you and rejecting what doesn't, self-serving fickleness
T6-2425.ex: 필요할 때만 찾아오는 그 친구는 감탄고토의 전형이에요.
T6-2425.x: That friend who only comes around when he needs something is a classic opportunist.
T6-2425.e: Literally 'swallow the sweet, spit out the bitter'.

T6-2426.m: cutting to the chase, skipping the preamble
T6-2426.x: We're short on time, so I'll cut to the chase and give you the conclusion first.
T6-2426.e: Literally 'remove the head, cut off the tail', leaving only the core.
T6-2426.t: Very common as 거두절미하고 at the start of a sentence.

T6-2427.m: staking everything on one throw, an all-or-nothing gamble
T6-2427.ex: 두 팀은 결승전에서 건곤일척의 승부를 벌였습니다.
T6-2427.x: The two teams fought an all-or-nothing battle in the final.
T6-2427.e: Literally 'heaven and earth on one throw of the dice'.

T6-2428.m: the feeling that times have changed completely
T6-2428.ex: 스마트폰으로 모든 일을 하는 걸 보면 격세지감을 느껴요.
T6-2428.x: Seeing everything done by smartphone, I feel how much times have changed.
T6-2428.e: Literally 'feeling of being a generation apart'.
T6-2428.t: Almost always used with 느끼다: 격세지감을 느끼다.

T6-2429.m: an ineffective effort that misses the real problem
T6-2429.ex: 근본 원인을 놔두고 대책을 세우는 건 격화소양일 뿐이에요.
T6-2429.x: Making plans while ignoring the root cause is like scratching an itch through your boot.
T6-2429.e: Literally 'scratching an itch through your boot'.

T6-2430.x: Though I lack much, I will devote my humble efforts to the country.
T6-2430.e: Literally 'the labor of a dog or horse': a modest way to pledge loyalty.
T6-2430.t: A humble expression used about one's own efforts, never about someone else's.

T6-2431.m: a woman of breathtaking beauty, a femme fatale
T6-2431.ex: 그녀는 옛 소설에 나오는 경국지색 같은 미인이었어요.
T6-2431.x: She was a beauty like the country-toppling women of old novels.
T6-2431.e: Literally 'beauty that topples a country', as a king neglects his rule.

T6-2432.m: better to be the head of a chicken than the tail of an ox
T6-2432.ex: 대기업 말단보다 작은 회사 사장이 낫다는 게 계구우후죠.
T6-2432.x: Better to run a small company than be at the bottom of a big one.
T6-2432.e: Literally 'a chicken's mouth rather than an ox's rear'.

T6-2433.m: a stopgap measure, a temporary fix
T6-2433.ex: 그 정책은 문제를 덮는 고식지계에 불과합니다.
T6-2433.x: That policy is nothing more than a stopgap that covers up the problem.
T6-2433.e: Literally 'a plan just to rest for now'.
T6-2433.t: Often followed by 에 불과하다 'is nothing more than'.

T6-2434.m: it takes two; you can't do it alone
T6-2434.ex: 고장난명이라고, 혼자서는 이 일을 해낼 수 없어요.
T6-2434.x: As they say, one hand can't clap; I can't do this alone.
T6-2434.e: Literally 'a single palm can hardly make a sound'.
T6-2434.t: Pronounced [고장난명]; the native saying 손뼉도 마주쳐야 소리가 난다 means the same.

T6-2435.ex: 두 할아버지는 평생 관포지교를 나눈 사이입니다.
T6-2435.x: The two grandfathers shared a lifelong friendship.
T6-2435.e: Named after Guan Zhong and Bao Shuya, ancient Chinese friends who trusted each other completely.

T6-2436.m: honeyed words hiding a dagger, two-faced
T6-2436.x: He smiles on the outside, but he hides a knife behind sweet words.
T6-2436.e: Literally 'honey in the mouth, a sword in the belly'.

T6-2437.m: rival powers each holding their own territory
T6-2437.x: The smartphone market was once an era of many rival powers.
T6-2437.e: Literally 'many heroes carving up and holding land'.
T6-2437.t: Often used for business or politics: 군웅할거의 시대 'an age of rival powers'.

T6-2438.ex: 그는 권모술수에 능한 정치인으로 알려져 있습니다.
T6-2438.x: He is known as a politician skilled in scheming.
T6-2438.e: Literally 'schemes of power and tricks of strategy'.

T6-2439.m: a golden rule, a sacred precept
T6-2439.x: I lived treating my father's words as golden rules.
T6-2439.e: Literally 'golden rules and jade articles': precious laws.

T6-2440.x: They built a precious friendship through hard times.
T6-2440.e: Friendship strong as gold and fragrant as orchids.
T6-2440.t: Pronounced [금난지교] — ㄹ becomes ㄴ after ㅁ.

T6-2441.m: a strong sense of how things have changed between then and now
T6-2441.ex: 고향에 다시 가 보니 금석지감을 금할 수 없었어요.
T6-2441.x: Returning to my hometown, I couldn't help feeling how much had changed.
T6-2441.e: Literally 'the feeling of now versus the past'.
T6-2441.t: Don't confuse 금 'now' here with 금 'gold' in 금석 'metal and stone'.

T6-2442.m: a situation you can't back out of once started
T6-2442.ex: 일을 이미 시작했으니 기호지세로 끝까지 가야 합니다.
T6-2442.x: We've already started, so like riding a tiger, we must see it through.
T6-2442.e: Literally 'the situation of riding a tiger': getting off means being eaten.

T6-2443.m: fallen flowers and flowing water; the fading of spring, passing time
T6-2443.x: Like fallen petals on flowing water, youth passes quickly.
T6-2443.e: Literally 'falling flowers, flowing water', an image of late spring and decline.

T6-2444.m: neck and neck, hard to tell which is better
T6-2444.ex: 두 선수의 실력은 난형난제라 우승을 예측하기 어려워요.
T6-2444.x: The two players are so evenly matched that the winner is hard to predict.
T6-2444.e: Literally 'hard to call one the elder, hard to call one the younger'.
T6-2444.t: Close in meaning to 막상막하, which is more common in everyday speech.

T6-2445.x: Wealth and glory are, in the end, nothing but a fleeting dream.
T6-2445.e: A man dreamed of a lifetime of glory, then woke under the south branch of a tree.

T6-2446.x: Like an awl in a bag, he quickly revealed his talent.
T6-2446.e: Literally 'an awl in a bag': its point always pokes through.

T6-2447.ex: 노마지지라고, 선배들의 경험을 무시하면 안 돼요.
T6-2447.x: Experience is wisdom, so don't ignore your seniors' know-how.
T6-2447.e: An army lost its way and followed an old horse home: experience guides.
