T6-2448.m: a precarious situation, on the brink of collapse
T6-2448.ex: 당시 나라는 누란지세의 위기에 처해 있었습니다.
T6-2448.x: At the time, the country faced a crisis as precarious as stacked eggs.
T6-2448.e: Literally 'the state of stacked eggs': ready to topple any moment.
T6-2448.t: Often in 누란지세에 처하다 'to be in a precarious situation'.

T6-2449.m: versatile, able to handle anything big or small
T6-2449.ex: 그는 능소능대해서 어떤 일을 맡겨도 잘해요.
T6-2449.x: He is so versatile that he does well at whatever you give him.
T6-2449.e: Literally 'able in small things, able in big things'.
T6-2449.t: Can work as a 하다 adjective: 능소능대하다.

T6-2450.m: losing the truth among too many paths; getting lost in too many options
T6-2450.ex: 전공을 너무 많이 바꾸다 보니 다기망양이 되고 말았어요.
T6-2450.x: Switching majors so often, I ended up lost among too many paths.
T6-2450.e: A lost sheep couldn't be found because the road kept forking.

T6-2451.m: siding with your own faction and attacking others
T6-2451.ex: 정치권의 당동벌이 때문에 국민들이 실망하고 있습니다.
T6-2451.x: People are disappointed by politicians backing their own side and attacking the rest.
T6-2451.e: Literally 'band with the same, attack the different'.
T6-2451.t: Pronounced [당동버리] — the ㄹ carries over to the next syllable.

T6-2452.x: Mother turned pale with shock when she heard about the accident.

T6-2453.ex: 세 친구는 도원결의를 하듯 함께 창업하기로 약속했어요.
T6-2453.x: The three friends vowed, like sworn brothers, to start a business together.
T6-2453.e: From Three Kingdoms: Liu Bei, Guan Yu and Zhang Fei swore brotherhood in a peach garden.

T6-2454.ex: 인터넷에 떠도는 도청도설을 그대로 믿으면 안 됩니다.
T6-2454.x: You shouldn't believe the hearsay floating around online.
T6-2454.e: Literally 'heard on the road, repeated on the road'.
T6-2454.t: Don't confuse with 도청 'wiretapping', which is written with different characters.

T6-2455.m: if the price is the same, pick the nicer one
T6-2455.ex: 동가홍상이라고, 가격이 같으면 디자인이 예쁜 걸 사세요.
T6-2455.x: If the price is the same, buy the one with the nicer design.
T6-2455.e: Literally 'same price, red skirt': at equal cost, choose the prettier.

T6-2456.m: every great journey starts with small steps
T6-2456.x: As the saying goes, climb from the bottom: study the basics step by step.
T6-2456.e: Literally 'to climb high, start from low ground'.
T6-2456.t: Also used to mean the higher your position, the humbler you should be.

T6-2457.m: perseverance; grinding an axe into a needle
T6-2457.ex: 마부작침의 자세로 꾸준히 연습하면 꼭 성공할 거예요.
T6-2457.x: If you practice steadily with an axe-to-needle attitude, you'll succeed.
T6-2457.e: Literally 'grind an axe to make a needle': patience achieves the impossible.

T6-2458.m: a bosom friend, a very close friend
T6-2458.ex: 그와 나는 어릴 때부터 막역지우로 지내 왔어요.
T6-2458.x: He and I have been bosom friends since childhood.
T6-2458.e: Literally 'a friend with no friction between you'.
T6-2458.t: Pronounced [마격찌우]; 막역한 사이 'close relationship' is common too.

T6-2459.ex: 정직이 최고의 미덕이라는 것은 만고불변의 진리입니다.
T6-2459.x: That honesty is the greatest virtue is an eternal truth.
T6-2459.t: Almost always in 만고불변의 진리 'an eternal truth'.

T6-2460.x: I hope everything you do goes smoothly in the new year.
T6-2460.e: Literally 'ten thousand matters all flowing through'.
T6-2460.t: A favorite New Year's greeting phrase: 만사형통하세요.

T6-2461.m: fixing things after it's too late
T6-2461.ex: 사고가 난 뒤에 안전 점검을 하는 것은 망양보뢰입니다.
T6-2461.x: Doing safety checks after an accident is mending the pen after the sheep are gone.
T6-2461.e: Literally 'mend the pen after losing the sheep'; in Korean it stresses lateness.
T6-2461.t: The native proverb 소 잃고 외양간 고친다 means the same and is more common.

T6-2462.ex: 타국에서 일하는 그는 늘 망운지정에 잠기곤 했어요.
T6-2462.x: Working abroad, he was often lost in longing for his parents.
T6-2462.e: Literally 'the feeling of gazing at clouds' toward where one's parents live.

T6-2463.x: Scholars of the fallen kingdom left their grief for the lost country in poems.
T6-2463.e: A prince saw barley growing on the ruins of his old capital and wept.

T6-2464.x: Meditation makes your mind clear as a bright mirror and still water.
T6-2464.e: Literally 'bright mirror, still water': a mind without distractions.

T6-2465.x: With this much evidence, the outcome is crystal clear.
T6-2465.e: Literally 'as clear as looking at fire'.
T6-2465.t: Usually as 명약관화하다 or 명약관화한 사실 'an obvious fact'.

T6-2466.m: completely illiterate, unable to read even the simplest letter
T6-2466.ex: 그 시절에는 목불식정인 사람이 적지 않았어요.
T6-2466.x: In those days, quite a few people couldn't read a single letter.
T6-2466.e: Unable to recognize even the simplest character, one with just two strokes.
T6-2466.t: The native saying 낫 놓고 기역 자도 모른다 has the same meaning.

T6-2467.ex: 그 섬은 마치 무릉도원처럼 평화롭고 아름다웠어요.
T6-2467.x: The island was as peaceful and beautiful as an earthly paradise.
T6-2467.e: From a Chinese tale of a fisherman who found a hidden village beyond a peach-blossom stream.

T6-2468.m: a friendship so deep you'd die for each other
T6-2468.ex: 두 장군은 문경지교를 맺은 사이로 유명합니다.
T6-2468.x: The two generals are famous for a friendship they'd die for.
T6-2468.e: Literally 'a neck-cutting friendship': friends willing to lose their heads for each other.

T6-2469.m: oneness of self and the world
T6-2469.ex: 산속에서 자연과 하나 되는 물아일체를 경험했어요.
T6-2469.x: In the mountains, I experienced being one with nature.
T6-2469.e: Literally 'things and self as one body'.
T6-2469.t: Pronounced [무라일체] — the ㄹ links to the next vowel.

T6-2470.m: filial devotion; repaying one's parents' care
T6-2470.ex: 부모님을 모시고 사는 그의 반포지효에 감동했어요.
T6-2470.x: I was moved by his devotion in caring for his parents.
T6-2470.e: Young crows are said to feed their aging parents in return.

T6-2471.m: acting as if no one else exists, arrogant and inconsiderate
T6-2471.x: You shouldn't act as if nobody else is around in public places.
T6-2471.e: Literally 'as if no one were beside you'.

T6-2472.m: a pale-faced bookworm with no real-world experience
T6-2472.ex: 백면서생이라 사회 경험이 부족하다는 말을 들었어요.
T6-2472.x: I was told I lack real-world experience, being just a bookworm.
T6-2472.e: Literally 'white-faced student' who stays indoors reading.

T6-2473.ex: 회사는 부도 직전의 백척간두에 서 있었습니다.
T6-2473.x: The company stood on the edge of bankruptcy.
T6-2473.e: Literally 'the top of a hundred-foot pole'.
T6-2473.t: Common as 백척간두에 서다 'to stand on the brink'.

T6-2474.m: husband and wife in perfect harmony
T6-2474.ex: 두 분은 부창부수로 식당을 함께 운영하세요.
T6-2474.x: The couple runs their restaurant together in perfect harmony.
T6-2474.e: Literally 'husband sings, wife follows'; now used for any harmonious couple.

T6-2475.x: The pyramids are one of the Seven Wonders of the World.
T6-2475.e: Literally 'cannot be thought of or discussed'; originally a Buddhist term.

T6-2476.m: going a long way gladly, not minding the distance
T6-2476.x: He came all the way to his friend's wedding, not minding the distance.
T6-2476.e: Literally 'not considering a thousand li far'.

T6-2477.x: Filled with grief and outrage, independence activists sought to regain the country.
T6-2477.e: Literally 'sorrow and anger, indignation and lament' over injustice.

T6-2478.m: a relationship like fire and ice, total incompatibility
T6-2478.ex: 두 사람은 빙탄지간이라 같은 팀에 둘 수 없어요.
T6-2478.x: The two are like ice and fire, so we can't put them on the same team.
T6-2478.e: Literally 'the relation between ice and burning charcoal'.

T6-2479.m: split into many factions, torn apart
T6-2479.x: In the end, the party was torn apart by internal conflict.
T6-2479.e: Literally 'divided in four, split in five'.

T6-2480.m: a life-or-death resolve, fighting to the end
T6-2480.x: He prepared for the exam with life-or-death determination.

T6-2481.m: a lie repeated enough becomes accepted as truth
T6-2481.ex: 삼인성호라고, 거짓 소문도 계속 퍼지면 사실처럼 믿게 돼요.
T6-2481.x: As they say, if three people say there's a tiger, a rumor starts to seem true.
T6-2481.e: If three people claim there's a tiger in the market, people believe it.

T6-2482.m: life and death, joys and sorrows shared
T6-2482.x: The comrades shared life and death on the battlefield for a long time.

T6-2483.m: putting public interest before private interest
T6-2483.x: Public officials should put the public interest before their own.

T6-2484.ex: 회의에서 새 정책을 두고 설왕설래가 오갔습니다.
T6-2484.x: There was a lot of back-and-forth over the new policy at the meeting.

T6-2485.x: The older I get, the more I long for my hometown.
T6-2485.e: A dying fox turns its head toward the hill where its den was.

T6-2486.m: always reading, never putting a book down
T6-2486.x: My grandfather never put down his books his whole life.
T6-2486.e: Literally 'the hand never releases the scroll'.

T6-2487.m: pure and innocent, without a trace of guile
T6-2487.x: The child's pure, innocent smile warmed my heart.
T6-2487.t: Most often as an adjective: 순진무구하다, 순진무구한 눈빛.

T6-2488.m: knowledge brings worry; ignorance is bliss
T6-2488.ex: 식자우환이라더니 너무 많이 알아서 오히려 걱정이 많아요.
T6-2488.x: Knowledge is a burden, they say; knowing too much just makes me worry more.
T6-2488.e: Literally 'knowing letters brings worry and trouble'.

T6-2489.m: appearing and vanishing like a ghost, elusive
T6-2489.ex: 그 도둑은 신출귀몰해서 경찰도 잡지 못했어요.
T6-2489.x: The thief came and went like a ghost, so even the police couldn't catch him.
T6-2489.e: Literally 'appearing like a spirit, vanishing like a ghost'.
T6-2489.t: Often 신출귀몰하다; the folk hero 홍길동 is the classic example.

T6-2490.x: Everyone in the meeting room went pale and speechless at the unexpected news.
T6-2490.e: Literally 'struck dumb and losing one's color'.

T6-2491.m: false advertising, a fine front hiding something worse
T6-2491.ex: 광고와 실제 제품이 너무 달라서 양두구육이라는 비판을 받았어요.
T6-2491.x: The product was so unlike its ad that it was criticized as false advertising.
T6-2491.e: Literally 'hang a sheep's head, sell dog meat'.

T6-2492.x: They say a burglar paid our neighborhood a visit last night.
T6-2492.e: Literally 'the gentleman on the roof beam', a magistrate's ironic name for a thief.
T6-2492.t: Humorous and indirect; in plain speech just say 도둑.

T6-2493.m: utter illiteracy, unable to tell similar letters apart
T6-2493.ex: 어로불변이던 그가 지금은 책을 쓰는 작가가 되었어요.
T6-2493.x: He once couldn't tell one letter from another, but now he's an author.
T6-2493.e: Unable to tell apart two similar-looking characters, 'fish' and 'Lu'.

T6-2494.m: wouldn't dare even dream of it
T6-2494.ex: 집을 산다는 건 언감생심 꿈도 못 꿔요.
T6-2494.x: Buying a house? I wouldn't even dare to dream of it.
T6-2494.e: Literally 'how dare such a thought arise in my mind?'
T6-2494.t: Often used as an adverb-like phrase before 꿈도 못 꾸다.

T6-2495.m: the dead of winter, bitter winter cold
T6-2495.ex: 엄동설한에 난방도 없이 지내는 이웃들이 있습니다.
T6-2495.x: Some of our neighbors live through the dead of winter without heating.

T6-2496.m: enormous strength and spirit, mighty enough to move mountains
T6-2496.x: That general displayed might enough to uproot mountains.
T6-2496.e: From Xiang Yu's song: 'strength to uproot mountains, spirit to cover the world'.
T6-2496.t: Unlike most four-character idioms, this one has six syllables.

T6-2497.m: winning every battle, an unbroken winning streak
T6-2497.ex: 우리 팀은 이번 시즌에 연전연승을 거두고 있어요.
T6-2497.x: Our team has been winning game after game this season.
T6-2497.e: Literally 'fight after fight, win after win.'
T6-2497.t: Usually used with 거두다 or 하다: 연전연승을 거두다 'to win one victory after another.'

T6-2498.m: bitter enemies forced to cooperate, strange bedfellows
T6-2498.ex: 두 경쟁 회사가 위기 앞에서 오월동주하는 상황이 되었습니다.
T6-2498.x: The two rival companies ended up as uneasy allies in the face of the crisis.
T6-2498.e: Literally 'Wu and Yue in the same boat' — two warring ancient states sharing one boat in a storm.

T6-2499.m: good and bad perishing together, indiscriminate destruction
T6-2499.ex: 무리한 단속은 옥석구분의 결과를 낳을 수 있습니다.
T6-2499.x: Heavy-handed crackdowns can end up harming the innocent along with the guilty.
T6-2499.e: Literally 'jade and stone burn together' — fire doesn't care which is precious.
T6-2499.t: Often misused as if 구분 meant 'distinguish'; for sorting good from bad, say 옥석을 가리다 instead.
rel: jade and stone, the good and the bad

T6-2500.m: loving mountains and rivers, enjoying nature
T6-2500.x: My grandfather lives in the countryside, enjoying the mountains and streams.
T6-2500.e: From Confucius: the wise delight in water, the virtuous delight in mountains.
T6-2500.t: Here the syllable 요 means 'to enjoy' — the same character is read 락 or 악 elsewhere, a classic reading trap.

T6-2501.m: haste makes waste, more haste, less speed
T6-2501.x: Haste makes waste, as they say, so let's do it slowly and carefully.
T6-2501.t: Often followed by 이라고 하다 to quote it like a proverb, similar to 급할수록 돌아가라.

T6-2502.m: a fierce clash between two equally strong rivals
T6-2502.x: The final was a titanic clash between two powerhouse teams.
T6-2502.e: Literally 'dragon and tiger strike each other.'
T6-2502.t: Common in sports news as 용호상박의 대결 or 용호상박을 벌이다.

T6-2503.m: warding off misfortune and inviting good fortune
T6-2503.ex: 설날에 부적을 붙이는 것은 원화소복을 바라는 풍습이에요.
T6-2503.x: Hanging talismans at New Year is a custom of wishing to ward off bad luck and bring good luck.
T6-2503.e: Literally 'keep disaster far, call fortune near.'

T6-2504.m: living a carefree, leisurely life at one's own pace
T6-2504.ex: 은퇴 후 그는 바닷가에서 유유자적하며 살고 있어요.
T6-2504.x: Since retiring, he has been living a leisurely life by the sea.
T6-2504.e: Literally 'easygoing and doing what suits oneself.'
T6-2504.t: Works as a verb with 하다: 유유자적하다 'to live a carefree life.'

T6-2505.m: sacrificing someone dear for the sake of discipline or principle
T6-2505.ex: 감독은 읍참마속의 심정으로 주장을 경기에서 제외했습니다.
T6-2505.x: With a heavy heart, the coach dropped the captain from the game for the sake of discipline.
T6-2505.e: From Three Kingdoms: Zhuge Liang tearfully executed his favorite general Ma Su for disobeying orders.
T6-2505.t: Typically appears as 읍참마속의 심정으로 'with the heart of one who must punish a loved one.'

T6-2506.m: a hopeless fight against overwhelming odds
T6-2506.x: Fighting a big corporation alone is like throwing eggs at a rock.
T6-2506.e: Literally 'striking a rock with an egg.'
T6-2506.t: The everyday native equivalent is 계란으로 바위 치기.

T6-2507.m: constantly splitting and regrouping, shifting alliances
T6-2507.ex: 선거철이 되면 정당들의 이합집산이 또다시 반복됩니다.
T6-2507.x: Every election season, political parties split up and regroup again.
T6-2507.t: Mostly used about politicians and parties, often with a critical tone.

T6-2508.m: a moment feeling like years, waiting impatiently
T6-2508.ex: 합격 발표를 기다리는 하루가 일각여삼추 같았어요.
T6-2508.x: Waiting a day for the exam results felt like an eternity.
T6-2508.e: Literally 'one moment is like three autumns' — i.e. three years.
T6-2508.t: Usually followed by 같다: 일각여삼추 같다 'every minute feels like years.'

T6-2509.m: settling something decisively in one stroke
T6-2509.ex: 그 문제는 일도양단으로 해결할 수 있는 일이 아니에요.
T6-2509.x: That problem isn't something you can settle with a single decisive stroke.

T6-2510.m: clear at a glance, neatly organized
T6-2510.ex: 이 표는 자료가 일목요연하게 정리되어 있어요.
T6-2510.x: This table organizes the data so it's clear at a glance.
T6-2510.t: Pronounced [일모교연]; most often used as 일목요연하게 정리하다.

T6-2511.m: a tiny lone boat, a small boat adrift
T6-2511.ex: 넓은 바다 위에 일엽편주 하나가 떠 있었어요.
T6-2511.x: A single little boat was floating on the wide sea.
T6-2511.e: Literally 'a boat like one leaf' — a small, fragile craft.
T6-2511.t: Also used figuratively for a person or country tossed about helplessly.

T6-2512.m: a fleeting dream, the vanity of life and glory
T6-2512.ex: 그 화려했던 시절도 이제는 일장춘몽이 되었어요.
T6-2512.x: Those glamorous days have now become nothing but a passing dream.
T6-2512.e: Literally 'one spring night's dream' — pleasant but over quickly.

T6-2513.x: I study every day with an attitude of never ceasing to improve myself.
T6-2513.e: From the Book of Changes: strengthen yourself and never stop.

T6-2514.m: ordinary people, any Tom, Dick, or Harry
T6-2514.ex: 그런 일은 장삼이사 누구나 할 수 있어요.
T6-2514.x: Any ordinary person could do something like that.
T6-2514.e: Literally 'Zhang's third son and Lee's fourth son' — just anybody.

T6-2515.ex: 그는 적수공권으로 서울에 올라와 회사를 세웠어요.
T6-2515.x: He came to Seoul with nothing and built a company.
T6-2515.t: Commonly appears as 적수공권으로 'with nothing to one's name.'

T6-2516.ex: 그녀는 학계에서 주목받는 전도유망한 젊은 과학자입니다.
T6-2516.x: She is a promising young scientist drawing attention in academia.
T6-2516.t: Usually used as an adjective: 전도유망한 + person, e.g. 전도유망한 선수.

T6-2517.m: untrodden, never achieved by anyone before
T6-2517.x: The athlete set a record no one had ever reached before.
T6-2517.e: Literally 'ground no earlier person has stepped on.'
T6-2517.t: Typically 전인미답의 + noun: 전인미답의 경지, 전인미답의 기록.

T6-2518.m: diligent self-cultivation, constantly honing one's skills
T6-2518.ex: 그는 오랜 절차탁마 끝에 명인이 되었습니다.
T6-2518.x: After years of relentless practice, he became a master.
T6-2518.e: Literally 'cutting, filing, carving, grinding' — how jade and bone were worked.

T6-2519.m: a frog in a well, a person with a narrow view
T6-2519.ex: 해외 경험이 없으면 정저지와가 되기 쉬워요.
T6-2519.x: Without overseas experience, it's easy to become a frog in a well.
T6-2519.e: Literally 'frog at the bottom of a well,' who thinks the sky is a small circle.
T6-2519.t: In everyday speech Koreans say 우물 안 개구리 instead.

T6-2520.m: a wife who has shared hardship since poorer days
T6-2520.ex: 성공한 뒤에도 그는 조강지처를 소중히 여겼어요.
T6-2520.x: Even after becoming successful, he cherished the wife who had stood by him through hard times.
T6-2520.e: Literally 'wife of grain dregs and husks' — she ate poor food with you.
T6-2520.t: Often used in stories about men who abandon such a wife after success.

T6-2521.ex: 왕은 주지육림에 빠져 나라를 돌보지 않았습니다.
T6-2521.x: The king indulged in lavish feasts and neglected his country.
T6-2521.e: Literally 'a pond of wine and a forest of meat.'
T6-2521.t: Pronounced [주지융님]: ㄹ becomes ㄴ after ㄱ, and then ㄱ nasalizes to ㅇ.

T6-2522.m: being outnumbered, the few can't beat the many
T6-2522.ex: 우리는 끝까지 싸웠지만 중과부적이라 결국 졌어요.
T6-2522.x: We fought to the end, but we were outnumbered and lost.
T6-2522.e: Literally 'the few cannot match the many.'

T6-2523.x: His explanation was so incoherent that it was hard to understand.
T6-2523.t: Pronounced [지리멸렬] with a double ㄹ sound; used with 하다 or 되다.

T6-2524.m: a true friend who understands you completely, a soulmate friend
T6-2524.ex: 그는 나를 진정으로 이해해 주는 지음이에요.
T6-2524.x: He is a true friend who really understands me.
T6-2524.e: Literally 'one who knows the sound' — a friend who alone understood a musician's playing.
T6-2524.t: Literary and rare in speech; 지음 also means 'making' from 짓다, so context matters.

T6-2525.ex: 요즘 드라마는 내용이 너무 천편일률적이라 재미가 없어요.
T6-2525.x: Dramas these days are so formulaic that they're boring.
T6-2525.e: Literally 'a thousand poems in one pattern.'
T6-2525.t: Pronounced [천펴닐률]; very often used as 천편일률적 'stereotyped.'

T6-2526.m: flawless and natural, without any trace of artifice
T6-2526.x: His writing is praised as flawless and completely natural.

T6-2527.x: That civil servant is known for being completely incorruptible.
T6-2527.t: Pronounced [청념결백]; typically describes officials and politicians.

T6-2528.m: speaking fluently and eloquently, a smooth talker
T6-2528.ex: 그는 처음 보는 사람 앞에서도 말을 청산유수처럼 잘해요.
T6-2528.x: Even in front of strangers, he talks as smoothly as a flowing stream.
T6-2528.e: Literally 'water flowing past green mountains' — speech that never snags.
T6-2528.t: Usually 말이 청산유수다 or 청산유수처럼; can hint at a glib talker.

T6-2529.m: birds of a feather, like sticks with like
T6-2529.x: Birds of a feather — the two of them became friends right away.
T6-2529.e: Literally 'grass and green are the same color.'
T6-2529.t: Often quoted as the saying 초록은 동색.
rel: people side with their own kind

T6-2530.m: falling like leaves in autumn wind, collapsing in large numbers
T6-2530.ex: 강한 상대 앞에서 선수들이 추풍낙엽처럼 쓰러졌어요.
T6-2530.x: Against a strong opponent, the players went down one after another like falling leaves.
T6-2530.e: Literally 'leaves falling in the autumn wind.'
T6-2530.t: Almost always used as 추풍낙엽처럼 with verbs like 쓰러지다 or 떨어지다.

T6-2531.m: a chaotic period of many competing rivals
T6-2531.x: The smartphone market is truly an era of fierce competition among many players.
T6-2531.e: From China's Spring and Autumn and Warring States periods of constant rivalry.
T6-2531.t: Usually used as 춘추전국 시대 about crowded markets or politics.

T6-2532.m: cutting through a mess decisively, solving a tangled problem swiftly
T6-2532.ex: 새 사장은 회사 문제를 쾌도난마로 해결했어요.
T6-2532.x: The new president cut through the company's problems decisively.
T6-2532.e: Literally 'a sharp knife through tangled hemp.'

T6-2533.m: tipping off the enemy by acting carelessly
T6-2533.ex: 섣불리 조사를 시작하면 타초경사가 될 수 있어요.
T6-2533.x: Starting the investigation too hastily could tip them off.
T6-2533.e: Literally 'beat the grass and startle the snake.'

T6-2534.m: a leading authority, a towering figure in a field
T6-2534.x: He was revered as the towering authority in Korean linguistics.
T6-2534.e: Literally 'Mount Tai and the Big Dipper' — things everyone looks up to.
T6-2534.t: Pronounced [태산북뚜]; a highly respectful, formal expression.

T6-2535.ex: 지도자가 떠나자 그 조직은 순식간에 토붕와해되었습니다.
T6-2535.x: Once the leader left, the organization completely fell apart.
T6-2535.e: Literally 'earth crumbles and roof tiles shatter.'
T6-2535.t: Usually takes 되다: 토붕와해되다 'to collapse completely.'

T6-2536.ex: 할머니는 어린 손자의 엉뚱한 말에 파안대소하셨어요.
T6-2536.x: Grandma burst out laughing at her little grandson's silly remark.
T6-2536.e: Literally 'face breaking open in a big laugh.'

T6-2537.m: stirring up trouble out of nowhere
T6-2537.x: Don't stir up trouble with unnecessary remarks.
T6-2537.e: Literally 'wind and waves on flat ground' — trouble where all was calm.
T6-2537.t: Collocates with 일으키다: 평지풍파를 일으키다 'to make waves for no reason.'

T6-2538.m: laughing so hard one doubles over
T6-2538.ex: 그 코미디 영화는 관객들을 포복절도하게 만들었어요.
T6-2538.x: That comedy had the audience doubled over with laughter.
T6-2538.e: Literally 'clutching one's belly and falling over.'
T6-2538.t: Pronounced [포복쩔또]; don't confuse 포복 'clutching the belly' here with 포복 'crawling.'

T6-2539.m: regret at being unable to care for parents who have died
T6-2539.x: Only after my parents passed away did I feel the regret of not caring for them enough.
T6-2539.e: The tree wants stillness but the wind won't stop; the child wants to serve, but parents are gone.

T6-2540.m: ordinary men and women, common folk
T6-2540.ex: 역사를 움직이는 것은 결국 필부필부의 힘입니다.
T6-2540.x: In the end, it is the strength of ordinary people that moves history.
T6-2540.e: Literally 'an ordinary husband and an ordinary wife.'

T6-2541.m: someone who never comes back or replies, no news at all
T6-2541.ex: 한 시간 전에 심부름 간 동생이 아직도 함흥차사예요.
T6-2541.x: My brother went on an errand an hour ago and still hasn't come back.
T6-2541.e: From the Joseon story of royal envoys sent to Hamheung who never returned.
T6-2541.t: Common and humorous in everyday speech for someone who's taking forever.

T6-2542.m: a battle of wits with feints and real attacks, mind games
T6-2542.x: The two coaches faced off with strategies full of feints and real moves.
T6-2542.e: Literally 'empty and solid' — hitting weak spots while hiding your own.

T6-2543.m: a wise mother and good wife (traditional ideal)
T6-2543.x: In the past, being a wise mother and good wife was considered the ideal for women.
T6-2543.e: Literally 'wise mother, good wife' — a traditional ideal now often criticized.
T6-2543.t: Today it can sound old-fashioned or sexist, so use it carefully.

T6-2544.m: all alone in the world, without any family
T6-2544.ex: 그는 혈혈단신으로 고향을 떠나 서울에 왔어요.
T6-2544.x: He left his hometown and came to Seoul all on his own.
T6-2544.t: Usually appears as 혈혈단신으로 'all alone, with no one to rely on.'

T6-2545.m: a way to make a bare living, means of subsistence
T6-2545.ex: 젊은 시절 그는 호구지책으로 공사장에서 막노동을 했어요.
T6-2545.x: When he was young, he did construction labor just to make ends meet.
T6-2545.e: Literally 'a plan to paste the mouth' — just enough to keep from starving.
T6-2545.t: Don't confuse it with 호구 'pushover' — a different, unrelated slang word.

T6-2546.m: good things come with many obstacles
T6-2546.x: They say good things come with hitches — it rained on our wedding day.
T6-2546.t: Often quoted as 호사다마라고 or 호사다마라더니 when trouble interrupts something happy.

T6-2547.ex: 그 사이비 종교는 혹세무민으로 많은 사람을 속였습니다.
T6-2547.x: That cult deceived many people by misleading the public.
T6-2547.e: Literally 'deluding the world and deceiving the people.'

T6-2548.m: getting along with others without blindly conforming
T6-2548.ex: 좋은 동료 관계는 화이부동의 자세에서 시작됩니다.
T6-2548.x: Good relationships with colleagues start with being harmonious without simply conforming.
T6-2548.e: From Confucius: a gentleman is in harmony with others but not identical to them.

T6-2549.m: pie in the sky, something you can't actually have
T6-2549.ex: 돈이 없으면 그 계획은 화중지병일 뿐이에요.
T6-2549.x: Without money, that plan is just pie in the sky.
T6-2549.e: Literally 'a rice cake in a painting.'
T6-2549.t: Everyday Korean says 그림의 떡 instead.
rel: a rice cake in a picture

T6-2550.m: the younger generation deserves respect, juniors may surpass their elders
T6-2550.x: They say juniors may surpass us — the new employee's skills are amazing.
T6-2550.e: From Confucius: those born after us deserve awe, for they may surpass us.

T6-2551.ex: 법원은 공사 중지 가처분 신청을 받아들였습니다.
T6-2551.x: The court granted the application for an injunction to halt construction.
T6-2551.e: Literally 'temporary disposition' — a court freezes things until the main ruling.
T6-2551.t: Common in news as 가처분 신청 'filing for an injunction' and 가처분 인용 'granting it.'

T6-2552.ex: 판결에는 가집행을 할 수 있다는 내용이 포함되었습니다.
T6-2552.x: The judgment stated that it could be provisionally enforced.
T6-2552.e: Literally 'temporary execution' — enforcing a ruling before it becomes final.
T6-2552.t: Pronounced [가지팽] — ㅂ and ㅎ merge into ㅍ.

T6-2553.m: deposit with the court, legal deposit
T6-2553.ex: 피고인은 피해자를 위해 법원에 손해배상금을 공탁했습니다.
T6-2553.x: The defendant deposited damages with the court for the victim.
T6-2553.e: Literally 'offer and entrust' — you hand money to the court when the other side won't accept it.
T6-2553.t: Used with 하다; in criminal cases 공탁 often aims to show remorse for a lighter sentence.

T6-2554.m: right of reimbursement, right of recourse
T6-2554.ex: 보험사는 사고를 낸 운전자에게 구상권을 행사했습니다.
T6-2554.x: The insurer exercised its right of recourse against the driver who caused the accident.
T6-2554.e: Literally 'right to seek compensation' from whoever was really responsible.
T6-2554.t: Pronounced [구상꿘]; nearly always paired with 행사하다 or 청구하다.

T6-2555.ex: 집을 사기 전에 등기부를 꼭 확인하세요.
T6-2555.x: Be sure to check the property registry before buying a house.
T6-2555.t: In full, 등기부 등본 is the certified copy people check before renting or buying.

T6-2556.m: right to counsel, right of defense
T6-2556.ex: 모든 피고인의 변호권은 헌법에 의해 보장됩니다.
T6-2556.x: A defendant's right to counsel is guaranteed by the constitution.

T6-2557.ex: 비자가 만료된 후에도 머물면 불법체류가 됩니다.
T6-2557.x: If you stay after your visa expires, it becomes an illegal stay.
T6-2557.e: Literally 'staying in a place against the law.'
T6-2557.t: A person in this status is called 불법체류자.

T6-2558.ex: 채권자는 그 증여가 사해행위라며 소송을 냈습니다.
T6-2558.x: The creditor sued, claiming the gift was a fraudulent transfer.
T6-2558.e: Literally 'an act that deceives and harms' — hiding assets from creditors.
T6-2558.t: Usually appears in 사해행위 취소 소송, a suit to undo such transfers.

T6-2559.x: The statute of limitations on that claim has already run out.
T6-2559.e: Literally 'time limit after which a right disappears.'
T6-2559.t: Collocates with 지나다 or 완성되다: 소멸시효가 완성되다 'the limitation period expires.'

T6-2560.m: good faith, the principle of good faith and fair dealing
T6-2560.ex: 계약 당사자는 신의성실의 원칙에 따라 행동해야 합니다.
T6-2560.x: Parties to a contract must act according to the principle of good faith.
T6-2560.t: Often shortened to 신의칙 in legal writing.

T6-2561.ex: 법원은 그 조항에 대해 헌법재판소에 위헌법률심판을 제청했습니다.
T6-2561.x: The court asked the Constitutional Court to review that provision's constitutionality.
T6-2561.e: Literally 'judging whether a law violates the constitution.'

T6-2562.m: exclusion period, statutory time limit for a right
T6-2562.ex: 이 권리는 제척기간이 지나면 행사할 수 없습니다.
T6-2562.x: This right cannot be exercised once the exclusion period has passed.
T6-2562.e: Literally 'period after which a right is cut off'.
T6-2562.t: Pronounced [제척끼간]; differs from 소멸시효 because it can't be interrupted or extended.

T6-2563.ex: 그는 길에서 노상방뇨를 하다가 즉결심판에 넘겨졌습니다.
T6-2563.x: He was referred to summary trial for public urination.
T6-2563.e: Literally 'trial decided on the spot' for petty offenses.

T6-2564.m: assignment of claims, transfer of receivables
T6-2564.ex: 회사는 거래처에 채권양도 사실을 서면으로 통지했습니다.
T6-2564.x: The company notified its client in writing of the assignment of the claim.
T6-2564.e: Literally 'handing over the right to collect a debt.'

T6-2565.x: The victim has the right to claim damages.
T6-2565.t: Pronounced [청구꿘]; often preceded by the thing claimed, e.g. 손해배상 청구권.

T6-2566.m: criminal compensation for wrongful detention or conviction
T6-2566.ex: 무죄 판결을 받은 그는 형사보상을 청구했습니다.
T6-2566.x: After being acquitted, he claimed compensation for wrongful detention.
T6-2566.e: Literally 'compensation in criminal matters' — the state pays for wrongful imprisonment.

T6-2567.ex: 매도인은 계약에 따라 그 토지를 환매했습니다.
T6-2567.x: The seller bought back the land under the terms of the contract.
T6-2567.t: Used with 하다; in finance 환매 also means redeeming fund shares.

T6-2568.x: Booms and recessions repeat according to the business cycle.
T6-2568.e: Literally 'the economy going around in cycles.'

T6-2569.x: Chip prices fell sharply because of oversupply.
T6-2569.t: Pronounced [공급꽈잉]; the opposite is 공급 부족 'shortage.'

T6-2570.x: As low interest rates continued, the problem of excess liquidity grew.
T6-2570.e: Literally 'too much flowing money' in the economy.
T6-2570.t: Common in economic news alongside 자산 거품 'asset bubbles.'

T6-2571.x: When prices rise, consumers' purchasing power falls.
T6-2571.t: -력 means 'power, ability' and is very productive: 경쟁력, 생산력.

T6-2572.x: The U.S. effectively abandoned the gold standard in 1971.
T6-2572.e: Literally 'system with gold as the base unit of value.'

T6-2573.ex: 달러는 세계의 기축통화 역할을 하고 있습니다.
T6-2573.x: The dollar serves as the world's key currency.
T6-2573.e: Literally 'currency that is the base axis' of world trade.

T6-2574.x: The bank set aside reserves to prepare for bad debts.
T6-2574.e: Literally 'lending loss' — money lent that won't come back.
T6-2574.t: Mostly appears in accounting terms like 대손충당금 and 대손상각.

T6-2575.ex: 이 투자는 수익이 높지만 리스크도 큽니다.
T6-2575.x: This investment has high returns, but the risk is also big.
T6-2575.e: From English 'risk.' The final k gets an extra vowel: ri-seu-keu.

T6-2576.ex: 회사는 비용 절감을 명목으로 직원을 줄였습니다.
T6-2576.x: The company cut staff under the pretext of reducing costs.
T6-2576.e: Literally 'name and item': what something is called, not what it really is.
T6-2576.t: The pattern ~을/를 명목으로 means 'under the name or pretext of ~'.

T6-2577.ex: 금융 위기 이후 심각한 신용경색이 나타났습니다.
T6-2577.x: A severe credit crunch appeared after the financial crisis.
T6-2577.e: Literally 'credit blockage': money stops flowing like a blocked blood vessel.
T6-2577.t: Pronounced [시뇽경색]: the ㄴ links into 용.

T6-2578.ex: 그 회사는 유상증자로 천억 원을 마련했습니다.
T6-2578.x: The company raised 100 billion won through a rights offering.
T6-2578.e: Literally 'paid capital increase': shareholders pay money for the new shares.

T6-2579.x: The stock price rose sharply on news of a bonus issue.
T6-2579.e: Literally 'unpaid capital increase': shareholders get new shares for free.
T6-2579.t: 유상 (paid) and 무상 (free) are an everyday pair: 무상 교육 means free education.

T6-2580.ex: 계속된 적자로 회사가 자본잠식 상태에 빠졌습니다.
T6-2580.x: Continued losses put the company into a state of capital erosion.
T6-2580.e: Literally 'capital eaten by silkworms': losses nibble away the equity bit by bit.

T6-2581.ex: 정부는 재정건전성을 높이기 위해 지출을 줄였습니다.
T6-2581.x: The government cut spending to improve fiscal soundness.
T6-2581.t: -성 turns a noun into '-ness' or '-ity': 안전성 (safety), 가능성 (possibility).

T6-2582.x: Some companies hid money in tax havens.
T6-2582.e: Literally 'tax + refuge place': a shelter where money escapes taxes.

T6-2583.ex: 두 시장의 가격 차이를 이용한 차익거래가 늘었습니다.
T6-2583.x: Arbitrage using the price gap between the two markets increased.
T6-2583.e: Literally 'profit-from-difference trading'; 거래 is 'going and coming' of goods.
T6-2583.t: Pronounced [차익꺼래]: ㄱ after ㄱ becomes tense.

T6-2584.ex: 고혈당이 오래 계속되면 합병증이 생길 수 있어요.
T6-2584.x: If high blood sugar continues for a long time, complications can develop.
T6-2584.e: Literally 'high blood sugar', a word-for-word match with English.
T6-2584.t: Pronounced [고혈땅]: ㄷ after ㄹ in Sino-Korean words becomes tense.

T6-2585.x: The doctor collected cerebrospinal fluid for testing.

T6-2586.ex: 장기 이식 환자는 면역억제제를 꾸준히 먹어야 합니다.
T6-2586.x: Organ transplant patients must take immunosuppressants regularly.
T6-2586.e: Literally 'immunity + hold-down + drug'. Final -제 = medicine: 진통제, 소화제.
T6-2586.t: Pronounced [며녀걱쩨제]: sounds link across syllables and the ㅈ after ㄱ turns tense.

T6-2587.x: He kept working even from his sickbed.
T6-2587.t: Also counts hospital capacity: 병상이 부족하다 means there are not enough hospital beds.

T6-2588.ex: 정확한 사망 원인을 밝히기 위해 부검을 실시했습니다.
T6-2588.x: An autopsy was performed to determine the exact cause of death.

T6-2589.ex: 경찰은 아직 정확한 사인을 밝히지 못했습니다.
T6-2589.x: The police have not yet determined the exact cause of death.
T6-2589.t: Homonym warning: 사인 also means 'signature' (from English 'sign') and 'signal'; context tells you which.

T6-2590.x: Quick CPR is crucial for cardiac arrest patients.

T6-2591.ex: 육종은 뼈나 근육에 생기는 드문 암입니다.
T6-2591.x: Sarcoma is a rare cancer that develops in bone or muscle.
T6-2591.e: Literally 'flesh swelling': a tumor of the body's connective tissue.
T6-2591.t: Homonym: 육종 (育種) also means 'breeding' of plants or animals; pronounced [육쫑].

T6-2592.ex: CT 촬영 전에 조영제 주사를 맞았어요.
T6-2592.x: I got a contrast dye injection before the CT scan.
T6-2592.e: Literally 'image-making drug': it makes organs show up on scans.

T6-2593.ex: 우리 몸의 뇌와 척수는 중추신경에 속합니다.
T6-2593.x: The brain and spinal cord in our body belong to the central nervous system.

T6-2594.x: Diabetes can damage the peripheral nerves.
T6-2594.e: Literally 'branch-tip nerves': the nerves at the body's outer ends.
T6-2594.t: 말초적 means 'trivial' or 'sensational', as in 말초적인 재미 (cheap thrills).

T6-2595.ex: 아버지는 일주일에 세 번 투석을 받으세요.
T6-2595.x: My father gets dialysis three times a week.
T6-2595.e: Literally 'filter through and separate': waste is filtered out of the blood.
T6-2595.t: Homonym: 투석 (投石) means 'throwing stones', as in protests; use the 받다 pattern for dialysis.

T6-2596.ex: 상처 감염이 패혈증으로 이어질 수 있습니다.
T6-2596.x: A wound infection can lead to sepsis.
T6-2596.e: Literally 'spoiled-blood condition'. -증 = medical condition: 우울증, 불면증.
T6-2596.t: Pronounced [패혈쯩]: ㅈ after ㄹ in Sino-Korean words becomes tense.

T6-2597.ex: 혈소판 수치가 낮으면 피가 잘 멈추지 않아요.
T6-2597.x: If your platelet count is low, bleeding doesn't stop easily.
T6-2597.e: Literally 'blood small plates', just like English 'platelet'.

T6-2598.x: White blood cells protect the body from bacteria.
T6-2598.t: Pronounced [배켤구]: ㄱ + ㅎ merge into ㅋ.

T6-2599.ex: 적혈구는 폐에서 받은 산소를 온몸에 운반합니다.
T6-2599.x: Red blood cells carry oxygen from the lungs throughout the body.

T6-2600.x: The cerebrum is in charge of thinking and remembering.
T6-2600.e: Literally 'big brain': the largest part of the brain.

T6-2601.ex: 소뇌가 다치면 몸의 균형을 잡기 어렵습니다.
T6-2601.x: If the cerebellum is injured, it's hard to keep your balance.
T6-2601.e: Literally 'small brain', which is also what Latin 'cerebellum' means.

T6-2602.ex: 전두엽은 판단과 감정 조절에 중요한 역할을 합니다.
T6-2602.x: The frontal lobe plays an important role in judgment and emotional control.
T6-2602.e: Literally 'front head leaf'. -엽 = lobe: 측두엽, 후두엽.

T6-2603.ex: 측두엽은 소리를 듣고 이해하는 데 관여합니다.
T6-2603.x: The temporal lobe is involved in hearing and understanding sounds.
T6-2603.e: Literally 'side head lobe': it sits by the temples.
T6-2603.t: Pronounced [측뚜엽]: ㄷ after ㄱ becomes tense.

T6-2604.ex: 해마는 새로운 기억을 만드는 데 중요합니다.
T6-2604.x: The hippocampus is important for forming new memories.
T6-2604.e: Literally 'sea horse', named for its shape, just like Greek 'hippocampus'.
T6-2604.t: 해마 is also the everyday word for the seahorse fish; context makes the meaning clear.

T6-2605.x: The amygdala processes emotions such as fear.
T6-2605.e: Literally 'almond body'; 편도 means almond, as does Greek 'amygdala'.
T6-2605.t: Don't confuse it with 편도선 (tonsils) or 편도 (one-way ticket).

T6-2606.ex: 도파민과 세로토닌은 우리 뇌의 대표적인 신경전달물질입니다.
T6-2606.x: Dopamine and serotonin are typical neurotransmitters in our brain.
T6-2606.t: Pronounced [신경전달물찔]: ㅈ after ㄹ becomes tense.

T6-2607.x: Eating food you like releases dopamine.
T6-2607.e: From English 'dopamine.' Also slang: 도파민 중독 for craving quick thrills online.

T6-2608.ex: 햇빛을 쬐면 세로토닌 분비가 늘어난다고 해요.
T6-2608.x: They say getting sunlight increases serotonin secretion.

T6-9001.forms: 지렁이도 밟으면 꿈틀한다더니 · 지렁이도 밟으면 꿈틀한다고요
T6-9001.m: even the meekest person will fight back if pushed too far (lit. even an earthworm wriggles when stepped on)
T6-9001.ex: 지렁이도 밟으면 꿈틀한다고, 늘 참던 동생이 결국 화를 냈어요.
T6-9001.x: Even a worm will turn — my brother, who always put up with it, finally lost his temper.
T6-9001.e: Literally 'even an earthworm wriggles (꿈틀하다) when stepped on': the weakest creature still reacts.
T6-9001.t: Like English 'Even a worm will turn.' Used when a long-suffering person finally pushes back, or as a warning not to push someone too far. 밟으면 is pronounced [발브면].

T6-9002.de: 미꾸라지 한 마리가 온 웅덩이를 흐려 놓는다
T6-9002.rom: mikkuraji han mariga on ungdeongireul heuryeo nonneunda
T6-9002.pr: 미꾸라지 한 마리가 온 웅덩이를 흐려 논는다
T6-9002.forms: 미꾸라지 한 마리가 온 웅덩이를 흐려 놓는다더니 · 미꾸라지 한 마리가 온 웅덩이를 흐린다고
T6-9002.m: one bad apple spoils the bunch (lit. one loach muddies the whole pond)
T6-9002.ex: 미꾸라지 한 마리가 온 웅덩이를 흐려 놓는다더니, 한 사람 때문에 분위기가 엉망이에요.
T6-9002.x: One bad apple spoils the bunch: the whole mood is ruined because of one person.
T6-9002.e: A single loach wriggling in the mud at the bottom stirs it up and clouds the water of the entire pond.
T6-9002.t: Also shortened to 미꾸라지 한 마리가 온 웅덩이를 흐린다. The related idiom 물을 흐리다 means 'to spoil the atmosphere of a group.'

T6-9003.forms: 하룻강아지 범 무서운 줄 모른다더니 · 하룻강아지 범 무서운 줄 모르고
T6-9003.m: the inexperienced don't know what to fear; fools rush in (lit. a day-old puppy doesn't know to fear the tiger)
T6-9003.ex: 하룻강아지 범 무서운 줄 모른다더니, 신입 사원이 부장님한테 대들었어요.
T6-9003.x: Fools rush in, as they say: a new employee talked back to the department head.
T6-9003.e: 하룻강아지 is a newborn puppy (하루 'one day' + 강아지 'puppy'); it is too new to the world to know that a tiger (범) is dangerous.
T6-9003.t: Pronounced [하루깡아지]. Said of a newcomer who boldly takes on someone far stronger or more experienced, with a mix of disapproval and amusement. 범 is a native word for 호랑이.

T6-9004.de: 서당 개 삼 년이면 풍월을 읊는다
T6-9004.rom: seodang gae sam nyeonimyeon pungworeul eumneunda
T6-9004.pr: 서당 개 삼 녀니면 풍워를 음는다
T6-9004.forms: 서당 개 삼 년이면 풍월을 읊는다더니 · 서당 개 삼 년이면 풍월을 읊는다고
T6-9004.m: you pick things up just by being around them long enough (lit. after three years at a village school, even the dog recites poetry)
T6-9004.ex: 서당 개 삼 년이면 풍월을 읊는다고, 카페 3년 차라 커피 맛을 좀 알아요.
T6-9004.x: Even the school dog recites poetry after three years: I've worked at a café for three years, so I know a bit about coffee.
T6-9004.e: A dog living at a 서당 (traditional village school) hears the pupils every day for three years and ends up reciting poetry (풍월, literally 'wind and moon').
T6-9004.t: Pronounced [서당 개 삼 녀니면 풍워를 음는다]. Often said modestly about skills you picked up just by being around something, without formal training.

T6-9005.forms: 닭 쫓던 개 지붕 쳐다보듯 하다 · 닭 쫓던 개 지붕 쳐다보는 꼴이 되다
T6-9005.m: left staring helplessly after something one has lost (lit. like a dog looking up at the roof after chasing a chicken)
T6-9005.ex: 버스가 바로 앞에서 떠나서 닭 쫓던 개 지붕 쳐다보듯 서 있었어요.
T6-9005.x: The bus left right in front of me, and I just stood there staring after it helplessly.
T6-9005.e: A dog chases a chicken, the chicken flaps up onto the roof, and the dog can only stand and stare up at it.
T6-9005.t: Pronounced [닥 쫃떤 개 지붕 처다보듯]. Describes the deflated feeling when something you were chasing, such as a chance, a deal or a bus, slips out of reach.
rel: to miss, to lose hold of

T6-9006.forms: 첫술에 배부르랴 · 첫술에 배부를 수는 없잖아요
T6-9006.m: you can't expect perfect results right away; Rome wasn't built in a day (lit. would the first spoonful fill you up?)
T6-9006.ex: 첫술에 배부르랴 하잖아요. 처음부터 잘할 수는 없어요.
T6-9006.x: You know what they say: one spoonful won't fill you up. Nobody is good at something from the start.
T6-9006.e: 첫술 is the first spoonful (술 'spoonful', as in 한술), and -랴 is an old rhetorical question ending: 'would one spoonful make you full?'
T6-9006.t: Pronounced [첟쑤레 배부르랴]. Used to reassure a beginner, or yourself, after a disappointing first attempt.
rel: getting started is half the battle

T6-9007.forms: 우물을 파도 한 우물을 파라고 · 한 우물을 파다
T6-9007.m: stick to one thing and see it through (lit. even if you dig a well, dig just one well)
T6-9007.ex: 우물을 파도 한 우물을 파라고, 그분은 30년 동안 빵만 만들었어요.
T6-9007.x: Stick to one thing, as they say: he made nothing but bread for thirty years.
T6-9007.e: If you dig a little here and a little there, you never reach water; keep digging one well and you will.
T6-9007.t: The short idiom 한 우물을 파다 'to devote oneself to one field' is very common, e.g. 한 우물만 판 장인 'a master who stuck to one craft'.

T6-9008.de: 열 번 찍어 안 넘어가는 나무 없다
T6-9008.rom: yeol beon jjigeo an neomeoganeun namu eopda
T6-9008.pr: 열 번 찌거 안 너머가는 나무 업따
T6-9008.forms: 열 번 찍어 안 넘어가는 나무 없다고 · 열 번 찍어 안 넘어가는 나무 없다잖아요
T6-9008.m: persistence pays off; keep trying and you'll win anyone over (lit. there's no tree that won't fall after ten chops)
T6-9008.ex: 열 번 찍어 안 넘어가는 나무 없다고, 계속 고백했더니 결국 사귀게 됐어요.
T6-9008.x: Persistence pays off: I kept confessing my feelings, and in the end we started dating.
T6-9008.e: 찍다 here means 'to chop with an axe': strike any tree ten times and it will fall.
T6-9008.t: Often used, half-jokingly, about persistently asking someone out or trying to persuade someone.

T6-9009.forms: 공든 탑이 무너지랴 · 공든 탑이 무너지겠어요?
T6-9009.m: sincere hard work never goes to waste (lit. would a tower built with great care collapse?)
T6-9009.ex: 공든 탑이 무너지랴, 그동안 열심히 준비했으니까 좋은 결과가 있을 거예요.
T6-9009.x: Hard work never goes to waste; you've prepared so hard, so you'll get a good result.
T6-9009.e: 공든 is 공(功) 'effort' + 든 'that has gone into' (from 들다): a tower built with real care won't fall down. -랴 is an old rhetorical question ending.
T6-9009.t: Used to reassure someone waiting for results. In news, 공든 탑이 무너지다 is used for years of effort being ruined in an instant.

T6-9010.forms: 구르는 돌에는 이끼가 끼지 않는다고 · 구르는 돌에는 이끼가 안 낀다잖아요
T6-9010.m: a rolling stone gathers no moss; if you keep active, you won't stagnate
T6-9010.ex: 할아버지는 구르는 돌에는 이끼가 끼지 않는다며 은퇴 후에도 매일 공부하세요.
T6-9010.x: Saying a rolling stone gathers no moss, my grandfather studies every day even after retiring.
T6-9010.e: A translation of the English proverb: a stone that keeps rolling never gets covered in moss (이끼가 끼다).
T6-9010.t: Pronounced [안는다]. In Korean it is almost always positive (keep moving and you'll keep growing), not the older English sense of criticizing people who never settle down.

T6-9011.de: 낮말은 새가 듣고 밤말은 쥐가 듣는다
T6-9011.rom: nammareun saega deutgo bammareun jwiga deunneunda
T6-9011.pr: 난마른 새가 듣꼬 밤마른 쥐가 든는다
T6-9011.forms: 낮말은 새가 듣고 밤말은 쥐가 듣는다고 · 낮말은 새가 듣고 밤말은 쥐가 듣는다잖아요
T6-9011.m: walls have ears; be careful what you say (lit. birds hear daytime words and mice hear nighttime words)
T6-9011.ex: 낮말은 새가 듣고 밤말은 쥐가 듣는다고, 회사에서 상사 험담은 하지 마세요.
T6-9011.x: Walls have ears, so don't badmouth your boss at work.
T6-9011.e: Literally 'birds hear what is said by day, and mice hear what is said by night': someone is always listening.
T6-9011.t: Pronounced [난마른 새가 듣꼬 밤마른 쥐가 든는다]. A warning to watch what you say, especially gossip and secrets.
rel: 발 없는 말이 천 리 간다

T6-9012.de: 말 한마디로 천 냥 빚을 갚는다
T6-9012.rom: mal hanmadiro cheon nyang bijeul gamneunda
T6-9012.pr: 말 한마디로 천 냥 비즐 감는다
T6-9012.forms: 말 한마디로 천 냥 빚을 갚는다고 · 말 한마디에 천 냥 빚을 갚는다
T6-9012.m: the right words can work wonders (lit. one word can repay a debt of a thousand nyang)
T6-9012.ex: 말 한마디로 천 냥 빚을 갚는다고, 먼저 진심으로 사과해 보세요.
T6-9012.x: The right words can work wonders, so try apologizing sincerely first.
T6-9012.e: 냥 (兩) was an old unit of money, and a thousand 냥 was a fortune; yet one well-chosen word can settle such a debt.
T6-9012.t: Pronounced [말 한마디로 천 냥 비즐 감는다]. Stresses that a sincere apology, thanks or tactful word can solve big problems. Also quoted as 말 한마디에 천 냥 빚 갚는다.
rel: 가는 말이 고와야 오는 말이 곱다
speak kindly and you'll be spoken to kindly

T6-9013.forms: 아니 땐 굴뚝에 연기 날까 · 아니 땐 굴뚝에 연기 나겠어요?
T6-9013.m: where there's smoke, there's fire (lit. would smoke rise from a chimney with no fire lit?)
T6-9013.ex: 아니 땐 굴뚝에 연기 날까, 그 두 사람 정말 사귀는 거 아니에요?
T6-9013.x: Where there's smoke, there's fire. Aren't those two really dating?
T6-9013.e: 아니 땐 is an old form of 안 땐 'unlit' (때다 'to burn fuel'): smoke can't come out of a chimney if no fire was made.
T6-9013.t: Used to suggest that a rumor must have some truth behind it, exactly like the English saying. Also quoted as 아니 땐 굴뚝에 연기 나랴.

T6-9014.de: 열 길 물속은 알아도 한 길 사람 속은 모른다
T6-9014.rom: yeol gil mulsogeun arado han gil saram sogeun moreunda
T6-9014.pr: 열 길 물쏘근 아라도 한 길 사람 소근 모른다
T6-9014.forms: 열 길 물속은 알아도 한 길 사람 속은 모른다더니 · 열 길 물속은 알아도 한 길 사람 속은 모른다고
T6-9014.m: you can never truly know what's in someone's heart (lit. you can know water ten fathoms deep, but not a person's heart one fathom deep)
T6-9014.ex: 열 길 물속은 알아도 한 길 사람 속은 모른다더니, 그 친구한테 속았어요.
T6-9014.x: You can never really know what's in someone's heart; that friend deceived me.
T6-9014.e: 길 is an old measure of depth, about a person's height. You can gauge water ten 길 deep, but not the inside (속) of a person only one 길 tall.
T6-9014.t: 물속 is pronounced [물쏙]. Said after being surprised or betrayed by someone you thought you knew.

T6-9015.forms: 웃는 얼굴에 침 못 뱉는다고 · 웃는 얼굴에 침 뱉으랴
T6-9015.m: it's hard to be harsh with someone who is friendly (lit. you can't spit on a smiling face)
T6-9015.ex: 웃는 얼굴에 침 못 뱉는다고, 웃으면서 사과하니까 화를 낼 수가 없었어요.
T6-9015.x: You can't spit on a smiling face: he apologized with a smile, so I couldn't get angry.
T6-9015.e: Literally 'you can't spit (침을 뱉다) on a face that is smiling at you'.
T6-9015.t: Pronounced [운는 얼구레 침 몯 밴는다]. Advice that a smile and good manners soften anger, e.g. when facing an upset customer. Also quoted as 웃는 얼굴에 침 뱉으랴.

T6-9016.forms: 쥐구멍에도 볕 들 날 있다고 · 쥐구멍에도 볕 들 날 있겠지요
T6-9016.m: every dog has its day; good times will come eventually (lit. even a mouse hole will get sunshine one day)
T6-9016.ex: 쥐구멍에도 볕 들 날 있다고, 힘내면 좋은 날이 꼭 올 거예요.
T6-9016.x: Every dog has its day, so hang in there; good days will surely come.
T6-9016.e: Even a dark mouse hole will one day catch a ray of sunshine (볕).
T6-9016.t: Pronounced [쥐구멍에도 볃 뜰 날 읻따]. Words of comfort after a long run of bad luck. Not to be confused with 쥐구멍에라도 숨고 싶다 'I want to crawl into a hole (from embarrassment)'.

T6-9017.forms: 공짜라면 양잿물도 마신다더니 · 공짜라면 양잿물도 마신다고
T6-9017.m: people will take anything if it's free (lit. if it's free, one would even drink lye)
T6-9017.ex: 공짜라면 양잿물도 마신다더니, 무료 시식 코너에 사람들이 길게 줄을 섰어요.
T6-9017.x: People will take anything that's free: there was a long line at the free-sample counter.
T6-9017.e: 양잿물 is lye, a caustic cleaning liquid (양 'Western' + 잿물 'ash water'): if it were free, people would drink even that.
T6-9017.t: Pronounced [공짜라면 양잰물도 마신다]. A humorous, slightly mocking comment on people who grab anything free; also said self-mockingly.

T6-9018.forms: 말 타면 경마 잡히고 싶다더니 · 말 타면 경마 잡히고 싶은 법이에요
T6-9018.m: the more you get, the more you want (lit. once on a horse, you want someone to lead it by the reins)
T6-9018.ex: 말 타면 경마 잡히고 싶다더니, 월급이 오르니까 이제 차도 바꾸고 싶어요.
T6-9018.x: The more you get, the more you want: now that my salary went up, I want a new car too.
T6-9018.e: Once you are riding a horse, you want a servant to hold the reins and lead it (경마 잡히다). This 경마 comes from 견마 (牽馬) 'leading a horse', not 경마 (競馬) 'horse racing'.
T6-9018.t: Pronounced [말 타면 경마 자피고 십따]. Describes how desires keep growing once one wish is met; often said self-mockingly.

T6-9019.forms: 개같이 벌어서 정승같이 쓰라고 · 개같이 벌어서 정승같이 쓴다더니
T6-9019.m: earn money through any honest hard work, but spend it nobly (lit. earn like a dog, spend like a high minister)
T6-9019.ex: 개같이 벌어서 정승같이 쓰라고, 그분은 평생 모은 돈을 기부했어요.
T6-9019.x: Earn like a dog, spend like a minister, as they say: he donated all the money he had saved over his life.
T6-9019.e: 정승 was a top minister of the Joseon court: earn money humbly through any hard, lowly work, but spend it generously and with dignity.
T6-9019.t: Pronounced [개가치 버러서 정승가치 쓴다]. 개같이 can sound rude on its own, but this proverb is well known and not vulgar; it is often quoted about people who donate hard-earned savings.

T6-9020.forms: 원님 덕에 나팔 분다더니 · 원님 덕에 나팔 부는 격이에요
T6-9020.m: to enjoy perks thanks to someone else's position, to ride on someone's coattails (lit. to blow the trumpet thanks to the magistrate)
T6-9020.ex: 원님 덕에 나팔 분다더니, 언니 덕분에 나도 공연을 맨 앞자리에서 봤어요.
T6-9020.x: They say you blow the trumpet thanks to the magistrate: thanks to my sister, I got to see the show from the front row too.
T6-9020.e: Literally 'thanks to the magistrate, one blows the trumpet'. When a Joseon county magistrate (원님) traveled, trumpeters marched ahead of him and shared in the grand procession and hospitality, though the honor was really his.
T6-9020.t: Close to 'riding on someone's coattails', but usually light and often self-mocking about an unexpected perk. For abusing borrowed power, use 호가호위 instead.
rel: borrowing another's power to throw one's weight around
